toward him sitting in his majesty, is no part of true Christian discipline, but (as *Erasmus* <note>Desiderius Erasmus (1466–1536), a Dutch philosopher and Christian humanist who critiqued church abuses.</note> has well suggested) a piece of Antichristian tyranny. It is a thing very *loathsome* and *burdensome* to be forced to reveal one's inner self to a person whose judgment, friendship, or faithfulness we cannot be sure of; and it is completely *intolerable* to be forced to speak of such things as we do not even allow ourselves to think about, especially in front of those we might suspect will take some sinful pleasure in hearing the discussion of them.

6. Therefore, the command for such a detailed *Confession* has no basis at all in either Scripture or reason. For neither the Apostles nor Christ himself required any such specific and complete listing of people's sins, nor did they leave instructions for their successors to do so. It is sufficient to confess them more generally with a serious declaration of hatred for the sins and a resolution to leave them. In this, if the penitent <note>A person seeking forgiveness for their sins.</note> intends to lie, he might just as easily lie about the number and circumstances of his sins. Thus, there is very little justification for this command.

But if he expresses his sorrow and resolution to improve, and because of some weakness or depression <note>original: "melancholy"</note> cannot fully grasp the promise of forgiveness based on sincere repentance without a visible and tangible seal—that is, *priestly absolution* <note>original: "Sacerdotal Absolution"; the formal release from guilt pronounced by a priest.</note>—I believe a priest, filled with the Spirit of Christ and holy compassion for a repentant member of his church, may rightfully and usefully (by the authority derived from the Apostles and their successors, and by the divine power that assists the sincere exercise of his ministry) seal the forgiveness of his sins by pronouncing his absolution, and so restore peace to his troubled mind. In such a case, his sins are as certainly pardoned as if Christ himself had personally forgiven him, for Christ undoubtedly confirms in *Heaven* whatever is done here on *Earth*. I suppose *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch jurist and theologian.</note> himself would not deny this, nor think it conflicts at all with his interpretation of *Saint John*, as he does not claim that the instances he mentions are the only occasions for forgiving or withholding sins, but merely the most significant ones.

7. And just as this *voluntary confession* in general to the priest for the sake of the penitent’s absolution is useful and praiseworthy, so too is a voluntary revealing of one's self in a *more specific way* to someone who can be trusted and is fit for the office. This allows the priest to have a more perfect understanding of the state of the person's soul and thereby provide more suitable and effective counsel, which is undoubtedly a very good thing.

8. But to force every believer every year (or more often) to give a detailed listing of all his transgressions in thought, word, and deed, along with all their circumstances, is nothing but a vile and dishonest excuse to pry into everyone's private thoughts. This is done so the priest can gain a personal advantage or share secrets with church politicians to strengthen their own interests, which consist of *preserving or promoting the honor, wealth, and power they seek in the world.*

And truly, by this means, the secrets not just of this man or that woman, but of entire families and cities, and even of whole provinces and kingdoms, [are revealed...]

...and of all Christendom, may flow together into that common cistern—or, if you prefer, a sea of ecclesiastical intelligence. This is the very "eye of action" and the soul of conduct in all affairs.

9. But although this would be a sweet morsel to this false clergy <note>original: "Pseudo-Clergy"</note> we are now describing, it would be "sour sauce" to the laity <note>The non-clergy members of the church.</note>. It is a foul mark of inevitable bondage for them to be forced, under pain of damnation, to prostrate themselves at least once a year before men who are themselves sunk many fathoms deep in earthly sin. It forces them to reproach themselves by accurately and precisely exposing their own faults to people whose sincerity, judgment, or friendship they cannot trust. I say that, besides the external slavery of this practice and the performance of a ceremony that goes against the grain even for good and honorable spirits, a man may be exposed to very great dangers and harms.

Anyone whose job is to hear men accurately and obligatorily accuse themselves at least once a year has an opportunity to unjustly defame them—either through quiet hints or more direct comments. This is more power than should be put into the hands of anyone who is not a saint on earth, and we assume there are very few of those in the political system we are discussing.

10. *Interrogatories* <note>original: "Interrogatories"; formal questioning or a series of questions.</note> from such confessors may very likely prove to be lessons in sin and lust for young men and women. Knowing family secrets can sow the seeds of infinite arguments between neighbors and even between members of the same family. It would be difficult for those who know so much about a person’s private interests through this "shriving" <note>original: "Shriving"; the act of hearing a confession and granting absolution.</note> to keep their "itching fingers" from meddling in their affairs. It would be equally hard to keep their own lustful desires from soliciting the chastity of those they find vulnerable or willing, or to keep from acting as meddling informants <note>original: "Intelligencers"</note> or "game-finders" for those pursuing the pleasures of *Venus* <note>The Roman goddess of love; here referring to sexual indulgence.</note>.

Furthermore, the pointlessness of their *penances* <note>Acts of devotion or self-punishment performed to show sorrow for sin.</note>—which are supposed to represent the true cost of the sin—may harden men into the belief that there is no great harm in sinning. It teaches them to view breaking the *Law of God* as something slight, cheap, and trivial. If, instead, the only *penance* for sin were the pain of giving it up—urged upon them by the certain expectation of that most dreadful judgment to come—even if no other condition were attached to *absolution* <note>original: "Absolation"; formal forgiveness pronounced by a priest.</note>, it would make men feel the weight of sin more clearly. It would make them hurry to get out from under its burden. But to draw to an end:

But if the Church should be so dogmatic <note>Asserting opinions as if they were facts.</note>—not only in things that the general population might see as going either way, but by concluding and requiring belief in things that are point-blank against either Scripture or Reason—how does that affect the person? Such things are impossible to be true according to the faculties of any unprejudiced person, such as: *that one and the same Body may be wholly and entirely in a thousand places at once, and at a thousand miles distance between all those places* <note>A critique of the doctrine of Transubstantiation.</note>; *that we may worship a carved Image*, and the like. They hold that their share in eternal bliss depends upon a hearty belief in the truth of the Church in all things, yet what she proposes—according to all their mental faculties—is not only unlikely but impossible to be true.

### CHAPTER XXII.

1. *The dreadful invention* <note>original: "Figment"</note> *of Purgatory.* 2. *That by this frightening fable, the entire mass* <note>original: "Moles"; from the Latin for a large structure, mass, or heap.</note> *of Superstition described so far is made infinitely more weighty and burdensome.* 3. *The Antichristian doctrine that Christ's satisfaction reaches only to freeing us from the guilt of sin, not the punishment.* 4. *The various types of drudgery and slavery this doctrine and the invention of Purgatory cast men into.* 5. *A refutation of the said doctrine and invention.* 6. *That it is impossible for the sincere-minded in this life to find either Hell or Purgatory in the next.* 7. *That there is no ground for this Antichristian Purgatory in either Scripture or the Church Fathers.* 8. *The gross fraud and grand mischief of this fiction.* 9. *The conclusion of the description of this second branch of Antichristianism.*

1. AND now, finally, to make up the full weight of this Antichristian yoke and burden, suppose there were added the fear of a Purgatory more frightening than anything the Pagans imagined. That is to say: suppose the Church should determine that no souls—unless they are absolutely pure and perfect in this life (a rank of people that either does not exist, or if they did, they would not be so immodest as to easily claim to be so)—should, upon their departure from this body, go into any state of ease or blessing. Instead, they must go into a state little different from the torments of Hell, except that they are not perpetual. These torments may last for many, many years, unless care is taken to relieve and rescue those who are in this sad and dismal place. I suppose the Church would present this to the uneducated people with every possible extremity of horror, telling them of many sad and ghastly...

# Chapter XXII. The terrifying invention of Purgatory.

...ghastly apparitions, who with pale faces <note>original: "wan countenances"</note> and mournful tones have made known their extreme distress in this infernal house of correction, and have begged for assistance by asking the living to pray and pay for them as much as they could, so that they might find relief.

2. Nor would they stop at exaggerating this unbearable calamity with every imaginable myth: namely, that the souls of men were seen in a vision—by some holy man of God or another—to be tortured in wonderful and horrible ways. Some were seen standing up to their knees, others to their navel, some to their armpits, and others to their very chin in a stream of fire and brimstone. Others are run through with iron rods and roasted over the fire like geese on a spit, while foul infernal demons <note>original: "Fiends"</note> blow the coals with their black mouths or—to save their own breath—with large brazen bellows. Others scoop up the grease that fries out of these roasted souls and pour it back upon them while it is scalding hot. Some are scourged with whips made of red-hot wires, others are fried in frying pans, and others are racked and turned around on a wheel full of hot, burning hooks. Others have their bowels torn out by the fiery, crooked stings of huge, overgrown toads and serpents; and lastly, others are put into vessels of hot, scalding metals. These dismal chambers of death re-echo all the while from their hollow roofs with the mournful howlings and hideous shriekings of these tormented ghosts.

By imbuing the minds of the people with these or similar terrible fantasies, the belief in them would certainly tighten the rack of this burdensome superstition (which I have been describing all this time) to the highest pitch that the wit of man can invent. Nor could the flames of this *Purgatory* fail to provide the very fire in which these slaves and vassals of the mystical *Pharaoh* <note>The author uses Pharaoh as a metaphor for the Pope, suggesting the Church hierarchy treats the faithful like the enslaved Israelites in Egypt.</note> and his hard taskmasters—I mean that apostate High Priest <note>The Pope.</note> with the rest of his corrupt hierarchy which I am describing—should drudge <note>original: "droyl"</note> and sweat, in order to finish the required "quota of bricks" <note>A biblical reference to the labor imposed on the Israelites in Exodus 5.</note> to build these sons of pride their pyramids and palaces.

3. Therefore, people are stripped and robbed of all the comfortable support that true faith in *Jesus* Christ affords. They are made to believe that the Passion and satisfaction <note>The theological concept of "atonement" or making amends for sin.</note> of Christ takes away only the guilt of mortal sins, but not the *eternal punishment*. However, they are told it is a great favor that, by the "Power of the Keys," <note>The authority claimed by the Church to grant or humble the soul, based on Matthew 16:19.</note> this eternal punishment is turned into a *temporary* one. This is a punishment which every person is bound to undergo and satisfy, either in this life or the one to come, and either in their own person or through someone else. That is, a person is bound to do or suffer such things themselves—or have others do so for them—as the Church shall appoint or accept as satisfaction. This is also understood to apply to *venial* <note>Slight or pardonable sins, as opposed to "mortal" or deadly sins.</note> sins. Lastly, they are taught that the spots and filth of sin clinging to our nature must be completely purged out by penance <note>original: "Satisfactions"</note> and penalties; if this is not fully done in this life, it must be perfected by the purification <note>original: "expiation"</note> of fire in the next.

I say, if the people should be deluded by such *Antichristian doctrine* as this, and have the sweet and easy yoke of Christ taken off their necks—which consists only in being sincere, to the best of our power, to live according to the plain...

# The Frightful Fiction of Purgatory. Book I.

...and the indispensable Law of Christ—wherein, when we fail, we are assured that both the *guilt* and the external *penalty* are taken away through the intercession of him who is our Advocate with the Father and a perpetual sacrifice for our sins—but instead of this easy and noble service, we should be fettered and held fast in that *Egyptian* bondage we have described; into what a world of slavery and drudgery would mistaken mortals be dragged!

4. How they would be forced to exert themselves by these hard taskmasters! What running from church to church, from shrine to shrine! What howling and muttering before this saint's image and that saint's image! What beating of breasts and kissing of pavements! What fastings and vigils, performed not for self-correction, but for satisfaction! <note>original: "satisfaction"; in this context, it refers to "penance" performed to pay the debt of temporal punishment for sin.</note> What long, exhausting pilgrimages from country to country, and from one end of the Earth to the other! What prayers and offerings to make the image—or at least the priest—smile! What kissing of unpleasant relics! What vows of celibacy and abstinence from meat! What floggings and flayings of the body! What public marketing <note>original: "Nundinations," referring to the trade or sale of spiritual goods as if at a market fair.</note> of pardons and indulgences! What awe and servility shown to the priest! What strict observation of fasts and festivals! What distressing anxieties <note>original: "Scrupulosities"</note> about unnecessary opinions! What lowly postures and pitiful looks in forced confessions! What wrapping of themselves in religious robes! What imprisoning and confining in nunneries and cloisters, in solitudes and hermitages! What creeping of dying men into monks' hoods <note>original: "Cowls"</note> and rolling in beds of ashes! What sprinkling with holy water! What anointing and besmearing with "enchanted" oils! What hastening to enroll themselves in this or that holy brotherhood to share in their merits! What shaving and paring away of children's inheritances to pay for hired masses and prayers, intended to sing the dying man's soul out of this imaginary Purgatory! In short, what endless circuits of drudgery and labor of body and mind does this *Egyptian* tyrant put his slaves through under the lash of this agonizing idea:

> "That the death of Christ is not for the forgiveness of
> "punishment, but only of guilt; and that he who would go to heaven must
> "travel there at his own personal cost and expense, and must satisfy in his
> "own person for his faults and corruptions in such ways as this corrupt
> "church has prescribed!"

This is not a method for freeing souls from the pains of *Purgatory*, but of enslaving them (as I have said) to a bondage worse than that of *Egypt*. it condemns them to gather stubble and make bricks, working and drudging to maintain the wealth and magnificence of this overbearing *Pharaoh* and his cruel taskmasters. This is a servitude as abominable and anti-Christian as can be invented or imagined. It absolutely changes the condition and nature of the Christian religion—which is the most free and noble faith, and most professedly opposed to the yoke of the *Mosaic Law*—into a poor, pitiful, ignorant, and servile system of training <note>original: "Pedagogie"</note>. It makes it not only exceed the burden of *Moses*, but (as I cannot emphasize too often) the very bondage of *Egypt* itself.

5. But though this fiction of *Purgatory* would be a very profitable invention...

### Chapter XXII. The Frightful Fiction of Purgatory.

This doctrine is an invention designed to increase the wealth and power of this false clergy <note>original: "Pseudo-Clergie"</note> and to bring vast revenues to their Church. While princes and peasants, the noble and the common alike, share a fear of Purgatory and a desire to be rid of it, no one—except those who are past all shame—can deny that it is a mere fiction. It has no foundation in truth and is, in fact, contrary to what is most certainly true.

For it is certainly true, and any good Christian may feel it to be so, that Christ has satisfied the debt for both *punishment* and *guilt*. It is complete nonsense to suggest that a sincere person should be justified by the merits of Christ’s suffering and the excellence of his person (he being that innocent Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world)—meaning they are legally regarded as righteous <note>original: "Forensal sense," referring to the theological concept of "forensic justification," where God declares a believer righteous in a legal sense.</note>—and yet still be handled or treated as sinners. To do so would be like acquitting a man in court and yet punishing him for the same crime, which is utterly foolish and inconsistent.

Therefore, it is clear that no external punishment awaits the sincere soul after this life. (I cannot speak for the insincere, for whom Hell itself is their portion.) There is no fire, no whips of the Furies or demons to afflict them, and no hellish bailiffs or terrifying officers <term>Pursuivants: officials or messengers who have the power to execute warrants or make arrests.</term> of Purgatory to arrest them. Instead, they may pass freely through all guards and scouts of the invisible regions, and not one would dare to molest them.

6. Furthermore, it is impossible and inconceivable that a person who was sincere-hearted in this life—who not only believed in Christ but followed his commands to the best of their ability and skill, who truly hated all appearances of sin and was only overcome by the pressures of the body with sorrow and regret—should carry any tormenting *Hell* or *Purgatory* within themselves once they are free from the body.

Once freed from the physical body with which he so often struggled, he finds his life comfortable because of his own sincerity and the assurance of the Love of God in Christ *Jesus*. What can death be to such a man but *life from the dead*? He who can possess his soul with patience while in a prison will certainly enjoy himself in the fresh air; and he who can walk upright in fetters may easily dance for joy when he is released from them. There is so little reason for a sincere Christian to fear such imaginary monsters <term>Mormos: bugbears or monsters from Greek mythology used to frighten children.</term> or "bugbears" once they have passed out of this mortal life.

<margin>1 Corinthians 3:15.</margin>

Some may indeed use a passage from Saint *Paul* as a pretext for *Purgatory*: *If any man’s work is burned, he shall suffer loss; but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire* (1 Corinthians 3:15). This is the only place in Scripture that offers them any support. Yet, even if it were meant to refer to a *Purgatory-fire* after this life, it would not serve their purpose at all. Nor do the various passages from the Church Fathers that seem to lean this way, though entering into those would be too lengthy a task. However, the interpretation given by Joseph Scaliger and Hugo Grotius <note>Scaliger (1540–1609) and Grotius (1583–1645) were highly influential Protestant scholars and theologians.</note> is so authentic and natural, and implies a Purgatory-fire so little, that this foundation will prove very slippery for those who try to build upon it. # The Frightful Fiction of Purgatory. Book I.

Scaliger and Grotius <note>Joseph Justus Scaliger and Hugo Grotius were world-renowned 16th and 17th-century scholars and theologians known for their expertise in historical and biblical interpretation.</note> explain the phrase **as if through fire** <note>original: "ὡς διὰ πυρὸς"</note> in this way: that he shall escape, **but only as one escapes from a raging fire**. They argue it is nothing but a proverbial expression signifying the great danger he will be in. **To be saved as if through fire is a proverbial expression, signifying the greatest danger** <note>original: "Σώζεσθαι ὡς διὰ πυρὸς est proverbiale, ad significationem summi periculi"</note>. So, the actual meaning is simply this: **He will hardly escape the dreadful judgment of God**.

As for Origen's <note>An early Christian theologian (c. 184–253 AD) who speculated about a purifying fire after death, though his views differed significantly from the later Roman Catholic doctrine of Purgatory.</note> **purification of souls by way of torment** <note>original: "ἡ μετὰ βασάνου κάθαρσις ψυχῶν"</note> and similar expressions from the Church Fathers, they will never prove the kind of **Purgatory** that these "masters of mischief" would build in the Universe. These men make sure that no one can do anything meritorious in that state, nor make any progress in grace and holiness—even though they call the fire "purifying" <note>original: "Purgative"</note>. They do this because if souls could improve themselves, it would lower the price of Pardons and Indulgences. It would make men careless about hiring **Masses** for the dead and take away all that expensive concern from friends for their deceased relatives. If people believed their loved ones could get themselves out of trouble through their own behavior and careful management in the other world, they wouldn't pay the Church to do it for them.

8. But however weak their proofs for **Purgatory** might be, their motives for inventing it are very strong. This fiction makes all their other **frauds** more effective. By using it, they frighten people into an easy and foolish state of mind where they are willing to give away anything—even to the point of impoverishing themselves and their children. They do this just to satisfy those who claim they hold the keys to this prison of **Purgatory**, hoping to be persuaded either to excuse them from ever entering it or, if they must enter, to deliver them from it as quickly as possible.

But the greatest **mischief** of this cheating invention is that it is a blasphemous insult to the merits and satisfaction of our dear Savior. It is a tyrannical oppression of the consciences of simple people. Furthermore, it is such a scandal to the more **shrewd** <term>original: "nasute," meaning sharp-witted or discerning</term> that it strongly tempts them to stop believing in religion altogether, or to doubt that the soul survives after death at all. These "false apostles" have so grossly and foully abused the belief in the soul’s immortality, merely to increase their own wealth in this life and to wallow in riches, honor, and physical pleasures.

9. This is a sufficient sketch of the **second branch of Antichristianism**, which consists of **piling up a number of troublesome and unjustifiable superstitious ideas and rituals**. By these, the "yoke of Christ" is made far more heavy than the laws of **Moses**. Indeed, the burden on Christians becomes almost equal to, if not greater than, the slavery of the **Israelites** in the land of **Egypt**—that **house of bondage**, as it is specifically called in the Scripture. Therefore, I believe this particular system of things I have described may very well be considered a significant part of **Antichristianism**.

# BOOK II.

## CHAPTER I.

1. *The positive goals of the Gospel which the other branches of Antichristianism oppose.* 2. *That claiming a right to the infallible interpretation of the laws of Christ is a supplanting of his Kingly Office.* 3. *An example of that danger in the interpretations <note>original: "glosses"</note> of the Pharisees.* 4. *Various passages of Scripture used to argue that the Church is infallible.* 5. *The first general answer to these arguments, by asking whether the promise of infallibility applies to the whole Church or only a part.* 6. *The second, by asking whether the promise is absolute or conditional.* 7. *A third, that the promise cannot be universal concerning every possible subject.* 8. *A specific answer to the first passage of Scripture.* 9. *An answer to the second and third.* 10. *Infallibility was a promise only to the first founders of the Christian Church.* 11. *The meaning of the phrase "the pillar and ground of truth."* 12. *A further explanation of that passage from Paul to Timothy.* 13. *That if it is understood to mean the Universal Church, it may only refer to the Church in the time of the Apostles.* 14. *And that the same may be said of the final argument.*

1. <image-desc>Decorative initial W featuring a stylized letter with floral and foliate scrollwork in a square frame.</image-desc> We have now finished with those parts of *Antichristianism* that oppose the *privative goals* <note>Privative goals: The "negative" goals of the Gospel, meaning what it intended to remove or abolish, such as idolatry.</note> of the Gospel of Christ, which were: *the removal of idolatry and the burden of superstition from the world*. We come now to its *positive goals*, which in general is *the advancement of the Divine Life*. This advancement occurs either *personally* in Christ, or through *propagation* <note>Spreading or reproduction.</note> among his members, the Church. The divine honors and offices to which the person of Christ is raised, and which are most obvious to notice, are those of *King*, *Priest*, and *Prophet*. The opposing or supplanting of these can be nothing other than the many abhorred parts of this wicked *Antichristianism*, whose image we are now portraying in its true colors.

2. Concerning the first of these: suppose any man, or group of men—under the pretense of being the true visible Church descended successively from Christ and his Apostles—should take it upon themselves to be the *infallible interpreters of the law of Christ*. Suppose they teach that all people must embrace and submit to their interpretations <note>original: "Glosses"</note>, no matter how harsh, improbable, or even impossible they may seem. If they declare it a deadly sin <note>original: "mortal sin"</note> for anyone to doubt their decisions in this matter, this would surely be a plain opposition to, or an utter supplanting of, the Kingly Office of Christ.

# Opposition against the Regal Office of Christ. Book II.

...the Kingly office of **Christ**, and the total removal of His exercise of sovereignty, which cannot be exercised in any way other than by commands and decrees. When a King has published these, if another person has the power to interpret them in any way he pleases, the **Kingly** power will really reside in the **Interpreter**, and not in the **King**. I say, this pretended right and power of **infallibly** interpreting does, in very truth, make the interpreter King, and the King a shadow or a **cipher** <note>Cipher: A mathematical symbol (0) denoting nothing, or a person of no influence or power.</note>.

Assuredly, no earthly Prince would think himself truly sovereign over his people if all the injunctions and edicts he made were not to carry the easy, natural sense which he intended, but were instead drawn to some other meaning by any exception, evasion, or any forced interpretation that some foreign potentate should put upon them. Therefore, whoever pretends to a right and **infallibility** in interpreting the law of Christ effectively makes Christ no law-giver, and consequently no King nor Governor in his Church. What could be more grossly **Antichristian** than that?

<margin>* In his *The Eating of Fish* <note>original: *Ἰχθυοφαγία* (*Ichthyophagia*), a colloquy by Erasmus satirizing religious fasting rules.</note>.</margin>
3. "Whoever has the right of interpretation, his opinion carries the weight of divine law" <note>original: "*Cui jus est interpretandi, hujus Sententia pondus habet legis Divinae*"</note> is a saying which, although **Erasmus** put it into the mouth of a common person, is nonetheless a great truth. Our Savior knew and noted the mischievous abuse of this presumption very clearly in the instance of the **Pharisees**. They could interpret away the force of the command, *Honor your father and your mother*, by claiming it was **Corban** <note>Corban: A Hebrew term for a gift dedicated to God. The Pharisees used this as a legal loophole to avoid financially supporting their parents.</note>. Because of this, it is impossible that Christ would allow any visible interpreter to have such an unlimited right as some argue for—a right that abuses his Church and takes his Kingly Office out of his own hands. <margin>Matthew 15:6</margin> For he observed there, *That the Pharisees had made the word of God of no effect through their traditions*; that is to say, through their exceptions, qualifications, and interpretations of it.

4. Ah, but they will pretend that Christ will make his Church **infallible**; and if they are so, he himself will really reign through them, as they will always interpret according to his mind. They will pretend that his making the Church **infallible** appears plainly from such passages of Scripture as these: <margin>* Matthew 16</margin> *That the gates of Hell shall not prevail against her*; <margin>* John 14</margin> and again, *I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever, even the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive, etc.* <margin>* John 16</margin> again, *When he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth.* <margin>* 1 Timothy 3:15</margin> To which they add the words of St. Paul to **Timothy**, where he seems to call the Church the **pillar and ground of truth.** <margin>* Chapter 4</margin> And lastly, that passage to the **Ephesians**, where Christ is said to have *given some to be Apostles, and some, Prophets, and others, Evangelists, and others, Pastors and Teachers, for the perfecting of the Saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ; until we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, and cunning craftiness whereby they lie in wait to deceive; But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the Head, even Christ.*

# Chapter I. Of pretended Infallibility.

Let these passages then be their official authorization <note>original: "Letters patent," a legal document from a monarch granting a right or title</note>, their grand, pretended commission for infallibly interpreting and never making mistakes in any decisions or conclusions; we shall easily discover that it is a mere pretense.

5. For I ask whether this promise of *infallibility* applies to the *whole* visible Church throughout history, or only to *some part*. It is clear that it is not an *absolute*, *unconditional* promise to the *whole*, because the different parts of Christendom disagree so much on matters of belief. But if it applies only to *some part*, where in these promises is that part named, so that their right of interpreting might be proven to the world? There is no *particular church* specified there—neither the *Greek* nor the *Roman*, neither the *Russian* <note>original: "Muscovian"</note> nor the *Armenian*, nor the Church of *Prester John* <note>A legendary Christian patriarch and king whose kingdom was often associated with Ethiopia in the early modern period</note>, nor any other church. From this, it is plain that no *particular church* can claim any right to such a privilege.

6. Again, suppose some *particular church* did have a promise; how does it appear that the promise is *unconditional* to this *particular church*? Is it not based on the assumption that they will seriously and sincerely apply their minds to find the truth, and purify their souls from all those worldly and physical obstacles to it? For this spirit of *infallibility* cannot reside in a body that is subject to sin. Purity of heart and life is the very light and clear organ—the very eye of the soul. To think of a privilege of *infallibility* without holiness is like imagining a promise to see without light or eyes.

Therefore, it is such a hypocritical idea that one cannot tell whether it is more to be mourned or laughed at when a church pretends that God has an unstoppable plan to make them *infallible* in every tiny detail <note>original: "Punctilio"</note> of controversy, and yet not a plan to make them *holy* and *good*. It is a sign they despise or hate *goodness* because it is contrary to their corrupt natures, but they desire the privilege of *infallibility* because it suits their natural pride; they use the boast of it as a tool to achieve all their deceitful goals. We might add to this that it is questionable whether the promise is made to any visible church at all, rather than to those who (like the Apostles) were chosen, sanctified, and faithful born-again <note>original: "Regenerate"</note> men. For none but these are truly the *Church of Christ*; if he fulfills his promise only to those who are his true Church, that is enough.

7. Furthermore, whether this promise is *conditional* or *unconditional*, we can be certain that this *infallibility* is not *universal* regarding every possible subject. Therefore, for a church to concern itself with things that are not necessary for salvation nor truly spiritually helpful <note>original: "edifying"</note> would be to go beyond their authorization or commission. By doing so, they would forfeit—or at least receive no benefit from—the promised assistance.

8. But let us specifically examine the texts of Scripture themselves. The first of these implies nothing more than this: that the Church of Christ shall never cease to exist, and that death shall never be able to triumph over her—neither to wipe her out in this world, nor to prevent her from a glorious immortality in the world to come. For "the gates of hell" <note>original: "πύλαι ᾅδου" (*pylai hadou*)</note> signifies no more than "death" <note>original: "ᾅδης" (*hades*)</note>, "abolition," or "the state of the dead." But this could be true of the Church even if it were not *infallible*. This first piece of evidence <note>original: "Allegation"</note> is that weak.

<meta>This page continues the argument that scriptural promises of "infallibility" are not absolute or universal, but are instead conditional on obedience and specifically directed to the original Apostles.</meta>

# Of pretended Infallibility. Book II.

9. As for the second point, it would be fortunate for those who cite these arguments if they were merely weak; in fact, they are strong evidence against their own position and support our view, which holds this *infallibility* to be *conditional*. For if you read the entire context, it goes like this: *If you love me, keep my commandments; and I will ask the Father, etc.* <margin>John 14:16, 17.</margin> This implies there is a *condition*: they must love *Christ* and keep his commandments if they expect to receive that Spirit which will abide with them *forever*. (In this context, "forever" means as long as they lived, as the word often signifies in Scripture.) It is further added that this is a Spirit that the *world cannot receive*. Therefore, this strongly implies that the Spirit does not reside in those who are worldly and focused on physical desires. 

This *conditional* nature of the promise is also suggested in the third passage cited: *When the Spirit of Truth comes, he will lead you (or guide you) into all truth.* That is, he will lead you as a *human being*, not haul or drag you like a stone or a mindless animal that has no free will. So we see plainly that this *infallibility* is *conditional* wherever it is mentioned.

And while I do not doubt that if the *condition* is met, the *promise* will be fulfilled for all people as far as is necessary for their salvation, these are not the best passages to use for that purpose. The *promise* here is not *general* but directed to specific men in certain circumstances. It is evident that it was meant for them in particular and does not imply a continuous succession. For the men he speaks to there are described as those he was physically present with, who would be reminded by the *Paraclete* <note>The Holy Spirit, acting as an advocate or counselor</note> of what he had said to them while he was present. They were those who were sorrowful because of his departure, along with other limiting circumstances that cannot belong to any future line of men, but were specific to the *Apostles* to whom he spoke.

10. Indeed, *infallibility* itself seems to be a promise most proper to them, as they were meant to lay the foundations of the Church and build the house of God. Since they have done this in terms plain enough regarding everything necessary for salvation, the promise of *infallibility* needs to go no further. The Church is safe forever after, provided she stays close to what was plainly delivered by her first founders; nothing else needs to be forced upon believers as an infallible requirement.

11. And as for that fourth citation, where the Church seems to be called *The Pillar and Ground of Truth*: <margin>1 Timothy 3:15.</margin> Suppose we accept the clever theory of *Cameron* and *Capellus* <note>John Cameron and Louis Cappel, influential 17th-century Protestant theologians</note> regarding this passage. They suggest that the phrase ["*The Pillar and Ground of Truth*"] should be separated from the preceding words (using at least a colon) and that we should understand what follows ["*without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness*"] to be merely a parenthetical *tribute* <note>original: "Elogium"</note> to the mystery of the Gospel. In this view, the Apostle was carried away by the importance of the weighty points he was delivering: *God manifested in the flesh, etc.* <margin>1 Timothy 3:16.</margin> 

Thus, *The Pillar and Ground of Truth* may actually be the preface to the grand points of Christian truth which—once that parenthesis is set aside—follow immediately after. This matches the common practice of the *Jews* to place before such fundamental principles of knowledge the title of "The Foundation and Pillar of Wisdom" <note>original: <term>יסוד ועמוד החכמות</term> / *Fundamentum & Columna Sapientiæ*</note>. If read this way, this passage is completely stripped of any power to prove the point for which it was cited.

# Chapter 1. Of pretended Infallibility.

<margin>Matthew 5:13, 14.</margin>
12. But if you apply this title to the *Church*, it was the *Ephesian Church* where *Timothy* resided, which vanished long ago. And what other church, besides every *individual church*, can use this passage to claim *infallibility*? The fact that these churches openly contradict one another disproves such a claim. Besides, the phrasing itself—[*pillar and ground*] <note>Refers to 1 Timothy 3:15, where the church is called "the pillar and ground of the truth."</note>—might not signify a guaranteed performance, but rather the duty they ought to perform. It is like when the Apostles are called the *light of the world* and the *salt of the earth*; these titles only signify what they ought to be, not what they were forced to be. For those who ought to be light and salt may nonetheless hide their talent or grow flavorless <note>original: "unsavoury"</note> through their own fault. This happened with *Judas* and all his successors—false apostles who call themselves the servants, but are actually the betrayers, of the Lord *Jesus*.

13. But lastly, suppose the *Church in general* at that time was meant here. It does not follow that because the *primeval* and *apostolic* Church was intended by God’s providence to present only the truth to the world as articles of belief, the Church throughout history should always do the same. Care was taken to ensure the Church's first establishment was truthful and solid. Once that was done—which was sufficient for "free agents" <note>Meaning humans acting with free will rather than being forced by God.</note> to manage the Church’s affairs correctly—the success of the Church depended on their own industry and faithfulness. At the very least, they were not assisted or driven by any miraculous or supernatural force to keep things pure and undefiled <note>original: "intemerate"</note>. In my view, what is considered sufficient for every individual is also sufficient for the Church: that the Christian doctrines and commands are faithfully recorded in the Gospels and other Apostolic writings. With the help of God’s ordinary grace (which is not irresistible), people may shape their lives and beliefs according to those things that are clear. And everything necessary for salvation is clear. If this rule had been followed, no error would have crept into the Church to this very day.

14. This last point also helps answer the final passage cited, as it seems only to describe a special provision by God to firmly establish His truth during the first ages of the Church. To this end, He appointed not only *Pastors* and *Teachers* (roles that still continue), but also *Apostles* who had a specific mission from Christ Himself, who breathed into them the Spirit of Truth. He also appointed *Prophets* and *Evangelists*—men specifically inspired and assisted to build the structure <note>original: "Fabrick"</note> of the Church according to Christ’s purpose, as He supervised everything through the miraculous help of His Spirit. Therefore, whatever was written for the public use of the Church while those to whom our Savior said *the Spirit would abide with them forever* and *lead them into all truth* were still alive—or whatever was approved by them—is truly certain and infallible. However, any later inventions or additions to the Church must be measured against this unerring rule.

# Of Pretended Infallibility. Book II.

<margin>Ephesians 4:10.</margin> These unerring Pastors and Teachers, Apostles, Prophets, and Evangelists, were not a promise made to all successive generations, but were an extraordinary gift. As the Text itself implies, Christ gave these gifts at that specific time—namely, during his solemn Coronation or Triumph when he ascended above all Heavens so that he might fill all things. He cast these down as a Royal Bounty <note>original: "Largess," a gift or money given by a superior to an inferior.</note> upon his Church for her speedy perfection <note>original: "completement"</note>, so that she might grow into the unity of the Faith and the Knowledge of Christ. This was done so that she might not be carried about with every wind of doctrine, but instead adhere only to that which was delivered by those heavenly-inspired and miraculously-assisted Ministers of the Gospel. 

I believe that acknowledging this fact would have been the only sure way to keep the Church in Unity forever. In contrast, the claim to *Infallibility* in the subsequent Church—where, in truth, it did not exist—and the resulting decision to impose things with the same authority as the Apostles themselves, would naturally become the source of all Error, Schism, and Confusion.

### CHAPTER II.

1. That the safe delivery of the Apostolic Writings down to us by the Church does not imply <note>original: "infer"</note> her Infallibility. 
2. That the plainness of Scripture in points necessary for Salvation removes the need for an Infallible Judge. 
3. That because the Scripture does not point to any Infallible Judge or any faithful Keeper of Traditions, it by that very fact <note>original: "ipso facto"</note> declares itself the only sufficient Guide. 
4. That there is not only no need for an Infallible Judge, but it is actually better that there should be none.

6. That although a visible Judge is necessary in civil court cases, it is not at all the same in matters of Religion. 
7. That every private person has not only a liberty, but a command, to judge for themselves in matters of Faith. 
8. The said Right or Privilege is also demonstrated by Reason. 
9. That the Reason or Judgment of every private man is not a "private spirit" in the scornful sense that some people use the term. 
10. That the claim to a right of judging for oneself in points of Faith does not make a man superior to his Church,

12. Nor does it imply that he thinks himself wiser than his Church, but rather that he is more careful of his own eternal concerns. 
13. That it is not his own private wisdom he sticks to, but the Wisdom of God, which is known to all who are not willfully blind. 
14. That the Church is not Infallible, as proved from the example of the Jewish Church. 
15. That the same reasoning applies to the Christian Church. 
16. That the lack of an Infallible Interpreter is no great loss to the common people. 
17. That their assurance of the truth of the Scriptures by the Spirit is a belief <note>original: "Tenet"</note> that should not be so arrogantly dismissed as some people suggest. 
18. That this Spirit is properly the Spirit of Faith, distinguishable from the Spirit of Knowledge and Wisdom. 
19. The notorious fraud and excessive mischief of this pretense of Infallibility.

## Chap. II. Of pretended Infallibility.

1. BUT having been defeated <note>original: "worsted"</note> in their scriptural arguments, they will claim logical proofs <note>original: "Demonstrations in Reason"</note>—based on the assumption that they are the true visible Church, having descended in an unbroken line from Christ and his Apostles—that *Infallibility* is forever granted to them as an inheritance.

Their first argument is, *That unless the Church were continuously Infallible, we could have no certain and Infallible belief in the Holy Scriptures, which are declared to be such by the Church.* But I briefly answer that, even supposing this continuous Church were a reliable and certain transmitter <note>original: "Conveyer"</note> of uncorrupted copies of the Holy Scriptures, it does not follow that they must be *Infallible Interpreters* of those Scriptures. This is no more true than saying that the faithful delivery of *Plato's* and *Aristotle's* writings to all future generations implies that those who delivered them are Infallible interpreters of them. For they might preserve the writings of either author by a diligent comparison of copies during every transcription; furthermore, there might be a special watchfulness of Providence over these Holy Writings to preserve them from any significant errors <note>original: "material blemishes"</note>, as they are so incredibly necessary for the continuation of those truths published by men who (as I have already indicated) were Divinely and Infallibly inspired.

<margin>Book 7. chapters 10 & 11.</margin>
I have already plainly demonstrated in my *Explanation of the Mystery of Godliness* that such writings exist, which are sufficient for passing down the knowledge of Christ and were written by those who were infallible witnesses of the Truth. I also showed how we may be assured that the books which commonly bear those titles are genuine, without any need to rely on the *Infallibility of the Church*. Therefore, I think it unnecessary to say anything further about it here.

2. In the second place they will claim, *That the Church must be Infallible, or else there will be no Infallible Judge of Controversies; indeed, there would not even be any Authority in the Church to manage its affairs.* But the answer is easy and brief: there is no need for any such *Infallible Judge*, and therefore no need for the Church’s *Infallibility*. This is because the Scripture is a *Sufficient Standard of Faith* <note>original: "Rule of Faith"</note> for all who have understanding, whether they are educated or uneducated, in all things necessary for Salvation. The belief and practice of these things will bring a person to Heaven.

The Spirit of God is therefore the only *Infallible Judge* here, and has declared as plainly as any successive human judges could—in those things necessary for life and Salvation—what is to be believed and what is to be done. If we believe and practice these things specifically, and also believe in general and without doubt <note>original: "implicitly believe"</note> in the rest of the Scripture, standing ready to obey it when its meaning becomes clear to us, we are in a safe condition. We need not doubt that it will go well with us in the afterlife <note>original: "other State"</note>. For it is obvious that what is necessary is made plain in the Word of God to all people; otherwise, Salvation would not be sufficiently revealed to the world. If it were not plain, then what we quoted above from St. *Paul* would not be true, nor would the Providence of God have been sufficiently watchful in laying the first foundations of his Church.

# On the Pretended Claim of Infallibility. Book II.

...necessary truths, God would have afterwards raised other people with the same Apostolic purity of life and the same power of performing miracles to supplement the former ones (which has never happened). Otherwise, those other necessary truths—taught by the first Apostles but not written down by them—would have been entrusted to *Tradition*. However, this would have been a very slippery <note>original: "lubricous"</note> and dangerous path, and one unlikely to be chosen by Divine Providence.

But if any such path had been taken, surely the Scripture itself (which everyone agrees upon) would have pointed it out to us. It would have also told us if an Interpreter had been established, so that whatever remains necessary for our eternal safety could be communicated to us without error. But since the Scripture is silent on this matter, it openly declares itself to be sufficient for all those who apply themselves to understanding it with sincerity and care. Certainly, every person—considering that their eternal salvation depends on it—will feel compelled to do this for themselves. Whereas, if others interpret the Bible for them, they might do it more carelessly or even dishonestly.

4. Besides that, it is an uninformed and foolish <note>original: "unskillfull and inept"</note> desire to want an *Infallible Judge* who has already settled <note>original: "concluded"</note> all controversies for us. For that would prevent or block that private and special communication which God has with those souls who are most dear to him. In a special way, He assures those souls of conclusions that cannot be reached by just anyone. But once the *Infallible Determination* of the Church has been passed, every person’s certainty will be the same, and God will have, so to speak, given the staff of authority out of his own hands. 

Therefore, since there is no external *Infallible Judge* to interpret obscure places in Scripture, God’s right to dispense his special favors is preserved. Men of a more devout and intellectual spirit are divinely employed and earnestly committed to extraordinary piety and holiness, so that they may win the favor of that inward Infallible Interpreter—the Holy Spirit, which the world cannot receive. By the light of His assistance, they are enabled to reach the true sense of those writings which He himself dictated to the Apostles and other holy men of God.

<margin>1 Corinthians 14:40.</margin>
5. And lastly, the claim *that the lack of Infallibility will take away the Authority of the Church* is a very weak conclusion. For her authority is perfectly intact when it comes to urging those truths and duties in Scripture that are plain to everyone—even to those who do not dream that they themselves are infallible. And those things that are plain are the ones most useful for our safe passage to Heaven. As for those doctrines that are more obscure, if they are nonetheless useful and edifying, as well as various rites and ceremonies, the Church has the authority to declare and appoint them even though she is not infallible. *Let all things be done decently, and in order.* But as for how the Church should behave toward Dissenters <note>those who disagree with the established Church</note>, I have spoken about that more extensively elsewhere and will not touch upon it here.

I will only add that in things that are truly debatable, I believe it is everyone's duty—whatever their private judgment and inclinations might otherwise be—to reach a compromise with the authority of the Church. For the sake of peace and order, they should be willing to be guided by the Church's decisions.

# Chapter II. On the Pretended Claim of Infallibility.

There is a third **logical fallacy** <note>original: "Sophism"</note>. It seems like a plausible objection against the idea that Scripture alone is sufficient to guide and rule us without a public, infallible interpreter. The objection is that this would be like arguing that civil law is sufficient on its own without a public **judge**.

However, we have already suggested that a **clear law** (and we assert that Scripture is clear in all matters necessary for salvation) may not need a judge. This is especially true when a person's conscience feels bound—on pain of eternal damnation—to understand it correctly. Furthermore, we suggest that having a public minister or interpreter explain Christ's law is not denied by those who believe Scripture is the sole rule of faith. This applies as long as the explanation is clearly based on the law and is obvious to all fair-minded people, whether they are unlearned or educated.

For my own part, as I said before, in passages that are not so clear, if interpretations are made that do not contradict other plain texts of Scripture and promote the goals of the Gospel (which I have specified elsewhere), I hope no one shall offend God by finding common ground with these interpretations. In such circumstances, we assume the interpreters have acted conscientiously and in the fear of God, rather than for their own selfish ends or worldly satisfaction. Undoubtedly, in this case, they can show their commission and prove they act by authority. <margin>1 Corinthians 14:26.</margin> *Let all things be done for the sake of spiritual growth.* <note>original: "edification"</note>

But it is a weak and flawed **inference** <note>original: "Illation"</note> to argue that because every **civil** dispute must be decided by a judge, there must also be an **infallible, decisive judge** for all the trivial and useless controversies that arise among Christians regarding Scripture and religion. Civil disputes cannot be left undecided without someone being harmed. However, no one is harmed by leaving those useless—or at least unnecessary—questions undecided. People may hold different opinions without or hurting one another, provided they stick to that known Law of Christ: the **Royal Law of Charity** <note>The "Law of Charity" refers to the command to love one's neighbor as oneself.</note>.

In fact, deciding such controversies through a pretended "Infallible Judge" would be a massive wrong to one of the parties. It would burden their consciences and restrict their liberty, making the way to Heaven narrower than Christ made it. That is exactly what an "Infallible Judge" does when they force their decisions on people under the threat of eternal damnation. But God, in His infinite wisdom and mercy, has not given the slightest hint that such a takeover <note>original: "Usurpation"</note> of power should occur. Therefore, since this "Infallible Judge" was not appointed by God and cannot be appointed by man, Scripture alone—and not these so-called infallible decisions—must be the rule of our belief.

Even worse, they would become the **judge of the Church** and thereby superior to the Church—and nothing could be more wild or extreme than that.

This seems like a major difficulty at first. But I answer that every individual has a **commission** from the very Word of God—even a **command**—to judge for themselves. For instance, where we are told to <margin>1 Thessalonians 5:21.</margin> **test**

8. But it is not *Scripture* alone, but *Reason* itself that plainly authorizes <note>original: "commissionate"</note> *private spirits*—as they call them—to judge for themselves. And since that which is offered to him is the whole Christian faith (for that is what makes a true church), it is plain that his *reason* and *conscience* are being appealed to, to decide whether the whole sum of the *matters of faith* <note>original: "Credenda"</note> in Christianity is true. That is to say: though the church, and he who argues on behalf of the church, have already judged and firmly concluded that the Christian faith is a true faith in its entirety and in every part, and make no appeal away from their own judgment regarding themselves; yet, regarding the person they would convince, they appeal to him to see if the grounds of their belief are solid. Thus, they imply and acknowledge that he is the judge for himself in these affairs, whether you call that faculty in him a *private spirit* or whatever you please.

### Chapter II. *Of Pretended Infallibility.*

...private *spirit*, it judging according to the *universal sense of human nature*, and in the way every person judges when they are unbiased. Nay, if this will not suffice, I say that the judgment which is made in this way is the judgment of that *Universal* King and Law-giver, the Eternal Son of God. It is his sentence in these cases, but written in the tables of our hearts and pronounced by our mouths as if by the *herald* <note>original: "Præco"</note> of a court. It is very far from being the judgment of a mere *private spirit*.

Rather, that should be called the judgment of a *private spirit*—even if it bears the title of an *Infallible Church*—which is decreed not according to the plain texts of Scripture as all unprejudiced men would certainly understand them, nor according to those indelible characters of Truth which Christ the Eternal *Word* <note>original: "Logos" (Greek for "Word" or "Reason")</note> has written in the rational souls of all mankind, but according to biased interest and depraved desires. The sentence of thousands, nay of millions, of such judges is more the verdict of a *private spirit* than the judgment of the lowliest *private* man who speaks from such principles as I have declared.

10. Now, as for that offensive accusation of *making oneself superior to the Church* by claiming a *judgment of discretion* <term>judgment of discretion: The Protestant principle that individuals have the right and duty to use their own reason and conscience to evaluate religious teachings.</term>; I say, he claims no more than what is necessarily given to him, as I have already demonstrated. For if there is an appeal to the *reason* and *conscience* of a *private man* in the effort to convince him, he is *by that very fact* <note>original: "ipso facto"</note> made a judge; and if being a *judge* in this sense is to be *superior*, he is necessarily superior. 

But I see no necessity that his being a *judge* in this way for himself makes him *superior* to his Church. Indeed, if he judged for his Church, he would thereby be their superior; but judging for himself only, he usurps no superiority over the Church. He is only obedient to Him who is superior to both—that is, to *Jesus Christ*—following His plain injunctions and precepts, whether written in the outward Word or legibly engraved upon the table of his heart. Therefore, to follow the plain and inevitable dictates of one's own conscience, which is the tribunal of God, is not to exalt oneself above the Church, but to submit oneself to God and exalt Him above all.

11. *Nor does a man make himself equal to his Church in this*; because he does not define truth for others, but for himself. In the meantime, he professes himself ready to obey the visible Church in such things as are not contrary to the express commands of God and Christ, and to those immutable characters of Truth which He has imprinted upon the souls of all men—which are found there unless gross violence and self-interest have obscured or erased them.

12. *Nor (in the last place) does he make himself wiser than his Church*; which would also be an offensive accusation. But without immodesty, it may be thought that a private man may be more concerned with his own important affairs, and more faithful to his own eternal interest, than many thousand men put together. Therefore, though he may not have as much intelligence and scholarship as they, he may conduct his own affairs more safely than if they were put into their hands—especially when those who pretend to be guides to Heaven for others seem to be wholly taken up with the things of this world, as if they had forgotten their intended journey.

Instead, it consists of the clear and obvious testimonies of the Word of God and the common, unquestionable notions of universal human nature. These were written by the finger of that Eternal **Wisdom** who created all things upon the minds of all men who are of sound mind. Therefore, it is a plain and readable copy of that **Wisdom**. So, he who adheres to it does not prefer his own **wisdom** over the **wisdom** of the Church but faithfully submits himself to the **Wisdom** of God. The Church ought to submit to this as well, rather than trying to erase those imprinted marks of Truth from the souls of men to enslave them to itself and the corrupt interests of its kingdom of darkness and massive deception <note>original: "Imposture"</note>.

14. But I have been more wordy <note>original: "copious"</note> than was necessary or intended in refuting this dream of **Infallibility**. Surely the **Church of the Jews** was as truly the Church of God as the visible **Christian Church** is, and it has promises just as magnificent in the book of **Isaiah**. For what is spoken in Chapter 54 applies to the Church of the **Jews** first, as **Grotius** <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645) was a Dutch humanist and theologian known for his biblical commentary.</note> has observed. There it is said, *That they shall all be taught by God, and that with everlasting kindness God will have mercy upon them.* Yet this Church made such a gross mistake that its governors and leaders did not recognize their **Messiah** when he came into the world, but instead put him to a most shameful death.

<margin>* Jeremiah 5:30–31</margin>

# Chapter 2: Of Pretended Infallibility.

...saying, "*The Temple of the Lord, The Temple of the Lord, etc.*" <note>Jeremiah 7:4</note> For all that those who call themselves "The Temple of the Lord" do is not necessarily right. This appears in the same chapter, where they are accused of committing idolatry openly in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. This could not have happened had they not fallen into the hands of blind and erroneous guides, who caused them to stumble in their ways and leave the ancient paths. Yet, in the meantime, these guides made that presumptuous boast: "*That the Law shall not perish from the Priest, nor the Counsel from the Wise, nor the Word from the Prophet,*" even while they were imagining mischief against the true prophets of the Lord, as you may see in Jeremiah 18.

But <margin>Micah 3:6</margin> Micah <note>original: "Micaiah"</note> says plainly, "*That for the prophets who are only for easy times and for good cheer, Night shall be upon them, and they shall have no vision; and it shall be dark unto them, so that they cannot divine. Such Seers shall be ashamed, and Diviners confounded, as having no answer from God.*" And <margin>Isaiah 56:10, 11</margin> Isaiah <note>original: "Efay"</note> complains that the watchmen of the city are blind; that they are ignorant shepherds who cannot understand; they all look to their own way, every one for jollity or gain. Thus it is clear that the Jewish Church, though it was in such a special manner espoused to God, was not secure from error but did actually fall into very great mistakes.

15. And the Christian Church has no greater assurance; for if avarice, pride, and sensuality seize upon its guides, it may also fall into as great errors and blindness. <margin>1 Corinthians 10:12</margin> The Apostle says, "*Let him that stands take heed lest he fall.*" It might have been a timely warning for the Church of Christ early on—which was not only tottering but almost universally lapsed into that widespread heresy of Arianism <note>original: "Arrianism"; a 4th-century theological movement that denied the full divinity of Jesus Christ</note>—to reflect upon itself: that while it stands, it stands upon its good behavior. It is not so infallibly wise that it cannot be surprised by error and overrun by it, unless true and sincere holiness clears its eyes and keeps it from being lost in such mists of darkness.

And truly, if the Church was so prone to error over twelve hundred years ago, it is high time for her to awake and consider if—after so many ages of ease, wealth, honor, and an abundance of all things—she has not "grown fat and kicked" <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 32:15, describing a people who become rebellious and forget God because of their prosperity</note> and cast the commandments of God behind her back. She may have brought in a merely carnal law of her own devising, more suitable to the will of the flesh and the advancement of her own worldly interests. But it is sufficient in this place to have demonstrated that *she may err*; to define exactly *how* she has erred is beyond the scope of my present discourse.

16. We have fully defeated that fiction <note>original: "Figment"</note> of pretended infallibility. Our opponents have no reason to mourn its downfall, except perhaps on behalf of the common people who are illiterate—as if they would be made incapable of any certainty of belief, and consequently of salvation, because they have no infallible grounds to build upon once the authority of the Church is taken away.

There is certainty in what the *Universal Church* agrees upon, and has agreed upon in all ages, and that is the *Scripture*. Such a *Universal Tradition* as the *Scripture* possesses is acknowledged as a firm *Foundation*. The *Church* may be an unfailing conveyor of the Bible down to posterity without being an infallible *Interpreter* of it. I must admit that the unfailing nature of this transmission may be a more complex matter than what every ordinary person <term>original: "Vulgar man"</term> can figure out for himself; though it is infinitely less difficult than proving that the *Church* which would claim him for their own *Community* is *Infallible*.

<margin>* Caelius Secundus Curio against Floribellus.</margin>
Indeed, I must confess, I do not know how it would be possible for a Church to even prove itself a Church—much less an *Infallible Church*—without the *Scripture*. And therefore, the belief in the *Scripture* seems to be the most immediate belief of all, as Curio <note>Caelius Secundus Curio (1503–1569) was an Italian humanist and reformer.</note> says well: *For how, I ask, can someone who doubts the faith and authority of the Divine Scriptures believe the Church, which has no authority without those same Scriptures?* <note>original Latin: "Nam qui de fide & authoritate Divinarum Scripturarum dubitat, quomodo, quæso, credet Ecclesiæ, quæ nullam habet sine eadem Scriptura authoritatem?"</note>

For our Savior Christ says, *No one comes to me unless the Father draws them.* <note>John 6:44</note> *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.* <note>John 10:27</note> For this reason, there is a *discerning spirit* in those who belong to Salvation, which tells them whether it is the Voice of God and Christ or not. <margin>John 10:4-5</margin> For the true *Shepherd* goes before them, and the sheep follow him *because they know his voice; but they will not follow a stranger, but will flee from him, because they do not know his voice*, as our Savior so excellently explains. I say, therefore, that the *Voice*, the *Call*, or even the *Whistle* (if you will) of the true *Shepherd* is the *Holy Scriptures*. By an immediate sense, people are assured that these are the *Call* of the Shepherd. Today, for those who belong to God's chosen ones <term>original: "election of God"</term>, these Scriptures are as the Voice of Christ and his Apostles when they were on Earth—the power of whose speech, assisted by the Spirit, led people captive into that Faith which brings Salvation.

And without any doubt, that same Word of Salvation—which is found in those Holy Records—will have the same effect upon the common people when it is seriously and zealously urged by men of sincere faith and upright belief, without mixing it with human inventions. As many as are ready will be won to an unshaken belief in the Truth of Christianity as it is presented to us in the Holy Scriptures. For the Scriptures themselves have the light, life, and very breath of Christ and his Apostles wrapped up within them, which rouses the common people to a firm and lively Faith. This remains true even though many subtle "sophisters" <term>deceptive reasoners</term> of the Kingdom of Darkness might try to entangle them with crafty and perverse reasoning or silence them in public debate. Therefore, they are kept safe in their belief in the Scripture by the power of that Spirit within them; by virtue of that Spirit, there is an unbreakable harmony and agreement between their own spirits and the Scripture, even though they cannot defend themselves with scholarly learning <term>original: "humane Literature"</term>, nor by sharp reasoning or the depths of Philosophy.

# Chapter II. Of Pretended Infallibility.

I think I may safely and properly call the *Spirit of Faith* a "doctrine of men" when it is viewed strictly on its own, separated from the *Spirit of Knowledge* and of *Wisdom*. This distinction between *Wisdom*, *Knowledge*, and *Faith* <note>original Greek: σοφία (sophia), γνῶσις (gnosis), and πίσις (pisis—likely a transcription error for *pistis*, meaning faith)</note> was noted long ago by Origen <note>Origen of Alexandria (c. 184–c. 253) was an influential early Christian theologian.</note> in his book against *Celsus* (Book 6), based on the writings of *Saint Paul*. Truly, I think his interpretation is remarkably solid. He suggests that the highest and greatest gift of the Spirit is that Divine *Wisdom* by which a person is largely able to understand the reasons and deeper philosophical foundations of the truth of the Christian mystery. 

The next gift is *Knowledge*—which includes things like understanding antiquity, history, comparing prophecies, and using the tools of external human learning, such as the liberal arts and languages. The third is *Faith*, which is included in the others but is a gift that is both more general and more necessary. Its nature is as I have already described: *an immediate adherence to the word of Truth found in the Scripture, through the power of that Spirit which lives in sincere and well-meaning souls who have a deep and perceptible fear of God and are ready to go wherever He calls them.* Because of an indescribable harmony between their hearts and the truth of Christ’s voice echoing in the Scriptures, these people will surely follow their true Shepherd’s call. They will turn away from the voice of the stranger and the "hireling" <note>A "hireling" is someone who works only for pay and has no true care for the sheep; see John 10:12-13.</note> who enters the sheepfold only to rob, kill, and steal.

From this, we see further that this pretended *Infallibility* of the Church regarding the Scripture is as useless as it is false. It is much as if the Moon should take it upon herself to testify for the Sun that he emits light; anyone who is not blind will necessarily see the sunlight even if the Moon were below the horizon. Likewise, the holy children of God—the chosen and faithful—will feel, taste, clearly see, and discern that the Scripture is the Truth of God. They recognize this by the light within the text itself, which corresponds with the Spirit derived from the Father of Lights that He has poured into their hearts. This, as I said, is the *Spirit of Faith*, and it is the certain portion of every member of Christ, whether or not they can prove things through *Knowledge and deep Reason*. 

If they are attacked by critics <term>original: "Cavillers"</term>, it is wise to send such people to their fellow church members to whom God has also given the *Spirit of Knowledge* or of *Wisdom*. Alternatively, it may be more prudent to let them go as they came; those who ask questions not with the goal of being seriously built up and instructed in the Truth, but for the sake of fault-finding, contention, and a conceited hope of puzzling the person they pretend to seek information from, are not worth the trouble of a conversation.

19. The fraudulent *goal* that this false Christian Church might be pursuing with this aggressive boast of *Infallibility* is very obvious, as are the *harmful consequences* of it. What could this lead to except making this anti-Christian power absolute? It allows them to decree and declare whatever would increase their own honor and wealth without anyone flinching or complaining <term>original: "whinching"</term>, no matter how contrary it seems to common reason, the express Word of God, and the commands of Christ. Because the Church's ruling is declared "Infallible," they claim it must be right, no matter how strange or contradictory it looks compared to any rule we might think is correct.

Indeed, they are so careful that even the *prayers* used in public and the celebration of the Holy Eucharist <note>The Christian ceremony of Holy Communion.</note> are *unintelligible*. This is done lest the power of certain scripture passages in the public service might release people from the blind obedience they are held in under this anti-Christian usurpation.

2. To this, you may add—and this really should have come first—an insulting description of the *Law of Christ*. They call it a book full of nothing but dangerous obscurities, a *flexible* or *lead rule* <note>original: "Lesbian or Leaden Rule." They claim these were not written by any divine command, but only because accidental circumstances moved the Prophets or Apostles to write them. And when they want to speak most modestly, they say it is an *insufficient law or rule*. Therefore, they claim it must be completed by rules of their own invention, or whatever they choose to force upon the world as *traditional doctrines*.

### Chap. III. *Other oppositions against the Regal Office of Christ.*

...and usages. I say, to **revile the Law of Christ** in this way is to nullify it, and by doing so, to nullify His sovereignty over His Church. This betrays the Church into the hands of a stranger, allowing him to treat the people however he pleases and to change times, laws, and customs. Consequently, nothing might remain in Christianity that could in any way oppose the interests of these usurpers.

3. In short, then, they may claim that the Scriptures are entirely obscure <note>original: "obscure all over"</note> simply because they are difficult in some places. But we have already sufficiently argued that enough of it is clear to enlighten the sincere seeker <note>original: "single-hearted"</note> on the path to eternal salvation. Under the pretense that some passages have uncertain meanings, they might remove the entire Bible from use. This is done so that the verses that clearly expose and rebuke their false doctrines and practices never reach the eyes of the people. For (as a Church Father <note>The "Fathers" were influential early Christian theologians and leaders.</note> once noted), "The Word of God is a lamp by which the thief is caught" <note>original Latin: *Verbum Dei est Lucerna, ad quam fur deprehenditur*</note>; and as our Savior Christ said long ago, *They hate the light because their deeds are evil.*

Furthermore, the accusation <note>original: "imputation"</note> that the Scriptures were merely written for specific occasions <note>i.e., the claim that the Epistles were only situational letters rather than eternal law.</note> is as weak as it is impious and blasphemous. It suggests that the Spirit of God would not assist the Apostles most when the situation demanded it. It implies He would have to study how to inspire and enlighten them, unable to do it spontaneously <note>original Latin: *ex-tempore*</note> or as the need arose, but would instead be caught unprepared. These ideas reek of gross worldliness <note>original: "carnality"</note> and ignorance regarding the very nature of God and His Holy Spirit. Christ promised the Spirit would never fail to be with the Apostles for the proper settlement of the Church's affairs; that is, it would not desert them as long as they lived and served in the ministry. Therefore, this must make the Scriptures extremely precious and of inestimable value to all sincere believers.

Therefore, any single paragraph from the letters of **Saint Paul**—to whom Christ appeared, calling him from Heaven and commissioning him as an Apostle to build the foundation and first structure of His Church—ought to be preferred over many thousands of so-called "infallible" councils, which could never show any such extraordinary commission to prove their own **infallibility**. For by that miraculous appearance to Paul from Heaven, and by appointing him as an Apostle, God proclaimed to the entire world that He would infallibly assist him. Therefore, what Paul shared with the world should be an irreversible law for all of Christendom. Consequently, to nullify the authority of Saint Paul’s writings is to abolish the very Law of Christ—a most rebellious and blasphemous undertaking against the sovereignty of Christ Himself.

4.
