Surely, these would be very **anti-Christian** examples: for instance, if the formal forgiveness <term>Absolution</term> for a person who kills his father or commits incest with his mother should be five or six times cheaper than for a person who takes two holy orders <note>Religious ranks or degrees.</note> in a single day, or who is

What could insult the essential Law of God and Christ more than making so many heinous transgressions seem less important than that trifle of human tradition: *only ordaining at certain times of the year?*

It is as if these leaders think they are wiser than the wisdom of God himself. they act as if they could entertain and educate the people more effectively with incredible and ridiculous stories than with the teachings of *Jesus* Christ and the sober, easy-to-understand historical truths that Divine Providence has recorded for the instruction of his Church.

In the end, this will surely deliver them to eternal death.

Since all of these are expressly against the commands or laws of Christ, it is a most reproachful and traitorous affront to him, the true Head of the Church. It is a plain declaration against his right of sovereignty to make any laws or institutes so contrary to those he himself has established.

9. The same applies to annulling <note>original: "nulling"</note> at any time whatever is binding according to the *universally-known laws of God and Nature*. For these are the laws of Christ, as he is the <term>Eternal Word <note>original: "Logos"</note></term>. Any power practicing this would reveal itself plainly as Antichristian.

## CHAPTER V.

1. *That the claim of repeating the offering <note>original: "Oblation"</note> of the real Body of Christ diminishes the excellence of Christ's priesthood.* 2. *Further details on the severity of this wicked insult.* 3. *Addressing a potential excuse <note>original: "subterfuge"</note>.* 4. *A more dangerous attack against Christ's priesthood and the primary purpose of his suffering.* 5, 6. *Claiming that Christ’s blood only removes the guilt of sin but not the punishment: how brutally Antichristian this is.* 7. *Further details on the severity of this spiteful act of Antichristianity.* 8. *That nothing can be more fundamentally Antichristian than this doctrine.* 9. *That this crime, given the circumstances, seems worse than that of Judas, along with the deceit of this wickedness.* 10. *Also, the great harm it causes.* 11. *Wrongs committed against Christ's role as Mediator.* 12. *An answer to some weak excuses.* 13. *A further disproof <note>original: "confutation"</note> of such Antichristian errors and bad practices.* 14. *The deception and harm of creating many mediators.* 15. *The specific harm this does to our growth in grace and holiness.*

It is regarded as a special honor and perfection of that office (Hebrews 9):

> *Nor did he enter heaven to offer himself again and again, the way the High Priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own. # Oppositions against the Priestly Office of Christ. Book II.

But this horrid reproach against the person of Christ is made even worse if they are so brutally serious about forcing it into the minds and beliefs of men that they will violently attack and even execute <note>original: "flay"</note> those who deny it. 4. Even if their malice or arrogance fails in that regard, they may still attack the sacred office of Christ’s *priesthood* with a more dangerous and harmful attempt. This is an ungrateful and insulting poison that would eat away the very heart and sweetness of the Christian religion. It would dampen and overshadow the grace and glory of the *priestly* <term>Sacerdotal: relating to priests or the priesthood</term> function of the Lord *Jesus* and nullify the main purpose of his sufferings. That purpose was to satisfy the wrath of God for the sins of the world by making himself an atoning sacrifice <note>original: "Propitiatory Sacrifice"</note> for them. This was done so that everyone who believes in Christ *Jesus*—following the gentle terms of that *New Covenant* which he established with his blood for the forgiveness of sins—might be certain of God’s favor. By striving to follow his commands according to the light and strength given to them, they are justified by faith in the suffering and merits of Christ, rather than by any works or merits of their own.

<margin>Romans 5:1</margin>
It is abundantly clear throughout all the writings of the Apostles that this is the essence of the New Covenant and the true summary of the most acceptable and joyful news of the Gospel. That is: *being justified by faith in a legal sense* <note>original: "Forensal sense"; a legal term referring to being declared righteous in a court of law</note>—meaning we are acquitted and cleared <note>original: "assoiled"</note> from the guilt of all our sins—as well as being sanctified and purified from them in varying degrees, according to our maturity and growth in Christianity. This clearance from guilt necessarily implies safety from punishment. As the Apostle says, *being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.* This is certainly the very nature and spirit of the Gospel message <note>original: "Evangelical Dispensation"</note>. It is the sweetest and most refreshing flower in all of God’s garden for fallen mortals, and it is the special motivation for sincere souls to be loyal, obedient children and genuine lovers of his Son, *Jesus*.

5. Therefore, it follows that nothing could be more savagely and brutally Antichristian than to uproot this comforting plant—this Tree of Life—from the church, which is God’s paradise. For such is the Cross of Christ, upon which that holy atoning sacrifice hung. The power of his death is a cooling balm that heals the wounds and stings of a troubled conscience—which is often most distressed in those who are most sincere. Therefore, the atonement of our dying Savior, found in his heart-wrenching suffering <note>original: "Soul-melting Passion"</note>, is presented to the soul as her only true cure.

These hardships should be medicinal and curative for whatever corruptions of nature we struggle with. However, to teach that they are merely for the satisfaction of sins already committed—as if the sacrifice and atonement of Christ on the Cross were not enough to calm the wrath of God unless every person also suffers for themselves the punishments from which Christ came to free us—is a direct attack on the Gospel. Nothing more "Antichristian" could ever be devised.

9. This doctrine seems abominable enough on its own; but if we consider the grounds and circumstances by which it is pushed into the Church by that Antichristian power we are describing, it becomes infinitely more hateful and cursed. *Judas* betrayed Christ for a piece of money into the hands of those who crucified him, for which his memory is cursed by all future generations. And yet, Christ was betrayed only to that which he was willing to undergo—namely, he willingly underwent the wrath of God so that he might shelter us from it, which was the very purpose of his Agony and Passion.

Now, suppose this false Church we are depicting should, for a piece of money, betray the very purpose and design of Christ's Passion, and completely frustrate and empty it of value. Would Christ not be worse betrayed here than by *Judas* himself? For *Judas* betrayed him only to what Christ intended: that he might be an offering <note>original: "Oblation"</note> to God for the forgiveness of sins for all believers. But this Antichristian Church, by frustrating the purpose of his suffering, is more barbarous than *Judas*. They betray the Savior of the world to an unwilling death and disappoint him of that prize for which alone he gave his dearest blood. They are more truly the murderers of this "Just One" than the very Jews who crucified him, because they rob him of that which was the "life" within his death, and which was prized by him above his own life: that is to say, his being a sufficient sacrifice and atonement for the sins of the whole world.

That Church which barters away this holy and weighty Article of the Christian Faith for profit—scaring the people into believing they must buy Pardons and Indulgences <note>A practice where people paid the church to reduce the punishment for their sins.</note>, hire priests to sing their souls out of Purgatory, or redeem themselves with sums of money from cruel imposed penances—must certainly, in this regard, act against the *priestly office of Christ* <note>original: "Sacerdotal office"</note> in the highest and most heinous manner imaginable.

10. This is the wicked *fraud* they commit, and the *harm* <note>original: "Mischief"</note> is equally great. # Chapter V. Oppositions against the Priestly Office of Christ.

In both cases, unless they die so perfect—a state which no modest person would ever imagine for themselves—they place the minds of serious people upon an unbearable torture of anxiety <note>original: "intolerable rack of solicitude"</note> regarding the torments of *Purgatory*. They terrifyingly describe these as being of the same nature as the pains of Hell, though not of the same duration. Alternatively, they swell the minds of the vain-spirited with unhealthy growths of pride, based on the conceit of such merit as never was, nor ever can be, in any living person who is only a human being. Lastly, they deface the unique glory of Christ and his religion, in which there really breathes nothing but sweetness, pity, and tender compassion. Our Head and Sovereign, the Lord *Jesus*, endured those great torments of both mind and body on the Cross to set his people free, so that they might serve him in a way of noble freedom <note>original: "Ingenuity"</note>, contrary to that bloody and cruel slavery <note>original: "vassalage"</note> in which Satan had previously enslaved the world.

Therefore, this false Church—through the fiction of Purgatory and the bloody, cruel penances imposed on the flock of Christ (by merciless whippings <note>original: "Flagellations"</note> and the stripping of skin <note>original: "excoriations"</note> from the flesh)—acts more like the priests of the Devil, that old tyrant, than like the ministers of the Gospel of the Son of God. They would make Christendom take on the same appearance <note>original: "hue"</note> as ancient Paganism again, and sell the children of *Israel* into a second *Egyptian* bondage to be afflicted and oppressed under those hard taskmasters. I have already abundantly noted how grossly Antichristian this state of things is.

11. But yet there is a further opposition against Christ's *Priestly office* <note>original: "Sacerdotal office"</note>, and a very significant one: the way he *intercedes and mediates for us with God*. Concerning this, the Scripture is very clear. Just as in the former case it stated that *Christ was offered but once*, so in this case it says *that our Mediator is but one*.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:5, 6</margin>
*For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

Here, not only is the doctrine asserted *that there is but one Mediator*, but the reason is added below: *who gave himself as a ransom for all*. Since this act is unique to him alone, there can be no Mediator between God and Man but him. The merits of his suffering <note>original: "Passion"</note> and all the perfections of his life are of such infinite virtue—since he is the declared Son of God—that to join the merits of any saints or angels with his in this regard would be a reproachful and blasphemous devaluing of the supreme excellence <note>original: "Supereminency"</note> of his condition.

Therefore, since the right of Mediatorship based on merit belongs to Christ alone, it must necessarily be an act of Antichristianism and an injury against Christ's person to join any other with him in that office. It is as if he himself were not sufficient, but were so weak and unable for that function that he required assistants <note>original: "coadjutors"</note>.

12. As for those arguments <note>original: "Allegations"</note> that *God will spare a city for the fifty righteous people in it*, and that *he would protect Jerusalem for the sake of his servant David, because he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord*, and that *he will be merciful to thousands of those who love him and keep his Commandments*: no reasoning from these Scriptures will apply to the matter at hand. For these all concern earthly matters <note>original: "Temporal concernments"</note>, where the fate of the righteous would be entangled with that of the wicked in the first place. As for the example of David, he is acknowledged to be a type <note>a symbolic figure foreshadowing a future reality</note> of Christ.

But if their *merits* add anything to the merits and sufferings of Christ, how was he a perfect High Priest, or how were his *merits* perfect?

Therefore, it is manifest that to create other *meritorious* mediators besides Christ is an Antichristian reproach and a slander against the perfection and excellence of Christ’s *Mediatorship*.

14. This priesthood has sold away the *unique mediatorship* of Christ, as well as the virtue of his precious death and passion, for a piece of money, not considering the grievous mischiefs that may come upon the Church by multiplying patrons and mediators.

For how easily are the careless people lulled asleep in security by thinking they have such a sure friend in this or that Saint, whom they have personally chosen for their patron! They honor them with certain superstitious ceremonies and think they have so obliged them that, even if they live however they please, they will nonetheless get safely to

I will not even mention the creation of entire swarms of other mediators based also on the account of their own merit. Therefore, it is manifest that to make other *meritorious mediators* besides *Christ* is an antichristian insult <note>original: "reproach and calumnie"</note> against the perfection and excellence of *Christ’s mediation*.

I say, the diverting of our devotion and affection away from Christ into so many side-streams, and onto objects from which there is infinitely less obligation for us to become good and holy, is nothing less than the hazard or loss of our eternal salvation.

It is plain, therefore, that the opposing and undermining the ends and usefulness of the priestly <note>original: "Sacerdotal"</note> office of Christ in the way I have declared would be a very significant part of that *idea of* Antichristianism which I endeavor to describe.

### Chap. VI. Oppositions against the rest of the Titles of Christ.

...is to have them wholly at their own devotion, and to abuse them and mislead them as they please, it would plainly be to act in an Antichristian way against this second title of Christ, *The Light*. This would defeat the purpose of his coming into the world, which was to be a *light to enlighten the Gentiles*, and to bring those who sit in darkness out of the prison-house. Christ has also passed this title down to his true followers and successors: *You are the light of the world*. What, then, are those who are not only failing to be shining lights themselves, but are also industrial promoters of darkness and ignorance, and diligent hinderers of any true light that others might bring into the Church?

4. The third title of Christ is *The Life*, as it is written in *St. John's Gospel: In him was life, and the life was the light of men* <note>John 1:4</note>. I believe *St. Paul* describes this life very favorably when he says *that the Kingdom of Heaven is not food or drink, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit* <note>Romans 14:17</note>. Christianity, therefore, is a gift of inward *life* that flows out into all commendable and useful actions. It is not a Babel <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, representing a state of confusion and division</note> of confusing and entangling opinions and useless observances, or a heap of ceremonies and ideas. Instead, it is a steady dwelling in God, who is *Love*. He will teach and enable us, through an inward sense of life, to love him with all our hearts and souls, and our neighbors as ourselves—which is the most important fulfillment of the whole Law.

Therefore, if instead of this holy gift of the Spirit and Life, there were introduced a rigid adherence to empty opinions and unhelpful observations of many different ceremonies, this would be an Antichristian offense against this third title of Christ. In doing so, we substitute tasteless theories and dead formalities in the place of the power and life of godliness.

5. The fourth title is *The Mighty God*. The *divinity of Christ* is an established article of our faith and such a vital part of his person that whatever belittles, weakens, or infringes upon it must be considered significantly Antichristian. Such practices would include the building of temples and altars, the burning of incense, and religious appeals and prayers to saints or angels.

Indeed, even if no prayers were offered to them, the solemn placement of the *relics of saints* in any church or chapel—making them the patrons or *guardian spirits* <note>original: *Tutelar Genii*</note> of a city or province—would be nothing less than *idolatry*. This is a superstition much like that of the ancient pagans with their *talismans* <note>original: *Telesms*</note>, their *protective statues* <note>original: *Palladiums*—referring to the sacred image of Pallas Athena believed to protect Troy</note>, and their *guardian gods* <note>original: *Dii Tutelares*</note>. The pagans imagined that the presence of these gods was kept nearby through these superstitious ceremonies, making them patrons and protectors of their cities and countries. Therefore, if Christians—by religiously placing the *relics* of a particular saint in a specific city—should be so superstitious as to place their *trust* in the *aid* of these saints against pestilence, war, thunder, earthquakes, or the like, believing them to be powerful and kind protectors of the place, this would undoubtedly be a kind of religious worship. It could be nothing less than the sin of *idolatry*.

## Oppositions against the rest of the Titles of Christ. Book II.

It is idolatrous, just like *invocation* <note>original: Invocation; the act of calling upon a saint or deity in prayer</note>, because it likewise attributes to that specific invisible power what belongs only to **God**. For there is no certainty of the presence—and consequently the assistance—of an invisible power in any one place, unless the nature of that power is to be in all places at once. Therefore, anyone who places their *trust* for aid and assistance (in the manner I have described) in a particular invisible power, treats that power as *omnipresent* <term>present everywhere at once</term> or *omniscient* <term>all-knowing</term>. These are the incommunicable attributes of God; to do this is to commit *idolatry*, as I have argued more fully above in similar cases.

By giving these divine honors, we equate such patrons or mediators with the only-begotten Son of God. This makes him less than he is, and just like them; that is to say, it obscures the uniqueness of his divinity and effectively denies his Godhead.
<margin>* Colossians 2</margin>

Yes, you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, etc.* The meaning of this is surely that, although the *Israelites* sacrificed to God as they thought (or claimed) according to the Law of *Moses* during their time in the wilderness, because they also served and acknowledged other gods besides him, he concludes—rightly and justly, even by human reasoning—that they did not really serve him at all. That is, they did not acknowledge him to be what he was: the only true God. Because they failed to understand the excellence of the Object to whom divine worship is due—acting as if God were so common that there could be many like him—they did not direct their worship to him, but to a fantasy or idol of their own making, to which they profanely gave the name of *Jehovah*. For the true *Jehovah* was not so low a being <note>original: "vile a Being"; here meaning common or of little value compared to his true status</note> that anyone else could share in divine honor with him.

It is the same with Christ, who is the same true God, blessed forever. Anyone who gives the *divine honor* due to him alone to saints or angels denies his *divinity* and makes him just like one of them. This would be one Antichristian way of undermining his Godhead: by making mere creatures equal to him.

These are the true *Israelites*, in whose mouth is found no guile <note>original: guile; deceit or cunning</note>, and who—through the guidance of that Spirit by which they are regenerate—follow the Lamb wherever he goes.

# Oppositions against the rest of the Titles of Christ. Book II.

9. Therefore, since *Christ* is such a true *Father* to his genuine Church—renewing and regenerating their minds through his Spirit into the holy feelings that belong to all those who are indeed the sons of God—treating them as if they were mere statues made of wood or stone, or rather dead material to be carved upon and inscribed with whatever a self-proclaimed "Infallible Power" chooses to engrave on them, is a major Antichristian insult against the Fatherhood of Christ. 

It acts as if he does not produce living children who possess a sense of discernment in spiritual things (just as any animal birth possesses natural senses). Instead, it treats the chosen people of God as nothing more than a count of logs, bricks, or stones to be shaped or ordered according to the whims and arrogance of a self-willed power. This power, under the pretense of an "infallible and unfailing succession" that must exist in the Church, has stepped into the place of Christ.

"The greatest reverence is owed to a child" <note>original: Maxima debetur puero reverentia (Juvenal, Satires)</note> is a most true statement concerning every child of God. For there is a divine sense within them, against which anything unholy or distasteful will grate harshly. They will find anything false to be completely out of harmony with both those unchangeable principles of truth in their own unbiased minds and the written Word of God, which was recorded by the same Spirit that gave these Christians new life.

Therefore, as I said, to use these people as if they had no life, no spirit, and no sense of discernment—expecting them to passively accept the commands of this usurping power without any conviction or personal appeal to their conscience, like a notebook or a blank piece of paper that is written upon by whatever hand pleases—is a massive injury against Christ. He is the *Everlasting Father* and the holy regenerator who brings his true Church into his own life and likeness. 

But to murder and massacre these children of his because they so boldly "act like their Father" <term>original: Patrissare; to take after or imitate one's father</term>, and so conscientiously and carefully walk in their Father's footsteps while witnessing his truth to the world—I leave it to any man to judge if anything more hellishly Antichristian could be imagined against the Fatherhood of Christ than that. For what can be more hostile and contrary to a *Father* than to murder his genuine children, specifically because they so vividly resemble him and so faithfully stick to their Father’s virtuous practices and principles?

10. I might also add that exhausting the minds and bodies of men with countless external ceremonies—making them "dance" or "trot" from one superstitious ritual to another—might cause the spiritual birth to fail. It is similar to how over-exerting women with dancing or hard labor often causes them to miscarry during a natural pregnancy. However, I will not dwell on these things.

# Chap. VI. Oppositions against the rest of the Titles of Christ.

[This power would] be a subverter of the *peaceable* government of *Christ*, and be the author of an Antichristian tyranny and confusion. For example, if this usurping power should invent new articles of belief for its own benefit, contrary to the known principles of Scripture and reason, and require the Church of *Christ* to profess these; as well as appoint suspicious rituals, smelling strongly of idolatry and superstition; it would be nearly impossible for this not to cause vast divisions and tears in the Church, filling the world with strife and opposition.

Also, if they should make it their business to define the sense of Scripture with a more restricted meaning than was necessary for the Church, and force their determinations and expositions upon men as essential points of belief; this would also work greatly against the *peacefulness* of the Church. Men are, in a way, naturally <term>propending</term> <note>original: "propending"; meaning naturally inclined or leaning toward</note> to think one way or another in matters that are not necessary for salvation. Therefore, unnecessary violence would be done to the consciences of men, thereby setting the world on fire. In contrast, what is general is broad and unifying; it includes everyone and allows them to live peaceably side by side without jostling or crowding.

12. But the *folly* and *fraud* of this over-refined curiosity is the effort to gain—or rather extort—respect from the people. It is an attempt to make their office seem significant, their learning great, and their judgments <term>unerrable</term> <note>original: "unerrable"; meaning infallible or incapable of making an error</note>, so that they may feel their own authority and make others feel it, even to the point of causing discontent and instability within the Church of *Christ*. It is as if living as an example, urging the practice of what is plain in Scripture, and maintaining an orderly discipline in those matters would not gain them more respect and make them more honorable in the eyes of both God and man. Or as if they would not appear more infallible by following in the footsteps of him who is *the Way, the Truth, and the Life*, rather than by grossly abandoning that path for the sake of worldly advantages. The discovery of such *frauds* must surely make them hateful to all men. And finally, as for having their authority felt, Christ has shown them the way, if they would only follow it: <margin>Matthew 7:29 & Chapter 23</margin> *He taught as one having authority, and not as the Scribes; for they say, and do not.*

13. This is one way of acting *Antichristianly* against that sacred title of *Christ, The Prince of Peace*. There is another way, more foul and detestable than a heart unacquainted with the "depths of Satan" could imagine; and that is, if this Antichristian power we are describing should take it upon themselves to release the princes of Christendom from the *oaths* and *covenants* they make to one to another to maintain peace, as well as to release subjects from their *oaths of allegiance* to their sovereigns. Would this not break into pieces all the bonds of unity that not only religion but the laws of nature provide, thus destroying the sacredness of an *oath*, which is the *end of all strife*? <margin>Hebrews 6:16</margin> How then can that power claim a right of succession to the *Prince of Peace* while it removes the strongest bond of peace that human affairs are capable of?

## CHAPTER VII.

1. *Any system that naturally opposes and suppresses the Divine Life is Antichristian in the highest degree.* 2. *Such as Idolatry, Superstition, and all the previously mentioned oppositions to Christ's offices and titles.* 3. *The opinion of a power in the Sacraments "by the work performed" <note>original: "ex opere operato"; a Latin theological term meaning that a sacrament is effective simply by the act of doing it, regardless of the person's spiritual state</note>, and the idea that we do not need to pay attention during our devotions.* 4. *Empty rituals and "dumb shows," and being satisfied with the mere performance of a religious duty, regardless of the spirit behind it.* 5. *Easy Absolution and trivial penances.* 6. *Full Indulgences purchased with money from Church authority.* 7. *A general note concerning the harms of various oppositions against the Divine Life.* 8. *The deceptive appeal of imagining a Church power and pomp greater than that of an Empire.* 9. *The weakness of the arguments for such a claim.* 10. *The resulting harm in turning the minds of the clergy away from the study of truth and holiness:* 11. *Indeed, making them oppose everything that is true and holy if it conflicts with their goals of ambition and greed.* 12. *That such a proud, "Luciferian" <note>original: "Luciferian"; referring to the pride and fall of Lucifer; used here to describe extreme arrogance or worldly ambition in the church</note> power as this would be the very ruin of the Kingdom of Christ on Earth;* 13. *And the turning of his Church into a mere marketplace or fair.*

# Chapter VII. The Divine Life in General.

...suffering all those hardships during his pilgrimage here on Earth, and of submitting himself to the shameful and inexpressibly painful death of the Cross; for anyone to oppose, supplant, or in any way defeat this serious and earnest design of his—through any sanctioned method or system of things—would certainly be *Antichristian* in the highest measure.

Let us now, therefore, consider distinctly and clearly the most significant ways of opposing or undermining this design. We will examine those depraved laws, constitutions, or practices in a Church that tend to extinguish the *Divine Life in general*, or are more *particularly* directed against its *root* or *branches*—namely, either against *Faith* (the belief in the essence of Christianity) or against those inestimable graces of *Humility*, *Purity*, and *Charity*.

<margin>Book I. ch. 12, 17, 18, etc.</margin>

2. To depict this opposition against the *Divine Life in general*, I do not need to paint with any new colors. Those various forms of *Idolatry* and *Superstition* which I have noted in the first and second sections of *Antichristianism*, and which lead people’s minds toward external rituals that accomplish nothing, instead elude the right intention of *Zeal* and *Devotion*. These should better our spirits and make us more inwardly and vitally holy and righteous. Instead, these external acts naturally put the *Life of God* in the soul to sleep or suffocate it; like false food, they either poison or starve it.

There are also those oppositions against the *offices* <note>original: "offices"; referring to Christ's roles as Prophet, Priest, and King</note> of Christ: vilifying his Law, removing it from the eyes of the people, or reading it and the public service in an unknown language <note>Refers to the use of Latin in the liturgy, which was not understood by the common people</note>. These include interpreting his serious commands as mere "advice" <note>original: "Advices"; some theologians argued certain moral commands were optional "counsels of perfection" rather than requirements</note> left to our pleasure to follow or ignore; false interpretations <note>original: "Glosses"</note> put upon *The Oracles of God* by pretended infallible interpreters; and defeating that mighty engine of obedience to Christ—which is the affectionate meditation upon his death and passion, and his direful sufferings for us—by diverting our thoughts and distracting them with several insignificant objects, petty advocates, and patrons <note>Refers to the veneration of saints and intercessors who "rob Christ of his honor"</note> who run away with our devotions. These rob Christ of his honor and our souls of the chief means of their sanctification and salvation. These, along with several other particulars I might mention, are plain Antichristian assaults and attacks on the *Divine Life in general*, and they tend to sweep everything away before them.

3. To these you may add those ungodly assumptions: that it is sufficient to count our prayers without fixing our minds on what we say; that a more wandering and general attention will suffice while our specific thoughts wander to whatever else we please; and that the Sacraments confer *Grace* "by the work performed" <note>original: "ex opere operato"; the Catholic doctrine that sacraments are effective by the very act of being administered, regardless of the recipient's internal state</note>. It is even argued that the very difference between the Sacraments of the Old *Covenant* and the New is that the former conferred Grace "by reason of the work of the worker" <note>original: "ratione operis operantis"; depending on the faith and devotion of the person performing or receiving the rite</note> while the latter do so "by reason of the work performed" <note>original: "ratione operis operati"</note>. They argue that no inward good intention is required in the person who receives the Sacraments. What can more weaken those earnest longings and hearty aspirations of our souls toward a real renewal of our natures into true holiness and righteousness than such corrupt ideas as these?

### Antichristian Oppositions against Book II.

4. Feeding the people with "dumb shows" <note>original: "dumb shows"; visual rituals or ceremonies performed without verbal explanation, preaching, or intelligible meaning</note>—instead of searching their consciences and stirring their zeal through understandable exhortations or forms of devotion that remind them of their duty, imprint holy things upon their minds, and inflame their desire for them—is another way of robbing the *Divine Life* of the nourishment it needs to grow. This also includes the general misconception regarding all *acts of religion*: the idea that a duty is fulfilled simply because the act is performed *externally*, regardless of the motivation. Such acts are meaningless unless they proceed from that fountain of life that should be overflowing <note>original: "ebullient"</note> in every born-again <note>original: "Regenerate"</note> Christian, and without which no one can reasonably consider themselves spiritually renewed. Certainly, such opinions, customs, and practices must eventually erase true and living holiness from the world.

5. Furthermore, we can imagine a more *Antichristian* poison that would wonderfully dampen and numb men in all their efforts toward true *sanctity*: that is, *easy absolution and minor penance after a routine confession*. For *confession* <term>Confession: the formal acknowledgement of sins to a priest</term>—which is so rigorously forced by this *Antichristian* Church I am now describing—is accompanied by the mistaken belief that upon receiving *absolution* <term>Absolution: the formal release from guilt or punishment for sin, granted by a priest</term> and performing the assigned *penances* <term>Penance: an act of devotion or self-punishment performed to show sorrow for sin</term>, they are then "right and straight" and in as secure a condition as if they had never sinned. The just punishments of their offended consciences are quieted by the soft and false interference of the priest’s claimed authority to forgive where God has bound. (In reality, everyone is held accountable to that eternal judgment at the last day, no matter how much the priest pretends to have the power to release them here; they shall answer for what they have done in the flesh, and no *absolution* or *penance* can clear them unless they truly forsake their wicked ways and become sincere converts to God.) I say, from this system of *absolution* and *penance*, it must follow that the reins will be loosened on the necks of all men. They are led to understand what a trivial thing it is to sin against God when they can be reconciled on such easy terms. 

In contrast, it would create a greater sense of reverence and awe in men’s spirits to let them be condemned or acquitted by their own consciences. These consciences, well-assisted by the Word of God and the light of Reason and Nature, would apply the Law against them and never stop urging them until they have achieved a genuine sincerity of heart. When they have reached that state, Christ within them and His Word without them will absolve them and give them peace of mind. If necessary, they may also receive *absolution* from a sober and faithful priest whose honesty and exemplary life have made him fit for such a serious duty, as I suggested earlier when I touched upon this argument.

6. But the most outrageous *Antichristian* effort against the *Divine Life* would be the persuasion that, by paying certain affordable sums of money and performing minor superstitious acts, they can obtain—through the supreme ecclesiastical authority—full *indulgences* <note>original: "Indulgences"; documents sold by the Church that were claimed to reduce the time a soul spent in Purgatory</note> and *pardons* for vast numbers of years, and the certainty of freeing themselves or their friends from *Purgatory* <term>Purgatory: a place of suffering where the souls of those who died in a state of grace are purified before entering heaven</term>.

As, for example, suppose that some churches—or, if you will, many—may

### Chapter 7: The Divine Life in General

...may have purchased from the ecclesiastical sovereignty a permanent and full *indulgence* <term>Indulgence: In the Catholic tradition of this era, a grant that reduced the temporal punishment for sins</term>, so that he who prays before such an altar in this church should have free remission of all his past sins and security from punishment. Suppose that such a piece of *devotion* at some other altars, and in some other churches, would procure the pardon of sin and punishment for twenty, thirty, fifty, or a hundred thousand years; and that the saying of such and such prayers at such an altar would deliver a soul out of purgatory; that bowing at the name of *Jesus* may procure, *as often as it is done* <note>original: "toties, quoties"</note>, twenty years of pardon; that the mere stooping to kiss a cross on the pavement of a church earns an indulgence or pardon for all a man's sins; that the rattling off of so many prayers—especially if there is the weight of some consecrated medal, such as an *Agnus Dei* <note>original: "Agnus Dei"; literally "Lamb of God," a wax medallion blessed by the Pope</note> or something similar, attached to them—will save a soul out of purgatory; that one salutation of the Blessed Virgin shall gain eighty years of pardon; that saying a certain short prayer while devoutly looking on the picture of *Christ* shall obtain ten thousand days of pardon, and saying others no less than a million <note>original: "ten hundred thousand"</note> years; and for merely looking on a certain crucifix, six thousand years of pardon.

The examples of these suggestions would be infinite. I have produced enough already to imply a system in a church that is entirely opposite to, or destructive of, that life and holiness *Christ* came to plant in the world. Therefore, such a system cannot but be judged as very foully *Antichristian*.

7. I do not need to go about proving the *falseness* and *unjustifiableness* of these proceedings, as they are damnable at first sight. Nor do I need to point out the fraud, since it is so obvious; which is, as I have suggested above in similar cases, the swindling <note>original: "emunging"; literally "wiping the nose," used here to mean tricking someone out of their money</note> of the people out of their money. The *mischief* here is the opposition to, or extinction of, the *Divine Life*, as it will also be in both its *root and branches*. Thus, we need not note any other *mischiefs* hereafter other than those comprised in the subjects we shall discuss, the *mischiefs* being expressed in the very titles of the argument. # Antichristian Oppositions against Book II.

...sorts of very respectable and profitable promotions <note>original: "Preferments"; positions of power or status within the church</note> to support everything. Why, you will say, this much is very good news, and it is desirable that it were so indeed: that since Religion is the most sacred and precious thing in the world, those who are the supporters and pillars of it in a special way should be the most richly splendid and adorned.

9. I confess that a man might think so at first sight. For it seems like nothing more than respect for God, whose servants they are by a more specific dedication. But by the same logic, our churches should be the most splendid as well as the largest buildings, especially since there is no danger of infecting these stone walls with either pride or any other unseemly passion.

But suppose that these intended "living stones" <note>A biblical metaphor from 1 Peter 2:5, referring to the believers themselves as the spiritual components of God's temple</note> of the Temple of God were as unmoved by pride or lust as the dead stones of the church walls; though this extreme glory, pomp, and excessive affluence of the world might do their character no harm, I believe they would admit they found little benefit in it—unless it were in acting as treasurers for the poor (which would be a somewhat secular employment) or in testifying to the world that Christian happiness does not consist of these things. Yet the world would not believe they were serious unless they actually gave those things up. As for the external pomp and splendor of their own persons, it is likely they would declare that if the houses of God—I mean the physical churches—were at least decently, if not in some cases gloriously, adorned, their eyes could view that with more pleasure than any imperial ornaments on their own heads and backs, which they could not see without the help of mirrors.

It would be a greater pleasure to them to see no poor people, except those who were healthily and handsomely dressed—not so filthily and miserably <note>original: "squalidly and forlornly"</note> that they appear as unpleasant eyesores in God's providence.

But to make rich miters <note>Mitre: A high, pointed liturgical headdress worn by bishops</note> and costly vestments <note>original: "Habiliments"</note> for a St. Peter or a St. Paul would not be like making a coat for the moon, but (which is just as ridiculous) like making a golden cape <note>original: "Cope"; a long cloak-like vestment</note> for the sun—as if his natural splendor did not outshine all such artificial ornaments. The flashiness of clothing may make the person who wears it be stared at; but unspotted holiness and virtue will make the possessor truly revered and adored.

<margin>1 John 5:19.</margin>
10. Therefore, this excessive grandeur in the governors of the church—even if they were as holy as the Apostles themselves—would not seem necessary, nor required, nor perhaps at all desirable. But for those who do not have such an Apostolic spirit (as the majority of the world does not, or rather very few do), the words of St. John have remained true in almost every age: *The whole world lies in wickedness* <note>original: "ὁ κόσμος ὅλος ἐν πονηρῷ κεῖται"</note>. In such people, this glorious display—this fair and glittering morning—will surely and suddenly turn into a foul day.

Since there are such worldly prizes to be aimed for, and such various types and levels of status <note>original: "Dignities"</note>, leading even to the very top of the highest sovereignty over the world, the spirits of all men will be inflamed with the desire and pursuit...

# Chapter VII. The Divine Life in General.

...pursuit of what lies so temptingly in their view, that hellish fire of ambition will become the very life and soul of the Church. All its activity and motion will derive from that hateful principle. As a result, nothing but the name of *spirituality* will remain. The minds of the clergy <note>original: "Clergie"</note> will be totally distracted from meditating on what is true, holy, and edifying, and instead will be completely drowned and immersed in worldly affairs.

For such are also *ecclesiastical promotions* <note>original: "Ecclesiastick Preferments"; positions of power or status within the church</note>, when they are sought to satisfy the lust of the eyes, the lust of the flesh, and the pride of life.

11. This mischief will not stop with the neglect of holy and divine meditation, or of useful and noble inquiries after truth. Instead, everyone will be puffed up by the status and dignity of their own position—especially the one whose superiority is so vast that he claims to be the *universal Bishop of Christendom, higher than all the kings of the Earth*. They will be driven so far by that furious spirit of *ambition* that they will not only neglect but actually oppose everything sacred and holy if it competes with any devised method of bringing wealth into the Church. This wealth allows them to lord it over others and present themselves grandly in their respective offices and dignities.

<margin>Revelation 11 <note>original: "Apoc. 11."; refers to the Book of Revelation, also known as the Apocalypse</note></margin>
Therefore, the genuine simplicity of the Christian religion will be corrupted and tainted. Laws and articles will be devised by this *infallible* priesthood that are directly opposed to the laws of Christ and the unchangeable rules of sound reason. Everyone’s ears will be filled with deceitful fictions and profitable lies, many examples of which we have already provided. The merits of Christ’s suffering will be belittled and diminished. Truth and justice will be banished, persecuted, and oppressed. The Old and New Testaments will be treated as nothing more than a dumb and dead letter with no meaning or information of its own; instead, all instructions must come directly from the Church, which is determined to dictate nothing that goes against its own worldly advantage. 

In other words, the "two witnesses" <note>A reference to Revelation 11:3-12, often interpreted here as the Spirit and the Word, or the Law and the Gospel</note> must be killed, and their corpses left breathless in the streets. Otherwise, those who *dwell on the Earth* (not those who are *redeemed from the Earth* and have their way of life in Heaven) would not be able to rejoice so much or send gifts to one another—that is, to mutually support and promote each other’s interests and merrily divide the world among themselves.

12. It is clear, therefore, that such a *Luciferian system of government* <note>original: "Luciferian Polity"; a system characterized by pride and the desire for power, modeled after the fall of Lucifer</note> would by its very nature clash with the Kingdom of Christ. It would totally defeat the grand purpose of the Gospel, which is the *renewal of the world in true righteousness and holiness*. For in this way, even those who should be the *salt of the Earth* <note>A reference to Matthew 5:13, meaning those who preserve and season the world with goodness</note> will become the most tasteless of all men. Every person’s judgment will be bribed by either the current possession or the eager expectation of such vast and extravagant promotions. 

Because there are so many ranks and degrees of these positions, the minds of the ambitious will find no rest until they reach the highest possible level. Therefore, they will necessarily be entangled and occupied with worldly projects for as long as they live, acting with great intensity and anxiety. These goals seem so great and make such a dazzling show in their imaginations. Since ambition and pomp in every rank make them desperate for money, no low-ranking candidate...

### Chapter 8: Faith, the Root of all Divine Graces

1. 2. For these leaders would look so much like *unbelievers* themselves that they would shake the *faith* of everyone under them. They would make people think there is nothing to expect after this life, because their leaders and guides lived so exactly according to the principle: *That there is nothing to be expected hereafter.*

3. It would lead people to believe nothing except this: *That the sum of our religion is merely a clever invention of made-up stories, doctrines, precepts, and ceremonies, designed to control the consciences of men and make the world easier to govern, but shaped by priests for their own worldly advantage.* We have already described the tenets <note>original: "Tenents"</note> and doctrines of this Church in this way, continually displaying the *frauds* and *self-interest* <note>original: "Self-endedness"</note> of all their errors and bad practices, so we do not need to repeat them here.

4. Thirdly, it would also oppose the Christian *Faith* to define its nature as something that must always be doubtful. Or perhaps it is because they mix some things into religion as "necessary to believe" that are impossible for anyone but a fool to believe firmly. In this way, the true and solid points of Christianity—those with enough evidence to convince any rational person—are thought to be obscure and uncertain because they are found in the company of such gross falsehoods or uncertainties, which nonetheless claim an equal right to be fully accepted alongside the clearest truths.

# Chapter 8: Faith, the *Root* of all *Divine Graces*

1. We will now proceed to those main parts of the *Divine Life*: the *Root* and the *Branches*. It is obvious that whatever kills the *Root*—which inevitably causes the whole tree to wither—must be Antichristian in the highest degree. Therefore, if I describe a way of managing *affairs* in the Church that naturally tends to extinguish *Faith* (which is the necessary *root* of the other *Divine Graces*), no one will doubt that I have described a very significant part of *Antichristianism* <note>original: "Limb of Antichristianism"; the author portrays the corruption of the church as a physical body or "limb" of the Antichrist</note>.

2. The first point regarding this is what we touched upon last: a system of government and such prestigious high offices that they would cause the Church to fall and sink into the World. This would turn those who should be the *Salt of the Earth* <note>A reference to Matthew 5:13. In the Bible, Jesus tells his followers they are the "salt of the earth," but warns that if the salt loses its flavor, it is useless.</note> into a tasteless mass with a worldly, dead, and dull spirit. Such people would value nothing of the Kingdom of God, being completely occupied with the profits and promotions of this present life. Because of this, they would look so much like *Unbelievers* themselves that they would shake the *faith* of everyone under them. They would make people think there was nothing to expect after this life, because their leaders and guides lived exactly according to the principle *that there is nothing to be expected hereafter*.

3. Secondly, the extreme cleverness of their organization and strategy in managing the affairs of their ecclesiastical empire would have a similar effect. If this "policy" surpassed all the cunning and hard work of secular princes, and if all the doctrines and duties that were most emphasized and practiced were clearly designed to increase the honor, power, or profit of the priesthood—this, I say, would go a long way toward turning the world into infidels. People would believe nothing except that the sum of our religion is merely a clever invention made of fictitious stories, doctrines, commands, and ceremonies. These would seem like tools to trap the consciences of men and make the world easier to govern, but they would be shaped by the priests to serve their own worldly advantage. We have already described the tenets and doctrines of this Church in this way, continually showing the *frauds* and *self-interest* <note>original: "Self-endedness"</note> behind all their errors and bad practices; we do not need to repeat them here.

4. Thirdly, it also opposes the Christian *Faith* to define its nature as something that must always be doubtful. I must admit I do not know what the trick <note>original: "fetch"</note> behind this is, unless it is to keep people's minds in a sickly and unhealthy condition <note>original: "valetudinarious condition"</note>—just as some deceitful doctors and surgeons do with bodies—so that they have to return to them more often and depend on them more. Or perhaps it is because they mix certain things into religion that must be believed, but which are so impossible that no one but a fool could firmly believe them. In this way, the true and solid points of Christianity—which have enough evidence to convince any rational person—are considered obscure and uncertain simply because they are found alongside such obvious lies or uncertainties. Yet, these lies claim the same right to be fully accepted as the clearest truths.

# Antichristian Oppositions against Book II.

4. ...The certainty of **Faith**, as if her own **Infallibility** were its foundation, causes her followers—those she nurtures—to both believe and admit to the **Uncertainty of Belief**. This is because they have no better foundation than what we have already shown to be hollow and crumbling.

But it is their only tactic <note>original: "Shift and Refuge"</note> to make their **Infallibility** the foundation of belief, since the matters they propose to be believed have no support from either the Bible or their own logic to be accepted. Therefore, since things are so uncertain at their core according to these principles, they must be satisfied with a dim and uncertain faith instead of a firm and solid one. This is, in fact, the destruction of **Christian Faith** and the substitution of a dizzying mental instability in its place.

5. Fourthly, that principle also tends to the ruin of **Faith** which assumes that without a proper **Apostolic Succession** of bishops and priests, there is no true Church, and therefore no true faith. This principle suggests that this succession may be interrupted by the improper ordination or consecration of a priest or bishop—for example, if the persons being ordained or consecrated were atheists or Jews, or were ordained by those who are, or if they maliciously do not **intend** to perform what they ought in the **Sacrament of Holy Orders** <term>Sacrament of Orders: The rite in the Catholic and Orthodox traditions by which a person is ordained as a deacon, priest, or bishop.</term>, as some call it. This is a notion capable of turning all people into **Skeptics** regarding their religious state, but it is a position absolutely against internal intuition and reason. It is as if a person could not feel in their own conscience whether they believed the truths of Holy Scripture or not, unless they were first certain that they were a member of a church that had an uninterrupted, lawful succession of the priesthood from the time of the Apostles to their own. In reality, nothing is more immediate to a person than their own **internal sense**, which no amount of clever but false arguments <note>original: "Sophistry"</note> can ever disprove.

6. Therefore, although this position may be spitefully aimed against the **Certainty of Faith**, the damage it can do to a thoughtful person is very small and insignificant. It is much like that irritable assumption <note>original: "peevish Supposition"</note> regarding the necessity of **Unity of opinion**—the idea that those churches that differ in any point have no certainty in anything. This would be an excellent hypothesis indeed, if only it were true; it would effectively argue for the usefulness of an **Infallible Judge of Controversies** <note>Infallible Judge: A reference to the Pope or a General Council, claimed by the Roman Catholic Church to be the final, error-free authority on religious disputes.</note> (if such a person could be found for love or money) by whom the parts of the Universal Church might be tightly bound together as if with iron clamps.

But there is no such strength in that theory, which will crumble into dust of its own accord if we consider that it cannot stand except on terms that would destroy the truth of all reason and religion in the world—since the whole world is divided in its judgments and conclusions concerning both. From this, it is plain that the attempt, though weak, tends toward bringing in **universal skepticism** in all things. In that deluge, the **Christian Faith** would also be drowned and perish along with all other truths, as there would be no Ark left for sanctuary to stay safe from the churning and swallowing waves of this ebb and flow <note>original: "reciprocating Euripus." Euripus is a strait in Greece famous for its violent and unpredictable currents that change direction multiple times a day. Here, it symbolizes mental confusion and instability.</note>.

7. But sixthly, I shall now provide an example of something that is not only poorly intended, but which will inevitably succeed in turning the world into **Atheists**...

### Chapter VIII: Faith, the Root of all Divine Graces

...or **Infidels**; and that is the glutting of them with **lying miracles**, and gulling them with delusions and deceptive <note>original: "couzening"</note> devices, whether you call them **pious frauds** or by whatever other fine names you please. For once falsehood is discovered in a Church that requires its followers to believe more on its own authority and infallibility than on the credibility of the matters they propose—I say, if they are once caught being slow <note>original: "tardy"</note> in forgeries and deceitful fictions in any points, especially those that serve their own profit, how can this fail to shake or rather ruin the entire framework of belief to its very foundations? How ruinous then must the **Christian Faith** be where such lies and fabrications <note>original: "figments"</note> are frequent, and almost as frequently discovered by those who are more discerning <note>original: "nasute"; literally having a keen sense of smell, meaning critically intelligent</note>? 8. So that I may be better understood, I will give you some brief instances of these impudent fabrications. As, for example:

> “If they should have the nerve to tell the people that a certain saint, when his head was struck off, walked four or five miles with it in his hand, only resting himself at every mile’s end to take breath through his open windpipe <note>original: "weasen-pipe"</note>. That another saint, being hospitably entertained at the expense of the lives of a cow and a calf, restored them again to life, and that they were both found the next day in their master’s meadows. That another saint saw the Devil behind the altar busily writing down men's sins on a piece of parchment; but it being a bit too small, he stretched it with his teeth, and his grip slipping, he knocked his head against the wall. That a certain female saint, being swallowed by a dragon, made a cross in the dragon’s belly, which burst him in pieces, so she was delivered. That a bishop, having cut off his own hand after it was polluted by the kiss of some over-affectionate female, had it suddenly set on again and healed by prayers addressed to the **Blessed Virgin**. The same thing happened to another saint whose legs were cut off at the knees; and to the head of another, which, after being cut off, sprang up and grew back on, but when lopped off a second time, its fall gave rise to a fountain or well. And lastly, that another female saint, who was to be hauled by ropes to her execution, was made so strong by crossing herself and calling upon the **Virgin Mary** that a whole team of oxen could not drag her to the place.”

9. But I have not yet finished. There is also that delightful fabrication concerning some saints: that they have had personal conversations with the **Virgin Mary**, and that she has been so kind to some that she has emptied her breasts into their mouths on their sickbeds for their unspeakable comfort. It would likewise be a "colossal" miracle, and beyond belief, that a certain **Holy House** of the Virgin should be carried out of **Palestine** into **Italy** by an invisible hand through the air <note>This refers to the legend of the Santa Casa di Loreto, the house of the Virgin Mary supposedly transported by angels</note>. Surely the angels of God would be very worthily employed in moving such stonework and timber! For a crucifix also to take a fifty-mile journey through the same element in a night would be a pretty fiction to provide for the faith of fools. The speaking of crucifixes would also help to make up the number of these either delusions or incredibilities.

For the matter boils down only to this: is it more likely that the Church—for her own advantage (which I see she eagerly and stubbornly pursues everywhere)—would knowingly and intentionally deceive me, or at least be mistaken in her own judgment? I have no proof of her *infallibility* <note>original: "Infallibility." The doctrine that the Church cannot err.</note> except her own boast, even when it is in her *interest* <note>original: "Interest." Personal or political gain.</note> to boast so. I say, the matter boils down to this: is it more likely that she is practicing fraud or falling into a mistake out of some blind superstition, or that by speaking *five words* <note>The Latin words of consecration in the Mass: *Hoc est enim corpus meum* ("For this is my body").</note> a priest should have the power to turn a piece of *bread* into a *man*? This is despite the *bread*, according to all my senses, remaining as much *bread* as it was before. This is a double *miracle*, and greater than any ever performed in the world so far; and it is almost as great a *miracle* that anyone should believe it.

> 19. But there are still greater—I cannot call them *miracles*, but rather downright *impossibilities*. First, that this bread is not turned into a man who is yet to be born, but into a man who already exists. This is the most difficult nonsense that can be offered for the human mind to consider. And yet, secondly, the bread is supposedly turned into a man—that is, into the *Man Christ*—in such a way that he is entirely in every place where this consecrated bread appears to be. This means he is in thousands of places at once, at very large distances from each other, which is as perfect a *contradiction* as any that can be proposed: that one and the same body should be entirely separate from itself. For how can it be *one* if it is divided from itself, since *unity* consists in being undivided, and *self-unity* certainly is *self-undividedness*? Therefore, if there is one "self" at *Oxford*, for example, and another at *Cambridge* at the same time, it is impossible for them to be one and the same *person*; their distance or division proves they are two distinct individuals. And thirdly and lastly, from this false assumption—that one and the same body may be in several places at once—it would also follow that one and the same person or body could be at the same time wholly within itself and wholly outside of itself; wholly above itself and wholly beneath itself; on its own right hand and on its own left hand. It could be *one* body and yet many bodies at once—or rather, no body at all, but a spirit, or to speak more truly, *nothing*. One and the same *person* might meet himself and greet <note>original: "complement"</note> himself, might move and rest at the same time, might lie down and walk simultaneously, might be many miles away from a friend and present with him at the same time, and might be in heaven one moment and on earth the next without passing through any of the regions in between. We have noted many such inconsistencies <note>original: "Incongruities"</note> above, so there is no need to dwell on them any longer here.

### CHAPTER 9

1. Humility as the proper characteristic of the person and spirit of Christ. 2. The desire for ecclesiastical sovereignty is contrary to this divine grace. 3. The pretext for this ambition—that the visible Church, being one, requires one visible head—along with the answer to it. 4. 1. We proceed now to describe as vivid an opposition as possible to the **first branch** of the **Divine Life**, namely, **Humility**. This is such a special characteristic of the nature and character of Christ's own spirit—and so pronounced by him when he was on Earth (<margin>Matthew 11:29</margin> *Learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart*)—that anything perfectly opposite to it must be essentially **Antichristian** in any person. This is especially true in those who, in a more specific way, presume themselves to be the **successors** of Christ and his apostles. He warned his apostles long ago against pride, acting like lords, and the desire for superiority, saying, <margin>Luke 22:25, Mark 10:42</margin> *The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them call themselves "benefactors." But it shall not be so among you.*

<margin>1 Peter 5:2–3</margin> Peter remembered this lesson and tried to pass it on to others, advising the pastors to feed their flocks *not for dishonest gain <note>original: "filthy Lucre." Refers to money or profit gained in an unscrupulous or shameful way.</note>, but with a willing mind; not as being lords over God's heritage, but being examples to the flock.* How contrary to this it would be, then, if a so-called "supreme pastor" (whom others in their various subordinate roles would naturally imitate) should not only **lord it** over his flock, but also tyrannize over kings and emperors? Like Lucifer <note>Lucifer: A name used for the devil, specifically referring to his fall from heaven due to his pride and desire to be equal to God.</note>, he would place himself on the same throne as God and Christ—or rather, displace them—and dominate absolutely according to his own will, treading underfoot the clearly published laws of God.

2. Let us, therefore, dip our brush a little deeper into the same colors we used to describe that part of Antichristianism which was opposed to the Divine Life in general. Let us portray more fully an ecclesiastical system that appears most clearly **Luciferian** and **Antichristian**, and most diametrically opposed to that holy **humility** that was recommended by Christ to his successors.

3. First, he will pretend that it is unfit that the visible Catholic Church being one, should not be united under *one visible Head*. This reasoning, however—though it makes a pretty show at first sight—will vanish into smoke when closely looked into. For this is but a clever elegance <note>original: "quaint concinnity"</note> urged on behalf of an impossibility. To create such an Office for one man, which no one man in the world is able to perform, implies that something is possible which is indeed impossible. From this it is plain that the *Head will be too little for the Body*, which therefore will also be a piece of mischievous asymmetry or lack of fitness <note>original: "Inconcinnity"</note>. No one mortal can be a competent *Head* for that Church which has a right to be *Catholic* <term>universal</term>, and to overspread the face of the whole Earth. There can be no such *Head* but *Christ*, who is not merely Man, but God invested in Human nature, and therefore is present with every part of his Church and every member thereof at whatever distances.

But to set some one Bishop over the whole *Church* would be to suppose that great *Bishop of our Souls* is absent from it—he who has promised *he will be with her to the end of the World*. And, you may be sure, he is not an idle spectator, but a careful *Feeder* and *Governor* of the souls of those who really believe in him and sincerely obey him.

4. Nor does the *Universal Church* <note>original: "Church-Catholick"</note> on Earth lose her *Unity* by this; for she is under *one common Head* of the whole Church, both Triumphant <note>The part of the Church already in heaven.</note> as well as Militant <note>The part of the Church still struggling on earth.</note>. To address the objection more directly: Christ is a *Visible Head* of his Church to those who can approach his Court in that glorious *Metropolis* in Heaven. There, undoubtedly, he is to be seen sitting on his *Sapphire Throne* in great Majesty and Glory, and there his true Subjects, in a short time, may either see him themselves, or at least converse with those who have frequent recourse to him and wait in his presence.

And no man, I think, will say that any large Empire has an *Invisible Head* simply because the Emperor has placed his Palace in the chiefest Province of his Empire and never comes within the view of some parts of his Dominion, or because multitudes of men never see him, having never had the opportunity of visiting the parts where the Emperor's Court is. Whereas *Jesus Christ*, the *Head of his Church*, was seen here on Earth for a good while, and was also seen to travel from here into the higher Regions of his Kingdom, and in due time will visibly return here again to take account of those who administer his affairs in these lower Provinces. Therefore, Christ is a more *visible Head* in his large Empire than any Emperor is in his. Thus it is evident that there is no need for any *one Visible Head* of the Church besides Christ himself.

5. But despite all of this, this ambitious Patriarch whom I describe will lead the world to believe that it is very appropriate for there to be *one visible Head of the Universal Church*. This person would succeed Christ, or rather someone whom the Patriarch would pretend to be the Prince of the Apostles. He claims that his See <term>the seat of authority of a bishop</term> is that *Apostolic See*, and that there is a necessity for *Unity in the Church*. He argues that to settle all controversies there should be some such person, though this plea must seem very weak and frivolous to any impartial <note>original: "indifferent"</note> man. For, as I have already suggested, the Church will be sufficiently *one* by being under *one Head, Christ Jesus*, and under *one Law*, which is the *Word of God*. This Word has already been proved sufficiently plain in all things necessary for life and salvation. But for other things, whether *Ceremonies* or *private opinions* <note>original: "Conceits"</note>, they do not at all break the *Unity* of Christ's Kingdom. It will be truly and conspicuously His so long as it professes the Faith of His Apostles; let them otherwise use whatever different *Rites* they will, or differ as much as they can in *unnecessary opinions*—provided always that none of these *Rites* or *opinions* are really and plainly against the *Apostolic Doctrines*, which are the universal and irreversible Law of Christ's Empire on Earth. For in this way, though the *Catholic Church* is varied in its external practices, it will still visibly be the *bride of Christ*, even if she is dressed in many colors <note>original: "ἠμφιεσμένη ποικίλα"</note>, and clothed with a garment of various floral patterns and hues.

It would have ended or prevented all disputes among the Apostles themselves or anyone else concerning them.

# Chapter IX. The Divine Grace of Humility.

That is to say, the dragon that dwells between the two seas—just as Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch scholar and theologian.</note> interprets the watery *Leviathan* in the Psalms as referring to Pharaoh, King of Egypt, because his dominion extended between <margin>Verse 2, 3.</margin> two seas. *In that day sing to her, "A vineyard of red wine; I the Lord do keep it, I will water it every moment; lest any hurt it, I will <margin>Verse 6.</margin> keep it night and day." He will cause those of Jacob to take root; Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit.* 

But this was a longer digression than I intended.

1. We return to the pursuit of the matter at hand and pass on to the next *Antichristian opposition*; and that is against the second branch of the *Divine Life*, which is *Purity*. Here, omitting any talk of hypocrisy—which is one kind of *impurity* that cannot help but be very frequent in such a religion as I have described so far, consisting so much in outward shows and superficial <note>original: "superficiary"</note> formalities—we will direct our pen to drawing such an image of *impurity* as is more gross and disgusting <note>original: "fulsome"</note>. The chief parts of this are *fornication*, *adultery*, and *sodomy*. I say, therefore, that if the very structure and character of church government <note>original: "Ecclesiastick Polity"</note> or doctrine were such that it naturally either necessitated or encouraged such uncleanness as these, would this not be a clear Antichristian opposition to that *Christian purity* to which we are all called?

2. And I believe such a structure would be the one I shall now describe <note>original: "delineate"</note>, beginning with smaller things first. We will suppose, therefore, a *great number of holy days* in which men shall be restrained from working in their honest occupations. We will also suppose that the practice of their religion on those days takes up no significant time (unless it is in some playful <note>original: "ludicrous"</note> parades) and is of such a nature that it does not examine the hearts of men at all, nor plant the fear of God in them, nor truly kill <note>original: "mortify"</note> the desires of the flesh. They are merely spectators of "dumb shows," as it were, and listeners to a public service of which they do not understand a single syllable. When this is finished, they think they have done enough—and perhaps they do not even do that much—yet they are forbidden from any secular work under the threat of the Church's high displeasure. Thus, they may be more safely found in a tavern, ale-house, or brothel <note>original: "Baudy-house"</note> than working at their trades.

Therefore, I ask: regarding men with undisciplined <note>original: "unmortified"</note> minds, who have no opportunity to be forearmed against the temptations of the flesh through a deep and understandable worship of God in public, or a ministry that truly moves the soul, but are instead forced to be idle—what can these men fall into more naturally than drinking and excess? When joined with this imposed idleness, such habits must surely lead them to such acts of impurity as opportunity offers. It is a well-known proverb that "Idleness is the mother of all mischief."

> ->These things make you love; these things protect what they have made;<-
> ->These things are the cause and the food of a pleasant evil.<-
> <note>original Latin: "Hæc ut ames faciunt, hæc quæ fecere tuentur, / Hæc sunt jucundi causa cibusque mali."</note>

And therefore, does not the large number of festivals, joined with a dead and spiritless form of religious worship where the participants are merely spectators of a silent performance <note>original: "dumb show"</note>, as I said before, become a school of lewdness and a nursery for impurity?

3. Again, suppose an order of men—and a large one at that—who eat and drink the best, live in constant idleness, and survive only on the labor of others. Suppose they are neither engaged in the more subtle and captivating studies of philosophy and noble theory (which might use up their excess strength and energy), nor in any deep or soul-consuming devotion. Instead, they merely recite <note>original: "patter over"</note> their religious duties and set prayers as an external obligation; even if these are understood, there may be little in them that affects the mind enough to restrain the body at all. Suppose, I say, these men—despite their natural capacity and fitness for marriage—should be condemned to perpetual **celibacy** <note>original: "Cælibate"</note> by an irrevocable vow. If this vow is taken rashly and unwisely, contrary not only to the Law of God but to their own nature and temperament, what can be the natural result but frequent **fornications**, **adulteries**, or foul **acts of sodomy**? Therefore monks, or **priests**, or whoever they may be who are tied to this law under these circumstances, cannot fail (unless by a miracle) to at least attempt to break the laws of God or nature—if they do not frequently, in fact, break them—filling the Christian world with the foul stench of their impurities. And it is likely they might find their targets more easily among the female nuns <note>original: "Votaries"</note>, if those women were also assumed to have offered themselves up without considering their own temperaments, or were maneuvered <note>original: "contrived"</note> into monasteries through the deception and pressure of others.

4. But even imagine these men were more secluded; the world is still wide enough. If the common saying is true, "**She is chaste only because no one has asked her**" <note>original Latin: "Casta est quam nemo rogavit"</note>, then since they are so well-provided for and have so little to do but study such deceits, it will not be hard for them to obtain their prize. Indeed, they do not even need to seek out opportunities, as these are offered to them in some parts of their religious duties, such as in the privacy of **auricular confession** <note>term: The practice of whispering sins privately into the ear of a priest</note>. Temptation would be this strong even if the power of conscience and the fear of punishment were still fully intact.

5. But suppose some of the learned should declare **simple fornication** to be no sin, and argue that **adultery** is a lesser sin than breaking a **vow of celibacy**...

# CHAPTER XIII.

*1. The excellence of Charity, and that it is the very life and soul of the social order <note>original: "Polity"; the organized structure of a government or church</note> of Christ. 2. A description of the nature of Christ's Kingdom from Scripture. 3. A collection of the properties of his government from the previously cited prophecies; and that they are all the effects of Charity. 4. To which the Kingdom of Antichrist is opposite. 5. The oppression of the poor and needy by this Antichristian social order. 6. The defrauding of men of their estates based on false accusations of heresy. 7. The imposition of barbaric penances. 8.
