1. The final branch of the Divine Life is *charity*. It is the summit, the top branch, the flower—indeed, the very essence of Christianity. It is the life and soul of that pleasant and comforting social order and Kingdom of Christ which was predicted in the Holy Scriptures. This kingdom should be most directly represented by the clergy <note>original: "Ecclesiastick persons"</note>. The seriousness, humility, and exemplary nature of their conduct <note>original: "Conversations"; in this period, the word referred to one's entire way of life and behavior, not just speech</note>, along with the influence of their powerful teaching and their comforting, fair discipline, should reach a more refined improvement of people's behavior than civil laws usually aim for. That is to say, it should make people more sober and pure in their interactions, more fair and reasonable in their demands, more generous and compassionate toward the poor, and more faithful, sincere, kind, and honest with one another than political laws can achieve. This would establish that *Kingdom of Christ* on Earth which would truly prove to be the great joy and happiness of all the nations of the world, fulfilling their desires and expectations. For there is indeed nothing more desirable than *Christ’s Kingdom*, which we pray for every day, according to the descriptions of it in the Prophets and the Psalms.

3. According therefore to this description of the Kingdom of Christ, it is plainly a Kingdom of *Peace* and *Love*, the dominion of that divine virtue of *Charity*, and reveals itself in the defending, righting, and easing of the poor; in the lowliness and meekness of the governors; and in the truth and faithfulness of them in managing their affairs without any guile or deceit; in the unity and friendly sociability <note>original: "conversableness"</note> of people; in the ending of war and hostility; and in the protection of the Saints of God from persecution and slaughter. All these *blessings* are included in the reign of Christ according to the above-cited predictions; and are all of them the *effects of Charity*, just as St. *Paul* has described that grace by its excellent fruits.

<margin>1 Corinthians 13.</margin>
For *Charity is kind*, full of acts of humanity; *seeks not her own*, much less what belongs to others, whether out of envy or greed. *Charity is not puffed up* with pride and arrogance: *has no pleasure in unrighteousness* or deceitfulness, *but rejoices in truth and faithfulness*. *Charity does not easily think evil of men*, or behave herself inappropriately <note>original: "unseemly"</note> out of a bad opinion she conceives of them in matters of morality or religion. *Charity is so far from inciting others to war that she is hardly provoked to anger*, but is patient and long-suffering; she is so far from persecuting and murdering the good that she will not be overly severe even to those who are no better than they should be. For *Charity bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things*. She is so far from persecuting, imprisoning, or from racking and killing innocent and good men (who are endowed with the true fear of God) based on worldly jealousies and suspicions—that is to say, for fear the spreading of the truth of the Gospel should tear down their usurped empire of idolatrous tyranny and superstition.

# Chap. XIII. Oppositions against that Divine Grace of Charity.

4. Let us suppose, therefore, a company of men who pretend to succeed *Christ* and his *Apostles* (who, if they be his legitimate successors, should also succeed him in the graces of his Spirit) to be quite contrary, in the administration of the affairs of the Church, to that description of the *Kingdom of Christ* found in the Prophets and Psalms. Would this not, in truth, prove to be a most palpable and remarkable limb <note>original: "Limb," here meaning a prominent member or agent</note> of *Antichristianism*?

# Of Heresy and Schism. Book II.

...schismatics. Yet in their own judgment, I suppose this does not carry little weight, as their true assessment is revealed by their actions. They deem a heretic so odious or contemptible that he is not worthy of the common privileges of mankind, nor of the protection that the laws of human society afford; they believe he should not have the security of a promise, even when confirmed by an oath—claiming that faith does not need to be kept with heretics <note>original: "Faith being to be kept with Hereticks." This refers to the controversial medieval principle *haereticis non est servanda fides*, which suggested that promises made to those deemed heretics were not legally or morally binding.</note>. I will not mention here that they have made the penalties for *heresy* capital <note>original: "capital," meaning punishable by death.</note>. How justly they do this—even if a man were a heretic in matters of belief, provided it was not out of pride and conceit, but out of invincible ignorance <note>A theological term for a lack of knowledge for which a person is not morally responsible.</note>—I will not discuss here.

2. It will be of greater use to consider what constitutes real *heresy* or *schism*, so that the sincere and knowledgeable Christian may not be insulted, nor the less skillful frightened by these bugbears <note>original: "Bug-bears," imaginary terrors used to frighten children; here, it refers to empty threats or labels used to cause fear.</note>. Those who raise such a great cry against the heinousness of these sins would use their zeal and rhetoric more effectively if they were faithful enough to give us a right definition of them. Otherwise, while they pretend to be so industriously desirous of peace and unity in the Church, they may only create more occasions for dissension and animosity. For to label more things as *heresies* and *schisms* than there actually are is to create more quarrels than are necessary. I will acknowledge as readily as anyone that *heresy* and *schism* are very grievous crimes, even of the deepest dye; but then, the act must be truly *heresy* or *schism*—not whatever the spite, interest, or prejudice of a domineering party chooses to call so, under the pretense that they are that *one Catholic Church* from whose doctrine (no matter how false or corrupt) any dissent must be *heresy*, and from whose communion (no matter how idolatrous its practices) any separation must be *schism*. No, certainly; those high sins of *heresy* and *schism* are not committed against this or that particular synagogue, no matter how numerous its members, but against that *ancient and truly Catholic and Apostolic Church*. He who sins against her *unity* sins against his Creed, which has taught us to say, *I believe one Catholic and Apostolic Church*. Because these words may be abused to make the Church look less *Catholic* and *one* than it truly is, I shall offer an easy explanation of their meaning.

3. I believe, therefore, that the object of our belief in this clause of the Creed consists of these three propositions:

First, that the Church of God, in which eternal salvation is to be found, is only *one*. That is to say, a man cannot be saved in just any religion, as some playfully imagine, but that there is only one way of salvation which is revealed to God’s true Church, and all must come under its guidance before they can be saved.

<margin>* Chapter 1.</margin> Secondly, that this Church of God is now a *Catholic Church*—not local <note>original: "Topical," meaning restricted to a specific place.</note> or national, as it was in the commonwealth of the Jews <note>The ancient nation of Israel.</note>, but a Church that is by right intended to spread over the face of the whole earth. It is destined to do so by Providence, as expressed in several passages from the Prophets. *From the rising of the sun to the going down of the same, my name shall be great among the Gentiles, etc.,* as *Malachi* foretold. And *David* says in the second Psalm, *Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession.*

### Chap. XIV. Of Heresy and Schism.
<sig>P 4</sig>

Thirdly and lastly, this *one Catholic Church* <note>The word "Catholic" here means "universal," referring to the whole body of Christian believers throughout the world, rather than specifically the Roman Catholic denomination.</note> should not be stretched so wide as to be recognized in places where Apostolic doctrine—the faith and practice delivered and commanded by Christ or his Apostles—is attacked <note>original: "oppugned"</note> and contradicted, and where entirely contrary doctrines and practices are introduced.

On the other hand, it should not be made so narrow as to exclude groups of men from being part of this *Catholic Church* when they do, in fact, maintain Apostolic doctrines and practice the primitive customs of the Church established by the Apostles or Christ himself. That is to say, the proper definition of this *one Catholic Church* is that it rejects nothing of the Apostolic doctrines and repeatable customs <note>original: "imitable Usages"</note> which were commanded by Christ or his Apostles to the Church, and that it neither teaches nor establishes anything that is directly <note>original: "point-blank"</note> opposite to them, or to the Word of God to which Christ and his Apostles give testimony.

Therefore, the *true Catholic Church*, both as a whole and in every specific group within it, is that which takes for its visible laws and customs—by which it also becomes visible to the world—the laws and customs of Christ and his Apostles, and nothing contradictory to them.

This, I hope, will be acknowledged by all men as the easiest and most natural sense of this article of the *Christian Creed* that the words allow.

4. From this, I think a person may easily discover what *heresy* is—that which is justly deemed such a hateful sin. Namely, it is *a dissent from the Catholic Church even in those things that are Apostolic.* For by those things alone—they being complete and uncontradicted within her—does the Church reveal herself to be that *one and only Catholic Church of Christ.* To dissent from any part of this Apostolic doctrine out of a spirit of contradiction and self-conceit would indeed be a hateful sin against the authority she has to instruct and fill the world with this saving truth. I say, such dissent would be *heresy* in the most loathsome circumstances imaginable.

The next degree of this sin would be dissenting from the Catholic Church in things that are generally agreed upon, even if they are not expressly part of Apostolic doctrine, provided they are not plainly discordant with the Word of God or the unchanging principles of human understanding.

The third and last degree is to dissent from the decisions of one’s own particular National Church in circumstances similar to those mentioned above.

These degrees seem to have a very close connection with what we have defined, most properly and primarily, as *heresy*. However, considering that even Ecumenical <note>original: "Oecumenical," meaning "universal" or "world-wide" church councils.</note> Councils themselves may err, and that Scripture is sufficiently plain in matters necessary for salvation, and that the affairs and character <note>original: "Genius"</note> of particular nations are exceedingly different and changeable, and that General Councils are very difficult and slow to assemble—I must not be too hasty to label a dissent here as *heretical* (not even a dissent from a universal doctrine or custom) so long as it does not infringe upon Apostolic laws and doctrines. # Of Heresy and Schism. Book II.

To dissent from, or to refuse to subscribe to the decrees of any church whatsoever that are plainly contrary <note>original: "repugnant"</note> to Apostolic doctrines, would not only not be *heretical*, but actually *heroic*—especially if that dissent is likely to bring personal trouble or hardship to the dissenter.

5. And now, regarding *schism*, much the same judgment can be made. It is plain that *schism*, truly so called, is *a separation from the Catholic Church, or from any National Church which is part of it, even when that church proves itself to be Catholic—that is to say, even when it is Apostolic, and offers no opinions or practices except those which conform to the customs and doctrines of Christ and his Apostles.* To separate from the Church in such circumstances as these, I confess, would be a great and damnable sin. 

But if someone separates from the Church in other matters because of an "invincible suspicion" <note>A term from moral theology meaning a doubt or belief that a person cannot overcome by reasonable effort at the time.</note> that consenting to or doing a certain thing would be sinful and displeasing to God—even if those opinions might actually be true and the practices harmless in themselves—I believe that although this makes a person *materially* a *schismatic*, he is not *formally* so. <note>In philosophy and theology, "materially" refers to the act itself (the person did separate), while "formally" refers to the intent and moral nature of the act (the person did not intend to rebel against God's truth). Therefore, he is not a "true" schismatic in his heart.</note> Such a person is rather to be pitied than reproached.

<margin>Revelation 18</margin>
However, if a person separates from a part of the church (if it can even still be called a part of the church) that imposes opinions and practices plainly contrary to the commands of Christ and his Apostles, then separation in this case need not be pitied, nor should it be reproached; rather, it should be highly commended and applauded. That divine voice warrants such sober separatists when it calls out: *Come out of her, my people, lest you partake of her sins and of her plagues.* <note>A reference to Revelation 18:4, traditionally interpreted by Protestants of this era as a call to leave the corruptions of the Roman Catholic Church.</note> For "coming out" in this instance would really be "entering in" to the true Church, and standing still would be remaining disconnected from it. As one author speaks very sharply and truly: *He is not joined to the Church who is separated from the Gospel.* <note>original: "Is Ecclesia non jungitur qui ab Evangelio separatur."</note>

6. Therefore, from this true and definite understanding of things, it is manifest how outrageously and uncharitably—even "Antichristianly"—this false church acts against the true members of Christ by calling them *heretics* and *schismatics*, and "renders and tearers" <note>Those who rip or tear apart the unity of the church.</note> of the Church's unity. In truth, they are so far from being *heretics* that they are the faithful witnesses of *Jesus* and the only sincere members of the Apostolic body. They keep to that one foundation of which *Christ* is the chief cornerstone. 

Furthermore, they are so far from being *schismatics* in their separation from such a church as I have described (where gross idolatry and superstition have overflowed everything) that by separating, they have redeemed themselves from this *Babylonian* or *Egyptian* captivity <note>Biblical metaphors for exile and slavery, used here to describe being under the power of a corrupt church.</note> and returned to that City which is at unity with itself and must never change—I mean that one and only true Catholic Church which is truly *Apostolic*. For if it is true *that he is not joined to the Church who is separate from the Gospel*, I think it must also be true that he who is sincerely joined to the *Gospel* cannot be separate from the Church. 

Therefore, all this noise about "tearing and rending the Church" is merely a loud accusation made by men who feel their own usurped power and interests shaking. It is as if they fear their power will break into pieces at this resurrection of the true Apostolic Church, and at Christ's recovering of power into his own hands to raise that promised and long-expected Kingdom of Righteousness upon the earth.

# Chap. XIV. Antichristian Oppositions against—Charity.

7. And yet, in the fourth place, although this false Church is so perfectly "Antichristian"—as I have described—grossly idolatrous and wretchedly superstitious, and though she loudly and constantly complains about the "tearing of the *Unity* of the *Catholic Church*" (as she phrases it); despite all this, we will assume she is so hypocritically fussy and scrupulous that she refuses to "contaminate" herself by joining in a worship service with those of the true and Apostolic Church. She does this even if there is nothing in their service but what is based on the Apostles' teachings; she will not even join in the Lord’s Prayer, or in giving thanks before a meal, nor say "Amen" to the shortest short prayer <note>original: "Ejaculation"</note> or hymn of praise <note>original: "Doxologie"</note> that might come from the mouths of those who belong to the Apostolic body. She will not even say grace herself, for fear that these true followers of the Apostles might join in or add their own "Amen."

And yet, believe it or not, this "synagogue of deceivers" claims to be so passionate and hardworking for the "unity of the *Catholic Church*" that it surpasses all else. Meanwhile, they are so full of bitterness and insults against these "*heretics*" (as they call them) that they will label them—and indeed any church other than their own—the "Church of the Devil." They even declare that God would not be God if He did not damn them, and they forbid their followers from offering so much as a *Rest in Peace* <note>original: "Requiem"—a Mass or prayer for the souls of the dead.</note> for their souls when they have departed this life.

8. But this is all just theatrical posturing. Their devilish *fraud* in pursuing this refusal to socialize in any religious duty between themselves and those they choose to call *heretics* is obvious. They do it because they fear that interaction in religious matters might reveal the truth to those who are only held to this false Church by believing lies. I mean not only lies that were framed long ago for the advantage of their Church, but also the misinterpretations and falsehoods they feed their followers about those they call *heretics*. They falsify their *doctrines* and slander their behavior as they please. By banning conversation with them, they keep their followers believing the vile opinions created by their low slanders.

Besides that, by being so fussy about refusing to communicate with them in any religious duty, they show off the great *sanctity* of their own hypocritical <note>original: "Pharisaical"—referring to the Pharisees, whom Jesus criticized for focusing on outward ritual while ignoring inner virtue.</note> church, as I mentioned before. This creates a hatred and loathing of everyone who opposes them. Such schemes and practices from those who talk so much about peace and unity in the Church is a double iniquity, and the highest violation of *Charity* that has not yet turned into physical violence. This church was certainly the "false woman" <note>original: "Whore"—a reference to the judgment of Solomon (1 Kings 3), where the false mother was willing to have the child divided in two.</note> who ruthlessly called for the child to be divided, not the true mother. It is most certain that any church that wants Christians to disagree on things they actually agree on, and wants to split them apart where they would naturally join together—namely, in *Apostolic doctrines and practices*—must be an unfaithful and "adulterous" church.

1. But there are still more obvious revelations of this Antichristian opposition to the divine virtue of *Charity*—the "Royal Law" <note>The "Royal Law" refers to James 2:8: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."</note> of the Kingdom of Christ. This kingdom is described by the peace and security of those who live under it: *No one shall destroy in God’s holy mountain.* <note>Isaiah 11:9</note>

Therefore, in the fifth place, how plainly *Antichristian* would it be for those who claim to be the special successors of Christ if they were to prove to be instigators of war and busy engineers of destruction within Christendom? They would be clever in cruelty and revenge, barbaric in their executions, and merciless to the poor—hating them even for their poverty. They would be poisoners of Princes, even using that Bread <note>A reference to historical allegations that Catholic agents poisoned rivals using the consecrated host of the Eucharist, most notably the rumor concerning the death of Holy Roman Emperor Henry VII in 1313.</note> with which they pretend to feed souls for everlasting life. The High Priests themselves, the heads of this Antichristian system <note>original: "Polity"</note>, would be either the masterminds or the admirers of such villainous poisonings and murders.

She is that cruel and arrogant *harlot drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus* <note>A reference to the Whore of Babylon from the Book of Revelation</note>, as well she might be.

...spirits on tenterhooks <note>original: "tenter-hooks"; a state of painful suspense or anxiety</note> in their reaching after the bewitching prizes which are ever flashing before their eyes, rather than a permissible framework of a modest order of Government to keep up wholesome discipline in the Church—can we imagine any state of things more contrary to the spirit of *Humility* than this?

And then again for *Purity*: For this lofty High Priest <note>A reference to the Pope</note> to stoop so low as to give his seal of approval to *fornication*, by receiving an annual tribute <note>A tax paid by brothels to the church</note> from the *prostitutes* of his capital city, and to enjoin celibacy upon his priests—as if he meant to drive them into the nets so that these *prostitutes of Venus* <note>original: "Nuns of Venus"; a satirical term for prostitutes</note> may never lack business—to fill the world with members of religious orders <note>original: "Monasticks"</note>, and to disregard all kinds of debauchery as long as the laws of the Church are observed, is the most effective method imaginable to make *Christendom* a cage of unclean birds, and so to completely wither or cut off that branch of the Divine Life which we call *Purity*.

And now, lastly, for *Charity* <note>In the sense of Christian love or *caritas*</note>: What can be more contrary to it than to weave into law or religion things that are not only naturally unjust, but barbarously cruel? This includes not only killing those who are innocent, but torturing to death with the most savage torments even those who are the most dear and faithful members of Christ—and even for that very reason, because they prove themselves to be so. That which makes the barbarity of these successors of the Devil still more hateful is their ensnaring of men regarding that Mystery which was the pledge of the greatest love of Christ that could be expressed. It was intended as the most endearing and binding cement <note>original: "agglutinating Cement"</note> for all those who are called by his name, so that they should be united to one another with the sincerest love and affection possible. Now, therefore, that this sacred pledge of love, friendship, and unity in the Church—I mean the *Sacramental Body and Blood of Christ* (which is a living commemoration of that inexpressible love he showed to his Church by laying down his life for us)—should be made the main engine and trick for trapping, and afterwards for cruelly torturing and butchering, his most faithful members; what more horrid, more cursed, and more Antichristian abuse can there be of our Lord *Jesus*? Or what hostility against him could be more damnable or diabolical?

Indeed, what conspiracy against human nature could be more tragic or dreadful, or what plot so obvious for making mankind mere slaves and servants, taking away from them that privilege <note>The faculty of reason and individual conscience</note> by which alone they are distinguished from brute beasts?

8. What then shall we think of those numerous swarms of that pretended *Infallible Church* we have described? They are ready to quarrel with any Christian passenger in his pilgrimage through the wilderness of this world if he denies the *transubstantiation* of a *round white wafer into a perfect man* <note>The Catholic doctrine that the bread of the Eucharist becomes the literal body of Christ.</note>, after a priest has said certain words over it—even though the *wafer*, upon the most careful examination of our senses, is not changed one bit from what it was before. Yet, upon the boast of the *infallibility* of this church, a man must believe it against all sense, scripture, and reason, or else die the most cruel kind of death that criminals are ever put to. Who can help but look upon such a pack of men as these as not only *anti-Christian*, but *anti-human*—as sworn enemies of the human race <note>original: "tanquam juratos humani generis hostes"</note>, an accursed company of bloody thieves and robbers, and sworn conspirators against the sons of *Adam*? With all their strength, they endeavor to maul them and martyr them, to subdue them and enslave them both body and soul, and to tyrannize over them more cruelly than it is fit for any man to do over brute beasts.

# Chapter XVII. A Recapitulation of the whole Idea.

Can anything be imagined more *Antichristian* than this, or more contrary to that noble and Divine Spirit of Charity and sweet kindness that was so visible in the Lord *Jesus Christ*? He is so frequently called in Scripture *the Son of Man*, to whom belongs that expected Kingdom of Peace, of holy Love, and of Humanity.

9. Therefore, from this short sketch, I think one may see that I have given a very true and faithful *concept* <note>original: "Idea"</note> of what constitutes real and essential *Antichristianism*, and truly I think I have shown it at its highest possible level. For some might try to excuse the matter by saying that this *Pseudo-Christian* <term>Pseudo-Christian</term> <note>False-Christian; from the Greek 'pseudes' (false). A church that claims the name of Christ but acts against his teachings.</note> Church does not openly deny Christ or his Gospel, does not persecute everyone who bears the name of a Christian, and, lastly, does not set up *images* to the deities of the Pagans, such as *Mars*, *Venus*, and the rest. To these points I briefly answer:

To the first: It would not be in their interest to deny the whole truth of the Gospel, for then their power and reputation would fail in the world. However, it would be in the interest of the true Church of God if they did so; therefore, they are the worst enemies possible, doing more mischief under the guise of friendship than any declared enemy can. Furthermore, there is compelling evidence in the Scripture that *Antichrist* is to be a Christian in external profession, not a *Pagan* or any other stranger to the Church.

To the second: The fact that they do not kill everyone called a Christian shows that their malice and cruelty is more precisely directed against Christ, in that their spite is only against his true and sincere members. For those who are spared are not truly Christ’s servants, but the vassals <note>original: "vassals"; subjects or underlings, here implying those who follow the Pope's authority rather than Christ's.</note> of this High-priest—or at least he considers them to be so—otherwise they could not escape his fury. Thus, his opposition to Christ is only more calculated and targeted, not less fierce or malicious.

And to the last point: that they worship the *images* or persons of the *Blessed Virgin*, *St. Peter*, *St. Paul*, etc., instead of *Venus*, *Neptune*, or *Mars*. Suppose a mighty ruler, who was as virtuous as he was powerful, issued severe decrees against adultery and sexual immorality. And suppose those guilty of the crime apologized to their Prince in this way: "It is true, *Great Sir*, that we have committed sexual immorality, but we beg you to notice how excusable the circumstances are. For we are not such vulgar and crude fornicators as to defile ourselves with just anyone. Instead, we only choose those for whom we have a very great respect and complete love—and that is because of their close relationship to your Highness: namely, your daughters, sisters, and nieces, and others who are closer to you than usual." Would not such an apology enrage the Prince with even greater wrath against their wicked behavior?

How hateful and ridiculous, then, would such a plea be regarding this *Spiritual Fornication* <term>Spiritual Fornication</term> <note>A biblical metaphor common in the 17th century where idolatry—the worship of anything other than God—is compared to marital unfaithfulness or adultery.</note> with the nearest relations and friends of our Blessed Savior? Can *Spiritual Adultery*, which is *Idolatry*, committed with the *Blessed Virgin*, *St. John*, and others, be more tolerable than the same committed with *Diana*, *Apollo*, and other mortals declared to be gods by the Heathens?

Indeed, would not this latter case be merely *simple fornication* or *adultery*? Since in such unholy people there is no turning away from

So, I see not the slightest reason left to doubt that I have decoded the *concept* <note>original: "Idea"</note> *of the most perfect and most detestable Antichristianism* possible.

10. And thus, having fully completed the *sketch* <note>original: "Draught"</note> of the *concept* of *Antichristianism*, I might, following the method I mentioned, apply it to the state of the Church that has fallen into apostasy <note>original: "apostatized thereinto"</note>.

But because some people are so difficult to convince that any corruption of the Christian Church—so long as they still formally claim *Jesus* to be the *Christ*—can amount to the creation of that famous and notable *Antichrist* whom the prophecies seem to point toward. These people insist with all dogmatism that he must be an open denier of *Jesus*, and someone who expressly claims to be the expected *Messiah*, rather than a supposed successor or disciple of the true *Christ*. Therefore, I think it very appropriate, before I proceed to the *application of my concept of Antichristianism*, to conduct a more thorough search into the *Prophecies*. From there, I hope to demonstrate with irrefutable evidence that such an *Antichrist* in the main—as represented in that *concept*—is also prefigured or foretold by the Holy Prophets. That is to say, an Antichrist who, while committing such abominable villainies as I have listed, still claims to be part—indeed, the head—of the Body of Christ, which is his Church.

For unless I do this, I know that ignorance and falsehood are so evasive <note>original: "shuffling"</note> that they will think they can escape everything by saying that I have indeed made an elaborate <note>original: "operose"</note> description of *A true concept*, but not *The true concept of Antichristianism* that my title claims. In other words, they will say the Church does indeed act very wickedly, and in some sense in an "Antichristian" way in these failures, but that it does not amount to being the *Antichrist* properly and specifically so-called and pointed to by the predictions of the Prophets.

Therefore, we are forced to look into these prophecies before we go any further. We are more easily persuaded to do so because the method is naturally effective either way. My first intended method was, after this description of the *Concept of Antichristianism*, to make a precise *application of it to the fallen condition of the Church*, to discover who *in fact* <note>original: "de facto"</note> is that Great *Antichrist*; and then to apply the *prophecies to the historical events*, to show that they also point toward <note>original: "indigitate"</note> the same thing my *concept* reveals. My current proposed method is: *After this description of the concept of Antichristianism, to search the Prophecies to find that their descriptions of Antichrist* are, in their main points (for neither are the *Prophecies* concerning Christ predictions of all his specific actions), most clearly in agreement with the *concept* we have given. Furthermore, I will show that the *Antichristianism* which they foretell is a *corruption* or *apostasy of the Church that still formally claims to be Christian*, exactly as we have described in our *concept*. And then, finally, to make a more precise *application of our concept of Antichristianism*, now justified by its agreement with the prophetic pre-dictions, <note>The page ends mid-word on "predictions."</note>

# Chapter 17. Concerning the Predictions in Scripture.

...predictions, applied to the state of apostasy <note>original: "Apostatized state"</note> in the Church for so many ages until our own times. This will provide a fuller demonstration <note>original: "plenarie eviction"</note> of the incredible truthfulness of the prophecies. And it is just as sound and natural a method to prove the truth of the prophecies by the completeness <note>original: "Fulness"</note> of historical events, as it is to illustrate the nature of those events by applying the prophecies to them.

However, in the meantime, it will be necessary in this current search to refer to historical events in some way; for who can explain a prophecy without any reference to actual events? The history we need to reference is either separate from the concept <note>original: "Idea"</note> we have outlined (and will be introduced when interpreting specific passages), or it consists of general knowledge regarding the various parts <note>original: "Limbs"</note> of the anti-Christian system <note>original: "Antichristianism"</note> I have described—matters of which almost no one is ignorant or unconvinced in the main. 

Therefore, without any confusion or obscurity, we can proceed to our intended search of the prophecies. We will do this partly by referring to our concept <note>original: "Idea"</note> in areas that need no further proof, and partly by citing history where necessary, to provide a more complete demonstration of the truth of our concept of the anti-Christian system. Once this is finished, we will make a more precise <note>original: "punctual"</note> application of it, both to undeniably convict the guilty and to clear the innocent of all such unfair accusations <note>original: "Aspersions"</note>.

# The PREFACE to the Reader.

->READER,<-

<margin>The main prejudices against this current discourse.</margin>
I am not ignorant of the many **prejudices** this **work** <note>original: "Performance"</note> I present to you may face; it being a **treatise** entirely focused on the **interpretation** of **prophecies**, and chiefly those of **Daniel** and the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. For it is all too true that some men look upon such **attempts** as very vain and frivolous, having concluded beforehand that all **prophecies** are unsolvable **enigmas** <note>original: "Ænigms"</note> and **riddles**, utterly incapable of any certain **solution**. Others, whose **objection** <note>original: "Exception"</note> would be more significant if it were true, hold a notion that searching into **prophecies**—especially those of the **Apocalypse** and of **Daniel**—tends toward nothing else but **sectarianism** <note>original: "Faction"</note> and **confusion**, to the trouble and unsettlement of the affairs of **Christendom**, and to the hazard of the **overthrowing** <note>original: "subversion"</note> of **states** and **kingdoms**, and the ruin and destruction of the **Church** of **Christ**. And perhaps there may be others who, though they neither deem the obscurity of these **prophecies** impossible to overcome, nor the study of them dangerous—but rather of good use and great consequence—are yet so well satisfied already concerning these things by those highly praised and scholarly **works** <note>original: "Elucubrations"</note> of Mr. **Joseph Mede** <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638) was a famous English scholar whose work on the Book of Revelation was considered the gold standard in the 17th century.</note>, that they may in all likelihood judge any new **essays** here to be needless and redundant. With these three grand **prejudices**, I imagine myself burdened regarding the **nature** of the **subject** I write about; besides whatever particular **objections** men may be prone to make against any parts of the **work** itself. But I do not despair of more than fully clearing myself of them all.

<margin>That divine prophecies are not impossibly obscure, and that it smells of blasphemy and profaneness to pronounce them so.</margin>
2. For concerning the first point, I think there is no man who has the fear of **God** before his eyes but would be ashamed to stand by any such **assertion**. It borders so nearly on **profaneness** and **impiety**—indeed, on open **blasphemy** against the **Spirit** of **God**—as if He dictated such things to the holy **prophets** as are not sense, nor ever to be understood by any reader of them. Can there be anything more **skeptical** against **divine inspiration** than this, or anything that more undermines the very foundations of the **Christian religion**? But we need not labor very anxiously in refuting an **error** so universally condemned by all parties who are at all serious in their **religion**. For the obscurest **books** of **prophecy**—I mean those of the **Apocalypse** and **Daniel**—are commented

# The Preface to the Reader.

...agreed upon by **Catholics** <note>original: "Papists"</note>, **Protestants**, and **those who are neutral**, whereby they have all given their consensus that the **Visions** are understandable. But whatever obscurity there may be in them, I think my present efforts <note>original: "pains"</note> ought to be the more acceptable because I have contributed so much to a clear and certain way of interpreting them. I have laid down such assured **grounds** and **principles** <note>original: "Rudiments"</note> that if a man carefully observes them and finds **history** to be applicable within the scope of these **laws**, he can no more fail to find the right meaning of a **prophecy** than he would fail in translating the true sense of a **Latin** or **Greek author** while keeping to the **rules** of **grammar** and the known interpretations found in **dictionaries**.

Having kept to these **laws** myself so strictly and carefully, I dare appeal to all the world to judge if I have not provably <note>original: "demonstratively"</note> made out the sense of such **Visions** as I have undertaken to explain. And for my own part, I must freely profess that I found it no such hard thing to understand those **prophecies** I have interpreted. I am certainly persuaded that neither any such greatness of **intellect** <note>original: "Parts"</note> nor **abundance** of **learning** is required to understand these things as much as **integrity** of heart and **lack of prejudice** in the mind. For if that **Spirit** of life be once revived in a man, he will—by virtue of his **regeneration** or **new birth**—not only see with his eyes but feel with his hands the truth of these **mysteries**. <margin>Daniel 12:10.</margin> *None of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand*; namely, as many as apply themselves to the search of such things, who will also in the meantime be so prudent as not to prejudge what they never yet had the opportunity to carefully examine.

<margin>The greater the danger there is from false and unskillful interpretations of prophecies, the greater value there ought to be placed upon the labor of those who search out such as are exact and true.</margin> 3. 7. First, for example, in his interpretation of the Beast that "was, and is not." Therefore, how awkward <note>original: "harsh"</note> must it be to say of it *while it is in existence* that it *was*? But how plain a contradiction it is to say it *is not* while it *is*, or that it is *not yet born* when it has continued for so many ages, and does and is to continue uninterruptedly for so many more? 

If we apply this to any particular person still alive and in health, who is to live many more years, will it not go against common sense to say of him, "he *was*, and *is not*," while he is alive and in being? Besides that, "not yet born" <note>original: *necdum tamen natam esse*</note> does not at all specify his succession under the eighth King more than the seventh; that being left out in this interpretation which is most plainly and significantly meant in the prophecy: namely, that the Beast *was to cease to be for a time*. Therefore, it is a necessity that there should be eight Kings, even though there are only seven Heads of the Beast. For the Beast, in his non-existence, could neither lack nor have a Head.

Not only *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch legal scholar and theologian who favored historical rather than prophetic interpretations</note>, but Mr. *Mede* <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential scholar of the Book of Revelation</note> himself understands those "Antichrists" to be the *false Christs* whom our Savior predicted in the Gospel of *Matthew*. Those were the ones who would appear before and after the destruction of *Jerusalem*, which was the "last hour" <note>original: ἔσχάτη ὥρα</note> of the Jewish Commonwealth. 

However, since "last hour" signifies nothing more than "last time" <note>original: καιρὸς ἔσχατος</note>—for the underlying term is indifferently rendered as either "hour" or "time"—and since the "Fourth Kingdom" in the book of *Daniel* is the last one, the time of that Kingdom may also be what is meant by the "last hour." From this, the passage in *St. John* <margin>* 1 John 2:18</margin>—[*My little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that the Antichrist is coming <note>original: ὅτι ὁ ἀντίχριστος ἔρχεται</note>, even now there are many antichrists, by which we know it is the last hour*]—may carry this meaning, assuming the prediction is written somewhat concisely: 

That the "last time" in Daniel’s calendar of his four kingdoms—that is to say, the last kingdom, which is the *Roman*—was then underway. During this kingdom, the *Little Horn* <term>Little Horn: a symbolic figure from the Book of Daniel representing a blasphemous power that rises out of the Roman Empire</term>, which is called here "Antichrist," shall come upon the stage. "This is *the* Antichrist" (John says), "that famous Antichrist whom you may have heard of from the book of *Daniel*, but he is still a long way off." Therefore, to speak of what more closely concerns you now: "*Even now there are many antichrists*" (whom our Savior, not Daniel, predicted), "*by which we also know it is the last hour*." In this second instance, however, I do not mean the last of the four kingdoms of *Daniel*, but the last hour of the Jewish nation, according to what our Lord predicted. 

Or, to put it more briefly: "*My little children, it is the last hour*," meaning the last of the four kingdoms, the *Roman*. And just as you have heard that the famous *Antichrist* will come then (during that last hour), so also now, in the final hour of the Jewish government, there are many antichrists. From this, we may gather that it is the "last hour" of the Jewish state, because these many antichrists attend this last hour just as that one famous Antichrist will attend the other.

In some sense such as this, I do confess that the *Antichrist* or *Antichristianism* which I have treated so far may be referred to by that very name in this scripture text, although I will not argue with anyone who chooses to interpret it differently. *Grotius* explains this "famous Antichrist," of whom they might have heard, as referring to *Barchocab* <note>Bar Kokhba, the leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome in 132 AD, who was initially hailed by some as the Messiah</note>. # Whether the grand Degeneracy of the Church be predicted Book I.

5. The same author also interprets "Who is the liar?" <note>original: "τίς ἐστὶν ὁ ψεύστης;" from 1 John 2:22</note> as referring to *Bar Kokhba* <note>original: "Barchocab," the leader of the second-century Jewish revolt against Rome</note>, and translates it as "Who can be a greater impostor?" <note>original: "Quis potest esse major impostor?"</note> and I believe very rightly. For it would be a weak <note>original: "dilute"</note> matter for the Apostle to describe Antichrist only by the simple denial of *Jesus* being the Christ—that great King, Priest, and Prophet sent by God, to whom all nations should flow. For such Antichrists are all infidels, who are innumerable. Therefore, such a "denier of Christ" is hinted at here as one who, by playing the impostor and by making himself Christ—or by putting himself in the place of the true Christ, who is *Jesus*—denies *Jesus* to be the Christ. By denying him, he denies the one who sent him and witnessed that he was his beloved Son, whom everyone should hear. Such an Antichrist was *Bar Kokhba* especially, who by making himself the *Messiah* <note>original: "Messias"</note>, did thereby plainly deny that *Jesus* was he.

But just as there were notable types <note>original: "eximious Types," meaning symbolic forerunners</note> of Christ among the people of the Jews, whom the same prophecies touch as well as Christ himself; so it is easy to conceive that *Antichrists* might also arise among those people. All things happened to them in figures, which were types of the famous Antichrist in the Christian Church, and one and the same text might point at both—as it is not hard to conceive that this text does.

For as for that great Antichrist which I have described in my *Idea of Antichristianism*, it is plain that he puts *Jesus* out of his Kingly, Priestly, and Prophetic office, usurping all that for himself or conferring it upon others, as is there extensively declared. Therefore, by making himself such an absolute Head of the Church, he does by that very act <note>original: "ipso facto"</note> cut off *Jesus* from being Head of the same, and thereby reveals himself to be that notorious Antichrist in Christendom. And by denying that *Jesus* is that supreme King, Priest, and Prophet to whom all are to listen and obey, whose decrees and words are an immutable Law, he thereby also denies the Father who sent him, as much as any other Antichrist among the Jews can be imagined ever to have done. For which of them was ever said to have professed himself an atheist?

6. This implies they did not read "the Antichrist" <note>original: "ὁ ἀντίχριστος"</note>, but "whom you heard that he is coming" <note>original: "ὃν ἀκηκόατε ὅτι ἔρχεται"</note>. And he adds, "and now he is already in the world" <note>original: "καὶ νῦν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν ἤδη"</note>, much like that phrase of *St. Paul*: "For the mystery [of iniquity] is already at work" <note>original: "Τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται"</note>.

The meaning of both may be this: namely, that whereas those to whom St. *John* wrote had heard rumors or reports of that extraordinary <note>original: "eximious"</note> *Antichrist* who was to come into the world in the end times—prompted (I have no doubt) by *Daniel's* prophecies of the *little horn* and of that *king of pride* who would exalt himself above all—the fulfillment <note>original: "Event"</note> of these prophecies was further off. Though they would certainly happen at last, John focuses their minds on such *Antichrists* as were nearer at hand. Though these were only the types and figures of that great *Antichrist* to come some ages later, they were of more immediate concern for them to notice. In the meantime, he describes *Antichrist* in such a way that while it points more obviously to these forerunners of the future *Antichrist*, the description, when searched more narrowly, also applies firmly to that great *Antichrist* himself. This is because it implies someone who, by way of imposture, puts himself in the place of *Jesus*, the true *Christ*, King, Priest, and Prophet appointed by God, to whom all must submit. Not only have *Bar Kokhba* and similar false *Messiahs* <note>original: "Messiaſſes"</note> in the *Jewish* commonwealth done this, but he who has so made himself the Head of the Church as to nullify the laws and doctrines of *Christ* is understood to do the same.

7. I must confess that the opposition and intrusion of this grand *Antichrist* among *Christians* is more indirect and subtle than the claims of those false *Messiahs* among the *Jews*. However, we should also notice that the *Christians'* *Messiah* or *Christ* is more spiritual than what the *Jews* expected. Therefore, it is no wonder that their *Antichrist* is of a different nature—not a crude and violent invader of the empire of *Christ*, but a more cunning impostor and insinuating hypocrite.

Nor should we wonder that *Christendom* has been so slow to discover this *Antichrist* after he arrived. The same thing happened to them as befell the *Jews*, who could not recognize their *Messiah* when he walked and talked before their eyes every day. Both of these mistakes arose from a similar prejudice and false preconceived notion. The *Jews* imagined a *Messiah* who would conquer kingdoms for them and make them a rich and powerful people on Earth—so crude <note>original: "crass"</note> and external a concept did they have of his power and office. Likewise, *Christians* imagined such an *Antichrist* as one who would discard the outward profession of *Christ* and directly and openly oppose him in his kingdom.

8. But fraudulent and hypocritical opposition is just as real, and even more harmful, than that which is open and direct. And he who calls another Lord and King, but claims a power to abolish <note>original: "abrogating"</note> his laws,

This meaning, I think, will appear very plain to any impartial <note>original: "indifferent"</note> judgment; and I need not dwell on it any longer, having suggested something to the same purpose before. This is true only in effect, because they also sacrificed to other gods, and so did not sacrifice to *Jehovah* the true God. He is so matchless a Perfection that he cannot have any rival or partner in religious worship; because they did this for others, they effectively <note>original: "interpretatively"</note> disowned *Jehovah* from being what he was. Therefore they did not sacrifice to him—not even when they pretended to—but rather to a figment of their own imagination. And lastly, in this very Epistle, *St. John* says *that he who denies that Jesus is the Christ denies both the Father and the Son.* But who ever heard that *Bar Kokhba* or any other Jewish false messiah <note>original: "Pseudo-christ"</note> directly denied the God who was the Father of our Lord *Jesus Christ*? Several similar examples occur in Scripture, which are so obvious that it is unnecessary to list them. These may serve as proof of the reasonableness of our interpretation.

# Why Prophecies are to be obscure. Book I.

...and so just. For it is fit that knowledge that is so far removed above human capacity should be received with as humble and profound veneration as possible. This *obscurity* and *mysteriousness* earns respect for all truths, but it is most due to those that are the greatest and the most beyond our natural reach, as this matter of *Prophecy* is. 

Besides that, this *obscurity* acts as a check to restrain or oppose that hasty fervor and heat with which men are usually carried toward the knowledge of things to come. While it falls to the share of very few to be immediate receivers of such visions, if anyone is, all men are ready to throng and crowd around him out of that natural curiosity and desire to be instructed concerning future events. Upon this fiery and restless itch for the knowledge of the future, Providence has cast this bridle of hard and enigmatic <note>original: "Ænigmatical"</note> uttering of prophetical predictions. 

He has done this just as he has placed the laws of natural shame and modesty—along with the added institutions of religion and human policy—upon that impetuous inclination to experience the pleasures of the marriage bed. This ensures that such strong inclinations may not be satisfied without the ceremony of some tedious attendance and expectation. And it may be that this expectation and hope, being a kind of foretaste <note>original: "prelibation"</note> of enjoyment, may in both cases lengthen out the pleasure.

2. But there is also a great necessity for this *obscurity* which we have not yet mentioned: that these divine predictions concerning the Church of God may not be easily understood—or understood at all—by those who are meant to fulfill them until the appointed time comes, when they can be revealed without harm to the true Church. That is to say, things are not to be so clearly foreshadowed <note>original: "prefigured"</note> that they would conflict too much with the principle of free will in man. 

By this principle, a man determines his own ways according to his own pleasure, unless he is miraculously called to do otherwise by Heaven. A divine prediction so plain that it certainly informed a person that he would perform an act leading to his own shame and destruction—or one that served as a conspicuous and infallible mark to all the world that he was that odious person destined for an ill fate—would undoubtedly cause him to refuse to fulfill it, simply for his own honor and security. Unless God should use a strong force upon him to make him fulfill the prophecy, he would omit any such circumstances as were described beforehand, in order to erase the identifying characteristics of his own person from the prophecy.

As for example, if *St. John* had said expressly that by the *Two-horned Beast* and by *The Whore of Babylon* he meant a succession of Bishops of *Rome* with their whole hierarchy adhering to them, it would be a hard thing to believe that this universal bishop <note>original: "Oecumenical Prelate"</note> would not have been tempted to *change his see on the seven hills* <note>Rome is traditionally known as the city on seven hills</note> to hide his shame, so that he might not seem to be the man at whom the prophecy pointed. 

At the very least, they would never have written *Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> upon the Pope's crown, as it is written on the *Whore of Babylon*, if they had been aware that his Holiness was so much involved in that vision. Nor can we imagine that, if instead of *666*, the number *25* <note>This likely refers to the theories of 17th-century writers like Francis Potter, who argued that 25 was the "root" of the number of the Beast and found it throughout Roman Catholic structures</note> had been said to be the *Number of the Beast*, the Church of *Rome* would have favored that number as much as they have. Many more such instances could be produced.

# Chapter II. Why the Prophecies are to be obscure.

But God could hardly be said to *leave man to his own devices* <note>original: "leave man in the hand of his own Counsel"</note> and let him act freely according to his own nature, if He were to speak these Divine revelations <note>original: "Oracles"</note> concerning future things in such a plain and exposed manner, and yet still bring about their fulfillment.

3. Besides this, communicating the knowledge of future things concerning the Church to her enemies may result in her harm; it is generally unsafe to let an adversary gain intelligence regarding our plans and purposes.

This is not only true regarding men, but also regarding those invisible enemies of the Church who constantly attack and oppose her under the leadership of the "Prince of the Power of the Air" <note>A biblical reference to Satan.</note>. These spirits are the great supporters and helpers of the "children of disobedience." A remarkable <note>original: "eximious"</note> instance of this was noted by Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential English scholar of biblical prophecy.</note> from St. Augustine. He describes how the Devil—who in ancient times had enough skill in mathematics to puzzle the Athenians with the problem of "doubling the cube" <note>The Delian Problem, a famous unsolved geometric challenge from antiquity.</note>—calculated the proportion between the Outward Court of the Temple and the Inward Court. He apparently found the ratio to be about 1260 to 365. He immediately concluded *that Christianity would last only 365 years in the world, and that Paganism would then rise again.* Therefore, attempting to boost the credit of his own false predictions by using this stolen, but misunderstood, prophecy from the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>, he spread it abroad so that he might hinder people from converting to the faith of Christ. This, I think, is argument enough to persuade us how necessary it is for holy prophecies to be wrapped in enigmatic coverings. They must be made into interpretations that are uncertain due to their slippery <note>original: "lubricities"</note> and indeterminate nature, until either the actual events occur, or some faithful interpreter—specially assisted by God—provides their clear solution.

4. Now, as for the art of hiding predictions and what it consists of: although I will not attempt to explain the whole subject, I will provide as large a portion of it as will at least suffice for our current purpose. I shall include this in the explanation of these few *Prophetic Figures* or *Schemes*, which I will venture to call *Diorismus* (Specific Limitation), *Hylasmus* (Materialization), *Henopœia* (Unification), *Zoopœia* (Personification), *Israelismus* (Israel-characterization), *Ellipsis* (Omission), *Metalepsis* (Substitution), *Homonymia* (Ambiguity), *Antichronismus* (Time-reversal), and *Icasmus* (Comparison). Most of these serve as much to embellish and decorate the external shell <note>original: "Cortex"</note> of prophecies as they do to conceal and cover their more precious inward meaning.

5. *Diorismus* is a stylistic device <note>original: "Scheme"</note> of the prophetic style that polishes the literal wording with an appearing sense of a very exact and determinate account of things, whether in terms of *Number*, *Proportion*, or *Specification*. This strikes the imagination <note>original: "Phancy"</note> more strongly; just as a settled and unmoved object makes a stronger impression upon the sight than one that is moving, as ordinary experience tells us. Similarly, any specific concept affects the mind more vigorously and tangibly than what is more general and vague.

I believe an example of the first type of this figure is found in Revelation 2: *You shall have the affliction of ten days.* In this case, I must confess I could never imagine that being spoken as anything other than a figure of speech—a *Diorismus*. It is a subtle suggestion of a most perfect and full persecution,

# The Definitions and Illustrations Book I.

As is suggested by the following words, *Be faithful unto death,* etc. See the commentaries of Vatable <note>François Vatable (d. 1547), a French humanist scholar and noted Hebraist.</note> and Drusius <note>Johannes Drusius (1550–1616), a Flemish Protestant scholar and expert in Hebrew and Jewish studies.</note> on this passage; they provide several examples of the number **ten** being used to mean "many." If we suppose the **Ten Horns** on the Beast have this meaning, there is no absurdity in admitting it; though I do not criticize the hard work of those who are so concerned with finding exactly ten and no more. For an exact count may more powerfully convince the stubborn, while others may be satisfied that the number simply suggests the state of the Empire when it was divided into a significant number of kingdoms or principalities enjoying sovereign power within themselves.

And that the **one hundred forty-four thousand** standing with the Lamb on Mount **Zion** are not to be thought of as exactly that many or that few. Anyone will grant this who notices that the number 144 is simply the square of 12. Therefore, according to the style of the ancient Kabbalah <note>original: "Cabbala"; a Jewish mystical tradition often used in numerical interpretation.</note>, it symbolically signifies the "apostolic nature" <note>The number 12 is associated with the twelve apostles.</note> of that company, rather than their specific head-count—any more than 666 is the exact number of those who follow the Beast.

I also suspect that those **7,000 names of men** said to be killed in that great earthquake in **Revelation 11** is spoken only by way of a prophetic *diorismus* <note>original: "Diorismus"; a rhetorical term for a specific, defined number used to signify an indefinite but significant quantity.</note>; but I shall discuss its true meaning in the appropriate place.

I will offer a fourth example: the **1,260 days**. Since these are simply the breakdown <note>original: "Diduction"</note> of those larger measurements of **three and a half times** or of **forty-two months** into smaller parts, it is reasonable to suspect that this was done to vary the phrasing and to polish the external structure of the prophecy. By numbering those times or months as 1,260 days, it does not necessarily mean we should expect fulfillment down to the exact prophetic day. In such massive events, one day among so many is insignificant and of little use, especially since the starting point <note>original: "Epocha"</note> from which the time is to begin is uncertain. Furthermore, as Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), a famous scholar of biblical prophecy.</note> has suggested, varying the time into "months" and "days" respects the works of **Light** and the works of **Darkness**. Therefore, the duration for those under the rule of Light is counted in **days**; but for those under the rule of Darkness—the **Moon** being the governor of the night—it is counted in **months**.

Therefore, a man might reasonably imagine that there is a flexibility in this calculation of the **three and a half times**, or the 42 months, into 126 decades of days, just as there is flexibility in those "times" and "months." Any variation, slightly above or below, that does not exceed a decade does not ruin the calculation <note>original: "breaks no squares"; an old idiom meaning it doesn't matter or cause a problem.</note>. Divine prophecies are not intended for the display of God's omniscience (for who does not know He can calculate events down to the smallest moment of an hour?), nor are they meant to satisfy excessive human curiosity, but rather for the use and spiritual exercise of His Church.

The witnesses lying unburied for **three and a half days** is another excellent <note>original: "eximious"</note> example of this numerical *diorismus*; but the meaning may be the same as "three and a half times," as I have suggested elsewhere.

Nor is this doubling of the five months sufficiently grounded in the fact that the time is mentioned twice in the prophecy. (For the mention of the same number twice in prophecy or history does not warrant adding them together to make a new total, as if it were a bill of particulars.) Finally, it is not likely that the Spirit of God would indicate <note>original: "indigitate"</note> 300 years by those "twice five months," because the duration of the **Saracens'** Empire was much longer, and the continuation of the **Caliphate** at **Baghdad** does not match that length of time.

The infestation of **Italy** by the **Saracens** from the year 830 to 980 would have been a more plausible explanation if it had matched the timeframe; but it extends beyond the year 980. For in the year <note>original: "anno"</note> 1001, the **Saracens** were expelled from **Capua** by **Otto**; in the next year they besieged **Salerno** <note>original: "Salernum"</note>; in the year 1008 they were forced to end the sieges of **Bari** <note>original: "Barium"</note> and **Capua**; and in the year 1017 they invaded **Italy** again, besides other fights and troubles afterward. This is enough to show that "five months" of years cannot be well applied to their molestation of **Italy** either, though I think Mr. **Mede** has made the argument look as handsome as possible. But the attempt was as unnecessary as it was unsuccessful. For there is no exactly determined time intended by these **five months**. Instead, it is only an elegant specific definition <note>original: "Diorism"</note> regarding the symbol <note>original: "Type"</note>, which are **locusts**. Since a locust's lifespan does not reach the space of a year, it was appropriate, by way of a chronological displacement <note>original: "Antichronismus"</note>, to count their time by **months**. And what number is more fitting than **five**? Not only because it may be a symbol of incompleteness (as **Ribera** <note>Francisco Ribera (1537–1591), a Spanish Jesuit theologian.</note> suggests, and those **locusts** are said only to **torment**, not **kill**), but also in respect to the length of their life, which, according to **Pliny**, **Aristotle**, and other naturalists, is in all likelihood about **five months**. So the solution to the mystery of these numbers is not merely found in such a chronological displacement, where the figurative number determines the true one, but also in a specific definition <note>original: "Diorismus"</note>, where this accuracy is expressed in the outer shell <note>original: "Cortex"</note> of the text, but not intended in the inward meaning. This scheme is used here with a special elegance because of how it reflects the noted lifespan of those creatures used as the symbol.

<header>The Definitions and Illustrations Book I.</header>

"Prepared for the hour and day and month and year" <note>original: "ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν"</note> may, as interpreters generally observe, signify nothing more than their readiness at the appointed time, whether at a day, month, or year. For by "the hour" <note>original: "τὴν ὥραν"</note> in all likelihood the Prophecy meant not that specific part of time which we call an hour, but "the season" <note>original: "τὸν καιρὸν"</note>. The Greek article prefixed to "hour" may suggest this, as it is only attached to that word. The sense might have been, *Ready at the time appointed, whether day, month, or year*, which is to say, at any time. 

But the historical event is so exact and conspicuous that I do not doubt the meaning is: *Ready* "at the season" <note>original: "εἰς τὸν καιρὸν"</note>—namely, "both a day and a month and a year" <note>original: "καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν"</note>. This is ready at that season indicated by adding a day, a month, and a year together; these together make up 396 days, which "in prophetic style" <note>original: "stylo Prophetico"</note> are so many *years*. This corresponds exquisitely to the historical event, and therefore it is a certain marker to fix this prophecy of the **Euphratean Horsemen** to the affairs of the **Turkish Empire**. By this, as well as by the description of the **Breastplates** of these horsemen, we know to what **ages** of the world this prophecy belongs, and consequently the preceding prophecy of the **Locusts**. Therefore, noting their time as more than a mere <term>Diorism</term> <note>A rhetorical or prophetic device where specific details or numbers are used to define a subject.</note> for the sake of adorning the prophecy was unnecessary.

9. **Examples of Proportional Diorisms** are like these in **Revelation 8**: *The third part of the trees was burnt up, the third part of the ships was destroyed, the third part of the sea became blood; and in chapter 12: The third part of the sun was smitten, and the third part of the moon, etc.* In these cases, **Third** does not signify the literal proportion of what was destroyed compared to what escaped; rather, the Empire at large which was attacked is pointed out by this number. This has a trace of the **Kabbalistic spirit** <note>original: "Cabbalistick Genius"; referring to the mystical Jewish tradition of finding symbolic meaning in numbers.</note>, where practitioners use **Numbers** as symbols for things, as I have already noted. Similarly, the **Tenth part of the city** is not literally one-tenth of the city as it then existed, but refers to a city whose size bore the proportion of a **tenth** part to what it had once been, as Mr. **Mede** has carefully calculated.

To this category you may also refer **Revelation 18**: *Give back to her double according to her works, and fill for her a double cup.* This is spoken so definitively as if she should be repaid with exactly twice as much as she had injured others; however, the sense is only that she should be fully punished for all her injurious dealings.

10. **Examples of Specific Diorisms** are common <term>Synecdoches</term> <note>A figure of speech where a specific part represents the whole, or a specific species represents a general category.</note> that put the **species** in place of the **genus**. Because a species is a more determinate object, it strikes the imagination more strongly and with greater satisfaction. Thus, the imagination is more loudly alarmed by being informed that a thing or person shall be "burnt" or "consumed with fire" than if it were only said they should "perish" or "be consumed" without specifying the manner. In the same way, to **make war** is more determinate and specific than to **oppose**; to be **beheaded** is more specific than simply to **die** or be **killed**; and to be **slain** is more specific than to be **destroyed**. Lastly, **King** is a more specific term and strikes the imagination more fully than **Supreme Magistrate**, or any other more general and consequently more diluted title. Examples of this third kind of **Diorism** occur throughout the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> and indeed everywhere in the Prophets.

# CHAPTER III.

1. *Hylasmus <note>original: "Hylasmus"; from the Greek word "hyle" meaning "matter." A prophetic figure where spiritual or abstract concepts are represented by physical, material objects.</note>: what it is, along with its various kinds. 2. Excellent examples of each kind. 3. What the first and most important kind of Henopoeia <note>original: "Henopœia"; a prophetic figure where a group or a succession is represented as a single individual or unit.</note> is. 4. Evidence from the Book of Daniel that a single beast signifies a "Body Politic" (a state or government). 5. That a succession of individuals is represented by one individual. 6. That one individual beast represents a kingdom or Body Politic from its beginning to its end. 7. That one single man or woman also represents a Body Politic in prophetic style. 8. What the second kind of Henopoeia is. 9. What Zoopoeia <note>original: "Zoopœia"; the representation of something inanimate or abstract as a living creature.</note> is, with examples. 10. A second kind of Zoopoeia proved and illustrated with examples.*

1. **Hylasmus** is a prophetic scheme that makes a strong impression on the imagination by presenting solid and tangible objects—things that, in logic, would be considered "Subject" or "Matter." The first kind is identical to a *Metonymy of the Subject* <note>original: "Metonymia Subjecti"; a figure of speech where the container or place is used to refer to the people or things within it.</note>; for example, when a **City** is used to represent its **Inhabitants**, or a **Temple** represents those who **worship** inside it. Examples of this kind are found everywhere.

For the second kind, I would point to representations involving buildings, pavements, and similar structures. These are composed of solid and tangible materials, yet they are mystical or spiritual symbols of something else entirely. Examples of this kind include the **Inner** and **Outer Court** of the Temple—the one **proportional** <note>original: "Symmetral"</note>, the other **unproportional** <note>original: "Asymmetral"</note>. This signifies the Christian Church: at one time in her purity, and at another in her transition into idolatry. Similarly, the **Holy City** being trampled by the Gentiles signifies the Christian Church being overrun by paganism. Thus, the "city" <note>original: "$\pi\acute{o}\lambda\iota\varsigma$" (polis)</note> in this case is a symbol of a "state" or "Body Politic" <note>original: "$\pi\text{o}\lambda\iota\tau\epsilon\acute{\iota}\alpha$" (politeia)</note>, just as the **Temple** may represent the living Church of Christ.

2. An excellent example of this kind of *Hylasmus* is the description of **Jerusalem** in *Revelation 21*, with its high wall and twelve gates. Through a prophetic *Diorism* <note>original: "Diorism"; a precise definition or specification, often using specific numbers.</note>, the dimensions of the city are determined to be twelve thousand furlongs, the wall is one hundred forty-four cubits, and the materials are gold, pearls, and precious stones. Yet this city, described in such **material** <note>original: "Hylastically"</note> terms, has a deeply spiritual meaning; it signifies nothing other than the Church of Christ restored to its original Apostolic purity.

However, the most notable instance of a prophetic *Hylasmus* is the description of the Temple by **Ezekiel**. I must say that Saint John alludes to this in several passages of Revelation. I think anyone who reads the 47th chapter of Ezekiel will easily grant that it is an *Hylasmus* rather than a literal description.

Finally, the destruction of the city of **Babylon** in the *Revelation* is also a remarkable example of this scheme. Although it generally belongs to this second kind of *Hylasmus*, things are described there largely through the first kind—a *Metonymy of the Subject—not of the container, as before, but of the occupant* <note>original: "Metonymia Subjecti, not continentis... but occupantis"</note>. This is because the objects of their spiritual dealings are revealed and described in such physical detail.

### The Definitions and Illustrations: Book I.

3. The next prophetic scheme is **Henopoeia** <note>original: "Henopaia"; from the Greek words for "one" and "make." A figure of speech where a group or a succession of people is represented as a single individual.</note>, which is the most graceful, but also as obscuring as any. The first and most important kind of this scheme is the collection of a multitude of individuals into the appearance of one individual; it also includes representing a succession of individuals or groups as one single, standing individual. This is an ancient method of delivering mysteries, as anyone will see if they thoroughly consider <note>original: "perpend"</note> the nature and truth of the ancient **Kabbalah** <note>original: "Cabbala"; a traditional Jewish system of mystical scriptural interpretation.</note>. I believe it can easily be proven that Daniel, St. John, and even St. Paul imitated this in their prophecies.

<margin>Daniel 7.</margin>
4. Regarding the collection of a **multitude** into the appearance or representation of one individual, this is clear in the Book of Daniel. One individual **Lion** there denotes the entire kingdom of the **Babylonians**; one **Bear** denotes the kingdom of the **Medes and Persians**; one **Leopard** denotes the kingdom of the **Greeks**; and the **fourth beast** denotes the **Roman Kingdom**. It is true that the text says, "*The four beasts are four kings*"; but the **Vulgate** <note>original: "vulgar Latin"; the 4th-century Latin translation of the Bible.</note> has it as "*four kingdoms*," as does **Theodotion** <note>A 2nd-century scholar who translated the Hebrew Bible into Greek.</note>. Furthermore, the text explicitly says that the **fourth beast is the fourth kingdom upon earth**. Similarly, the **Ram** and the **Goat** in the eighth chapter (according to the interpretation of **Grotius** <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch legal scholar and theologian.</note> based on the Hebrew idiom) are **Kingdoms**, even though they are said to be **Kings**. And where it is written, "*And the rough goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king*," it makes no sense unless this **Goat** signifies either a succession of kings or a kingdom. Indeed, even if it meant a succession, it would be a very awkward interpretation to make the **great horn** the first king and the **body** represent the rest of the lineage. Therefore, unless we want to distort things beyond all measure, the **body** of the goat must signify the kingdom of **Greece**, while the **horns** signify the supreme power. This is consistent with what Grotius has written, and I do not doubt that his interpretation is true. I think hardly anyone could be so foolish as to read Daniel and not be convinced that in prophetic imagery, one individual beast signifies a multitude of people organized together into the body of a kingdom.

5. But just as the **great horn** of the male goat is said to be the first king, the **four horns** undoubtedly signified four succeeding kings in this divided kingdom in their various lineages <note>original: "series"</note>. Thus, four successions of individuals, for as long as they would last, were represented under the appearance of four single individuals—namely, those **four horns**. And truly, when it is obvious that one individual beast represents the succession of a multitude for many ages together (who are mortal, just like individual men) joined <note>original: "coagmentated"</note> into the body of one kingdom, it would be a very trivial and stubborn thing to object to the idea of a succession of single persons being represented under the appearance of **one head** or **horn**.

6. That one and the same beast stands for a kingdom or empire from its rise to its fall is plain in both Daniel and the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. For the four beasts are said to rise out of the great sea (Daniel 7), and the destruction of the fourth is described in that same chapter. This fourth beast is supposed to trample the third, just as the third is later declared to have defeated the second in the following chapters. In the Apocalypse, the rise of the beasts is recorded, as is their destruction in the lake of fire and sulfur. From this, it is evident that one individual beast represents not only a mul-

7. Irrational creatures are not the only things used as unifying symbols <term>original: "Henopoetick Types"</term> of a multitude collected into one government; rational ones are used as well. These things are so easy and so obvious that I am afraid I have spent too long on them.

8. I will only note a second kind of unifying symbol <note>original: "Henopæia"</note>, which is also useful to consider: that is, when things of different natures are comprised under one symbol. # Book I: The Definitions and Illustrations
