10. But we will also take notice here of a second kind of *Zoopœia* <term>original: "Zoopœia"; a rhetorical figure where life or personality is given to inanimate objects or deceased people</term>, which may seem less harsh and more elegant. This occurs when free actions are attributed to free agents who, despite this attribution, may be no more the cause of those actions than if they were inanimate beings or did not exist at all. According to this figure is that passage by *Virgil*, placed in the mouth of *Aeneas* as he slays *Turnus*:

->*It is Pallas who sacrifices you with this wound, Pallas*<-
->*who takes vengeance from your guilty blood.*<-
<note>original Latin: "Pallas te hoc vulnere, Pallas Immolat, & pœnas scelerato ex sanguine sumit." from Virgil’s Aeneid, Book XII.</note>

*Pallas*, despite being dead, is said to slay *Turnus*. He did nothing directly toward the killing; rather, his previous suffering only gave *Aeneas* the reason to take revenge.

According to this figure of speech, a larger allusion or parable might be constructed. For example, if *Aeneas*, instead of slaying a single man, had sacked a city, put every man, woman, and child to the sword, burned their houses, and left them as a heap of stones in revenge for the death of *Pallas*, he might say of his deceased friend that it was *he* who inflamed the courage of the soldiers to scale the walls; that it was *he* who issued that just, though severe, edict to slay man, woman, and child; that it was *he* who burned down their houses and leveled their city; and, finally, that they deservedly found him a more dangerous enemy after his death than while he was living. Certainly, this figure of speech would be very easy to understand and would carry with it an extraordinary level of rhetorical sophistication and elegance.

<margin>* Revelation 6:9</margin>
This same pattern <term>original: "Scheme"</term> is found in the scriptural example of the souls crying out from under the altar, "O Lord, how long..." (Revelation 6:10). This is nothing but a parable signifying that their deaths demanded vengeance from the justice of God. "Those souls," says *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch jurist and theologian famous for his work on international law and biblical exegesis.</note>, "being released from the body, bear witness to the death they endured much more than blood does." <note>original Latin: "Eæ animæ corpore solutæ multò magis quàm sanguis mortem toleratam testantur."</note> For he had said before, "The blood of Abel demands vengeance, and so do the souls of the martyrs." <note>original Latin: "Sanguis Abelis vindictam poscit, sic & animæ martyrum."</note> Therefore, a *Zoopœia* is acknowledged in both cases.

*Alcazar* <note>Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Spanish Jesuit who developed the preterist interpretation of Revelation.</note> also comments on the passage: "To say that the souls seek vengeance is the same as saying that their blood seeks it." <note>original Latin: "Idem est dici Animas petere vindictam ac dici earum sanguinem illam petere."</note> *Tychonius* <note>A 4th-century North African theologian known for his influential rules for interpreting Scripture.</note> speaks to this same effect, as you may see in *Ribera* <note>Francisco Ribera (1537–1591), a Jesuit theologian and doctor of theology.</note>. All of this confirms this second kind of *Zoopœia*, which attributes free and living actions to free agents. In reality, these are not their own free actions, but rather the necessary consequences resulting from something these people have suffered or are suffering. This is a prophetic pattern <term>original: "Scheme"</term> well worth noticing.

10. But we will also take notice here of a second kind of *zoopoieia* <note>original: Zoopœia; a rhetorical figure where life or personality is attributed to inanimate things or the dead</note>, which may seem less harsh and more elegant. This occurs when free actions are attributed to "free agents" who, in reality, may be no more the cause of those actions than if they were inanimate beings or did not exist at all. According to this figure is the passage from *Virgil*, placed in the mouth of *Aeneas* as he slays *Turnus*:

->*It is Pallas, Pallas who sacrifices you with this wound,*<-
->*and takes vengeance from your criminal blood.*<-
<note>original Latin: *Pallas te hoc vulnere, Pallas / Immolat, & pœnas scelerato ex sanguine sumit.*</note>

*Pallas*, being dead, is said to slay *Turnus*, even though he did nothing personally toward the slaying; rather, it was only what he had suffered that gave *Aeneas* the reason to take revenge.

According to this figure of speech, a larger allusion or parable might be constructed. Suppose *Aeneas*, instead of slaying one single man, had sacked a city, put man, woman, and child to the sword, burned their houses, and left them as a heap of stones in revenge for the death of *Pallas*. He might say of his deceased friend that it was *he* who inflamed the courage of the soldiers to scale the walls; that it was *he* who issued that just, though severe, edict to slay man, woman, and child; that it was *he* who burned down their houses and leveled their city; and, lastly, that it was *he* whom they deservedly found to be a more destructive enemy after his death than while he was living. Certainly, this figure of speech would be very easy to understand and, at the same time, carry with it an extraordinary level of rhetoric and elegance.

<margin>* Revelation 6:9</margin>

### Chapter 4: On Certain Prophetic Schemes

The elegance <note>original: concinnity; a skillful or harmonious arrangement</note> is marvelous to consider, the symbolic type being so clear a prophecy of what has happened within these last ages in breaking from that tyrannical bondage of the *Italian Pharaoh* <note>a Protestant reference to the Pope or the Roman Catholic Church, comparing the Reformation to the Israelites' escape from Egypt</note>. But such instances as these are infinite.

6. The next obscuring scheme is *Ellipsis*, which is the omission of some word or words which are required to determine the sense. Examples of *ellipses* occur everywhere in the Old Testament, in the *Psalms*, *Job*, and other books. But by an *ellipsis* here, I do not understand merely the lack of something to make up the full sense, but such an artificial defect as shall make the sense seem complete even without the supplement understood. For that seems to be the nature of these *Apocalyptic Visions* especially: they are made so as to seem very tidy and express, very complete and articulate in the very outward shell <note>original: cortex</note>, like a book that has some pleasing embellishments on the cover as well as the history of truth within.

<margin>Revelation 5:1</margin> 
7. I have little doubt that this may be alluded to in that expression concerning this volume of visions: that it was *written within and without*, according to the ancient manner of the Cabbalistic mysteries. Regarding these traditions, *Parmenides* held the principle: "That there is a twofold traditionary knowledge: the one according to truth, the other according to opinion" <note>original: Διττήν τε εἶναι φιλοσοφίαν, τὴν μὲν κατ᾿ ἀλήθειαv, τὴν δὲ κατὰ δόξαν</note>. (Truth is called *emeth* <note>original: אמת</note> in *Daniel*, in contrast to his enigmatic visions). The other consists of types or parables accommodated to the imagination and taste of the common people.

*St. Jerome*, *Rupertus*, and several others also understand this description of being "written within and on the back side" as referring to a *literal* and *mystical* sense. *Grotius* claims the text is not punctuated correctly, and reads it thus: "written within, and sealed on the back side" <note>original: γεγραμμένον ἔσωθεν, καὶ ὄπισθεν κατεσφραγισμένον</note>, and so on. This implies there were books written on the back side and sealed within. The great *Hugo* <note>Hugo Grotius, a famous 17th-century legal and theological scholar</note> is such an unfortunate interpreter of the *Apocalypse* even in these lesser matters. But to return to the subject at hand.

8. The difference between those two kinds of *ellipses* we have described may be seen in these examples: In *Exodus 3*, where *Moses* asks God His name, He returns this answer: *I am that I am*. This is an elliptical speech, which when fully supplied is: *My name is I am that I am*. Something like this is also in the *Apocalypse*: <margin>Chapter 1:4</margin> *Grace to you and peace* "from him who is, and who was, and who is to come" <note>original: ἀπὸ τοῦ ὁ ὤν, καὶ ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος</note>, which would be more full as "from the one named 'He who is, and who was, and who is to come'" <note>original: ἀπὸ τοῦ ὀνομαζομένου ὁ ὤν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος</note>. But these *ellipses* are such that they reveal the defect of what is to be supplied.

But sometimes it is not so, as in *Revelation 17:8*: *The Beast which you saw, was, and is not, and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition*. And a little after: *When they beheld the Beast that was, and is not, and yet is*. This seems like a smooth, entire sense in the exterior shell <note>original: cortex</note> of the prophecy, whereas no good sense at all can be made of it unless one conceives some such *ellipsis* as before: "The beast which you saw is named 'was and is not'" <note>original: Τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες ὀνομάζεται ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν</note>, and, "beholding the beast which is named 'was and is not,' though he is" <note>original: βλέποντες τὸ θηρίον ὅ,τι ὀνομάζεται ἦν & οὐκ ἔστι καίπερ ἔστι</note>. But to have been this explicit would have laid this mystery too open, which ought to be largely concealed, and there-

<meta>This page continues the definitions of "prophetic schemes"—symbolic techniques used in the Bible to convey hidden meanings. It follows a discussion on "Ellipsis," where certain details are omitted to create a specific effect.</meta>

[there]fore it was thus carefully locked up in this prophetic *ellipsis* <note>original: ellipsis; the omission of words needed to complete a grammatical construction but which are understood from context</note>. We will discuss this text more fully in its proper place.

9. *Homonymia* <note>original: Homonymia; the quality of having the same name or symbol for different things</note> is the variety of meanings in one and the same symbol, where only one is intended to be understood; otherwise, it would be identical to an *Henopœia* <note>a previously defined term referring to the fusion of multiple things into one symbol</note> of the second kind. This *Homonymia* may occur by accident <note>original: ex accidenti</note>—and is no more difficult than the ordinary double meanings of words, where the context determines the sense—or it may be intended on purpose to create a more graceful engraving upon the external shell <note>original: cortex; the outward "skin" or literal story of a vision</note> of a **vision**. 

For example, in the **Vision of the Witnesses** <note>see Revelation 11</note>, I suspect that the *three and a half days* they lie dead in the street do not signify *three and a half years* (as they do at the beginning of that vision), but rather *three and a half times*, which is 1,260 years. Indeed, I confess I more than suspect this; I am well assured in my own judgment of its truth. However, whether there is any likelihood of them *also* signifying *three and a half years* will be better determined by future events. If they did mean both, it would not be a simple *Homonymia* in this symbol of *three and a half days*, but an *Henopœia* of the second kind.

10. *Metalepsis* <note>original: Metalepsis; a figure of speech where an effect is attributed to a person or thing that is merely present at the time, rather than the cause</note> is a prophetic scheme where an effect or event is transferred or attributed to some prominent **person** merely, or at least mainly, because the place and time coincide with theirs; the same logic applies to **things**. I must admit this scheme is very poetic, but it is neither inelegant nor unusual. It is similar to these lines by *Virgil*:

->*The white Bull opens the year with his golden horns*<- <note>original: Candidus auratis aperit cum cornibus annum Taurus</note>
->*— — — — — — — and again,*<-
->*When Libra has made the hours of day and sleep equal.*<- <note>original: Libra dies somnique pares ubi fecerat horas</note>

In these examples, because the constellations *Taurus* and *Libra* are in conjunction with the **Sun** at those times, those effects (the start of spring or the equinox) are attributed to them, even though they are really the **Sun's** work alone and not theirs.

<margin>* Revelation 6:4.</margin>
That such a *Metalepsis* exists in the prophetic style is proven by the example of the **Rider of the Red Horse** in the *Apocalypse* <note>the Book of Revelation</note>. He is armed with a **great sword** in his hand and is said to **take peace from the Earth**. In reality, nothing else is signified except that during this emperor’s reign there would be furious killing and slaughter in the Empire, though through no fault of his own. For the text says *they should kill one another*, as if it deliberately provided that key to unlock the meaning of the vision, as Mr. *Mede* <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential English scholar known for his "Key to the Revelation"</note> has judiciously observed. His interpretation of the **first six seals** is so solid that I think it is impossible for any unbiased reader, taking everything into account, not to be convinced of their truth. This is why I am so confident in this prophetic figure I have described.

11. *Antichronismus* is an obscuring scheme in prophecy which substitutes one measure of time for another: such as a **week** for **seven years** (as in *Daniel*), a **month** for **thirty years**, or a **day** for a **year**. This figure seems to be used in the Apocalyptic visions not only for the sake of concealment, but for proportion and appropriateness <note>original: Decorum</note>, so that the external shell <note>original: cortex</note> of the prophecies does not lack <term>τὸ πιθανὸν</term> <note>original: to pithanon; the quality of being probable or having narrative credibility</note>—that winning and pleasing believability of a story.

<summary>This page defines three technical "prophetic schemes"—Homonymia, Metalepsis, and Antichronismus—used in biblical prophecy to hide deeper meanings behind a plausible narrative surface. The author uses examples from Virgil and the Book of Revelation to explain how symbols, timing, and chronological scales are manipulated by the biblical authors.</summary>
<keywords>Homonymia, Metalepsis, Antichronismus, Joseph Mede, Book of Revelation, Virgil, prophetic time, symbolism, Four Horsemen, Daniel</keywords>

--- Page 265 ---
Therefore these *Antichronisms* <note>original: Antichronismi; a prophetic device where time is distorted or compressed to fit the scale of the symbol</note> are a necessary result of that prophetic *Henopoeia* <note>the symbolic fusion of many things into one entity</note> that shrinks vast empires and other political bodies—along with their long histories—into the shape of beasts or single individuals. To ensure the length of their lives doesn't seem unrealistic for their form, it was necessary to disguise their duration by using "days" to stand for "years." Their lives could be shortened by many accidents; but to say a beast, a woman, or two witnesses lived for 1,260 years would not maintain the *plausibility of the narrative* <note>original: λόγου πιθανόν (logou pithanon)</note>, but would look like an unbelievable story.

12. It would also be unbelievable for the *dead bodies of the two witnesses to lie unburied in the open streets of the city for three and a half years*; they would begin to stink within *four days*, as was noted regarding the body of *Lazarus*. How awkward would it have been to represent the witnesses' bodies lying dead in the streets for 1,260 years straight? Therefore, even though their lying slain and unburied was the most accurate and vivid representation of the condition of those symbolized by the *two witnesses* for 1,260 years, the laws of *appropriateness* <note>original: τὸ πρέπον (to prepon)</note> and *plausibility* <note>original: τὸ πιθανόν (to pithanon)</note> in storytelling had to be followed.

It was requisite that these 1,260 years should be disguised under the symbol of *three and a half days*. This signifies the same thing as "three and a half times"—since the Hebrew words for "days" <note>original: ימים (yamim)</note> and "years" <note>original: שנים (shanim)</note> are used interchangeably—and these "three and a half times" signify 1,260 years. In this way, both the truth intended by the prophecy is faithfully delivered, and the artistic beauty of the prophecy’s literal surface <note>original: cortex; the outward "shell" or literal layer of the vision</note> is carefully maintained. This is achieved not only by shrinking the time, but also by attaching it to the end of the 1,260 days through a *continuation of the literal story* <note>original: Lemmatosynechia; Latin: Corticis Continuatio</note>.

And this prophetic figure, which I call *Antichronism* <note>original: Antichronismus</note>, is not just my own guess but a solid truth. I have already proven it in my book, *The Mystery of Godliness*, and I will further prove it with mathematical certainty in my combined explanation of the 17th and 13th chapters of the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: Apocalyps</note>.

13. *Icismus* <note>a prophetic scheme where symbols resemble the things they represent</note> is the device that plays by far the largest part in all the visions of *Daniel* and *Saint John*. It is simply the representation of things and events through symbols that look like the things they stand for. Because there are many such symbols, the skill of interpreting prophecy becomes more difficult. However, it is not at all impossible, though some overly refined thinkers like to imagine it is. They pretend to feel horror and fear at the strange mention of various beasts and the clashing of their horns. Yet, if they would set aside their pickiness, they would understand that these prophetic hieroglyphics could become familiar to them much more easily than the knowledge of *heraldry* or *blazonry* <note>the study of coats of arms and family symbols</note>, which is not such a deep or impossible subject to master.

<meta>catchword: CHAP.</meta>

The author argues that interpreting these symbols is a systematic skill, comparable to learning heraldry.</summary>

# CHAPTER V.

1. *The great usefulness of an alphabet of prophetic <term>iconisms</term> <note>symbolic images or figures</note>.*
2. *The best way of reaching the correct sense of them.* 3. *What weight the <term>onirocritics</term> <note>interpreters of dreams</note> of the ancients may contribute toward determining their meaning.* 4. *That the same reasoning applies to the signification and interpretation of dreams as it does to visions, provided they are purely symbolic and not <term>complexional</term> <note>arising from the physical state or "humors" of the dreamer's body</note>.* 5. *Angels: their ministry in all affairs of Providence is a noted premise in the ancient <term>Cabbala</term> <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note> and in the Book of Revelation.* 6. *Ascension into Heaven.* 7. *The Air as the special region of devils.* 8. *Balances.* 9. *Beast; <term>Wild Beasts</term> <note>original: Θηρία (Theria)</note> representing idolatrous kingdoms.* 10. *The reason why a Lamb signifies a single person, and why wild beasts signify idolatry as well as cruelty.* 11. *Blasphemy: proof that it signifies idolatry, based on reason, the use of Scripture, and the authority of interpreters.* 12. *Blood.* 13. *Bow and Arrows; Buildings; Burial.*

<margin>In his *On Divination in Sleep* <note>original: Περὶ τῆς καθ' ὕπνον Μαντικῆς</note>, chapter 2.</margin>
1. We have shown where the obscurity of prophecy mainly lies, and by the explanation of the previous figures, we have already done something toward making the skill of interpreting easy for us. However, because there are so many and such various examples of the latter type of prophecy, we believe it is necessary to bring the most significant of them into one *alphabet* and to set down their meanings. Taking notice of these will greatly help in easily deciphering the true meaning of all enigmatic prophecies in Scripture. For what *Aristotle* says of enigmatic *dreams* is also true of these types of *visions*: "He is the most skillful interpreter of dreams who is best at discerning similarities and resemblances; for as for dreams that are straightforward, anyone can judge them." <note>original Greek: Τεχνικώτατός ἐστι κριτὴς ἐνυπνίων ὅστις δύναται τὰς ὁμοιότητας θεωρεῖν, τὰς γὰρ εὐθυονειρίας κρίνειν παντός ἐστι.</note>

Now, the *visions* of *Daniel* and the *Revelation* are not of the nature of *straightforward dreams* <note>original: Εὐθυονειρίαι (Euthyoneiriai)</note>, but are *enigmatic dreams* <note>original: Ἐνύπνια αἰνιγματώδη (Enypnia ainigmatōdē)</note>, representing things through symbols or similarities. Therefore, having a settled and determinate meaning (established upon solid and rational grounds) for such symbols and *iconisms* will necessarily contribute much to enabling us to interpret these prophecies with ease and success, or to help us understand and approve—or with judgment disapprove—the interpretations of others.

2. For my own part, I know of no more solid method for settling and securing the true sense of these *symbols* than by attending to what the Scripture itself declares about them, and by strictly observing what reason will naturally suggest or discover concerning how well they represent things. To this, we may add the support of those who have written as *onirocritics* (interpreters of dreams), whether they wrote mostly from their own reason and observation, as *Artemidorus* claims, or (which is more to our purpose) have made a collection of the most ancient writings of that kind, such as *Achmetes* the son of *Seirim* has provided for us; it can- <note>The text continues on the next page with "not..."</note>

# CHAPTER V. Of Certain Prophetic Schemes.

...can only strengthen our assurance of the meaning of such *symbolic images* <note>original: "Iconisms"</note>.

3. And these works of Achmetes especially, as they are the *dream-interpretations* <note>original: "Onirocritics"</note> of three famous interpreters for the Kings of India, Persia, and Egypt; and therefore, being so ancient and so Eastern, they are more likely to have a greater connection with the prophetic schemes of Holy Scripture. The first of these is Syrbacham, interpreter to the King of India; but he "Christianizes" so frequently and so obviously that his antiquity may be highly suspected, and must necessarily be concluded to date after the coming of Christ. The second is Baram, interpreter to Saanisan, King of Persia; and the last is Tarphan, interpreter to Pharaoh, King of Egypt. The use of their interpretations is approved even by expositors of quite different viewpoints—I mean Hugo Grotius and Mr. Joseph Mede, who has the honor of being the first to break the ice in this business.

4. Nor should there be any hesitation because these are the interpretations of *dreams* and not of *visions*. For besides the fact that there is a great affinity between *visions* and *dreams*—both being phantoms impressed on the imagination, not by any free act or excitation of ourselves, but in a merely passive way, with the external senses being essentially dulled in both (which is why these *dreams* <note>original: ὀνείρατα (oneirata)</note> are also called *spectacles* <note>original: θεάματα (theamata)</note> in Achmetes)—the question is not about the source from which they come or the manner in which these divinatory impressions arrive, but rather what they represent or signify. If it is granted that they prefigure such things rightly and naturally in *dreams*, it is manifest that they will do the same in *visions*. For I am speaking of such impressions that do not arise from the *effects* of a person's physical temperament <note>original: "Complexion"</note> or any other natural cause, but act as a mere type or prefiguration.

Therefore, it will not be irrelevant to occasionally add the support of these *writers on dreams* to the evidence we produce from Scripture and reason for interpreting such *symbols* or *images* as we shall include in our *Prophetic Alphabet*, which I shall now present.

5. **Angels.** There is such frequent mention of the ministry of *Angels* in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, and their presidency is so clearly assigned to everything there, that I cannot omit taking notice of this scheme among the rest. This is true even though perhaps it does not fall strictly under the notion of an *image* <note>original: "Icasmus"</note>, as they are the instruments of Divine Providence rather than its emblem. But if we reflect upon their common representation (which doubtlessly took its ground from the *Mosaic Cherubim*), and how well they are equipped with wings for the quicker dispatch of those services expected of them, they are not insignificant of that *Wisdom* that is *said* 
<margin>* Wisdom 8.</margin>
to be more quick and moving than any motion, and to reach from one end to another mightily and sweetly to order all things.

But the fact that *Angels* are in these *Apocalyptic visions* so constantly and particularly set over every negotiation of Divine Providence is exceedingly consistent with the sense of the Book of *Daniel*. For instance, that great change in *Nebuchadnezzar's* condition is said to come to pass by the decree of the *Watchers* (in Hebrew: *irin* <note>original: עירין</note>; the Greeks would say *guards* <note>original: φύλακες (phylakes)</note>, and the Latins *sentinels* or *watchers* <note>original: "Excubitores or Vigiles"</note>, by which are understood *Angels*). This is also consistent with the sense of the ancient *Cabala* <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note>.

...Kabbalah, which makes the number *seven* a symbol of the *Sabbath rest* <note>original: Sabbatism</note> of God (in which He rests from His works), and calls that number "the guard" <note>original: φυλακίτις (phylakitis)</note> in relation to the work of these "Sentinels" or "Watchmen" <note>original: Excubitores or Vigiles</note>—those holy *Angels* whom God employs in the administration of His Providence.

6. *Ascension into Heaven*. Since a Kingdom or political system is so clearly compared to the *World* or *Universe* (as we shall see under that title), it is an easy analogy to compare the *Heavens* to its high places and honors <margin>* Chapter 14:12.</margin>. This is the meaning of the passage in **Isaiah**: *How you are fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!* For you have said in your heart, *I will ascend into heaven*, etc. "You had aspired to the highest dignity," <note>original: Aspiraveras ad summam dignitatem</note> as the scholar François Vatable notes. And Achmet writes in his *Interpretation of Dreams* <note>original: Onirocritics</note>, chapter 161: "If someone sees that he sits as if in heaven, he shall be famous and great." <note>original: Εἰ δ' ἴδῃ τις ὅτι κάθηται ὡς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὀνομαστὸς ἔσται καὶ μέγας</note> And in the following chapter: "If the King sees that he flew up into heaven, he shall find a status and a name greater than other kings." <note>original: Εἰ δ' ἴδῃ ὁ βασιλεὺς ὅτι ἀνήπτατο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, εὑρήσει ὕψος καὶ ὄνομα πλέον τῶν ἄλλων βασιλέων</note> And a little after: "If the King sees that, having ascended, he sat in heaven, he shall take control of a greater country than he currently possesses." <note>original: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ ὁ βασιλεὺς ὅτι ἀνελθὼν ἐκάθισεν ἐν οὐρανῷ, μείζονα χώραν ἧς ἔχει κατακυριεύσει</note> Thus Achmet writes based on the records of the *Indians*, *Persians*, and *Egyptians*. All of this clearly shows that *Ascending into Heaven* signifies the gaining or increasing of political ranks and honors.

7. *Air*. That the *Air* is considered the place of the Devil’s empire appears from *Ephesians* 2: *And you, who were dead in trespasses and sins, in which in times past you walked according to the course of this world, according to the Prince of the power of the Air, the spirit that now works in the children of Unbelief*; that is to say, in infidels who have not submitted themselves to the Kingdom of God, but serve idols and follow the desires of their own minds. Regarding this passage, the scholar Johannes Drusius notes (quoting the *New Offering* <note>original: מנחה חדשה (Minchah Chadashah), a Hebrew commentary</note>): "It should be known that from the earth up to the Expanse [the sky], everything is full of spiritual troops and officers." <note>original: Sciendum à terra usque ad Expansum omnia plena esse turmis ac præfectis</note> Following this opinion of the Hebrew Rabbis, the Apostle speaks again in Chapter 6: *For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against Principalities, against the world-rulers of this darkness* <note>original: πρὸς τοὺς κοσμοκράτορας τοῦ σκότους τούτου</note>, against those who hold onto the rule of this lower world, this dark, misty air; *against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places*. <note>original: πρὸς τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις</note> For "heaven" here means the same thing as the "Expanse" does in the *New Offering*—the space from the clouds downward, as it is defined in *Genesis* 1. Otherwise, how could these wicked spirits be said to be "cast down to hell in chains of darkness" <note>original: σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρωθῆναι</note> and "kept in eternal bonds under darkness" <note>original: δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τηρηθῆναι</note>, as both *Peter* and *Jude* declare?

But enough of this, especially since when *Air* appears in prophetic visions with the meaning we have discussed, it is usually a simple metonymy <note>term: metonymy; a figure of speech in which a concept is referred to by the name of something closely associated with it (like "the Crown" for a King)</note> rather than a symbolic image <note>original: Icasmus</note>.

8. *Balance*. It is easy for anyone to understand that a *Balance* (a scale) signifies *Justice*, as it is a primary tool for "commutative justice" <note>term: commutative justice; fairness in exchange and mutual dealings between people</note>. It is a perfect symbol for exactly weighing out and sharing all things—or rather, for dispensing all things accurately. Achmet notes, from the *Indian Dream-Interpreters* <note>original: Onirocritics</note>, chapter 15: "If anyone sees in a dream a balance being weighed in some place, let him understand this to represent a judge." <note>original: Ἐάν τις ἴδῃ κατ' ὄναρ ζυγὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ σταθμιζόμενον, τοῦτο εἰς πρόσωπον νοεῖτω κριτοῦ</note> I will not bother to copy how he compares the "scales" <note>original: πλάστιγγες (plastigges)</note> to the ears of the Judge, and the "weights" in those scales to the arguments presented by both sides, which the judge must weigh with an impartial hearing.

### Chapter 5. Of Prophetic Symbols <term>original: Iconisms</term>.

...hearing. And again in the same chapter, "If he sees the balance level <note>original: δεξιὸν (dexion) — right-handed or favorable</note> and clean, let him understand that the judge of that place is just." <note>original: Ἐὰν τὸ ζύγον ἴδῃ δεξιὸν καὶ καθαρὸν, νοείτω ὅτι ὁ κριτὴς τοῦ τόπου δίκαιός ἐστιν</note> He more particularly discusses the condition of the *Scales* and the *Beam*; but there is enough here already to show how recognized an emblem a *Balance* is for *Justice*. He also suggests the same regarding "the measures" <note>original: τὰ μέσια (ta mesia)</note>.

9. *Beast*. Saint Paul describes at length in 1 Corinthians 12 what a plain resemblance there is between a *Body Politic* <term>a people organized under a single government</term> and a *living creature*. It is easy to conceive that just as a living creature has distinctly framed parts ordered in relation to one another—so that they are all moved for the good of the whole by the power residing in the brain through the spirits spreading throughout—so it is in a *Polity*. There, several orders and ranks of men are held together by one common law (which is like the life and spirit of the Body Politic) and are moved and directed for the common good by the command and appointment of the Sovereign Power, which is the "Head" of this kingdom or polity. 

Therefore, it is no wonder that men or nations framed into a Body Politic, called a kingdom, are represented in the Book of *Daniel* under the resemblance of *living creatures* <note>original Hebrew: חיון (Chayun) or חיות (Chayot)</note>. These are rightly translated by the Septuagint <term>the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</term> as "wild beasts" <note>original Greek: θηρία (theria); Latin: Feræ</note>, as they are the kind that appear in those visions. Regarding this, the scholar Grotius notes on Daniel 7 (where there is mention of four great beasts ascending out of the sea): "They are called beasts because those empires were idolatrous, as Facchiades <note>a Jewish commentator</note> notes here." <note>original: Ideo Bestiæ, saith he, quia Idololatrica erant Imperia, ut notat hîc Facchiades</note> 

But they are called beasts not only for their idolatry, but also for their bloody *tyranny*, as Grotius has noted excellently well on Matthew 20. There, Christ declares that whoever would be greatest and first in his kingdom must be the minister and servant of the rest, and not "lord it" or "exercise authority" <note>original Greek: κατακυριεύειν (katakyrieuein) or κατεξουσιάζειν (katexousiazein)</note>—that is, not swagger over their inferiors as the *rulers of the Gentiles* do. Grotius says, "This opposition shows why in the Prophets the empires of the world are depicted as beasts, while the Kingdom of Christ is depicted by the image of a man." <note>original: Hæc oppositio, saith he, ostendit cur apud Prophetas Imperia mundi, Bestiarum; Regnum Christi, Hominis imagine, depingantur</note> 

By *Beasts* here, we are to understand *wild beasts*, as the word usually signifies. In that sense, it exactly matches the *Seventy's* <term>the Septuagint translators'</term> Greek word *theria* (from which the Latin word *Ferae*, which always signifies wild beasts, is derived by turning the Greek letter 'theta' into 'phi' according to the Aeolic dialect). Otherwise, the kingdoms of the world might simply be called "living beings" <note>original Greek: Ζῶα (Zoa)</note>, as the four beasts in the *Apocalypse* <term>the Book of Revelation</term> are called. As the scholar Joseph Mede has rightly observed, those four beings allude to the *Camp of Israel* distributed into four quarters. They are called "living beings" and not "wild beasts" <note>original: θηρία (theria)</note>, as that would be a very unfit title for any polity where *humanity* and *equity* hold sway.

10. But such a title would be even less fit for the true body of *Christ*, and least of all for the *Lamb* himself. Nor would the *Lamb* be a fit prophetic representative of one single person, except that Christ had already received that title, being called by John "The Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world," as he is indeed that *Paschal Lamb* whose blood is the *salvation* of his people. 

Therefore, unless there is a unique exception like this <note>original: Instantia Monodica</note>, it is most assuredly true that an *animal* or *beast* in the *prophetic* style signifies not one single man, but a *company*, *polity*, or *kingdom*. For how can they be said to have *horns* and *heads*, and those horns and heads be expressly interpreted by an *angel* from *heaven* as *kings*, if the beasts as a whole did not signify kingdoms rather than single persons?

<margin>Book 2. chapter 10.</margin>
But why these wild *Beasts* should imply *Idolatry* as well as *Cruelty* in their symbolic representation <term>original: Type</term>, the reason lies a little deeper, but it is not impossible to understand. I believe it is this: because idolatrous worship is situated within the borders of the mere *Bestial* or *Animal nature*, as may appear from what I have written in my *Mystery of Godliness*, to which, for the sake of brevity, I refer the reader.

11. *Blasphemy*. *Blasphemy* used to represent Idolatry is also a symbolic likeness <term>original: Icasmus</term>, and the analogy is clear enough. For what reproachful words are to God through the *Ears*, the worshipping of *Images* or *any Creature with religious worship* is to the *Eyes*. In either way, that which is a disgrace and a belittling of God is declared. Therefore, it is no wonder that the prophetic style—which favors a skillful concealment—substitutes one kind of *Blasphemy* for another: specifically, that blasphemy which is "through words or speech" for that which is "through actions or symbols," as *Chrysostom* <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407 AD), an influential Archbishop of Constantinople known for his preaching.</note> distinguishes regarding Divine predictions. <note>original Greek: διὰ λόγων ἢ ῥημάτων... διὰ πραγμάτων ἢ τύπων (dia logon e rhematon... dia pragmaton e typon)</note>

But it is noteworthy that the Scripture also in several places terms *Idolatry* as *Blasphemy*. As in *Isaiah*: <margin>Chapter 65:7.</margin> "I will recompense into their bosoms your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the Lord, who have burnt incense upon the mountains, and blasphemed me upon the hills." This was certainly not done through words, but through actions—by their acts of Idolatry. "Those who worship Idols as if they were Gods reproach God for the arrogance of [attributing] Divinity [to others]," says *A Lapide* <note>Cornelius à Lapide (1567–1637), a Jesuit exegete known for his massive biblical commentaries.</note>. <note>original Latin: "Qui colunt Idola quasi Deos, exprobrant Deo arrogantiam Divinitatis"</note> <margin>Chapter 20:27, 28.</margin> A similarly clear passage is in *Ezekiel*: "Thus says the Lord God, Yet in this your fathers have blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me: namely, when I brought them into the Land for the which I lifted up my hand to give it to them, then they saw every high hill and all the thick trees, and they offered there their sacrifices, and thereby presented the provocation of their offering, etc." The same interpreter again explains this as their idolatries, as does *Gaspar Sanctius*. <margin>Verse 31.</margin> Again, *Deuteronomy* 31: "When they shall have eaten and filled themselves and grown fat, then will they turn to other Gods and serve them, and provoke me." So our Translation says, but the Hebrew has it *naatzuni*, which properly means, "they will blaspheme me." <note>original Hebrew: נאצוני</note> This is also how it is translated by the "Seventy" <term>the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</term> in *Isaiah* 52:5: "continually my name is blasphemed." <note>original Hebrew: כל-היום שמי מנאץ (kol-hayom shemi menaatz); Greek: διὰ παντὸς ὄνομά με βλασφημεῖται (dia pantos onoma me blasphemeitai)</note> Likewise, the word *naatzah* is rendered in *Ezekiel* 35:12 as, "I have heard the voice of your blasphemies." <note>original Greek: ᬕκουσα τῆς φωνῆς τῶν βλασφημιῶν σου (Ekousa tes phones ton blasphemion sou)</note> The word in the original Hebrew is *naatzot*. <note>original Hebrew: נאצות</note>

Lastly, it is also observable that in *Psalm* 69:9, where the Prophet *David* says, "The reproaches of those who reproached you" <note>original Greek: οἱ ὀνειδισμοὶ τῶν ὀνειδιζόντων σε (hoi oneidismoi ton oneidizonton se)</note>—which is the same as if it had been "the blasphemies of those who blasphemed you"—"are fallen upon me." The Chaldee Paraphrast <term>the Aramaic translation/commentary of the Bible</term> interprets this as the reproach God receives by having His worship shared with Idols, even though it is expressed as blasphemy or insults of words (for that is what *oneidismos* signifies). Therefore, seeing that the children of *Israel* are said to "blaspheme" when they stray in their worship of God and turn to Idols, it is very easy to understand, by the rule of related terms, that this Idolatry of theirs may well be called *Blasphemy*.

Accordingly, *Alcazar* <note>Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Jesuit theologian.</note> interprets the *Names of Blasphemy* in the *Apocalypse* <term>the Book of Revelation</term>, which are on the seven heads of the Beast, as the Temples of Idols. And *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch jurist and theologian.</note> paraphrases the phrase "full of names of blasphemy" as "Full of gods, as they were so called." <note>original Greek/Latin: γέμον ὀνομάτων βλασφημίας (gemon onomaton blasphemias); Plena diis qui ità dicebantur</note>

<summary>This page argues that in prophetic language, "wild beasts" represent idolatry due to their animalistic nature, and "blasphemy" is a symbolic term for idol worship, supported by various biblical passages and scholarly interpretations.</summary>

# Chapter 5. On Prophetic Symbols <note>original: "Iconisms"</note>

...were spoken to the injury of the true God <note>original Latin: "dicebantur in veri Dei injuriam"</note>. So easily is it acknowledged on all hands that *Blasphemy* may be substituted for *Idolatry*. And it is the most appropriate and significant <unclear>symbol</unclear> <note>original: "Iconismus"</note> that can be, for nothing expresses the detestable nature of *Idolatry* as well as it does. For *Idolatry* is as absolute a mockery <note>original: "subsannation"</note> and vilification of God as malice could invent; it is as bad as if they should call him by the names of all that base, lifeless matter that they make their images out of, and proclaim him to be no better than it. For by giving divine worship to an image, they make it equal to him. And this *Blasphemy* is proportional in other more worthy objects that are not God: for they are infinitely worthless in comparison to him, and therefore it is an infinite reproach and horrid blasphemy against God to worship anything besides him.

12. *Blood*. That *Blood* is a symbolic representation <note>original: "Hieroglyphick"</note> of *Slaughter*, Providence itself seems to take for granted by sending beforehand the prodigy of "raining blood" before the outbreaks of war and bloodshed—as history reports and all people naturally interpret. And where the Apostle says, *You have not resisted unto blood*, the meaning is *unto death*, whether it is meant mystically or naturally. But even where *Death* is meant mystically, there is mention of *Blood*: as when the Prophet is commanded to denounce one who sins defiantly <note>original: "with an high hand"</note> against the Law of God, saying that he shall surely die (speaking of eternal death); yet, if the Prophet fails to give this warning, it is said that the sinner's *Blood* shall be upon the Prophet. And in chapter 14, verse 19, even *natural death*, where there is no actual spilling of blood, is expressed this way: *or if I send pestilence into the land, and pour out my fury upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast*. Upon which Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch legal scholar and theologian.</note> rightly notes from the Aramaic translation <note>original: "Chaldee Paraphrast"</note>, "To the Hebrews, 'Blood' refers to every kind of premature death" <note>original Latin: "omne mortis immaturae genus Sanguis Hebraeis"</note>. *Blood* therefore signifies *Death*, and "bloody" signifies "dead"; because, as it is written, *the life is in the blood*. Correspondingly, Achmetes <note>An 8th-century author on dream interpretation, often citing Egyptian, Persian, and Indian traditions.</note>—according to the understanding of the Egyptians and Persians—says: "Blood is the power and life of man" <note>original Greek: Τὸ αἷμα δύναμις τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ ζωή ἐστι</note>, where letting out his blood must mean his death. By analogy, destroying the strength of anything, or that power or virtue by which it is what it is, is the "death" of that thing, regardless of whether it is animate or inanimate.

Interpretation of Dreams <note>original: "Onirocrit."</note>, 249.
</margin>
13. *Bow and Arrows*. They naturally signify aiming at something, and *hitting the mark* signifies successfully reaching the goal of our endeavors. But it may more specifically refer to *Victory in war*, especially because they are warlike weapons. Achmetes says, from the dream-interpretation books of the Egyptians and Persians: "If a man dreams he holds a bow and arrows in his hand, he shall victoriously triumph over his enemies" <note>original Greek: 'Ἐὰν ἴδῃ τις ὅτι ἐκράτει βέλη καὶ τόξα, ἐπιχαρήσεται ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐχθροῖς αὐτοῦ'</note>.

*Buildings*. Achmetes, according to the sense of the Indian interpreter: "If one dreams he is in a house of marble or stone, it signifies long life, and riches where thieves cannot break through nor steal" <note>original Greek: 'Εἰ δ' ἀπὸ μαρμάρου ἢ λίθου τὸ κτίσμα, ὁ ἰδὼν ἔσται πολίζωος, καὶ τὸ πλεῖτος αὐτοῦ ἀκαταμάχητον'</note>.

Ecclesiastes 6:3.

According to the first meaning is that passage in *Ecclesiastes*: *If a man begets a hundred children, and lives many years, and his soul is not filled with good, and also that...*

...that he has no burial, I say that a miscarriage <note>original: "untimely birth"</note> is better than he. Otherwise, not being buried may signify only that what the vision portends will not be quite finished; burial being the consummation of all things, even of death itself. Because of this, when Leonas Syrus dreamed that he was dead but not buried, Artemidorus interpreted it to mean that he would be victorious but not crowned. However, Menander of Smyrna, also dreaming that he was buried, was crowned victor at the Olympic Games. Therefore, not to be buried is a bad sign in visions that portend good, but a good sign in those that portend evil. And Achmetes expressly states, according to the sense of the Indian Interpreters: "The lack of burial rites is judged as a hope of salvation" <note>original Greek: "Ἡ στέρησις ἐνταφίων εἰς ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας κρίνεται"</note>. If anything is missing that hinders the interment, it signifies hope of recovery to life.

### CHAPTER 6.

1. **Candle**. 2. **Character**. 3. **Clouds of Heaven**. 4. **Crown of precious Stones**. 5. **Darkness**; **Day**; **Death**. 6. **Desert** <note>original: "Desart"</note>. 7. **Dragon**, a figure of the *Devil* according to the ancient <term>Cabbala</term> <note>Cabbala: A tradition of mystical or secret interpretation of scripture</note>, and then of the chief political powers that oppose the Church. 8. **Drunkenness**. 9. **Eagle**; **Earthquake**. 10. **Eclipses**. 11. **Eye**, a <term>Hieroglyphick</term> <note>Hieroglyphick: A symbolic image used to represent a concept or word</note> of Counsel and Prudence. 12. **Fishing**; **Fish dead in the Sea**. 13. **Fire**, the different significations thereof. 14. **Fire from Heaven**, its exact significance of Excommunication. 15, 16. **Flesh**, two notable significations thereof. 17. **Flood** <note>original: "Floud"</note>; **Fornication**; **Frogs**. 18. **Gems and precious Stones**; **God**.

Astrampsychus and Nicephorus wrote:

-> "To see torches indicates the light of one's affairs." <note>original Greek: "Φωστῆρας εἰδεῖν πραγμάτων δηλοῖ φάος"</note> <-

And Artemidorus, in *book 2, chapter 9*: "A candle seen burning bright in the house is good; for it signifies the acquisition of property and abundance for all" <note>original Greek: "Λύχνος δὲ καιόμενος ἐν οἰκίᾳ λαμπρός, ἀγαθός· πρόσκτησιν γὰρ σημαίνει καὶ εὐπορίαν πᾶσιν"</note>. Lastly, Achmetes, according to the meaning of the Egyptians and Persians, says: "If anyone has lit a torch and carries it: if the dreamer is a king, it is judged to lead to glory, victories, and the destruction of enemies; if he is a commoner, he will find status proportional to the torch" <note>original Greek: "Εἴ τις ἀνῆψε λαμπάδα καὶ φέρει αὐτὴν , εἰ μέν ἐστι βασιλεὺς ὁ ἰδών , εἰς δόξαν καὶ νίκας , καὶ ὄλεθρον ἐχθρῶν κρίνεται· εἰ δὲ κοινὸς , εὑρήσει ἀξίωμα ἀνάλογον τῆς λαμπάδος"</note>. # Chapter VI. of Prophetic Iconisms. <note>iconisms: symbolic figures or representations</note>

them against a man's will, "affliction and distress from a man's enemies in proportion to the darkness" <note>original Greek: θλίψιν ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν ἀναλόγως τῷ σκότει</note>.

2. **Character.** That *servants* and *soldiers* received *marks* upon their foreheads and hands, by which it might be known to whom they belong, is a piece of indisputable antiquity, as there is sufficient testimony of this in various authors. See what is collected <note>original: "congested"</note> by Mr. Mede and Grotius regarding Revelation 13 <note>original: Apocal. 13</note>. But in the prophetic style, it does not imply that there is any visible mark in the hand or on the head of those who are said to be marked. Rather, it only signifies that there is an open profession of belonging to the one whose mark they are said to receive. For these are only *types* of ownership <note>original: "Propriety"</note>, and are no more to be conceived as being really imprinted upon those said to bear them than those whole kingdoms of men, called *Beasts* in the prophetic style, are to be imagined as being metamorphosed into *bears* or *leopards*. For all these are typical attributes, not real physical ones.

3. **Clouds of Heaven.** In the language of Scripture, they seem to signify *power and great glory*. Achmetes, in Chapter 194, says: "If the king sees that he sits on clouds being carried wherever he wishes, he shall rule over his enemies and find victories and joys unexpectedly" <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ ὁ βασιλεὺς ὅτι κάθηται ἐν νεφέλαις ἀγόμενος ἔνθα θέλει, ἐχθρῶν δεσπόσει, καὶ εὑρήσει νίκας καὶ χαρὰς ἀπροσδοκήτως</note>, according to the thinking of the *Persians* and *Egyptians*. And in Chapter 162, according to the *Egyptians, Persians*, and *Indians*: "If the king sees that he has flown up as if to heaven where the stars are, he shall find height and a name greater than other kings" <note>original Greek: Ἐι δ᾽ ἴδῃ ὁ βασιλεύς ὅτι ἀνήπτατο ὡς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἔνθα οἱ ἀστέρες, εὑρήσει ὕψος καὶ ὄνομα πλέον τῶν ἄλλων βασιλέων</note>. And again in the same chapter: "If he sees that, having gone up, he sat in heaven, he shall conquer a greater country than he already possesses" <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ ὅτι ἀνελθὼν ἐκάθησεν ἐν οὐρανῷ, μείζονα χώραν ἧς ἔχει κατακυριεύσει</note>. The sense of all this is that riding upon the *clouds* and *ascending into heaven* signifies honorable prosperity, success against one's enemies, and the enlargement of power and dignity.

4. **Crown of Gems and precious Stones.** Achmetes, drawing from the dream interpreters <note>original: "Onirocriticks"</note> of the *Indians*, Chapter 247, writes: "If he sees that a crown of precious stones and pearls was placed on his head, in proportion to the ornament and beauty of the crown, whoever he may be, he shall find wealth, height, and glory" <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ ὅτι ἐτέθη ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ αὐτοῦ στέφανος ἐκ τιμίων λίθων καὶ μαργαριτῶν, ἀναλόγως τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ τῷ κάλλει τοῦ στεφάνου, ὅστις ἂν εἴη, εὑρήσει πλοῦτον καὶ ὕψος καὶ δόξαν</note>. In this case, the force of the interpretation relies most upon the *gems* or *precious stones*, as they are the emblems of riches, status, and honor. They also have a more mystical meaning in this very chapter, signifying "the brightness of divine doctrine or truth" <note>original Greek: τῶν δογμάτων τῶν θείων λαμπρότητα</note>. But in Chapter 248, they are only interpreted as worldly things according to the mind of the *Egyptians* and *Persians*:

> "If another sees these things, namely pearls and precious stones, and that he has obtained an abundance of them, he shall find proportionable riches and honor" <note>original Greek: Ἄλλῳ ἐὰν ἴδῃ ταῦτα, viz. Pearls and precious Stones, ὅτι εὐπόρησε... εὑρήσει πλοῦτον ἀνάλογον καὶ δόξαν</note>.

5. **Darkness.** See *Candle* and *Eye*.
**Day.** See *Time*.
**Death.** *Death* is a dissolution of body and soul, and therefore properly belongs only to a natural animal. However, by analogy, it may be transferred to all "bodies politic" <note>bodies politic: organized political groups, such as nations or states</note>, which the prophetic style represents under the figure of animals or single persons—whether by the simple name of *man* or *woman*, or by specific roles such as *whore* or *wife*.

It also introduces the concept of "death" as a metaphor for the dissolution of political entities.</summary>

# A Concise Alphabet Book I.

witness, or the like. Now, just as life and spirit are to a natural animal, so are rule and power to figurative persons or animals in the prophetic sense, which are political bodies. Therefore, just as the loss of the former is the death of the one, so the loss of the latter is the death of the other. And because there is a spirit in all things, even in those things that are inanimate, the fading or vanishing of that spirit may be said by analogy to be the *Death* of those things. Instances of this are innumerable. I will only add that, just as in the Hebrew idiom "not to be" is "to be dead," so in analogy, anything that is not what it was—namely, anything that is changed from its former condition—this change may be considered a kind of *Death*, as *Death* is ordinarily said to be a "Change."

6. *Desert.* That *Desert* refers to Paganism is something *Alcazar* <note>Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Spanish Jesuit theologian who interpreted the Book of Revelation</note> pronounces with great confidence when speaking of the Woman in the wilderness: "In which phrasing it should be noted that the 'Desert' undoubtedly symbolizes 'Paganism'" <note>original Latin: *In qua locutione notandum est per Desertum proculdubio figurari Gentilitatem*</note>. For this opinion, he produces a cloud of witnesses, including Clement of Alexandria, Origen, Ambrose, Basil, Jerome, Gregory, Hilary, Hesychius, etc. The reason for this symbolic representation <note>original: "Hieroglyphick"</note>, I believe, is this: the idolatry of the Pagans took place much in woods and groves, and on the tops of mountains and waste places. Furthermore, the Hebrew names of their demons, *Shedim* <note>original Hebrew: שדים; often translated as "devils" or "destroyers"</note> and *Se'irim* <note>original Hebrew: שערים; meaning "hairy ones," often referring to goat-demons or satyrs</note>, refer to the *fields* and *deserts*. Besides this, idolaters do not rise above the level of mere animal life, and their worship and devotion is little higher than that of the *Elephant* or the *monkey* <note>original: "Cercopithecus," a genus of long-tailed African monkeys</note>. The greed and bloody cruelty of the Pagan kingdoms further fulfill the suitability of this type. Consequently, wherever such a condition of things exists as this typifies—that is to say, whatever kingdoms or empires practice paganism—they *by that very fact* <note>original: "ipſo facto"</note> become a *Wilderness* or *Desert*.

7. *Dragon.* The Hebrew word is *Tannin* <note>original Hebrew: תנין</note> and signifies *Dragon* or *Serpent*, and also *Sea monster* <note>original: "Cetus"</note>, being the great serpent or dragon of the sea. Accordingly, the Seventy <note>The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> render "the great whales" in Genesis 1 as "the great sea-monsters" <note>original Greek: τὰ κήτη τὰ μεγάλα</note>. The ancient tradition <note>original: "Cabbala"</note> of Moses assures us that it is a figure of the *Devil*. It may be that, although one is noted chiefly, the *Serpent* there may have a prophetic singular representation <note>original term: "Henopœia"; a rhetorical device where a group or a continuous entity is represented by a single individual or figure</note> within it, signifying the entire principality of Satan—that Kingdom of Darkness which has been forever in opposition to the Kingdom of God. Therefore, it is no wonder that those kingdoms which have afflicted the Church in such a special manner have been represented under this figure, such as *Egypt* and the *Roman Empire*.

<margin>Isaiah 51.</margin>
<margin>Chapter 29.</margin>
> *Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the Lord; awake as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Are you not the one who cut* Rahab <note>that is, Egypt; see the commentary by Forerius</note> *and wounded the Dragon?* This refers to *Pharaoh*, as *Ezekiel* plainly speaks: *I am against you, Pharaoh King of Egypt, the great Dragon that lies in the midst of the rivers.* And because he lies thus in the rivers, he is called *Leviathan*, as if he were a *water-serpent* or a *whale*. *Psalm 74: You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces and gave him to be food for the people in the Wilderness.* "Heads of the Leviathan" <note>original Hebrew: ראשי לויתן</note>; *as if this Leviathan, like the Dragon in the Apocalypse, had more heads than one.*

# Chapter 6: Of Prophetic Imagery <note>original: "Prophetick Iconisms"</note>

These considerations clearly suggest to us that the *Seven-headed Serpent* in the *Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note>, which is the *Roman State* or *Kingdom*, is represented this way not only because of that old *Serpentine* form that tempted our first parents, but also as a reflection of that tyrannical Kingdom of *Egypt* which is symbolized by the image of a *Dragon* and *Leviathan*. This type refers not only to *Pagan Rome*, but to *Pagano-Christian Rome* as well. For all *seven heads* belong to the body of the *Dragon*; and the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is*, is just as much the *Dragon* as it is not the *Dragon*. Therefore, it is as much *Egypt* (and I wish I could not say more) as it is the Church of God or the Kingdom of his Son *Jesus*.

8. *Drunkenness*. This is sometimes taken to mean being so filled and intoxicated with the pleasures and riches of this world that one becomes regardless and senseless of the things of God. *Isaiah 29:*
> Stop yourselves and wonder; cry out and cry: They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink. For the Lord has poured upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes; the prophets and the rulers, the seers has he covered.
Such a negligent stupor and drunkenness is often cast upon men by the prosperity of this world. *Achmetes*, in his *Indian Interpretations, chapter 3*, says: "If anyone dreams he is drunk with wine, he will find riches and power proportional to his drunkenness." <note>original Greek: Ἐάν τις ἴδῃ ὅτι ἐμεθύσθη οἴνῳ, εὑρήσει πλοῦτον ϗ ἐξουσίαν ἀνάλογον τῇ μέθῃ.</note> He affirms the same thing in the following chapter according to the traditions of the *Egyptians* and *Persians*. There is also a *Drunkenness* from the *Cup of Affliction*, which is often mentioned in the Scriptures.

9. *Eagle. Isaiah 40:31.*
> But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not be faint.
And *Exodus 19:4.*
> You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to myself.
*Artemidorus, book 2, chapter 20:* "For poor men to dream they ride upon an eagle is good; for it signifies they will be supported and greatly helped by wealthy people." <note>original Greek: Ὀχεῖσθαι ἀετῷ, πένησι μὲν ἀγαθόν· ἀναληφθέντες γὰρ ὑπό τινων πλουσίων ὠφεληθήσονται οὐ μικρά.</note>

10. *Earthquake*. We usually translate the Greek word *seismos* <note>original: σεισμὸς</note> as "earthquake," but it also signifies more generally any shaking or concussion. For example, *Hebrews 12:26:* "Once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heaven" <note>original Greek: Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ σείω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν, ἀλλὰ ϗ τὸν οὐρανόν</note> where the author says this *shaking* signifies the removal of those things that are shaken. *Haggai 2:21: Speak to Zerubbabel, Governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth, and I will overthrow the thrones of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations.* This is a plain "removal of those things that are shaken" <note>original Greek: μετάθεσις τῶν σαλευομένων</note>. A similar ruin and overturning of things is described by the effect of a *seismos*—an *earthquake* properly so called—in *Jeremiah 4:24: I beheld the mountains, and look, they trembled, and all the hills moved slightly.* In verse 26, he interprets this just as *Haggai* did before: *I beheld, and look, the fruitful place was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down, etc.*

<meta>catchword: Achmetes</meta>

Achmetes, drawing from the *Indian, Persian, and Egyptian dream interpreters* <note>original: "Onirocriticks"</note>, says: "If a king sees that his city or his land was shaken, it is judged as a sign of war between nations and a plot against him." <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ τις βασιλεὺς ὅτι ἐσείσθη ἡ πόλις αὐτοῦ ἢ ἡ γῆ αὐτοῦ, εἰς πόλεμον ἐθνῶν & ἐπιβουλὴν κατ' αὐτοῦ κρίνεται.</note> Artemidorus, in book 2, chapter 46, writes: "A shaking earth signifies that the affairs of the observer will be moved. Indeed, chasms, earthquakes, and collapses bring harm to all people, destroying them or their possessions." <note>original Greek: Γῆ κινυμένη τὰ πράγματα τοῦ ἰδόντος κινηθήσεσθαι σημαίνει. χάσματα δὲ καὶ σεισμοὶ καὶ συμπτώσεις πάντας ἀνθρώπους ἀδικοῦσι, καὶ διαφθείρουσιν αὐτοὺς ἢ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν.</note> But this is such an easy symbolic image <note>original: "Iconism"</note> that it was unnecessary to provide so many examples.

10. *Eclipses.* What the eclipses of the heavenly lights mean will be easily understood if we consider what the *sun* and *moon* represent in the *political world* <note>original: "Political Universe"</note>. For they are certainly the highest-ranking positions in that "heaven." We will discuss this more under their specific titles. In the meantime, it will be enough to briefly note from Achmetes that, according to the *Indian, Persian, and Egyptian dream interpreters*, if the sun be "unlit and without rays" <note>original Greek: ἀφώτιστος & ἄνευ ἀκτίνων</note>—meaning without brightness (in such a color, I suppose, as Virgil describes:
-> *When he [the sun] covered his bright head with a dark, rusty glow* <note>original Latin: "Cùm caput obscurâ nitidum ferrugine tinxit"</note> <-
and without rays)—"this inglorious obscurity and duskiness refers to the person of the king and implies a diminishing of his glory." <note>original Greek: τὸ πάθος καὶ ἀδοξία εἰς πρόσωπόν ἐστι βασιλέως</note> "But if a person sees that an eclipse of the sun occurred, the king will find affliction and war from enemies." <note>original Greek: Ἐάν δ' ἴδῃ τις ὅτι τοῦ ἡλίου ἐγένετο ἔκλειψις, θλίψιν καὶ πόλεμον ἐχθρῶν εὑρήσει ὁ βασιλεύς.</note>

They give the same judgment regarding the *moon* and the *stars* if they are "dim, unlit, or dark" <note>original Greek: ὀλιγόφωτα, ἀφώτιστα, or σκοτεινά</note>. "Let the suffering be judged as falling upon the people and the king’s rulers." <note>original Greek: Τὸ πάθος εἰς λαὸν & τοὺς ἄρχοντας βασιλέως κρινέτω.</note> See chapters 167 and 168. These things are too simple to dwell upon and will necessarily be accepted once it is granted *that the universe is a prophetic symbol of a kingdom or government*, as we shall clearly show in its proper place.

<margin>* Aristotle’s *Topics*, book 1, chapter 14.</margin>
11. *Eye.* "The light of the body," says our Savior, "is the eye." And Aristotle says: "As sight is in the eye, so is the mind in the soul." <note>original Greek: ὡς ὄψις ἐν ὀφθαλμῷ, νοῦς ἐν ψυχῇ</note> That is, the eye of the soul is the understanding or intellect. So it is plain that the eye is a symbolic image <note>original: "Iconism"</note> of *knowledge*, just as darkness and blindness are symbols of *ignorance*—a common expression in the Bible.

But there is also a particular suitability in using the *eye* to signify human policy and foresight <note>original: "Prospection"</note>. That organ of the body is not only in the head but is the chief guide of it and the whole body, being able to reach much further and act more quickly than any other sense. Therefore, "to look far ahead" <note>original Latin: "Prospicere in longitudinem"</note>—that is to say, to wisely consult beforehand for the right management of affairs and to plan strategies <note>original: "contrive Counsels"</note> that best ensure the future safety of things and the advancement of a state's interests—the eye is a fitting symbol of this skill. The Egyptians seem to have suggested this in their well-known hieroglyph, *a scepter with an eye on top of it*. Here, it is clear that the *eye* signified that political skill, foresight, and counsel necessary for managing and ordering state affairs for their greatest security and promotion. That *eyes* signify the administration of Divine Providence as well seems to be suggested in Zechariah 4:10, though we do not have time to dwell on that here.

12. *Fishing.* Artemidorus, in book 2, chapter 14, says: "To catch many large fish at once is good and brings profit to all." <note>original Greek: Λαμβάνειν ἰχθύας ἅμα πολλοὺς καὶ μεγάλους, ἀγαθὸν καὶ κέρδος φέρον πᾶσιν.</note> To dream of catching many...

[Fishes that are many] and great are good, and portend profit to all that dream so. *Achmetes*, chapter 178: "If anyone dreams that he catches fishes by angling in the sea using bait, he shall find riches, etc." <note>original Greek: Ἐάν ἴδῃ τις ὅτι ἠγκίστρευσεν ἰχθύας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ δελεάσας, εὑρήσει πλοῦτον, &c.</note>

*Fish dead in the sea,* according to *Artemidorus*, book 2, chapter 18: "To seem to see or find dead fish in the sea is not good; for it signifies the disappointment of our hope, and that what we expect will not come to pass." <note>original Greek: Ἰχθῦς νεκρὸς ἐν θαλάσσῃ ὁρᾷν δοκεῖν ἢ εὑρεῖν, οὐκ ἀγαθόν· ματαίας γὰρ ἐλπίδας σημαίνει, καὶ τὰ προσδοκώμενα οὐκ ἐῶσι τελεσθῆναι.</note>

<margin>Matthew 3:11</margin>
13. Fire. *Fire* is a versatile symbol and signifies both good and ill, but always in a way of consumption or destructiveness. However, when it destroys that which is bad, it is good. The *Holy Spirit* itself is compared to *fire*, as John the *Baptist* witnesses of Christ: *He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire;* such a *fire* as is to burn up the chaff but save the wheat, as is suggested in that passage. So also in *Malachi* 3: *Who shall abide the day of his coming? For he is like a refiner's fire, and like fuller's soap. And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver;* that is, consume away their dross <note>term: dross | the scum or impurities that form on the surface of molten metal</note>. There are many instances of this sense of *fire*, but it is unnecessary to provide more.

But for *fire* in the other destructive sense, it is even more obvious. I shall name one place among many; *Isaiah* 66:15: *For behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebukes with flames of fire. For by fire and by sword will the Lord plead with all flesh, and the slain of the Lord shall be many.*

The fitness of *fire* for signifying consumption or destruction has been noted by *Artemidorus*, book 2, chapter 8: "It is the property of fire to destroy all matter." <note>original Greek: Ἴδιον δὲ πυρὸς πᾶσαν ὕλην φθείρειν.</note> And in the same chapter he says it signifies—if there is a considerable quantity of it in the heavens—"an incursion of enemies," <note>original Greek: πολεμίων ἔφοδον</note> and their coming from that specific direction in the quarter of the sky where it is seen. Correspondingly, *Achmetes*, according to the sense of the *Indians*, chapter 159, says: "If anyone was burned by a flame, he shall die in a war of enemies." <note>original Greek: Εἴ τις ἐκάη ἀπὸ φλογός, ἐν πολέμῳ ἐχθρῶν τελευτήσει.</note> And of the *Persians* and *Egyptians*, chapter 160: "If a king sees that the pillars of his palace were on fire, it signifies another kingdom, and the destruction of the great men whom he himself appointed." <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ βασιλεύς ὅτι οἱ κίονες τοῦ παλατίου αὐτοῦ ἐφλογίζοντο, βασιλείαν ἄλλην σημαίνει, καὶ ἀπώλειαν τῶν μεγιστάνων οὓς αὐτὸς ἔστησεν.</note> And again, "If the king sees that his hair was set on fire, he will lose his people in war." <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν ἴδῃ ὁ βασιλεὺς ὅτι ἐφλογίσθησαν αἱ τρίχες αὐτοῦ, τὸν λαὸν ἐν πολέμῳ ἀπολέσει.</note> And lastly, he says that if his chariot appears to be set on fire, "his kingdom shall be humbled." <note>original Greek: ταπεινωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ.</note> The symbol of *fire* is so destructive everywhere, and it particularly denotes destruction by war and hostility, as can be seen from these citations.

14. Fire from Heaven. *Fire from heaven* and thunder may very well be the same thing, "because lightning is nothing else than fire," <note>original Greek: Ὅτι ὁ κεραυνὸς οὐδέν ἐστιν ἄλλο ἢ πῦρ</note> as *Artemidorus* says, book 2, chapter 8. But in allusion to Elijah bringing down fire from *heaven* upon those groups of fifty men sent to him by Ahaziah to arrest him, the fame of that eminent miracle may make the *bringing down fire from heaven* into a proverbial phrase for performing exceedingly great miracles. This may be a valid interpretation, but we are seeking a symbolic image <note>original: Iconismus</note>.

*Fire from heaven*, therefore, according to *Artemidorus*, may signify "the threat of those who are in authority;" <note>original Greek: ἀπειλὴν ὑπερεχόντων</note> and

# A compendious Alphabet Book I.

...that very fitly, *Heaven* being the place of dignity in the political universe. But nothing is so threatening as that *Fire* or *Lightning* that goes before *Thunder*. What, therefore, can be more significant of *Excommunication* than this? This is especially true if it is conceived to be hurled not by some lower official, but by a Universal <note>original: Oecumenical</note> Bishop, the Head of the *Catholic Church*, who is placed in the higher regions of the political *Heaven*. This analogy will be even more exact if we consider what *Artemidorus* <note>A 2nd-century Greek professional diviner and author of a famous book on dream interpretation.</note> observes about *Thunder*: *For thunder and lightning do not unite, but actually separate things that were joined.* <note>original Greek: Οὐ γὰρ ὁ κεραυνὸς ἑνοῖ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἡνωμένα χωρίζει.</note> In the same way, *Excommunication* splits off a member from the Church.

There is a further consistency in the idea that Excommunication should be called *Thunder and Lightning*, or *Fire from Heaven*, because it is the threat <note>original: commination</note> of Hell-fire. The destruction of *Sodom* was a symbolic precursor <note>term: Type | a person, event, or thing in the Old Testament believed to foreshadow something in the New Testament</note> of this, as it was burnt by fire from Heaven, as Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1639), an influential English scholar and theologian known for his studies on the Book of Revelation.</note> has judiciously observed. And what is the final *Great Conflagration* <note>original Greek: Ἐκπύρωσις (Ekpyrosis) | a Stoic concept of the periodic destruction of the cosmos by fire</note> but *Fire from Heaven*? Whoever takes it upon themselves to condemn men to that destruction may very well be said to *bring down fire from Heaven* upon them, which is exactly what the thunderbolt of *Excommunication* threatens.

<margin>Galatians 3:3</margin>
15. *Flesh.* In Scripture, *Flesh* is understood as whatever is opposite to the *Spirit*. I mean this in a moral or mystical way, and all of it is to be consumed by the *Spirit* and by Fire. But more particularly, *Flesh* sometimes signifies what are commonly called *Carnal Ordinances* <note>term: Carnal Ordinances | outward physical rituals or religious laws, as opposed to internal spiritual devotion</note>, in the same sense meant by St. *Paul*: *Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made perfect by the flesh?* Here he is speaking of the Law of *Moses*.
<margin>Hebrews chapter 7, verse 16</margin>
And the author of the letter to the *Hebrews* says even more clearly, when speaking of Christ and comparing him with the *Mosaic Aaron*: *Who is made (he says) not according to the law of a physical commandment, but according to the power of an endless life.* And even closer to our purpose, in chapter 9, verse 10, he speaks of *a religious service which consisted only in foods and drinks, and various ceremonial washings, and carnal ordinances imposed on them until the time of Reformation.* By *Flesh*, therefore, we may understand all the external rituals and institutions that men have recklessly piled upon Christianity, whether they are merely useless or else superstitious and idolatrous. For these are to the spirit of Christianity like the excess weight of a gross, overgrown, and unwholesome *flesh* is to the human spirit—*a useless burden upon the earth.* <note>original Greek: Ἐτώσιον ἄχθος ἀρούρης | a phrase from Homer’s Iliad</note>

16. But there is another sense of *Flesh* frequently mentioned in the books of dream interpretation <note>term: Onirocritics | the art or practice of interpreting dreams</note>. *Artemidorus*, book 3, chapter 23: *It is not good for a rich man to dream he eats his own flesh, for it signifies the utter destruction of his wealth or property.* <note>original Greek: Πλουσίῳ δ᾽ οὐκ ἀγαθὸν ἐσθίειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων σαρκῶν, προῤῥίζον γὰρ ἀνατραπῆναι τὸν βίον καὶ τὴν ὕπαρξιν τοῦ ἰδόντος σημαίνει.</note> *Achmetes* <note>Achmet, son of Seirim, the purported author of a 9th-century Greek book on dream interpretation drawing on Arabic and Egyptian sources.</note> says in chapter 283, according to the *Indian*, *Persian*, and *Egyptian* interpreters: *If anyone dreams that he found or ate the meat of dragons, he shall find wealth in proportion from a very great king.* <note>original Greek: Εἰ δ᾽ ἴδῃ τις ὅτι κρέας δρακόντων εὗρεν ἢ ἔφαγον, εὑρήσει πλοῦτον ἀνάλογον ἀπὸ μεγίστου βασιλέως.</note> This is like the *Israelites* eating the flesh of the *Leviathan* in the wilderness, for the *Leviathan* or *Dragon* represents the King of *Egypt*. And again, in chapter 285: *If anyone dreams that he ate the meat of a scorpion which he killed, he shall take the property of such an enemy.* <note>original Greek: Εἰ δ᾽ ἴδῃ τις ὅτι ἔφαγε κρέας σκορπίου ὃν ἐφόνευσε, τοιᾶτε ἐχθρᾷ ὕπαρξιν λήψεται.</note> And, lastly, according to the *Indians* in chapter 87: *If someone dreams that his own flesh has increased, he will acquire gold and wealth in proportion to the flesh.* <note>original Greek: Ἐάν τις ἴδῃ ὅτι ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ ἐπλεόνασε, χρυσοῦ καὶ πλοῦτον ἀναλόγως τῆς σαρκὸς κτᾶται.</note>
