### Chapter IX. Of Prophetic Symbols <note>original: "Prophetick Iconisms"</note>

[...thun]der, that he had glorified him, and would glorify him again. See *Fire*.

5. **Time**. That a *Time* and *Times* and *half a Time* in the Book of *Daniel* signifies three and a half years, we have the agreement <note>original: "suffrage"</note> of Grotius, and indeed no interpreters that I know of disagree. But this figure of speech is not referable to any of the prophetic schemes which I have set down, but is a mere *general synecdoche* <note>original: "Synecdoche Generis"; a figure of speech where a general term is used for a specific one</note>; just as *Hour* is a *specific synecdoche* <note>original: "Synecdoche Speciei"; a specific term used for a general/indefinite one</note> when it is used to mean an indefinitely short time, as it is sometimes. For example, 1 *Thessalonians* 2:17: *“But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time, etc.”* The Greek has it, "for a season of an hour" <note>original Greek: πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας</note>. Also *Philemon* 15: *“For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that you might enjoy him for ever.”* For a *season* is in the Greek "for an hour" <note>original Greek: πρὸς ὥραν</note>.

This use of an *Hour* in ordinary writing is, as I said, only a *specific synecdoche*, but in the prophetic style there is a *precise determination* <term>original: "Diorismus"; a specific definition or limiting of a term</term> in it. But as for a *Day* when it is taken for a *Year*, it is an *image based on likeness* <term>original: "Icasmus"; a comparison or representation based on similitude</term>, because there is a circuit of the sun in each, and therefore they bear a resemblance to one another. From this it follows that if *one Day* stands for *one Year*, then proportionally *one Month* of days will stand for *thirty years*.

6. But that numbering by *Months* is appropriate to the works of Darkness—as reflecting upon the cycles of the *Moon*, which is the governor of the night—and numbering by the courses of the *Sun* is appropriate to the works of Righteousness. This, as I have noted already, is an observation by Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1639), an influential English biblical scholar known for his interpretations of the Book of Revelation.</note>, and is exactly true in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. There, the *continuing of the Beast* and the *profaning of the holy City by the Gentiles* is calculated by *Months*; but the *Prophecy of the Witnesses*, as well as their martyrdom and their lying unburied, is calculated by *Days*. The stay of the *Woman in the Wilderness* is also numbered by *Days*, and by a *time and times and half a time*. According to this specific system of assignment <note>original: "curiosity of Appropriation"</note>, this must necessarily signify three solar years and a half, even though they fall short by nearly twenty days. But "Neither the Judge nor the Prophet cares for small trifles" <note>original Latin: "Modicum nec curat Prætor nec Propheta"</note> is better applied here than how Grotius applies it. Hence it is demonstrable that there is a concealed or silent latitude of at least twenty years in these 1,260 days, which are the same as a *Time and Times and half a Time*; and that the first measure may be an *Icad* <note>likely referring to a unit of ten</note>. But because the number sixty is heard <note>original: "sounds"</note>, and that is silent in this number, it is not improbable that a *Hexecad* <note>likely referring to a unit of sixty</note> might, if necessary, be taken for the first measure or divisor of 1,260. But I have expressly noted above that 1,260 days is a *precise determination* <note>original: "Diorismus"</note>.

7. **Trees**. That *Trees*, according to their various sizes and height <note>original: "procerity"</note>, signify various ranks of men, is plain from the Book of *Zechariah*, chapter 11: *“Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour your Cedars. Howl, Fir-tree, for the Cedar is fallen, because all the mighty are spoiled. Howl, you Oaks of Bashan, for the forest of the vintage is come down.”* Those few words, *“All the mighty are spoiled,”* are a certain key to the parable, and show that the prophecy does not point at *Trees*, but *Men*; and therefore Vatablus <note>François Vatable (d. 1547), a French humanist and Hebrew scholar.</note> and other interpreters interpret it accordingly. That proverbial poem <note>original: "Iambick"</note> says,

that it is his duty to be so, and that the high act of religion and devotional love which is due to him should not in any measure be diverted toward another. Instead, the eye of our mind should be wholly fixed upon him. This is the duty of every rational soul, whether she is in an external covenant with God or not. 10. We see, therefore, the analogy between *whoredom* and *idolatry*. For as in *whoredom* that special kind of passion and its proper effects, which are due only to a legitimate husband, are diverted toward some other person; so in *idolatry* the height and flower of our divinest affection—which is religious devotion and adoration, along with the outward signs due to God alone—are directed toward and exercised upon some creature, whether idols of wood and stone or any other things which are not God. This is a fundamental reason for this frequent *symbolic image* <note>original term: "Iconism"</note> in Scripture.

To this you may add a few other resemblances: the provocation of God's jealousy against those especially who are in an external covenant with him; the ornamental pompousness in *idolatry*, which corresponds to the garishness of whores and the way they deck themselves out to allure their lovers <note>original: "Paramours"</note>; and also the natural inclination and tendency to fall into this sin. It is as natural to the corrupt condition of the soul to dote on a visible object of worship as it is for the body to seek the pleasures it anticipates from every enticing object, were it not for a higher law forbidding it in both cases. To this you may further add the lack of remorse that men easily fall into in both sins; they drift down the stream so easily, and their animal nature is so much gratified by them. 
<margin>Proverbs 30:20</margin>
*Such is the way of the adulterous woman in both senses: she eats and wipes her mouth, and says, "I have done no wickedness."* 
And lastly, just as being engaged in whorish practices extinguishes the love and respect due to a husband, so being enticed into *idolatrous worship* completely suffocates and kills that divine sense through which we truly enjoy God and know our true duty to him, and relish those indispensable points of obedience by which we are meant to honor him.

So deep and weighty a meaning <note>original: "sense"</note> is hidden under this one prophetic *symbolic image* <note>original term: "Iconism"</note>, *fornication* or *whoredom*. This symbol seems to be used so specifically in the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note> not only as a just reproach of the sin, but for its exquisite meaning, as it so fully and truly represents the nature of *idolatry*.

12. But though this *symbolic image* <note>original term: "Iconism"</note> of the *wine-press* signifies slaughter or an abundant shedding of blood, yet we must remember that death and slaughter themselves do not always signify something *physical*, but sometimes something *moral* or spiritual. And for my part, I do not doubt that the passage in Isaiah <note>original: "Esay"</note> 63 ["*Who is this that comes from Edom, with his dyed garments from Bozrah, &c:* and again, *I have trodden the wine-press alone, and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments*"], whatever other sense it has, also contains an allegorical meaning. As the Church Fathers have interpreted it, it concerns Christ's spiritual victories, which I shall have occasion to discuss more extensively in the proper place.

13. *Woman* and *Women*. I have already noted that in a prophetic scheme, a *Woman* signifies not one *single woman*, but a *body politic*. For example: *I have heard a voice as of a woman in labor* <note>original: "travel"</note> —— *the voice of the Daughter of Zion*, Jeremiah 4:31. But this scheme is so common that there is no need to insist upon more examples. Here *Zion* (meaning its inhabitants) is called both *Woman* and *Daughter*. The second term is used in a sense of delicacy and nobility, as if we should say in English, *the Damsel Zion*. 

But there is another sense of *Daughter* which is clear in Ezekiel 16, where he calls *Jerusalem* a harlot (verse 35): "Therefore, *O harlot, hear the word of the Lord, &c*." And in the course of the charge or complaint, he declares how *Jerusalem* with her *daughters* was worse than her two sisters, *Sodom* and *Samaria*, with their *daughters*. Yet these sisters are said (verse 45) *to have loathed their husbands*, which is to say, to have been unfaithful and to have committed idolatry. Therefore, a capital city <note>original: "Metropolis"</note> along with its lesser towns are considered *mother* and *daughters*, and consequently all are *women*. But if they are idolatrous, they are the kind of *women* who will defile those who join with them in public worship.

But there is yet another sense of *Woman*, not *political* but more *physical* and *mystical* <note>original term: "Cabbalistical"</note>: that is, the life, senses, and physical desires of the body. This is a *woman* that we must take special care not to be polluted by, either by over-passionately agreeing with her suggestions, or by over-deeply sympathizing with or indulging in the pleasures she would allure us with, thereby fixing our desire upon her. For not only idolatry, but all other wicked acts <note>original: "Enormities"</note> arise in us from listening to the false counsel of this "domestic *Eve*."

And that it signifies this in the *Hebrew idiom* is manifest from several instances. But the very symbol itself is explained...

# Chapter 9: On Prophetic Symbols

...is explained in Genesis 37, where the sheaves of Joseph's brothers are said to bow down to Joseph's sheaf—that is, to worship Joseph's sheaf. The Greek text says, "Your sheaves worshipped my sheaf" <note>original: Τὰ δράγματα ὑμῶν προσεκύνησαν τὸ ἐμὸν δράγμα</note>. Upon hearing this, his brothers immediately interpreted the dream, saying to him, "*Shall you indeed reign over us?*" or, "*Shall you indeed have dominion over us?*" This means: shall we be your subjects, or fall under your power? 

Similarly, in Isaiah 45:14, speaking of the subjection of the Ethiopians and Sabeans to King Cyrus, he says, "*They shall come after you; in chains they shall come over, and they shall fall down before you.*" The Greek translation has it: "*They shall worship you*" <note>original: προσκυνήσουσί σοι</note>. All of these instances signify submission and subjection to a person's sovereignty. I will add only one more passage: Genesis 27, regarding Isaac's blessing upon Jacob: "*Let people serve you, and nations bow down to you; be lord over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you.*" The word used in both places is "acts of worship" <note>original: προσκυνήσεσιν</note>, and it clearly signifies obedience or subjection in a general sense.

But even if the word did not have that general meaning on its own, and only denoted the specific act of bowing or worship, it might still represent subjection in a broad sense within the **Prophetic Style** <note>original: Stylo Prophetico</note> through a <term>Diorismus</term> <note>A rhetorical device where a specific part or action is used to represent a whole category—in this case, the act of bowing representing the entire state of being a subject.</note>.

**World**, See *Heaven* and *Earth*.

15. These are the chief **symbolic** <term>Icastick</term> <note>Derived from the Greek 'eikastikos,' meaning relating to images or representation.</note> terms that occur in the prophetic style. If they happen to be more numerous than we require for this specific discourse, I still consider my efforts worthwhile in light of what I discussed in my *Mystery of Godliness*. Furthermore, they are highly useful for understanding the primary visions and prophecies in Scripture. 

I hope I have demonstrated—partly through this **Alphabet of Symbolic Images** <note>original: Alphabet of Iconisms</note> and partly through my explanation of the preceding prophetic patterns—that it is just as easy to translate a prophecy or vision from this prophetic style into ordinary language as it is to translate one language into another. The difficulty in understanding prophecies is essentially no greater than understanding common speech, once a person has learned the established meanings of the unique **symbols** <term>Icasms</term> used within them. Just as ordinary speech has many **words with multiple meanings** <term>Homonymies</term>, so too does the prophetic style have its own symbols. Therefore, no one should be criticized for trying to understand the prophecies of Scripture any more than they would be for studying its histories. Prophecy is nothing more than history written in advance; once it is fulfilled, it is as plain a history as any event that was never prophesied.

16. We will now add a few **Rules** concerning the **Preference** of one interpretation of prophecy over another, and then conclude.

->The First Rule<-

> *An interpretation that stays close to the established examples and the analogy of the prophetic style is to be preferred over interpretations that are created at will according to the private imagination of the interpreter.*

The basis for **this rule** is that it is safer to follow a proven example than to lack one and rely entirely on one's own private opinion. Since the style of the Prophets is effectively a unique language or dialect, there is a necessity to understand things according to the established meaning of that dialect, and not accor—

<header>Rules for Interpreting Prophecies. Book I.</header>

...according to what it would sound like in our own language. This is as foolish and ridiculous as if an Englishman, hearing Latin spoken where the word *thief* <note>original: "Fur"</note> is occasionally mentioned, should think the *fur* of an Alderman’s gown was meant; or if, upon hearing the sound of *every sickle* <note>original: "πᾶν δρέπανον" (pan drepanon)</note> in Greek, his imagination should immediately think of a *dripping-pan*. And yet, it is just as discordant and out of place to interpret the <term>Iconisms</term> <note>A term for the symbolic images or "icons" used by prophets to represent reality.</note> of the Prophets according to whatever ideas are either common or peculiar to ourselves. 

It is a mistake to think that because *vices* and *virtues* are sometimes depicted as *women* or *beasts*, we should apply that same meaning to the **prophetic style**. In prophecy, these figures always signify a <term>Body Politic</term> <note>A "Body Politic" refers to a collective group of people acting as a single political entity, such as a nation, state, or church.</note>, even in those specific visions where they have abstract labels written upon them. For example, in Zechariah 5:7, the *woman* in the *ephah* <note>An ephah was a standard ancient Hebrew unit of dry volume, often represented as a large basket or container.</note> is said to be *Wickedness*. Despite this label, the scholar Vatablus <note>François Vatable (d. 1547), a renowned French Hebraist and theologian.</note> understands this woman to represent the *Ten Tribes* who revolted into idolatry, and other interpreters explain it to the same purpose. To interpret *hail* as *hardness of heart* is just like interpreting Latin or Greek by whatever English word sounds nearest to them. This is *moving into a different category* <note>original: "μεταβαίνειν εἰς ἄλλο γένος" (metabainein eis allo genos) — a logical fallacy described by Aristotle where one applies the rules of one subject to a completely different one.</note>, as Aristotle says, and shows that one has quite forgotten where they are or what they are doing.

### The Second Rule

> **That interpretation which maintains a single consistent meaning for the same words—especially within one and the same vision—is to be preferred over an interpretation that shifts back and forth, taking the same word in many different senses as it appears in different places of the vision.**

Telling "many tales" <note>original: "To be in many tales" — an idiom meaning to be inconsistent or to tell contradictory stories.</note> is considered a certain sign of a false story. Similarly, varying the interpretation of the same word within a single vision, without any clear reason, is a great demonstration of dishonesty and strain in the interpretation. it suggests that the interpreter was biased by some personal goal or interest and has done violence to the text for his own advantage. 

For example, if someone were to interpret the symbol of a *Beast* as signifying a *Kingdom* or *Empire* in one place, a single person within that empire in another, and then some great vice in a third, would this not be a mere clumsy patch? It is far better to interpret this *Beast* as a *Kingdom* or *Body Politic* in every instance within the vision. I could provide other examples of such trickery, but this one hint shall suffice.

### The Third Rule

> **That interpretation which concerns the affairs of religion and the Church of God, and is of the greatest use and service to us, is a more likely interpretation. It is to be preferred over one that relates less to us, or which suggests the Spirit of God predicted things with little or no regard for the usefulness of the Church.**

The truth of **this rule** appears not only from the constant examples found in prophecy—where it is rare to find any that do not relate to the Church of God in some special way—but also from the logic of the thing itself. Even the
<margin>* Revelation 6.</margin>
*riders of the red, black, and pale horses* were essentially scouts sent to inform the Church about the coming periods of her history. If the number of prophecies were not limited by this standard of usefulness to the Church, what would their boundaries be? And...

<header>Chapter 10: Rules for interpreting Prophecies.</header>

And if there is any meaning beyond this, why are there no prophecies concerning all nations and their affairs without any reference to the Church?

->The Last Rule<-

*Interpretations are more likely to be true when they are suggested to a mind that is unprejudiced and unbiased by any external considerations. This is in contrast to those made by people who may be influenced by self-interest, worldly hopes or fears, or any personal conflict or dislike that might create a false bias and make their judgment partial.*

The truth of this **rule** is obvious at first glance, but I must confess its usefulness is more limited and uncertain. For although it may be apparent enough in many cases that an interpreter is prejudiced by some of the ways I have mentioned, it is very difficult to be certain that any man is entirely free from prejudice; therefore, the application of the **rule** will be found more difficult. But where certain proof cannot be reached, careful conjecture may claim a right to take its place. Nor do we need to be overly concerned about the force or use of this last **rule**, as it concerns the interpreter more than the interpretation itself. It argues from the quality of the person rather than the solidity of their work—which is better examined by the three previous rules and other firm principles of reason and knowledge.

<page-num>262</page-num>
<header>The Two Parallelisms of Agreements. Book I.</header>

We have observed in our *Concept of Antichristianism*, beginning first with that first and most prominent feature of Antichristianism, *Idolatry*; we shall note this through all those *Prophecies* which we believe pointed toward it, whether in the Old or New Testament. We begin at the *Seventeenth Chapter of the Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps," the Greek title for the Book of Revelation.</note>, which is the "Royal Gate" that will let us in to view, with the greatest possible certainty and assurance, all those scenes of future things shown by *St. John* himself, by *St. Paul*, or by *Daniel*, concerning the Church of Christ in the state we have described.

Therefore, because it is of such great importance to be certain of the true meaning of the *Vision in that chapter*, I have decided to search for its genuine sense with more than ordinary diligence (and, I hope, with corresponding success). I believe I have achieved an undeniable clarity regarding the meaning of *both those Visions*—both here and in the *Thirteenth Chapter*—by carefully comparing them and demonstrating that both chapters address exactly the same things, and by strictly following the known *analogy of prophetic patterns* <note>original: "Analogy of Prophetick Schemes," referring to the consistent symbolic language used in biblical prophecy.</note>. This clarity is such that no one who is not willfully blind can fail to discern the truth.

2. Both these chapters share the exact same subject. Specifically, the *Two-horned Beast* is the same as the *Whore of Babylon*, and the *Seven-headed Beast with ten horns in the Thirteenth Chapter* is identical in every respect to the *Seven-headed Beast with ten horns in the Seventeenth Chapter*. The many *points of agreement* between these two pairs, as shown in the following two *parallels*, will abundantly prove this.

3. *The Parallelism of Agreements between the Two-horned Beast and the Whore of Babylon.*

->Agreement I.<-

The *Two-horned Beast* and the *Whore of Babylon* are both the restorers and promoters of idolatry within the Empire.

->Agreement II.<-

They both held the rule and government over the *Seven-headed Beast with ten horns*.

->Agreement III.<-

They both aspired to a majesty and power that was clearly imperial.

->Agreement IV.<-

They both performed miracles, or acted as a kind of magician or sorcerer, in order to restore idolatry.

->Agreement V.<-

They both pretend to be holy and put on a show of acting on behalf of Christ, when in fact they are the ones who introduce idolatry and Antichristian practices.

->Agreement VI.<-

They are both cruel and bloody persecutors of the saints and of the witnesses of *Jesus*.

->Agreement VII.<-

They are both described as having jurisdiction over the entire Empire, both in the East <note>original: "Oriental."</note> and the West <note>original: "Occidental."</note>.

This matches historical events in a remarkable way.

5. These are the two *Parallelisms of Agreements*. Regarding the second one, I dare say it is so exact and complete that the parallels between the *Seven-headed Beast* in *Chapter 13* and the *Seven-headed Beast* in *Chapter 17* account for everything mentioned in each chapter about that Beast. The first parallelism is not quite as precise: the *origin of the Two-horned Beast* has no parallel in the description of the *Whore*, and the *destruction of the Whore* has no parallel in the description of the *Two-horned Beast* as he is presented there. Therefore, the vision in Chapter 17 is unique because it also deals with the *judgment of the Two-horned Beast (the Whore)*, matching the very title of the vision: *I will show you the judgment of the great Whore*. 

However, this is no argument at all against them being the same person. This is especially true since the *Two-horned Beast* is also destined for destruction at the same time as the *Whore*, which is easily proven by the *chronological alignment of the Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyptick Synchronisms," a method of interpreting Revelation by lining up contemporary events across different visions.</note>. As for omitting the *origin of the Whore* to match the *origin of the Two-horned Beast*, that is also no argument against them being the same. Indeed, if an origin had been assigned to the *Whore* that was different from the *Two-horned Beast*, that would be significant; but this simple omission only shows the skill and precision of these visions, which maintain a sense of *decorum* in all things. Therefore, because it was not considered fitting or suitable to say a *Woman rose out of the Earth*—even though animals did so in Genesis 1:24—mentioning her origin was tactfully avoided.

6. A smaller number of agreements in each parallelism would have been enough to create a strong suspicion that the subjects of the visions in each chapter are identical (provided nothing contradicted it). By this, I mean *that the Two-horned Beast and the Whore are one, and the Seven-headed Beast is the same in both chapters*. How much more certain must we be of this identity when the agreements between these two parallelisms perfectly cover the entire substance of each chapter (except for those few passages I have already explained)? To make this even clearer, I will lay out the entire 17th Chapter before your eyes, and after every verse, I will add the parallel from Chapter 13. We will see that Chapter 13 absorbs the entire chapter.

## CHAPTER XI

1. *The great importance of proving the seven heads of the beast to be seven types <note>original: "sorts"</note> of governors.* 2. *That proving the seven-headed beast signifies the idolatrous Roman Kingdom or Empire insofar as it is <note>original: "quatenus"</note> idolatrous will go far toward proving the previous point.* 3. *That the seven-headed beast is a kingdom or empire.* 4. *And particularly the Roman.* 5. *That it is the idolatrous Roman Kingdom or Empire.* 6. *That it represents this idolatrous empire or kingdom throughout all the ages it remains idolatrous.* 7. *That it represents the Roman Kingdom or Empire only in those ages in which it is idolatrous. From this, the true meaning of the "slaying of the beast" and a further confirmation of the previous assertion can be understood.* 8. *That this complete representation of the idolatrous duration of the empire implies that no seven individual people <note>original: "single Persons"</note> can be its seven heads.* 9. *The same conclusion inferred—*

### Chapter 11: The Beast's Seven Heads represent Seven types of Governors. 269

<sig>A a 3</sig>

9. This is inferred from the fact that these *Seven Heads* are marked <note>original: "stigmatizing"</note> with the *brand of idolatry*, even though more than *seven*—in fact, all—of the *Pagan Emperors* were idolaters. 10. This is also clear from the common way of speaking when distinguishing *animals* by the number of their body parts. 11. And finally, it is clear from the certainty that the *Seventh Head* is not one *single person*, but a *succession* of rulers. 12. Any interpretation that assumes these *Seven Heads* are *seven single people* is not only false but impossible. 13. From what has been proven, it follows that the *Beast* in the 17th chapter of *Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note> is the *Roman Empire* having degenerated back into a form of *paganism*. 14. Likewise, the *Whore of Babylon* is not *Pagan Rome*, but *Pagano-Christian Rome* <note>Rome as a mix of Christian profession and pagan practices</note>. 15. The idea that *Antichrist* only comes at the very end of the *world* is a mere fantasy <note>original: "chimerical fiction"</note>. 16. The true subject of the visions in the 17th and 13th chapters of the *Book of Revelation*.

1. THE position I have mentioned, which is of great importance, is this: *That the Seven Heads of the Beast are not seven individual people—whether Emperors or any other supreme rulers—but seven types of governors who follow one after another.* Once this is cleared up, we can be absolutely certain about the true meaning and subject of the visions in these two chapters we are considering.

2. Indeed, we will make great progress in proving this important claim if we can first establish this preparatory conclusion: *That the Beast with seven heads and ten horns represents the idolatrous Roman Kingdom or Empire insofar as <note>original: "quatenus"</note> it is idolatrous—that is, during the time it is idolatrous, and no further.* I will attempt to demonstrate the truth of this proposition step-by-step.

Chapter 5.
Section 9.

3. First, regarding the idea that a *Beast* refers to a *Kingdom* or *Empire*: there is no need to repeat the proof here, as I have already demonstrated this in my *Prophetic Alphabet*. I also pointed out in my first rule for comparing interpretations of prophecy how absurd <note>original: "absonous"</note> and ridiculous it is not to interpret prophetic figures according to the established meaning and usage of the prophetic style. Finally, you may add that since the *seven heads of the Beast* are interpreted as *seven successive kings*, and the *ten horns* as *ten kings* reigning at the same time, the Beast must necessarily be a *Kingdom* or *Empire*.

4. Second, that this *seven-headed Beast with ten horns* is the *Roman Kingdom* or *Empire*: beyond the fact that those *ten horns* correspond to the Beast with ten horns in *Daniel* (which the Church has always interpreted as the *Roman state*), this sense is further fixed and determined <note>original: "defix and determinate"</note> by the *Whore of Babylon*. She is said to sit on this Beast with seven heads, and is almost universally understood to be *Rome* (the scholar *Alcazar* <note>Luis de Alcázar (1554–1613), a Jesuit theologian</note> cites at least twenty interpreters who agree). This must lead to the same conclusion. Finally, the Angel's interpretation—which says the *seven heads* of the Beast signify both *seven hills* and *seven kings*—plainly demonstrates that the Beast is *Roman*, as those hills are the hills of *Rome*. For how could the *seven hills of Rome* be called the Beast's *seven heads* if the Beast were not the *Roman Empire*?

# That the Seven Heads of the Beast Book I. 270

However, even *Ribera* <note>Francisco Ribera (1537–1591), a Jesuit scholar whose commentary on Revelation was widely studied</note> himself does not dare to deny that the *Seven Hills* signify *Rome*. *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch legal scholar and theologian</note>, commenting specifically on the text, states: "These hills are well enough known from poets and histories; no more famous feature could be used to describe Rome" <note>original Latin: *Noti satìs Montes ex Poetis & Historiis, nec ulla poterat ad describendam Romam adferri nota illustrior*</note>. This is universally the understanding of all interpreters. Even Bishop *Mountague* <note>Richard Montagu (1577–1641), an influential and controversial Anglican bishop</note>—who would extend the meaning to the *Turkish Empire* because it has gained possession of *Constantinople* (which history has also occasionally noted for its *seven hills*)—does not exclude *ancient Rome* from the Angel’s interpretation. 

But we can conclude with mathematical certainty that the *Seven-headed Beast* cannot be the *Turkish Empire*. This is because the prophecy describes an empire that had already continued a succession of *five heads* by *St. John’s* time, whereas the *Turkish Empire* did not even exist for many hundreds of years afterward. Furthermore, there was no empire whose capital city was famous for seven hills except for the *Roman* one. From this, we have every possible assurance that the *Beast with Seven Heads and Ten Horns* is the *Roman Empire*.

<margin>Chap. 5. Sect. 9.</margin>
5. Thirdly, it is clear from several indications that this *Seven-headed Beast* is the *idolatrous Roman Kingdom or Empire*. First, the very figure of a *Beast* (in the sense of the Greek word <term>wild beast</term> <note>original Greek: θηρίον; Latin: Fera</note>) signifies an *idolatrous kingdom or empire* in its own right. I have already demonstrated this in my *Prophetic Alphabet*, and this alone would be enough to prove this third part of our argument.

<margin>* Rev. 12.</margin>
In addition to this, we can observe that in every vision where this *Seven-headed Beast* is represented, there is something that clearly identifies him as *idolatrous*. For example, in *Revelation* 12, he appears as a *Dragon* or *Serpent*, which must necessarily be a *pagan power* or *idolatrous empire*. His shape is the very image of the *Devil*; he wages war against the Church of Christ, and his downfall leads to the exaltation of Christ’s Kingdom. Even *Grotius* himself acknowledges that this <term>great red dragon</term> <note>original Greek: πυῤῥὸς δράκων μέγας</note> is *Mars*, the presiding demon-god of the Roman state, which was as notoriously *idolatrous* as it was *cruel*.

Since it is certain that the *red Dragon* is the *idolatrous Roman Empire*, it is also clearly implied that the *Seven-headed Beast* in the 13th chapter is that same *idolatrous empire*. This is shown by the fact that it is the Beast healed of the deadly wound it received in its battle with *Michael’s army* <note>original: "Host of Michael"</note>. Furthermore, the *Dragon* is said to have given his power to this *Beast*, and this *Beast* is called the *Image of the Dragon* that was so mortally wounded. Similarly, in chapter 17, the *Seven-headed Beast* shown there is called the *Beast that was*—and who was that, I ask, if not the *Dragon*? Therefore, this *revived Dragon* <note>original Latin: Draco redivivus</note> or this *Image of the Dragon* must be an *idolatrous empire*, or the Empire returning once again to *idolatry*.

Finally, in case the reader is not paying close enough attention to notice the idolatry of the *Seven-headed Beast* in the 13th and 17th chapters based on the reasons I have given, the Spirit of God has even more explicitly branded him with this *characteristic* in both of those visions. In the 13th chapter, the *Name of Blasphemy* is placed on his seven heads, and in the 17th, his body is described as being full of the *names of blasphemy*. By *blasphemy*, the text means *idolatry*, as I have proven extensively in my *Prophetic Alphabet*.

# Chapter 11: There are Seven Sorts of Governors

<margin>See Chapter 3, Section 6.</margin>
Throughout all the time it was *this way* or *was meant to be this way*, it appears, first, from the general nature of these prophetic figures. In such figures, a *Beast* signifies a kingdom or empire in its entire succession and duration, unless anything is indicated to the contrary. This is clear from those examples in the Book of *Daniel*, where the *Four Beasts* signify four kingdoms in their entire successions, as well as from the very nature of that prophetic scheme which we call <term>henopoeia</term> <note>a rhetorical device where a multitude of individuals or a sequence of time is gathered into a single individual form</note>, which always accompanies these <term>iconisms</term> <note>symbolic representations or figures</note> of beasts. For a *henopoeia* is nothing other than a collection of both a succession [over time] and a multitude [of people] into one individual form or shape, whether it be human or beast-like <note>original: belluine</note>.

Again, because the *Seven-headed Beast* in the 13th chapter of Revelation is said to be the *image of the Dragon*, and the same Beast in the 17th chapter is said to be the *Beast that was* (which certainly was the *Dragon*), this shows that those visions intend to represent the Empire through all the times it was idolatrous. This includes the times of its primitive or purely pagan idolatry, as well as the *image* or *restoration* of it in a *pagan-like or idolatrous kind of Christianity*. Or, more fully stated: this Seven-headed Beast is represented under one of his heads as fighting and being wounded to death, but later revived. He is also said to have existed for a certain time, then to cease to be, but afterward to exist again, and then finally to perish. Therefore, the whole duration and continuance of the Beast seems to be comprised within this, divided into two parts by this death and the stopping <note>original: interceasing</note> of the Beast for a time. The plain sense of this is: *The Roman Kingdom or Empire has been and shall be a "Beast"*—that is to say, *idolatrous*—for a certain sequence of time, then cease to be so for a while, but afterward be idolatrous again, and then cease to be so forever. These prophetic figures, therefore—I mean these Beasts that display this meaning—must necessarily imply these two entire periods of time where the Empire is represented as idolatrous, just as someone who divides a line into two parts divides the whole line.

To all of this you may add that because the seven heads of the Dragon are represented as actually wearing crowns—even though five had already passed in *St. John’s* time, and only one was present, with the seventh not yet existing—it plainly suggests that the entire duration and succession of the Beast is shown all at once. This is even more evident because the seventh head is the last, under which the Beast perishes together with that head, as that elliptical text certainly implies in chapter 17, verse 11. The entire meaning of that verse is this: *And the Beast that was, and is not, even his head is the eighth, and is one of the seven; and he, together with his head, goes into perdition* <note>perdition: eternal punishment or ruin</note>. I shall have occasion to note this more fully in its proper place.

Therefore, it is reasonable to believe that the first head reaches back to the very beginning of the Beast—that is, of the *Roman Empire*—just as the last head reaches to its destruction. I will also add that the phrase "the ancient serpent" <note>original Greek: ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος</note>, while implying the *Roman Empire* as well as the *Devil*, may also suggest the antiquity of the one as well as of the other.

But during the time of that corrupted condition, when the Christian religion became **Paganish** and **Idolatrous**, it might rightly be said of the Empire then, **That it is the Beast that was, and is not, and yet is.** But the **Whore** <note>In the context of 17th-century Protestant commentary, the "Whore of Babylon" was typically identified as the Roman Catholic Church or its hierarchy</note> is said to ride this very Beast. 15. Nor can the vision be understood as referring to **Paganism** (strictly speaking) that would again overrun the Roman Empire a little before the end of the world under a **Chimerical Antichrist** <note>An "imaginary" or "fanciful" Antichrist; the author is arguing against those who believe Antichrist is a single person appearing only at the end of time</note> then to appear (as some are willing to imagine as an evasion). Instead, it is to be interpreted as an **Antichristianism** that has already seized it; for it is said that the truly Christian Caesar shall continue only **a short time.** This implies that the Antichristian state will continue for a long time in comparison to it.

Therefore, if this Antichristian state has not yet arrived, but everything is well, and that **Pagano-Christian** idolatry has not entered from the reign of **Constantine** to this very day, the reign of Antichrist would be at least three or four thousand years long. This is such a monstrous consequence, and so directly contrary to Scripture, that the position leading to it must necessarily be false.

16. Therefore, we may safely conclude **that the main subject of the vision in this 17th chapter of the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, as also of that in the 13th (which is essentially the same as this), is the state of the Roman Empire corrupted and degenerated from true and pure Christianity into a Paganish and idolatrous condition, because of the false direction and guidance of those in the Roman Hierarchy who took it upon themselves to rule the Empire in matters of religion. But also, that this idolatrous condition—both in the Hierarchy and the Empire—shall be changed after a certain period of time, and true Christianity shall overflow everything again, and idolatry shall never revive again.**

This is the summary account of these visions. We will now begin the explanation of every particular of each chapter, by which this general account may be demonstrated even more convincingly.

# His Combined Explanation of the Seventeenth Book, Part I.

### 1. What the precious stones and pearls signify. 2. How clearly the third agreement of the first parallelism is demonstrated. 3. What the golden cup signifies in terms of its metal. Verse 5: The names of whores inscribed on their foreheads. 2. That the whole sentence is the Whore's name; and how ridiculous it is to understand the word "Mystery" as a mere figure of speech <note>original: "Synecdoche"; a figure of speech where a part represents the whole</note>. 3. The interpretation of these parts of her name: "Mystery" and "Babylon." 4. Also of "Babylon the Great, the Mother of Fornications." 5. A demonstration of the fifth agreement of the first parallelism. 6. The different origin of the "Two-horned Beast" compared to others.

1. In this combined explanation, though I will not overlook other details, my main goal shall be to point out and confirm the agreements between the two parallelisms I have outlined above. For the sake of brevity, and without any further complex analysis, I shall guide my explanation by the order of the verses in the seventeenth chapter, passing from verse to verse. I will compare the sections from chapter thirteen (which I have added below) with what is contained in each verse of chapter seventeen, as I have previously indicated.

**Verse 1.** *The Judgment of the Great Whore that sits upon many waters.*
<margin>Chapter 3, Section 7.</margin>
<margin>Chapter 9, Section 9.</margin>
The *Judgment* or *Condemnation of the Great Whore*—the punishment to which she is sentenced—is a central part of this vision, and therefore the whole section bears this title. I do not need to repeat here what I have already fully taught my reader in my *Theory of Prophetic Symbols*: how in the prophetic style, a "body politic" <note>A collective group of people acting as a single political or religious entity</note> or a "multitude of people" and their "succession" over time is represented as *one individual appearance or shape*, whether *animal-like* or *human*. We called this symbolic device <term>Henopoeia</term> <note>A rhetorical tool where a group is personified as one individual</note>. Therefore, the reader will easily understand that the *Whore* is not a single or particular woman, but a symbol of a *body politic*. The fact that this body is called a *Whore* implies their *idolatry*, as I have abundantly proven in the explanation of that <term>Icasme</term> <note>original: "Icasme"; an image or representation used as a symbol</note> in my *Prophetic Alphabet*.

2. Furthermore, the fact that she is called the *Great Whore* may signify either the extreme level of her *infidelity* or the vast extent of her *jurisdiction*. The latter interpretation matches her being placed *upon many waters*. The Greek text says, "upon the many waters" <note>original: ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν πολλῶν</note>, where the second "the" seems to be demonstrative and emphatic, pointing specifically at the whole *Roman Empire*. For that is truly "those many waters"—a great sea or ocean in the prophetic style. From this, I conclude that the *Great Whore* is the *Roman Hierarchy* in a broad sense, meaning the *entire body of the idolatrous clergy throughout the Roman Empire*. However, I do not doubt that this accusation applies more notoriously to one part than another—more to the *Roman Church* than the *Greek Church*. This was especially true once the *Bishop of Rome* had taken the title of *Universal Bishop*, thereby uniquely entitling himself to all the foul failures of the Catholic Church.

# Chapters 12 and 13 of the Apocalypse

3. The vision of the *Two-horned Beast* also implies <margin>Parallelism 1, Agreement 7.</margin> a universal idolatrous corruption within the *Clergy*, occurring in both the *Eastern* and *Western* parts of the Empire. This is suggested by the *two horns* of that Beast, and also by its exercise of *all the power of the former Beast in its presence*. I will delay speaking about this until we reach the 15th verse of this chapter. Before I move on, I will only note that I proved in the previous chapter, through a clearly demonstrative method, that this *Great Whore* should not be understood as any political body that promoted idolatry while the Empire was Pagan. Instead, it refers to the Empire after it became and continued to be Christian, though contaminated with a *Pagan-like idolatry* of a new style. I have proven that this has already existed for many centuries, according to the clear meaning of this prophecy. Therefore, there should be no obstacle or doubt <note>original: "rub nor scruple"</note> regarding this.

**Verse 2. *With whom the Kings of the Earth have committed Fornication.*** That is to say, through the allurements and persuasions of this Whore, the *Kings* of the *Roman Empire* (which is called the *inhabited earth* <note>original: "οἰκουμένη" (oikoumene)</note>, as in Luke 2) have admitted and embraced idolatrous doctrines and practices, which is "Spiritual Whoredom." Perhaps this alludes to the *Ten Kings* mentioned in verse 13, who are said to *have one mind, and to give their power and strength to the Beast that the Whore rides*. ***And the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication:*** that is to say, the people of the Empire were so inflamed, intoxicated, and driven mad by the unhealthy heat of idolatrous zeal that it made them tragically quarrelsome against anyone who opposed or despised their beautiful *Diana* <note>A reference to the Roman goddess; here used to represent an idol that people defend with irrational passion</note>. It made them so foolish, overconfident, and heedless that they were exposed to all the deceits and injuries this intoxicating *Circe* <note>An enchantress from Greek mythology who turned men into animals with a magic potion</note> could inflict upon them.

2. Now, just as this *Great Whore* is said to be a promoter or restorer of idolatry, so too is the *Two-horned Beast*. Although he has *two horns like a lamb*, he is said to *speak like a dragon*, which means to <margin>Parallelism 1, Agreement 1.</margin> publish idolatrous edicts or doctrines. Furthermore, in verse 12, he is said to *cause the Earth and those who dwell in it*—meaning the Empire, as I said before—to *worship the first Beast whose deadly wound was healed*. And in verse 14, he *commands those who dwell on the Earth to make an Image to the Beast who was wounded by the sword and yet lived*. 

The meaning of the latter citation is this: the *Two-horned Beast*, through his authority and power of speech, persuaded those in the Empire (which was now purely Christian, and was therefore the death of the "Beast" as a pagan entity, as I demonstrated in the previous chapter) to reintroduce an appearance of idolatry. This was done under the pretext of better adorning and promoting Christianity. As a result, the slain Beast might justly seem to *revive* again in this *Image*. That is to say, the Empire could be said to become a "Beast" again by becoming idolatrous, just as the "death" of the Beast was the Empire’s cessation of idolatry. Therefore, to make an *Image* to the Beast that was slain is the same as making an *Image on behalf of* the Beast that was slain, so that he might at least live again in this *Image*. And it says in the very text, *and he lived again* <note>original: "καὶ ἔζησε, & revixit"</note>; so say the scholars *Vatablus* and *Grotius*. This means that upon the making of this *Image*, the slain Beast revived and lived within this *Image*.

# His Joint-Exposition of the Seventeenth Book I.

Therefore, it is no wonder that this *Two-horned Beast* is said to make *those who dwell on the Earth worship the first Beast whose deadly wound was healed*, since he was the healer and reviver of that beast and gave him the capacity to be worshipped—that is, obeyed, as I have noted in my Alphabet <note>The author's own organized list of symbolic terms and their definitions.</note>—especially in such commands as were impious and idolatrous. For this *Pagano-Christianity* <note>A term for a version of Christianity that the author believes incorporated pagan rituals and beliefs.</note> becoming the religion of the Empire, it was thereby made the law and commandment of the Empire, so that the healed Beast may be rightly said to be obeyed in the submission to it. From all this, it clearly appears that the *Two-horned Beast*, as well as the *Whore of Babylon*, was a restorer and promoter of idolatry in the Empire.

**Verse 3. *So he carried me away in the Spirit into the wilderness.*** This is not part of the vision itself, unless we treat the *Wilderness* as symbolic <note>original: "Hieroglyphical"</note>. Indeed, *Alcazar* <note>Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Spanish Jesuit theologian who interpreted Revelation.</note>, using the authority of many of the Church Fathers, makes it a symbol of *Paganism* <note>original: "Gentilism"</note>. But whether you consider the symbol or not, this *two-horned impious* or *wild beast* will naturally be understood to be in the wilderness, just as the *Whore* is declared to be there. And this Pagano-Christianity, of which they are both the authors—what is it but a kind of Paganism? So it would not have been unfitting <note>original: "inept"</note> to have made this one of the points of agreement in our first comparison <note>original: "Parallelism"</note>.

<margin>Parallelism 1, Agreement 2.</margin>
2. ***And I saw a Woman sit upon a scarlet-coloured Beast.*** Sitting upon a beast implies riding and guiding it, exciting and urging it toward this or that course as the rider pleases. Similarly, the *Two-horned Beast* is said to animate the *Seven-headed Beast* and to goad him toward those bloody edicts that seem to be alluded to in Chapter 13, verse 15: "That the revived Beast should speak, and cause as many as will not submit to him as a *Beast*—that is to say, as *idolatrous*—to be slain." This should be enough to suggest the truth of the second agreement of the first comparison: that both the *Whore* and the *Two-horned Beast* have governance and rule over the Beast with seven heads.

<margin>Parallelism 2, Agreement 2.</margin>
3. Now, as for the *scarlet color* of the Beast, it has a double meaning: one of tyrannical cruelty, and the other of imperial majesty. In the former sense, *Victorinus*, *Aretas*, *Zegerus*, *Viegas*, *Alcazar*, and others interpret it. In the latter sense, it is interpreted by *Cornelius à Lapide*, *Pareus*, *Ribera*, and *Grotius*. "The scarlet beast," says Grotius, "is surely because the cloaks of the Roman Emperors were accustomed to be dyed with that color" <note>original: "Fera coccinea, nimirum quia eo colore tingi solebant Imperatorum Romanorum Paludamenta."</note>. But where both meanings are so fitting, they are both to be understood by an *Henopoeia* <note>A rhetorical figure where several different concepts are represented by a single symbol.</note>, which brings many prefigured objects under one type. For now, however, I shall only take notice of the cruelty of the Beast as indicated by this bloody color. A similar thing is also depicted in the shape of the *Seven-headed Beast* in the thirteenth chapter, where his body is *like that of a leopard, his feet like a bear's, and his mouth like a lion's*. All of these are beasts of great prey and cruelty.

<margin>Paragraph 2. Agreement 2.</margin>
Nor is the Beast in the thirteenth chapter less remarkable for this foul sin. For just as the Scarlet Beast was full of *names of blasphemy*, dappled as it were with those black titles; so *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch jurist and theologian.</note> describes the *Leopard* as being spotted with various objects of idolatry. He is said *to blaspheme God's name* in the following verse, *and his Tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven*. To *blaspheme God* means, for example, worshipping him through *images*, or giving *religious worship* to others which is only due to him, thereby devaluing him and making him no better than a created being. To *blaspheme the Tabernacle of God* means to blaspheme the Body of Christ, in whom the *fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily* (as the Apostle speaks), by pretending that a piece of bread is the very Body of Christ. They claim this bread—which they put into that foul prison <note>A euphemism for the digestive system.</note> where a man's imagination is reluctant to descend—is that very same body, so full of stupendous glory. This glory is certainly wretchedly eclipsed when a morsel of bread is claimed to be truly him and is adored accordingly.

And, lastly, *to blaspheme those who dwell in heaven*—namely the saints—by declaring they are so ambitious and rebellious against God that they not only accept, but would actually extort religious worship from men through deaths, imprisonments, and various pressures and afflictions. This bloody Beast executes these punishments against the sincere members of Christ, having first branded them with the odious nickname of *heretics*. In this, the persecutors claim to show zeal and honor to the saints, while they are actually reproaching and blaspheming the saints as being cruel and inhumane toward men, as well as rebellious and treacherous toward God. This characterization of *blasphemy* upon the Beast is wonderfully true and significant, and we have now plainly established the second *agreement* of the second parallelism.

# His Joint-Exposition of the Seventeenth Book I.

*Adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls.* That purple and scarlet are imperial colors, we have already noted, and this is again confirmed by Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch theologian and jurist previously mentioned.</note> regarding this fourth verse. But it is appropriate here to observe that just as the Beast—which represents the entire Roman Empire—was called a "scarlet beast" even though that color was specifically for the heads of the empire (the Emperors themselves or the Senate), so too this *Whore* may be said to be *arrayed in purple and scarlet*. This refers to the Roman Hierarchy or the entire body of that clergy, even if these colors technically belong only to the Head, or at least to those higher governors of this body immediately under the chief Head. It is well known that these are the robes and habits of the *Roman Cardinals*. As for the *gold and precious stones and pearls*, this clearly refers to the Pope’s *Triple Crown* of gold, glistering with rich gems and precious stones, as well as to the pearls on his rich ceremonial robe, and so on. This shows that this vision has a more specific focus on the *Church of Rome* properly so called, though it may also glance at the entire idolatrous clergy of the Empire.

But this Head of the *Roman Hierarchy* with his *purple Cardinals* are so *emperor-like* and possess such *senatorial splendor* that it is obvious the Pope himself affects imperial power; his crown and vestments are so clearly imperial. And though the color of the Beast and the *Seventh Head*—distinct from this mitred Head <note>A "mitred head" refers to a bishop wearing a mitre; here, the Pope.</note>—implies there is an Emperor to be acknowledged as distinct from the Pope, yet this symbolic image plainly signifies that the Pope "plays the Emperor" as much as, or even more than, the actual Emperor does. This agrees wonderfully with historical events and is also plainly foretold in the 13th Chapter.

<margin>Paragraph 1. Agreement 3.</margin> Verse 12: *And he exercises all the power of the first Beast before him*; that is to say, he plays the Emperor as much or more than the Emperor himself. This must be understood especially as the *Two-horned Beast* residing at old Rome, who early on claimed the right of *Universal Bishop* and had it conferred upon him by the generosity of Phocas the Emperor. Afterward, he so greatly surpassed the Emperors that he made himself greater than they were. However, I do not hesitate to agree with Grotius that neither they nor their Empire has yet ceased to exist, just as the prophecy itself seems to testify, there being a Seventh Head of this Beast that is distinct from the Head of the *Two-horned Beast* or the *Whore*.

<margin>Paragraph 1. Agreement 3.</margin> 2. But the fact that this *Two-horned Beast* (specifically the chief and most eminent part of him) *exercises all the power of the first Beast before him* is marvelously fulfilled in the Pope playing the Emperor. For example, he wears not only a single mitre as a *Bishop*, but a *Triple Imperial Diadem* as if he were an *Emperor*. Consider also his purple vestments and crimson slippers; his title of *Our Lord God* <note>original: "Dominus Deus noster"</note>; his Senate of purple-clad Cardinals; his requirement that kings and princes kiss his feet; his receiving of tribute even from the most remote parts of the Empire; his canonizing of saints with the joint votes of the Cardinals; his sending of his legates to princes; and his revenue collected from brothels <term>stews</term>, and so on. (You may be more <margin>* Molinaeus, Various, Book 5, chapter 17.</margin> specifically informed about these and other similar matters by *Molinaeus* <note>Pierre Du Moulin (1568–1658), a prominent Huguenot (French Protestant) theologian.</note>). All of these were imitations of *Imperial Power and Dignity*. Thus, he can be said exactly to *exercise all the power of the first beast before him*.

### Chapters 12 and 13 of the Apocalypse

...eror. And this is even more obviously true because he takes all power in Church affairs away from the Emperor and exercises it solely himself. 3. *Having a golden cup in her hand, full of abominations and the filthiness of her fornications.* Regarding the word *abominations* <note>original: βδελύγματα (*bdelugmata*)</note>, Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch theologian and scholar.</note> says, "In the vision, it is understood as a foul-smelling liquid, but in reality, it refers to false gods, whom the Greeks call 'abominations'" <note>original: *In Visu quidem intelligendo humor foetens, in re verò Dii falsi, quos Graeci vocant βδελύγματα*</note>, and the Hebrews call *detestable things* <note>original: שקוצים (*shekuzim*)</note> and *abominations* <note>original: תועבות (*to'ebot*)</note>. Therefore, the *filthiness of her fornications* is the same as the former; they all signify the idolatry of the *Roman Hierarchy*. And as we have already demonstrated in the previous chapter that this *Whore* is not understood as *Pagan Rome*, this circumstance, among others, fits the Church of Rome very naturally. For this *woman with her cup in her hand* implies she is the initiator—not of a toast to health, but of this damnable pollution of idolatry. And whereas the Empire had grown chaste and indifferent to this folly and madness through the power of the pure Gospel of Christ, this woman—using this incentive, this *love potion* <note>original: *Virus amatorium*</note>—would inflame their spirits again with new lustful impulses toward *idols*, making them go astray from their God.

<margin>Chapter 8, Section 2.</margin>
4. But there is something further worth noting in this *golden cup*, which may explain the force of its bewitchment. From this it is plain that the magic and the miracles of the *Whore* and of the *Two-horned Beast* tended toward the same end: the reviving of idolatry again in the Empire, according to the fourth point of agreement in our first parallelism.

5. This thunder from that *Roman Vejovis* <note>Vejovis was an ancient Roman god associated with lightning and the power to strike down; here, the author uses it as a derogatory title for the Pope and his "thundering" decrees.</note> did not sour but rather sweetened this cup, making people drink it with a great deal of pleasure. It looked so much like the *cup of salvation* to those who drank it, once it was so authoritatively and terribly declared that those who refused it would undoubtedly perish. # Chapter 13 and the Thirteenth Chapter of the Apocalypse

I explained this when discussing the fifth verse in the previous chapter.

2. Here we shall only note that her **riding the Beast** implies her to be such a government <note>original: "Polity"</note> as had the governance of the whole Empire, and was not confined to one part of it. Just as he who rides a horse is not thought to ride only one part of him and leave the other unridden, but to ride the whole. So the **Whore** rides the whole Beast—that is, the whole Empire, both the **Eastern** <note>original: "oriental"</note> as well as the **Western** <note>original: "occidental"</note>. This agrees with the description of the **Two-horned Beast**, whom I believe is depicted this way in the Vision because of the two Imperial Patriarchates—the one at **Rome**, the other at **Constantinople**—dividing the Empire between them in a sense, just as the Eastern and Western **Caesars** did. But the entire clergy of the Empire—I mean the idolatrous clergy—are the body of this Whore or Beast, of which these two Imperial Patriarchates are the horns.

<margin>*Of the Last Times, book 2, chapter 17.*</margin>
3. Nor have I found anything yet in the other interpreters that can, according to the prophetic style, be interpreted as **Horns**, unless some such physical <note>original: "Concrete"</note> power as this may also have a place in the symbolism <note>original: "Type"</note>. But by a secondary <term>Henopaeia</term> <note>original: "Henopæia"; a rhetorical figure where several different things are unified into a single symbol.</note> (it being once admitted that these two Patriarchates are two real physical powers and dignities, for I understand the two Patriarchs themselves to be thus empowered), it may be that the **two horns** of the Bishop's Mitre are also hinted at, just as the **seven heads** signify both **seven hills** and **seven kings**. And **Joseph Acosta**, in his treatise on the *Last Times*, speaking of this Two-horned Beast, says: "Two horns are a symbol of Episcopal dignity—that is, the Mitre or the Infula (for this hat is two-horned). It appears, therefore, that this False Prophet will be some apostate Bishop and a pretender to religion" <note>original: "Duo cornua, Episcopalis dignitatis, putà Mitræ sive Infulæ, (hæc enim est Bicornis) insigne sunt. Videtur ergo quòd hic Pseudopropheta erit, Episcopus quispiam Apostata & simulator Religionis."</note>. **Cornelius à Lapide** also seems inclined toward this interpretation of the **two horns** of the Beast, and rightly understands that the interpretation is no more a reproach to the office of Bishop than the fact that there are **horns of the Lamb** <note>original: "Agni cornua"</note> is a reproach to Christ; rather, it is an argument for the excellence of that rank and function, since this great apostate endeavors to recommend himself to the world under that clothing and dignity.

Nor do we need to exclude Mr. **Mede's** interpretation, who understands these **two horns** as the power of **Binding and Loosing** <note>The biblical authority to forgive sins or impose spiritual discipline (Matthew 16:19).</note>, which this **pseudo-prophetic Beast** pretends is derived to him from the Lamb, Christ **Jesus**. For these two meanings, and more (if there were more as fit and convenient), may by a <term>Henopaeia</term> be tucked under this one symbol; provided first, as I have already said, that the symbol has one meaning plainly allowable according to the prophetic style. This style, everywhere in **Daniel** and the **Apocalypse**, understands **Horns** to mean some persons or others in high places and dignity, not abstract powers or virtues. For instance, one should not say an Emperor has **two horns** simply because he had the power of **Life** and **Death**. This is not justifiable in the prophetic style, nor would that sense alone support such a substantial emblem as this.

### His Joint-Exposition of the Seventeenth Book I.

5. **Which has the seven heads and ten horns.** The same description of the Beast in this regard is found in the thirteenth chapter, verse 2. And we have already noted that it fulfills the first agreement of the second parallelism.

**Verse VIII.** *The Beast that you saw, was, and is not, and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit and go into perdition;* **and go into perdition** <note>original: "καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγειν"</note>, that is, **into utter destruction** <note>original: "εἰς πανωλεθρίαν"</note>, or into final ruin. The context plainly implies this sense. Because it is said that before this last stage he **was not** (which implies he was previously destroyed), it naturally follows that this last destruction is a more significant one—final as well as last. Therefore, "perdition" <term>perdition</term> <note>From the Latin 'perditio', meaning utter ruin or eternal damnation; used here to signify total destruction.</note> is to be understood in the same sense as in the **Son of perdition** <note>original: "ὑιὸς ἀπωλείας"</note>, who is so called because he is to be utterly blasted and consumed by the brightness of Christ’s appearing. Consequently, this **perdition** is the very same spoken of in **Daniel**: *I watched until the Beast was slain (and he speaks there of the ten-horned Beast), and his body destroyed and given to the burning flame*, meaning it was to be utterly consumed. But because understanding this eighth verse is so important, I shall paraphrase it more extensively so that we may fully understand its aim, which I believe is as follows.

2. The Beast which you saw—and which you saw in the two former visions—is the same Beast, as shown by its primary characteristic: **seven heads** and **ten horns**. It is one and the same idolatrous kingdom or empire. This is evident from its "serpentine body" in the first vision, from the **names of blasphemy** on each head in the second, and from the **body full of names of blasphemy** in this third and last vision. However, the main purpose of this last vision (though it reflects on the earlier history of this idolatrous empire) is to represent this empire specifically during the period that began when the empire ceased to be purely Christian. This vision covers the time from when it was no longer untainted by idolatrous superstitions until the very time when idolatry, having run its course once more, is to be completely wiped out of the empire, never to return again.

3. Therefore, the Angel, counting the order of things as if on his fingers and pointing specifically at this period of time, says to John: **The Beast which you saw**, his name is (for the visionary style of prophecy easily allows for such omissions) **Was, and is not, and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit and go into perdition**. This name has fewer syllables than **Mystery, Babylon the Great, the Mother of fornications and abominations of the Earth**. <margin>Isaiah 8:1.</margin> But such long names are not unusual in Scripture, as appears in **Maher-shalal-hash-baz** <note>A symbolic name from Isaiah 8:1–4 meaning 'Hurry to the spoils!' or 'He has made haste to the plunder'.</note>, which in English is: *In making speed to the spoil he hastens the prey*.

## Chapter 17 and 13 of Revelation

The Idolatrous Empire is represented only during that period of time (according to the main purpose of this present vision) under which it would be appropriate to say: *“It is the Beast that was, and is not, but will ascend again out of the bottomless pit, and then go into perdition”*—that is to say, be finally destroyed, never to revive again. This vision of the Beast is to be understood as applying to that specific time or state of the Empire, and no other. Therefore, it was especially recommended to the Church of Christ for that season when the Empire ceased to be idolatrous.

5. The Angel, therefore, focusing his thoughts on those times of the Church, warns them in advance of a strange alteration of the Christian Empire. Even while they find it purely Christian and as yet untainted by idolatry, he warns that this pure and happy state will pass away and that the Beast will revive and come back into existence—meaning the Empire will again become idolatrous. This warning is so useful for those who receive it to strengthen them against those idolatrous innovations that would be brought into the Church. It is no wonder that the Angel's mind was fixed on those times when he solved the riddle <term>unriddled</term> <note>original: "unriddled"; to interpret or explain a mystery or prophecy.</note> of this vision for John, as if he were present among them then, forewarning them of the danger to come.

This is one way of determining the meaning of this vision for the intended time and state of the Idolatrous Empire aimed at here: by focusing our minds on those times when this "note" or "name of the Beast" is correctly applicable to him as something in the future, and not yet returned to existence—which was when the Empire was purely Christian.

6. But so that you may better understand the meaning of the vision and certainly grasp during which period of time this Idolatrous Empire is represented, the Angel says, "I will slightly change his 'note' or 'name' and call him *The Beast that was, and is not, and yet is*." This title considers him as present, although acknowledged as still to come, for it is a prophecy and not a history. But I say in this title he is considered as present, as those words most naturally imply: *“When they behold the Beast that was, and is not, and yet is.”* For we observe and watch things that are present. Therefore, "although he is" <note>original: "καίπερ ἐστὶ"</note> seems to be the more reasonable reading as well as the more authentic and approved one (and not "and shall be present" <note>original: "καὶ παρέσαι"</note>, as Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential English scholar and biblical interpreter.</note> would have it, following Arethas <note>Arethas of Caesarea (c. 860–935), a Byzantine commentator on Revelation.</note>). This denotes the Empire becoming idolatrous again as it once was, and therefore it is the Beast that *was*, yet it is also true that the Beast *is*. 

But this is not the same idolatry that consists of worshipping the ancient pagan deities like Mars, Venus, Vulcan, and so on. In this respect, it is the Beast that *was*, but *is not*. However, considering again, as I said, that only the objects of worship are changed—and that the saints are worshipped with the same kind of idolatry as the heathen deities were—it is, in that respect, pure <term>rank</term> paganism, though practiced upon new objects. Therefore, although the Beast may be said in one sense *not to be*, it is true in a very significant sense that *he is*. From this, it is evident that by the "Beast that was, and is not, and yet is," the Angel means this Roman Empire degenerated into a pagan-like or idolatrous form of Christianity; which

# His Joint-Exposition of the Seventeenth Book I.

...though it professes Christianity, it bears the image of the ancient Pagan idolatrous empire.

<margin>Parallel 2, Agreement 5.</margin>
So the *Image of the Beast* and the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is* correspond exactly to one another. For the "Image" is, and yet is not, the very thing of which it is an image, as anyone can easily acknowledge and understand. From this, the truth of the fifth agreement of our second parallelism plainly appears.

7. This interpretation that I have given of this verse is so natural and coherent that I think it would be impossible for anyone to doubt it, were it not for the obscurity arising from the elliptical <term>elliptical manner of speech</term> <note>original: "Elliptical manner of speech"; a concise way of speaking where certain words are left out, requiring the reader to fill in the gaps based on the context.</note> at the beginning of the verse: *“The Beast which you saw, was, and is not, and shall ascend, etc.”* For it seems to imply that this idolatrous Roman Empire did not exist in St. John's time, which would be contrary to historical truth. But I answer that there is an ellipsis to be supplied, and then this mistake will vanish. This addition may be made either as I have already hinted: *“The Beast which you saw, his name is: ‘Was, and is not, etc.’”* or like this: *“The Beast which you saw, was, and is not, and shall ascend, etc.”*—this is his Name, this is his character by which you shall understand during what succession of time he is to be expected.

For it should be understood that the Angel had before his sight the entire history of the Beast, divided into two parts by its temporary destruction <term>interemption</term> <note>original: "Interemption"; the act of killing, destroying, or breaking off a sequence. Here it refers to the temporary end of the Empire's idolatry.</note> during the introduction of pure Christianity into the place of Paganism, so that it might become the religion of the Empire. Now, as the Angel turned over these series of ages in his mind regarding the Beast, he could not label the first period with any title other than *“Is.”* For until that interruption of the Empire's idolatry by the victory of pure and untainted Christianity, it was not proper to say of the Beast that *“he was,”* since he was still in being; much less that *“he is not,”* as he was still in existence. Nor was it the right time to take notice of his rising again out of the bottomless pit, as he had not yet descended there; nor of his utter and final destruction <term>perdition</term> <note>original: "perdition"; state of final spiritual ruin or utter destruction.</note>, since he was destined to revive again after his first interruption.

8. Therefore, since this title was incompatible with the idolatrous empire during the first period of time it was considered, it is plain that the Angel, looking forward at these successions of ages and finding a season when the Beast ceases to be—but also foreseeing that he would rise up again and then, after a certain duration, finally perish—describes the Beast during that specific period. He titles him (in an abrupt and rapturous way, without first explaining that it is a title): *“The Beast that was, and is not, but would again emerge into being, and then finally perish.”* 

The Angel gives him this name while his eye is fixed on that interval <term>interregnum</term> <note>original: "Interregnum"; literally a period between reigns, used here to describe the gap when the Beast's idolatry had ceased.</note>—his temporary cessation from existence. Although the occasion for this name was temporary (just like that of the child who was called *Maher-shalal-hash-baz* <note>original: "Maher-shalal-hash-baz"; a prophetic name in the Bible (Isaiah 8:1) meaning "Hurry to the spoil!" or "Speed the plunder!" It served as a sign for a specific time.</note>), it may still be a permanent name for the Beast to show his place in history. For his condition and order of appearance in existence is noted here, rather than any statement about whether he existed or did not exist specifically in St. John's time. This, when duly considered and rightly understood, will easily remove the seeming difficulty of the text implying that the Beast did not exist during the time of St. John.
