### Chapter III: The Seventeenth Chapter of the Revelation

Fourthly, how wild a concept is it, again, to clap **Ten Horns** onto this one man or Beast—**Domitian**—centuries after he ceased to be? As I have noted elsewhere, **Grotius** does this when he claims these **Ten Horns** are the **Ostrogoths**, **Visigoths**, **Vandals**, **Gepids**, and others. Certainly, it would be required for **Domitian** to be raised out of Hell again to live upon Earth (as a recent author of an essay on the **Revelation** imagines) to make this part of the prophecy even slightly applicable to him. From this, the madness of **Grotius's** exposition is more fully detected, as it cannot be justified without the help of such incredible extravagances.

6. Fifthly, ***The Beast that was, and is not***, is the very same Beast which the **Whore** is said to **ride upon**, as is plain from the text: *The Beast which you saw, was, and is not*; and *the **Whore** rode upon the Beast which he saw*. Did the **Whore** (which **Grotius** interprets as **Roman Dominion** <note>original: "Dominatio Romana"</note>) therefore ride only during **Domitian's** time, and go on foot in the preceding and following ages?

Sixthly, the Beast which **John** saw, **Grotius** first interprets as **Roman Pagan Idolatry**. But was this Beast so short-lived as to be included within the space of the reign of seven Emperors? Or did this Beast live for a long time without any heads, then with seven successive heads, and then for a long time without heads again, such that it should be called the ***Beast with seven heads and no more?***

Seventhly, to call **Idolatry** in the abstract a **Beast** is entirely outside the prophetic style. To make one and the same Beast sometimes **Idolatry** and another time **Domitian** is to change substances into qualities and qualities into substances. It is to speak in contradiction to the express interpretation of the Angel himself, who says, *The Beast which you saw, was, and is not*, which in **Grotius's** method can be no one but **Domitian**. Nor is there any <term>subterfuge</term> <note>A deceptive stratagem or trick</note> to be sought in a second **Henopoeia** <note>original: "Henopœia" — a rhetorical figure where several things are unified into one</note> in this case. That figure is no shelter for bungled arguments and shifts from abstract concepts to concrete things of the same kind; rather, it is a proper way to categorize different matters that can be represented by a single symbol, as is easy to understand from what has been declared concerning that rhetorical scheme.

Eighthly, if **Domitian** is the Beast and the **Whore** is the **Roman Power**, then the **Roman Power** rides on **Domitian’s** back, as if **Domitian** were not the Head but the Body of the Empire—or, if you will, transformed by this marvelous interpretation into **Apuleius’s Ass** <note>A reference to the Roman novel *The Golden Ass*, in which a man is transformed into a donkey</note> for the **Roman Power** to ride upon. But then again, **Domitian** being the head of the **Roman Power** himself, he must by this account also ride upon himself, making a wonderful **Centaur** such as the most imaginative poets never even dreamed of.

7. Ninthly, if the **Whore** is the **Roman Pagan Power**, how can she be said to be the ***Mother of Fornications*** <note>In biblical prophecy, "fornication" often refers to idolatry or unfaithfulness to God</note>, and to intoxicate the Kings of the Earth from her cup with that kind of wickedness? For all the Earth, before the Empire became Christian, consisted of idolaters already, and they provided **Rome** herself with many various kinds of idolatry. This is an objection that neither **Grotius** nor anyone else, with all the <term>fetches</term> <note>original: "fetches" — clever tricks or stratagems</note> they have, will ever be able to <term>assoil</term> <note>original: "assoil" — to resolve, clear up, or answer</note>.

<margin>Revelation 17:5</margin>
Tenthly, this inscription on the **Whore of Babylon**: ***Babylon the Great***,

<header>A Refutation of Grotius upon Book II.</header>

The Mother of *Fornications* cannot be understood as *Pagan Rome*, as *Grotius* would have it, because the word [**Mystery**] is placed before it. This would be a very poor **Mystery** indeed if it were only a simple <term>synecdoche</term> <note>original: "Synecdoche"; a figure of speech where a part represents the whole, or vice versa</note> and meant nothing more than that *Pagan Rome* was another *Babylon*—that is to say, an idolatrous city. Oh, the depth of such a "Mystery"!

In the eleventh place, those *ten kingdoms* which *Grotius* would suggest are the *ten horns* were not kingdoms "within the borders of the Roman Empire" <note>original: "intra fines Imperii Romani"</note>, as he puts it, before the conversion of the Empire to Christianity. In fact, they did not exist before its subversion or its breaking apart into many kingdoms.
<margin>Revelation 17:13</margin>
How, then, could these *kings give their power to the Beast*? I do not mean only to *Domitian*, who is even further removed from them, but to *Roman Pagan Idolatry*, which by the time of this breakup had already ceased to be the religion of the Empire. Or how can they be said to *eat the flesh of the*
<margin>Verse 16</margin>
*Whore and burn her with fire*, when the city of *Rome* had ceased to be the *Pagan Whore* before these kings even existed? This is especially true before the city was assaulted and sacked by *Totilas* <note>The King of the Ostrogoths who captured Rome in 546 AD</note>, which occurred in the **Year 547**. By then, *Gentilism* <note>Paganism</note> had been cast out and the temples of their idols demolished all over the Empire around the year 399. This was the very year after the heathens expected Christianity to expire (based on the Devil’s mistake in calculating the proportions between the *Inward* and *Outward Court of the Temple*).

And again, in the twelfth place, how can those ten kings whom *Grotius*
<margin>Revelation 17:14</margin>
identifies be said to *fight against the Lamb* in his sense—that is, against Christianity on behalf of *Roman Pagan Idolatry*—when the Empire had already become *Christian*? The Empire was no longer that Pagan Beast to whom they would lend their aid and power against the preaching of the Gospel. Was it likely that ten such kings who were enemies of Christianity should, as *Grotius* says, "reign within the borders of the Roman Empire with the permission of the Romans themselves" <note>original: "intra fines Imperii Romani Romanis ipsis concedentibus regnare"</note>? *Grotius's* interpretation concerning the *ten horns* is impossible in every way.

8. In the thirteenth place, this destruction of *Babylon* is a perfect <term>destruction</term> <note>original Greek: "ἀπώλεια" (apōleia)</note>—a full and final ruin, symbolized by the *casting of a millstone into the midst of the sea*. But none of the *ten kings* mentioned by *Grotius* ever destroyed *Rome* in such a final manner.

<margin>Revelation 18:4</margin>
In the fourteenth place, that exhortation to the People of God to *go out of Babylon, lest they partake of her sins*, makes no sense in the time of *Totilas*. Would the Angel have all the Christians leave the city of *Rome* in the year 546 (and for several years leading back toward *Constantine's* time) simply because there might still be some pagan idolaters among them? Would they not rather stay in the city to better suppress and completely extinguish idolatry, rather than letting it spread further because the sincere Christians had left? Truly, this interpretation <note>original: "gloss"</note> by *Grotius* is very ridiculous and incredible; it suggests the Angel uttered such an irrational command.

Fifteenthly, if the command ["Come out of her, my people, lest you partake of her sins"] means, as *Grotius* interprets: "You, my people, when the army of Totila appears, go out to the Basilicas of the Apostles outside the city" <note>original: "Tu popule mi, ubi apparuerit Totila exercitus, exite ad Basilicas Apostolorum extra Urbem"</note>, it would follow that to have returned to the city after *Totilas* was gone would have been to return into *Babylon* and partake of her sins again. This is a very foolish and absurd idea.

9. Lastly,

## CHAPTER IV.

1. *That this mis-timing of visions must necessarily lead Grotius into similar absurdities in interpreting the thirteenth chapter, and that his exposition of the first verse contains at least nine or ten.* 2. *Four gross contradictions in the second verse.* 3. *As many inconsistencies or weaknesses in the third.* 4. *The same in the fourth and fifth.* 5. *Two absurdities in the sixth and seventh.* 6. *The same in the eighth.* 7. *Three difficulties in the exposition of the tenth verse.* 8. *Five inconsistencies in the eleventh.* 9. *His crude interpretation of the twelfth verse.* 10. *Four absurdities in the thirteenth.* 11. *Eight inconsistencies or weaknesses in his expositions on the fourteenth verse.* 12. *Three in the fifteenth.* 13. *Three or four more in the sixteenth and seventeenth.* 14. *And nine more in the eighteenth verse.* 15. *An astonishing consideration of the absurdity of Grotius’s expositions compared with his great talent and learning.* 16. *A useful conclusion from his weak performance: that all the interpretations by the Roman Catholics regarding these two chapters are extremely trivial and unbelievable.*

1. There are so many inconsistencies and contradictions—if not outright impossibilities—in the interpretation of the seventeenth chapter. In the first verse, he claims the *Beast with seven heads and ten horns* represents *Roman idolatry*. Regarding this, I will only point out that such <gloss>1</gloss> minor kings as some of these were—especially in comparison to the *Roman* Empire—hardly deserve to be called its "horns." Furthermore, <gloss>2</gloss> regarding idolatry, it is as if they were its specific defenders; yet no history mentions them attacking anyone so significantly on its behalf. In fact, *Judea* is a very inappropriate "horn" for an idolatrous "head" to wear. Additionally, <gloss>3</gloss> their wearing of crowns seems too magnificent an...

A meager decoration for those who are acknowledged (besides the smallness of the territories of some of them) to be tributaries to the Roman State. So the interpretation seems quite weak regarding these **Ten Kings**, and the prophecy appears useless, as it offers no information to the Church that might be helpful at any time.

<margin>Revelation 17</margin>
But now concerning the Beast itself: besides the fact that it does not follow the prophetic style to interpret a "Beast" as a vice rather than a <term>Body Politic</term> <note>A "Body Politic" refers to a state, empire, or organized political society.</note>, how can **Roman Idolatry** be represented by it? It is said to *ascend out of the Sea*, which Grotius admits means "to have an origin" <note>original Latin: *ortum habere*</note>. But Roman Idolatry could not be shown to St. John as something that would arise in the future, since it had existed in the world for many ages and was still continuing. Therefore, it was not to begin with the forty-two months to come, nor was it to end with them in Grotius's sense. Furthermore, the deifying of their **Caesars** did not create a "new" idolatry any more than adding other deities to their worship did. Nor did that idolatry continue for only forty-two months, as Grotius interprets "months" in this place. I say that neither Roman idolatry nor cruelty continued for only forty-two months; and therefore, the Beast described here cannot be "Idolatry raging in a beast-like manner" <note>original Latin: *Idololatria ferino more saviens*</note> in the sense Grotius intends.

Add to all this that making the **Seven Heads** represent the **Seven Hills** of Rome is a very unlikely explanation here. First, in the previous chapter, these heads are said to be **crowned**, which is not appropriate for hills. Second, in this chapter, one of them is **wounded** and **healed again**, which is just as inappropriate for these dead heaps of earth. Furthermore, it is very clumsy to attach seven literal heads and ten literal horns to a Beast that is supposedly an abstract concept <note>The author argues that you cannot put physical parts (heads/horns) onto a non-physical idea (idolatry).</note>. This is as nonsensical as saying the body of a bull is "Redness" in the abstract, and then placing a solid head and horns made of hard bone and flesh upon it. If a person is careful enough to count, they will find Grotius's interpretation guilty of at least nine or ten weaknesses or inconsistencies in this very first verse. But we proceed.

<margin>Verse 2</margin>
2. In the second verse, he makes **Claudius** the body of this beast (which is **panther-like**) and **Domitian** its mouth; nothing could be more outlandish than this. Since he acknowledges this Beast with seven heads and ten horns to also be "Roman Idolatry" in the 17th chapter, it follows that: 1. **Claudius** is both the body of the Beast and one of its heads; and 2. **Domitian** is the body, a head, and the mouth, as may be seen from what was noted in the previous chapter. Also, and this is as nonsensical as anything else, with **Claudius** being the body of the Beast and **Domitian** being the mouth, the body would be without a mouth for as many years as there were between the reigns of Claudius and Domitian—which was about forty years. Furthermore, the **Dragon** giving his power and throne to the Beast cannot be a prophecy of Roman Idolatry receiving it, because that had happened many ages before.

<margin>Revelation 13:3</margin>

Now, first, I say that it is a strained metaphor to say a building made of wood or stone is "wounded to death and then healed." But even if we suppose the Capitol was "wounded," the hill was not...

### Chapter IV. The Thirteenth Chapter of the Apocalypse

...not hurt, or at least not wounded to death. So, unless there were seven **Capitols** as well as seven Hills, the notion is very difficult to accept. But if you leave the **Capitol** and focus on the Hill, the Hill can no more be said to be wounded than a man's head can be said to be wounded when only his hat is cut. Again, the main point aimed at by **Grotius** in interpreting this **wounded head** as the fall of the **Capitol** is not true. $^3$ For idolatry was not lessened at all by the fall of the **Capitol**. Nor did the **Romans** fear that the worship of idols would fall after it; rather, they feared that the Empire would be ruined by the invasion of the Northern Nations. It is for this reason that the omen **"Rome, you shall rise again"** <note>original Latin: *Roma resurges*</note> is inscribed upon **Vespasian's** coin. And lastly, since it is said that all the world wondered at the Beast upon the healing of his deadly wound, it is obvious that some $^4$ more extraordinary thing than the rebuilding of the **Capitol** must be understood by it. For was it any wonder, enough to strike the whole world with awe, that the **Capitol** should be built up again by such a rich city and the mistress of the world? Truly, the great wonder would have been if they had *not* rebuilt it.

4. In the fourth section, he interprets **"And they worshipped the beast"** <note>original Greek: *καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ*</note> as **"They were slaves to idolatry"** <note>original Latin: *Idololatriae inservierunt*</note>. This is as if it were written, $^1$ **"They worshipped idolatry"** <note>original Greek: *προσεκύνησαν τῇ εἰδωλολατρείᾳ*</note>, which is a very awkward phrase. 

In the fifth section, **Domitian** is made the "Mouth" of the Beast, as was said before, and by attributing the reign of the Beast to him, $^2$ he represents the whole Beast. This is because **Domitian's** persecution is supposed to have lasted only three and a half years; for he began to persecute, says **Grotius**, in the thirteenth year of his reign and was killed in the sixteenth. $^3$ But this does not prove that his persecution was exactly three and a half years long; and **Baronius** <note>Cesare Baronius (1538–1607) was an influential Catholic cardinal and historian.</note> and other chronologists place the beginning of that persecution in the tenth year of his reign. Besides, $^4$ the text does not say, "He shall persecute for three years and a half," but rather that he shall **continue** for so long. But **Domitian** continued for more than three and a half years, for he reigned sixteen years according to **Grotius's** own admission.

5. In the sixth and seventh sections, he still identifies **Domitian** as the Beast. He explains the passage [***And there was power given him over every tribe, and people, and language***] as the power of his example leading to a more shameless practice of idolatry. That is one excuse <note>original: "shift"</note>. Another is this: that in his reign the **Dacians**, **Chatti**, and **Sarmatians** <note>Tribes from the borders of the Roman Empire in modern-day Romania, Germany, and Eastern Europe.</note> were overcome, and **Roman** idolatry was spread as a result—as if their idolatry were worse than that of those barbarians. But let anyone judge if such a weak <note>original: "lank"</note> and improper sense as this can fulfill the meaning of the prophecy, which speaks of a $^1$ **political**, not moral, power over the nations, and of something that is $^2$ **new**. But the fact that the **Roman Empire** had such a large dominion was true in the reigns of the previous Emperors as well as in his.

6. In the eighth section, he identifies the Beast—whom everyone (whose names are not in the Book of Life) worships—as **Domitian** in one explanation. He says that to $^1$ **worship** him is to imitate him in idolatry and cruelty. This is a very dull <note>original: "insipid"</note> interpretation, and there is no other example of such a meaning; he himself seems to lose confidence in it. Therefore, in his later explanation, **Domitian** is not the Beast, but **Idolatry** itself is—as if to $^2$ **worship idolatry** were a more acceptable phrase. But there must necessarily be this shifting and maneuvering <note>original: "fridging"</note>

...when an interpretation fits as poorly on a text as this one does.

7. In the tenth verse, *If any one strikes with the sword, he shall perish by the sword*, Grotius applies this to **Domitian**, who was stabbed by his servant **Stephanus**. But it seems to be $^1$ most natural to believe that the threats of *being led into captivity* and *perishing by the sword* were spoken about the same party. Therefore, since *captivity* is not understood to refer to **Domitian**, his being struck by the sword should not be understood as referring to him either. Instead, the prophecy concerns a **political body** <note>original: "Body Politick"</note>, and not a **single person**. For the $^2$ *patience and faith of the saints* also seems to imply a much broader exercise of these virtues than a period of three and a half years would require of them. There also seems to be an indication of being $^3$ freed from their troubles after this Beast is defeated; but if **Domitian** is that beast, not even the smallest part of their troubles ended with his death, as there were no fewer than eight grievous persecutions remaining afterward. Not to mention that there was a greater affliction upon the Christians in **Nero's** time than in **Domitian's**, whom **Tertullian** <note>An early Christian author (c. 155 – c. 220 AD) from Carthage.</note> calls merely "a portion of Nero" <note>original Latin: *Portionem Neronis*</note>. Therefore, the *faith and patience of the saints* were most exercised then. This further reveals the groundless and arbitrary nature of **Grotius's** explanation.

8. In the eleventh verse, he claims the **Beast with two horns like a lamb** represents the **art of magic**, and the **two horns themselves** represent **abstinence from certain foods** and **chastity** (or abstinence from women). He argues these were an imitation of Christianity and were therefore called the *horns of a lamb*. But because this Beast is said to *speak like a dragon*, it is implied that what he utters is for the honor of the **Devil**. There are several flaws in this interpretation: 
1. The **Beast** is described as an **art**, not a **political body**, which goes against the rules of prophetic style. 
2. The **horns** are interpreted as fake virtues rather than political powers held by certain men; political power is the genuine meaning of *horns* in the language of the Prophets, and this meaning should be established first before adding any other secondary meaning to the symbol. 
3. **Vowed celibacy and abstinence from foods** are so far from being the defining virtues of Christianity that they are actually rejected by it, being either parts or signs of the **Great Apostasy** <note>A term often used by Protestant reformers to describe what they saw as the fallen state of the Roman Catholic Church.</note> that was to take over the Church. 
4. There is a clear contradiction in the nature of this Beast: looking Christian-like but speaking for the Devil. However, if this Beast were **magic**, it would be strange if it did not speak the language of the Dragon. 
Lastly, the time period **Grotius** assigns to this prophecy—the reigns of **Domitian** and **Trajan**—does not fit his idea. These Emperors did not favor **magic**; in fact, the former was a persecutor of it, and specifically of that very **Apollonius** <note>Apollonius of Tyana, a famous first-century philosopher and reputed magician whom Grotius attempted to link to the prophecy.</note> whom Grotius believes is specifically pointed at in this prophecy.

9. In the twelfth verse, he claims that the **two-horned Beast exercising all the power of the former Beast before him** means that **magic** also had its own sacrifices just as idolatry did. But truly, although **magic** had sacrifices like idolatry, they were secret <note>original: "clancular," meaning hidden or underhanded</note> ones, because they were so horrible and cursed. **Philostratus** <note>A Greek writer (c. 170 – 247 AD) who wrote a famous biography of Apollonius of Tyana.</note> goes out of his way several times to clear **Apollonius** of that suspicion. This is a sign that **magic** did not have such an open practice of its abhorred sacrifices as this text would imply if **Grotius's** interpretation were true...

He bestows <margin>Natural History, book 30, chapter 1.</margin> this finishing praise <note>original: *Epiphonema*</note> upon the *Roman* State for doing so: *It cannot be sufficiently estimated how much is owed to the Romans, who removed these monsters, in which it was considered a religious act to kill a man, and indeed most beneficial for the world.* <note>original: *Non satis æstimari potest quantum Romanis debeatur qui sustulere monstra, in quibus hominem occidere religiosum erat, mundi verò etiam saluberrimum.*</note> And this certainly is properly that *Magic* which was distinguishable from pagan idolatry simply so called (which worshipped and invoked the Devil as well as the magicians did); but it was such that the *Roman* idolatry would not allow her to exercise her power in her sight upon any pretense. Nor did *Apollonius* exercise any such power, as he was a *Pythagorean* <note>A follower of the philosopher Pythagoras, who practiced vegetarianism and non-violence.</note> who abhorred all bloody sacrifices whatsoever.

10. In the thirteenth verse, Grotius interprets the *bringing down of fire from Heaven* as that lightning which happened at *Apollonius'* birth, and as that glimpse of light that *Achilles'* ghost gave at his departure after *Apollonius'* conference with him by night at his tomb. This is a very weak <note>original: "frigid"</note> interpretation. For why should that lightning which happened at *Apollonius'* birth be attributed to him as an effect of his magic, $^1$ when he was neither capable then of being a magician nor anything else? Besides, he was born before this prophecy was written, as *Grotius* himself must acknowledge and admit according to his own timeline; therefore, $^2$ on that ground, the interpretation is impossible. Also, that the glimpse of light which *Achilles'* ghost gave at his parting should be the act of *causing fire to fall from Heaven* is altogether incredible; $^3$ for this glimpse of light was upon the earth where the ghost was, and did not fall from the sky. Furthermore, it happened in $^4$ private, as the story in *Philostratus* <note>The biographer of Apollonius of Tyana.</note> will prove, and not *in the sight of men* <note>original Greek: *enōpion tōn anthrōpōn*</note>, which means in the face or view of the world.

11. In the fourteenth verse, he interprets the *making of an Image to the Beast* as *Apollonius'* boasting that he had raised up the ghost of *Achilles* in favor of idolatry. But who ever interpreted "to make an image" <note>original Greek: *poiēsai eikona*</note> (which means to make an image, picture, or statue) as raising a ghost? For even supposing "image" <note>original Greek: *eikōn*</note> could mean the same as "shadow" or "ghost" <note>original Latin: *Umbra*</note> (of which, nonetheless, I dare say there is no example), yet "to make an image" would not make good sense; because these "ghosts" are not *made* by magical summonings, but are only made to *appear*. 2. The text would not have said "to make" <note>original Greek: *poiēsai*</note>, which ordinarily signifies no more than "to do" <note>original Greek: *poiein*</note>, but rather "to have made" <note>original Greek: *pepoiēkenai*</note>, if it were a boast of something already done, and not a precept or command to do something. 3. If the sense were "saying that he had made" <note>original Greek: *legōn pepoiēkenai*</note>, it would also have been written—to continue the sense in the following verse—*and that it was given to him to give* <note>original Greek: *kai hoti edothē autō dounai*</note>, as anyone who observes the context of the whole sentence will acknowledge. Lastly, whereas Grotius suggests this conjuring of the ghost of *Achilles* was intended to revive the Beast who had the deadly wound, this contradicts what was acknowledged before: that this wound was healed by the rebuilding of the *Capitol*. Nor can this healing be naturally understood as anything more than the first-mentioned wound which the Beast received in the *Battle with Michael* <note>Referring to the war in heaven described in Revelation 12.</note>.

Lastly, it is a weak point <note>original: "lank business"</note> to take notice of one single statue for idolatry when there were already innumerable numbers of them in the Empire.

In the fifteenth verse, he interprets the Two-horned Beast's *giving life or breath to the Image, so that it would speak*, as referring to *Apollonius*'s conversation with the ghost of *Achilles*, or his own statue speaking. But even suppose his statue did speak (which *Philostratus*, who made it his business through travel and inquiry to know where *Apollonius* was buried, does not mention), it is not immediately to be attributed to magic, since such speaking by idols <note>original: "idol-garrulity"</note> is often noted in history without any such interpretation. 2. That *Image* which is said here to speak is also said to command that those who would not worship the Image of the Beast should be killed; but there is no record of any such edict from either the ghost of *Achilles* or the statue of *Apollonius* stating that those who would not worship their images should be put to death. 3. Furthermore, if the worship of the *Image of the Beast* is understood as a general reference to all images or idols, it is extremely difficult and forced to change the established meaning of the word "image" used three times before. Additionally, there is no proof that either the statue of *Apollonius* or the specter of *Achilles* ever gave a command that those who refused to worship images should be killed.

13. In the sixteenth and seventeenth verses, "And he causes all" <note>original: Καὶ ποιεῖν πάντας</note> seems most naturally to be spoken regarding the *Image of the Beast* in the preceding verse, of whom it was said "to make" <note>original: τὸ ποιῆσαι</note>. This was allegedly either the ghost of *Achilles* or the statue of *Apollonius*. But here, suddenly, *Magic* <note>original: *Magia*</note> is substituted as the subject, which is a strained explanation <note>original: "harsh shift"</note>. It is this *Magic* that supposedly makes all ranks of men enter into some religious society or another and, as a token of this, receive either the mark of a specific god—such as a thunderbolt for *Jupiter*, an ivy leaf for *Bacchus*, a helmet for *Mars*, or a trident for *Neptune*—or the names of such gods, or the number contained in their names; otherwise, they are not permitted to buy or sell.

Against this, I argue: 1. That the "Mark of the Sealed" <note>Referring to the 144,000 in Revelation 7 who receive God's seal.</note> is not a visible puncture or branding <term>stigmatism</term> <note>original: "stigmatism"; in this context, the act of branding or marking a person's skin, often used for slaves or devotees in the ancient world.</note>, and therefore it is likely that in a book as symbolic as the *Apocalypse* is, the *Mark of the Beast* does not signify something so literal and physical. 2. These fraternities or societies were not the result of *Apollonius*'s magic during the time of *Trajan*, as they were in use long before. Lastly, it is not credible, nor is there any history to support it, that no pagan could buy or sell unless he had such a sacred brand upon his body. This part of *Grotius*'s interpretation is entirely inadequate and groundless.

14. In the eighteenth verse, he claims that *Ulpius Trajanus* <note>The Roman Emperor Trajan (reigned 98–117 AD).</note> is the one to whom the number 666 belongs; but this is very groundless, and indeed against all reason. For it is a total mistake for him to think that the *Number* refers to the number of just any man's name whatsoever, because it is expressly said

And *Ribera* <note>Francisco Ribera (1537–1591) was a Spanish Jesuit theologian who wrote a highly influential commentary on the Book of Revelation.</note> removes any reason for such an error, interpreting the phrase ["*For it is the Number of a man*"] according to the mind of *Aretas* <note>Aretas of Caesarea (860–935) was a Byzantine commentator on the Apocalypse.</note> (or at least according to what he thought should have been his mind as well as his own) in quite another sense: "For number is properly human, and it belongs to one who has understanding and reason to count." <note>original: "Numerus enim proprius hominis est, & intellectum habentis ac ratiocinantis est numerare."</note>

2. If it were the "Number of a man," intended to identify someone most notably wicked and harmful to the Church, why must it be assigned to *Trajan*, when there were Emperors far worse than he? Indeed, he was a very good Emperor and not nearly as cruel a persecutor of the Christians as several others were; he was even one who easily stopped his persecutions once he was properly informed of the facts. He gained so much respect from the Christians themselves that they thought he had attained Heaven, and among the pagans, he was the subject of that favorable shout of the Senate to their *Caesars*: "Luckier than Augustus, better than Trajan!" <note>original: "Felicior Augusto, Melior Trajano"</note>

4. It is also very weak and suspicious to find this number in his *Prænomen* (forename) and not in his actual name.

Therefore, the total sum of the Name will not be 666, but 860, as anyone who calculates can see. For it is plain in the names *Neilos* (Nile), *Iesous* (Jesus), *Lateinos* (Latin), and several other examples that *Sigma*, even at the end of a word, signifies 200. This is most certainly true, and there is no excuse to avoid it, as *Maresius* <note>Samuel Maresius (1599–1673), a French Protestant theologian and a fierce critic of Hugo Grotius.</note>, Grotius's opponent, has fully proven against him. Indeed, Maresius has defeated him nearly everywhere, even though *Grotius* so inappropriately despises him, trampling him into the dirt under that insulting nickname of *Borborita* <note>A term of abuse meaning "filthy" or "mired in mud," used by Grotius to mock Maresius's character or arguments.</note>.

6. The Mark, the *Name*, and the *Number* all belong to the same person; therefore, if the *Number* belongs to *Trajan*, the Mark must be his as well. But was it true that nobody could buy or sell unless they had his mark on their hand or forehead?

7. "*Here is wisdom; let him that has understanding count the Number of the Beast*" is a preface that implies a different kind of numbering than simply adding up the numerical values of the letters in a name.

8. To what purpose was the setting down of the number 666 to denote the Emperor *Ulpius Trajanus*, when it never entered anyone's head that this number referred to him until *Grotius* happened upon it—and got it wrong at the same time?

9. And lastly, even if *Ulpios* did contain exactly 666 (as it most certainly contains 860), it would follow that there would be no obstacle to *Trajan* being that first Beast in the vision, according to *Grotius*'s explanation. But we must also remember that he had previously claimed *Domitian* was that Beast, and *Claudius* as well; so for him, a *Triumvirate* <note>A group of three people holding power.</note> of Beasts is somehow just *One* Beast. Furthermore, he claims it must be "Idolatry" in the abstract as well—which is grossly against our second rule of correctly interpreting prophecies. Thus, *Grotius*'s explanation of these two chapters of the Apocalypse is infinitely forced, distorted, groundless, contradictory, and inconsistent throughout.

And plainly, that part of anti-Christianity which consists of idolatry is foreshadowed and foretold in these visions, as we have explained in our *Joint-Exposition*.

1. Therefore, having cleared the path of all opponents and secured the correct sense of these two chapters of the *Book of Revelation*—since there is nothing strained or forced in our explanation of them, but everything follows the acknowledged laws of prophetic interpretation in the four rules I have laid down, and the usual meaning of the symbols noted in my *Prophetic Alphabet*—let us now take notice of a few important <term>consectaries: logical conclusions or deductions that follow from a previous argument</term>. These are partly contained in, and necessarily flow from, the continued and perpetual firmness of our *Joint-Exposition* of these chapters. First:

->Deduction 1.<-

<margin>* Revelation 17:10</margin>
<margin>See *Mystery of Godliness*, Book 5, Chapter 15, Section 2.</margin>
*That the forty-two months, which represent the duration of the seven-headed Beast with ten horns after the healing of his wounded head, are not months of days, but 1260 years.*

This necessarily follows from our *Joint-Exposition*, in which we have clearly demonstrated that the *Beast whose deadly wound was healed* and the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is* are absolutely and completely the same *Beast*. Therefore, they must of necessity have the same duration. But the duration of the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is* cannot be understood as forty-two literal months; therefore, those months must have a symbolic meaning and be interpreted as "months of years," just as there are "weeks of years" in the Book of Daniel. Now, the fact that the duration of forty-two months cannot be literally understood regarding the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is* is plain from this: it is said of the seventh King that he *should <note>original: "stay but a short space"</note> remain only for a short time.* This must be a specific characteristic of him, distinct from both the king immediately preceding and the one immediately succeeding him. This implies that both of those kings would remain longer than he did. And yet, that short-lived King continued for at least a hundred years, as history shows and as will be further demonstrated in the following deduction. Consequently, the *Beast* that *was and is not* must necessarily continue for more than three and a half years—indeed, for more than a hundred years. Since forty-two literal months are not fit to represent this length of time, it is manifest that these "months" signify 1260 years, which was the point to be proved.

->Deduction 2.<-

*That the Church was free from idolatry and anti-Christian corruption until about four hundred years after Christ.*

2. This is a primary truth and a mighty bulwark against the rampant fury of many fanatical sects that would reform everything into utter confusion, ugliness, and destruction, under the pretense of calling anything "idolatrous" or "anti-Christian" that does not agree with their own <note>original: "phancy"</note> imagination. But this deduction serves as a protection for the greatest and most significant truths of Christianity. It is as if the finger of God has signed off on the general consensus of the Church regarding those things that were then universally held or concluded in Councils—confirming that they were neither idolatrous nor anti-Christian.

### Consectaries from his Joint-Exposition. Book II.

<margin>*Revelation 17:10*</margin>
3. Now, the truth of this <term>consectary: a logical conclusion or deduction</term> is shown as follows: Regarding the Seventh King, who is called "the other" <note>original Greek: *ho allos*</note> (and whom I have proved to be the purely Christian Emperors), it is said of him that he must **continue for a short time**. Unless the prophecy is speaking entirely indefinitely and defines nothing by this, it must reasonably be thought to be about a third of the duration that this expression implies to be "long." This is because "short" and "long" are not absolute terms, but relative or comparative; they are two extremes that imply a middle ground. Therefore, we cannot better establish the definite concept of these terms than by imagining a line divided into three equal parts. We would look upon the whole line as representing "long," two-thirds of the line as representing "middle ground," and one-third as representing "short." From this, we may gather a universal rule for what proportion (to speak accurately and mathematically) "short" and "long" must bear to one another: in a strict sense, that which is exactly one-third of another thing is "short" in comparison to it. However, in common speech, even if it is a little more or less, it will <note>original: "break no squares"; an idiom meaning it will make no significant difference</note>.

There must either be some such way as this to establish this concept, or else "short" and "long" will signify nothing and be words spoken at random—except in cases where there is a known standard for the middle ground. For example, when we say a "tall man" or a "short man," it is taken for granted that an average height is a certain number of feet and no more. Having seriously considered the necessity of some definite concept for these two terms, and how naturally they fall into this proportion, I could not help but agree with such a clear <margin>*Mystery of Godliness, Book 5. Ch. 16. Sect. 9.*</margin> conviction. This is true even though I might rightly seem biased against it because of what I have written elsewhere concerning "a short time" <note>original Greek: *mikron chronon*</note>; however, I had not then weighed the matter as accurately as I have now.

4. If we accept that this is the genuine sense of the terms "short" and "long" as I have proposed, and we compare the duration of the Seventh King with the duration of the Sixth King (that is to say, the **Pagan Caesars**, who reigned from Julius Caesar to Constantine for about 360 years), it is plain that the duration of the Seventh King (the **Christian Caesars**) must be 120 years or thereabouts. When added to the year AD 312, when Constantine was converted to Christianity, this brings us to the year 432. I would not claim this is so strictly defined as to require mathematical precision in the proportion of "short" and "long," but rather allows for some latitude, as is appropriate for common speech. Nevertheless, it is necessary to refer to this mathematical idea so we can judge whether the use of these terms is reasonable or far-fetched.

What I leave more flexible here will be more specifically limited by the proportion of the **Inward** and **Outward Court of the Temple**. That calculation will restrict this time to slightly less than 400 years, but in a way that makes this current method of calculation very adaptable to it. For if we suppose the "short" term (120 years) is subdivided into three degrees or parts, anything above two-thirds of that may rationally be considered "short" in the first degree of comparison. And we must remember that the duration of the restored Beast is calculated by "months of years," which, as I noted above, suggests a margin of error of up to thirty years in the computation.

This conclusion is perfectly clear from the three preceding ones; it is unnecessary to add anything further to clarify it. If you wish, see my *Mystery of Godliness*, Book 5, Chapter 17, Section 10.

The *Whore* (who is *Antichrist*) is said to sit upon this Beast. The *Two-horned Beast* is the idol-worshipping clergy of the Empire under the two imperial <term>patriarchates: the primary jurisdictions of high-ranking bishops</term> of *Rome* and *Constantinople*. It is also proved that the *Whore* and the *Two-horned Beast* are one and the same, which fully confirms this sixth conclusion.

### <term>Confectary: A logical conclusion or deduction</term> VII.

> *That the ruin of the Fourth Monarchy, and the introducing of the Fifth—which is the Kingdom of the Saints of the Most High, as Daniel calls it—does not imply wars, looting, or the invading of the rights of any Prince or people (according to the style of prophecy). Rather, it merely means the renewing of the Empire into an evangelical purity in doctrine, worship, and Christian life.*

6. This is clearly shown in our **Joint-Exposition**, where it is manifest that the **Beast** (which represents the Roman Monarchy) is said to be slain and no longer <note>original Latin: *in rerum natura*</note> "in the nature of things" merely because pagan idolatry was expelled from it, or ceased to be the religion of the Empire. Similarly, the **Beast** was revived from the dead and brought into being again merely by re-introducing idolatry into the Empire and by <term>paganizing: treating Christian figures or symbols as if they were pagan idols</term> the objects of Christianity. 

This can also be further confirmed from the sixth Seal, where Heaven and Earth seem to fall together and the entire political universe appears to be dissolved; yet the Roman Empire itself remained in existence—there was only a change from paganism to the Christian faith. Regarding this sixth Seal, <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638) was a famous English scholar and influential interpreter of the Book of Revelation.</note> Mr. Mede himself notes the following: <note>original Latin: *Jam verò Mutationis hujuſce Objectum eſt Imperium Romanum; at non quà politicè à Cæſaribus gubernatum, ſed quà Satanæ principi ejúſque Angelis Dæmonibus religioſo nomine ſubditum.*</note> "Now indeed, the object of this change is the Roman Empire; but not as it was politically governed by the Caesars, but as it was subject to the prince Satan and his demon angels in a religious sense."

Therefore, it is evident that according to the prophetic style, this fourth idolatrous monarchy may be destroyed merely by once again exterminating idolatry and whatever is <term>Antichristian: contrary to the teachings or spirit of Christ</term> from within it. At that point, by that very fact, the true Kingdom of the Saints of the Most High begins—even if not a hair on any man's head falls to the ground, and no Prince or subject is injured in any of their rights or possessions. This conclusion is exceedingly clear and highly useful for calming the furious heat of certain fanatics who expect the Kingdom of the Saints to be like the worldly kingdom the Jews expected from a Messiah—one that would serve their own worldly advantage. But the love of the world has blinded the judgments of both groups alike.

### Confectary VIII.

> *That no exposition of the seventeenth chapter of the Apocalypse, which does not make the <note>original Greek: *ho allos*</note> "other" (or the Seventh King) purely Christian, can be true and perfect.*

7. This will be easily seen if we consider the wonderful harmony found, based on this supposition, between the thirteenth and seventeenth chapters of Revelation. In one chapter, the Beast is said *to be slain*, and in the other, it *ceases to be*. In one, it is the *revived image* of the Beast; in the other, it is the *Beast that was, is not, and yet is*. Although there are *eight kings*, there are only *seven heads* of the Beast; nothing can explain this except this hypothesis. For while the "other" (the seventh king) reigned, the Beast did not exist. 

However, if that head were not purely Christian but idolatrous, the Beast would still have been in existence and would have had eight heads in the Angel's own calculation. But it is plain that the Beast is supposed to cease existing, based on those words: *Was, and is not, and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit*. That excellent interpreter, Mr. Mede, failed to give the genuine sense of these words because he lacked this supposition. For he says it may be said...

### Conclusion IX.
### That the Whore of Babylon does not sit now at Constantinople, but that Old Rome is, if we may so speak, her Imperial Seat.

8. The truth of this conclusion appears from several points in our **Joint-Exposition**:

1. That the ***Whore of Babylon*** rides upon the ***Roman Empire*** and guides and governs it in matters of religion; this is not true of the ***Turk*** <note>The author uses "the Turk" to refer to the Ottoman Empire and its Sultan.</note> at ***Constantinople***. 

2. The ***Whore*** sits upon that city of seven hills that was, as it were, the ***Lady of the World*** in Saint ***John’s*** time (which is given as the surest characteristic of her seat), which we know ***Constantinople*** was not at that time. 

3. The Name of the Beast is found to be *Lateinos* <note>original Greek: Λατεῖνος, meaning "the Latin one" or "Roman." In the system of gematria, where letters represent numbers, this name totals 666.</note>. And though Bishop ***Montagu*** <note>Richard Montagu (1577–1641), a controversial English bishop and scholar.</note> has shown his wit and humor in finding the number 666 in the name *Maometis* <note>original Greek: Μαομέτις, a variation of the name Muhammad.</note>, I think he did it only to joke with his despised opponents and to play upon their ignorance. For how can 666 be supposed to mean the name of ***Muhammad***, whose name is written so variously by ***Greek historians***? For in the writings of ***Nicetas*** he is called *Moamet*; in ***Chalcocondylas***, *Mechmetes*; in ***Joannes Cantacuzenus***, *Machomet*; in ***Ducas Michael***, *Mechemet*; and finally in ***Joannes Cananus***, *Moameth* and *Machemete*. But he is nowhere called *Maometis* that I can find, nor is it likely that his name would end in *-tis*, but rather *-tes*. So I suspect that it is only a witty fiction <note>original Latin: *commentum*</note> of the Bishop’s to amuse himself.

4. The fame of the ***seven hills*** at ***Rome*** so overshadows any other that it is unlikely they are anything but the chief target in the description of the seat of the ***Whore***. If only one of the cities were intended, it would be intolerable to imagine that the prophecy is so slippery and flawed that—when there were two cities, one extremely famous for its seven hills and the other so little famous for them that it is frequently questioned whether it has seven hills at all—it should mean the latter and not the former. There is no hint in the text to suggest the latter or any way to favor it.

5. The ***Whore*** or ***Antichrist*** who sits on the seven hills existed many hundred years (as shown by the fourth conclusion) before the ***Turk*** was master of ***Constantinople***, which happened not much more than two hundred years ago. 6. Upon the forehead of the ***Whore of Babylon*** is written "***Mystery***"; but the ***Turk*** is an open and professed enemy of Christians.

### Chapter VI. The Demonstration of certain Synchronisms.

Since all agree that the true Church never ceased to exist, there must necessarily run alongside the times of the *Whore* or *Two-horned Beast* the *Virgin-Company* and these *Mournful Witnesses* in corresponding opposition to them. The latter exists because of a direct causal connection with the former. Therefore, this may serve as an example of the first method of proof mentioned, though it was not illustrated before.

The subject matter of those two mixed visions is also necessarily implied to occur at the same time as the first three "synchronals" <note>Events that happen at the same time.</note>, based on the accepted **hypothesis** that the true Church never fails. For in that case, what is the *Woman in the Wilderness* but this pure *Virgin-Church* hidden within the paganizing empire, which is the "Image of the Beast"? And what is the *Exterior Court* of the Temple, trampled by the *Gentiles*, but the Christian Empire—once dedicated to Christ and true worship—overrun again by a new kind of paganism <note>original: "Gentilism"</note> or idolatrous worship? This corruption so overflows that the true and *Virgin-Church* is hidden, in a sense, in this deluge of idolaters; at the very least, she is trampled down, debased, and made the outcasts of Christendom. Therefore, I say, from the very nature of these things and the close connection they have with one another, there is very clear evidence that the *Whore*, the *Two-horned Beast*, the *restored Beast* with *seven heads* and *ten horns*, the *False Prophet*, the *Virgin-Company*, the *Woman in the Wilderness*, the *two Witnesses*, and the *Exterior Court* of the Temple trampled by the *Gentiles* are all synchronal to one another.

3. But we will not altogether omit the more abstract method Mr. [Joseph] Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1639) was an influential English scholar who developed the system of "synchronisms" to interpret the Book of Revelation.</note> has used to prove these synchronisms. First, it is plain that the *Woman in the Wilderness*, the *restored Ten-horned Beast*, the *Exterior Court* trampled by the *Gentiles*, and the *mourning* of the *two Witnesses* are all of equal duration. The *Woman's* stay in the *Wilderness* is noted as *a time, and times, and half a time*, as well as 1,260 days; both expressions literally signify three and a half years. The duration of the *restored Ten-horned Beast* is set at 42 months, as is the trampling <note>original: "Conculcation"</note> of the *outer court*. The days of the *Mourning Witnesses* are also 1,260. All these measurements of time are equal to those of the *Woman in the Wilderness* and are literally three and a half years. If any one of these terms is meant symbolically, I think no one could be so skeptical or stubborn as to deny that the others are symbolic as well. Now, that these four are not only equal in length but also "synchronal" (occurring at the same time) will be briefly shown as follows:

Thus you can see that, according to Mr. Mede's <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), the scholar whose "synchronisms" simplified the complex structure of Revelation for 17th-century readers.</note> scheme of synchronisms, the company of 144,000 from the twelve tribes of Israel (sealed with the seal of God on their foreheads) acts as the common boundary <note>original: "communis Terminus," a shared endpoint or connecting point.</note> for all the parallel timelines on both sides of it. Specifically, it connects the series of the first six trumpeters on one side with our first six parallel events on the other: the restored Ten-horned Beast, the Whore of Babylon, the Two-horned Beast, the two mourning Witnesses, the treading down of the outer court (or Holy City), and the Woman in the Wilderness.

9. Consequently, we have a firm and secure grasp of the entire succession of events in these prophetic visions. By holding onto this middle section so strongly, the other parts cannot slip away from us; it will be easy to discover the necessary order of the rest. For the first six seals must come before the seventh, and the battle between Michael and the Dragon must come before the wounding or slaying of the Beast and his restoration. From the nature of these events and their order, it follows that they are synchronous—meaning they occur at the same time. I refer to the series of the first six seals and the battle of Michael with the Dragon. Furthermore, the inner court of the Temple—which the Angel found to be symmetrical <note>original: "Symmetral or Commensurable to his Reed"; meaning it was precisely measurable according to the divine standard.</note> or measurable by his rod—is also synchronous with the first six seals. This is evident because the symbol perfectly represents the conditions of those times. During that bloody war with the Dragon, the saints of God willingly sacrificed their lives for his cause. This is most appropriately represented by the Altar of Burnt Offerings <note>original: "Altar of Holocausts"; from the Greek word for a sacrifice consumed by fire.</note> located in the inner court of the Temple, and it clearly matches the vision of the fifth seal, 
<margin>Revelation 6:9.</margin>
where the souls of those who were killed are said to cry for vengeance from under the altar.

10. Additionally, in Chapter 11, the visions begin again from the same first epoch of time as the seals do. Therefore, the inner court must be perfectly synchronous with the first six seals, since the outer court began with the seventh.

Now, there are several remarkable signs in Chapter 10 that indicate a new series of prophecies begins from that first epoch; these are sufficient to convince anyone with any degree of insight. First, the magnificence of that "Angel" (as he is called) who has the open book in his hand is so great that it is highly probable he is none other than Christ himself. The description of those bright beams of glory is like those attributed to him in the first chapter. And since he is called "Strong," <note>original: "Ἰσχυρὸς" (Ischyros).</note> what is that but "Mighty God"? <note>original: "אל גבור" (El Gibbor).</note> He is portrayed with a rainbow around his head and his face shining like the sun; what can this represent but the Sun of Righteousness, who is the Eternal Word, and whose clothing is the world he himself created? 11. We may be even more certain of this if we consider that he takes the place of the seventh Angel and fills the space of the seventh Trumpet with seven Thunders. This is a clear sign that the entire course of the seven Seals has run through to the final thunderclap of the Day of Judgment—at least in the manner he thought fit to show at this time, before beginning fresh again.

12. Thirdly, by swearing that *there shall be time no longer, except in the days of the voice of the seventh Angel, when he shall sound, and the mystery of God shall be finished, as he had declared to his servants the prophets* <margin>Daniel 12:7.</margin> (in which there is certainly a reference to Daniel 12:7), it is plain that there is a pause in proceeding explicitly to the very end of the seventh Seal—that is, to the specific and final effect of the seventh Trumpet. This suspension strongly assures us that there is a **regression** <note>A structural "going back" to an earlier point in the timeline to start a new sequence of visions.</note>. And where would it return to, I ask, if not to the very first **epoch** of a new **series** of prophecies? Indeed, a regression is necessarily implied by the Angel’s oath that *there shall be no more time* than what is taken up by the seventh Trumpet, which does not sound until the Resurrection of the Witnesses, as you may see in the following chapter, verses 14 and 15.

13. It is an **opened book** now, whereas before it was a **sealed one**; the first was a book to be looked at with the eyes, while this is to be swallowed down into the belly. This suggests prophecies of a different nature than the former: the first, perhaps, regarding the **fate of the Empire**, and the other regarding the **Church**, as Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), a famous scholar of biblical prophecy.</note> argued. To have all this new preparation for no new purpose would be strange and incredible.

Although this might seem to refer to the *voice from heaven* in verse 4, there is little need for such a reminder for something that happened so recently. # The Demonstration of certain Synchronisms. Book II.

14. <margin>Revelation 10:4</margin> In Revelation 10:4, the voice is said *to speak* <note>original: "λαλεῖν" (lalein), meaning to utter a sound or speak</note>, whereas in verse 8 of this chapter, it is only said *to say* <note>original: "λέγειν" (legein), meaning to state or tell</note>. Therefore, it cannot easily be said that the voice was "speaking again," since it was not described as "speaking" <note>using the verb "lalein"</note> previously in that specific way. Consequently, the phrase in verse 8, *speaking with me again* <note>original: "πάλιν λαλοῦσα μετ’ ἐμοῦ" (palin lalousa met’ emou)</note>, most naturally refers back to Revelation 4:1. This indicates a new beginning of prophecies starting from that very **epoch** <note>A significant starting point in time.</note>.

15. But, sixthly and lastly: upon **John's** swallowing of the Book, we may observe circumstances that strongly suggest a new **series** of prophecies, in which the fate of the **Church** seems to be the primary concern. First, it is said to be *bitter in his stomach, though sweet in his mouth*. No reason can be given for these prophecies being more bitter than the previous ones if they concerned the same subject. It only makes sense if the first set concerned the **Empire** and this set concerns the **Church of God**. Therefore, the **fate of the Church** is contained in these, beginning from an epoch as early as those of the Empire. Secondly, the Angel says, *You must prophesy again* <note>original: "δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι" (dei se palin prophēteusai)</note>. This would be a very strange statement unless it meant he was to begin prophesying again from the first epoch of the times he had already covered. In another sense, he had already prophesied "again and again" by seeing and declaring the many visions he had already experienced. Thirdly, the fact that it is added, *Before many peoples and nations and tongues and kings*, is a sign that he is not just finishing a few remaining details. Instead, he must act more powerfully and *trace the matter back to its origins* <note>original: "altius rem repetere," a Latin phrase meaning to seek the matter from a higher or earlier source</note>. Having taken his nourishment by devouring the **little book**, he begins his race afresh from the first epoch, with a scope as universal as the prophecies of the **Seals** were.

16. These considerations, I think, should convince anyone that the eleventh chapter begins from the first epoch of the Apocalyptic visions. Furthermore, the twelfth chapter certainly does, as has already been demonstrated; there is no vision in the **Seals** that starts earlier than the *fight of Michael with the Dragon*. This proves that **St. John**, in this "second round" of prophesying, returns to the earliest epoch and begins a new series of prophecies—namely, those concerning the Church. Since this has been so clearly proved, I ask anyone if it is likely or even possible that he would begin with such a "headless" vision—one that would start three or four hundred years after the first epoch.

17. Therefore, it is certain that just as the **outer court** (trampled by the **Gentiles**) runs at the same time as the first six Trumpets of the seventh Seal, so the **inner court** runs at the same time as the first six Seals. This was the point to be demonstrated, and it is a conclusion of excellent use and great importance, as will appear in its proper place.

18. Finally, just as our "Middle Synchronisms" <note>Events that occur at the same time in the middle of the prophetic timeline.</note> have necessarily revealed those that came before, they will with equal ease and certainty reveal those that follow. The **thousand years** in which the **Saints reign**, **Satan is bound**, the **palm-bearing company** <note>The multitude holding palm branches in Revelation 7.</note> triumphs, and the **Heavenly Jerusalem is seen upon Earth**—all of these must plainly occur at the same time as the **seventh Trumpet**. <margin>Revelation 11:15.</margin> *And the seventh angel sounded, and there were great voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign for ever and ever."* So it is plain that the Millennial Empire of Christ...

# Chapter VI. The Demonstration of Certain Synchronisms.

<margin>Revelation 7:9</margin>
...and of his saints is under the seventh trumpet. The *Palm-bearing Company* <note>original: "Palmiferous Company"</note> also immediately follows the 144,000 Virgin Regiments, which occur at the same time as the first six trumpets; therefore, this company of *palm-bearers* must necessarily be under the seventh trumpet. The *Fall of Babylon* also ends at the same time as the sixth trumpet, and therefore the *New Jerusalem*, which follows it, must necessarily be found in the seventh. And, lastly, *Satan*—who fought with *Michael* throughout the first six seals and held such power in the kingdom of *Antichrist* during the first six trumpets—cannot be said to be bound, cast into the bottomless *pit*, and *sealed* up there for a thousand years until the Millennial Empire of Christ, the glory and brightness of the *heavenly Jerusalem* on earth, and the victory and triumph of the *palm-bearing company*. That is to say, not until the sounding of the last trumpet. Not only the *sequence* of simultaneous events <note>original: "Series of the Synchronals"</note>, but the very nature of the events themselves, forces the *binding of Satan* <note>original: "Ligation of Satan"</note> into this final period of time.

This is very easy and plain. But if anyone remains unsatisfied, he may read Mr. *Joseph Mede*, Part 2, *Synchronisms* 4, 5, 6, and 7, where he will find a more full and extensive demonstration of these events occurring simultaneously with the seventh trumpet. But how this *simultaneity* <note>original: "contemporizing"</note> is to be understood will better appear in the following chapter.

# That all the Vials are to be placed Book II.

1. I had almost forgotten to discuss the placement of the *Vials*. Mr. *Mede* places the first six of these within the period of the sixth trumpet for this brief reason: because they are the seven last plagues of the Beast, they must begin when the Beast starts to decline toward ruin. However, it was proven earlier that the 42 months of the Beast's dominance and victory over the saints ended at the very end of the sixth trumpet, just as all those middle simultaneous events <note>original: "Synchronals"</note> do. And it is equally true that the *throne* of the Beast does not grow dark before the fifth vial. Therefore, he concludes that at least five vials, if not six, come before the seventh trumpet.

<margin>Revelation 21:9</margin>
2. Mr. *Mede*’s reasoning <note>original: "Ratiocination"</note> would be very solid if we could be certain that the "42-month" duration of the Beast means what he thinks it does. Specifically, he assumes this reign is to be understood *absolutely*—that the Beast shall reign for exactly that long and no longer. However, it might be meant *comparatively*: that after 42 months, he will no longer reign with such absolute power and victory over the saints. In this view, he can no longer keep them so suppressed that they are unable to form a distinct political body <note>original: "Polity"</note> capable of defending themselves against his tyranny and cruelty.

This second interpretation may be just as valid a meaning for the prophecy as the first. Specifically, as soon as a political body of truly evangelical or apostolic Christians appears—those who are not superstitious, idolatrous, or persecuting and bloody, but who join together in the plain points of the Christian religion, making no other *fundamental* requirements than what the clear word of God requires, and leaving people free in other matters—then the 42 months of the Beast may be said to have expired in terms of the absolute totality of his reign. Furthermore, because something has been set in motion that will certainly lead to his ruin, he is described in prophetic style as if he were ruined already. Mr. *Mede* followed this same logic when interpreting the passage in *Isaiah* <note>original: "Esay"</note>, "*Babylon is fallen, is fallen.*" In the time of *Isaiah*, only the first groundwork for her ruin had been laid by the *Medes*. By throwing off the *Assyrian* yoke, winning their liberty, and building the city of *Ecbatana* under their new King *Deioces*, they laid the foundations of a kingdom that would eventually prove fatal to the city of *Babylon*.

<margin>Revelation 11:15</margin>
<margin>John 12:31</margin>
We also cannot fully understand the passage in the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note> regarding the sounding of the seventh trumpet, which is spoken of in such grand terms: "*The kingdoms of the world have become the kingdoms of the Lord and of his Christ.*" I must confess that I suspect the most sensible meaning of this is similar to the words of our Savior: "*Now is the judgment of this world; now shall the prince of this world be cast out.*" Yet, the "prince" actually remained in possession until the time of the Emperor *Constantine*. Therefore, in the same sense that the kingdoms of the world become the kingdoms of Christ at the start of the seventh trumpet, the Beast has lost his kingdom and his 42 months have expired.

3. Therefore, great caution must be used when interpreting prophetic expressions. They always sound very grand and lofty, expressing things in a way that fills the mind and strikes the imagination. If, however, they were written strictly and narrowly, focusing on every <term>petty detail</term> <note>original: "Μικρολογία" (mikrologia)</note>, it would

4. Nor is this only a possible meaning of the end of the 42 months of the Beast coinciding with the sixth trumpet, but it is also very probable. First, because the seventh trumpet is one of the *woe-trumpets*, and therefore signifies ruin and destruction in some sense or other. The second *woe* has passed (that is to say, its symbolic foreshadowing has passed, in the same sense that the poet Ovid says, "Janus has an end" <note>original Latin: *Janus habet finem*. Janus was the two-faced Roman god of beginnings and transitions; the phrase implies one period ending as another begins.</note>). But it is plain that the effect of the sixth trumpet may continue after the seventh has begun, just as the effects of the first seal and first trumpet continue after the second ones have begun. The succession in the effects of these parts of the visions does not always lie like the square stones of a pavement, but rather like the scales of fish, where one reaches over part of the other. (But this is just a side note.) *And behold, the third woe comes quickly*, which is this seventh trumpet. This trumpet, therefore, is a blast of destruction upon all the powers that oppose the kingdom of Christ. This supposes, therefore, that he is going on "conquering and to conquer," and that all the work is not finished at the entrance of the seventh trumpet; rather, so much remains to be done that, in all likelihood, the 42 months of the Beast have not ended in any sense other than the one I have already defined.

<margin>Revelation 10:3, 4</margin>
5. This will appear even more reasonable if, in the second place, we consider the *seven thunders*, which I do not doubt are the contents of the seventh trumpet. The *text says that the mighty angel (whom commentators usually interpret to be Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah) cried with a loud voice, like when a lion roars; and when he had cried, the seven thunders uttered their voices* <note>original Greek: *ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς*</note>. Therefore, this roaring of the Lion of the tribe of Judah throughout those seven thunders—and the division of the space of the seventh trumpet into seven portions—implies a state of war and seven notable battles and victories, or judgments and triumphs. This implies that a vast territory <note>original: "Continent"</note> that rightfully belongs to the kingdom of Christ remains unsubdued at the beginning of the seventh trumpet. Therefore, it is very reasonable that a very great share of the *Roman Empire* may still be under the jurisdiction and guidance of the *two-horned beast*, even at the first blast of the last trumpet or within the sound of the first thunder.

But there is no smoke unless there is some fire, nor any fire unless there is combustible matter. Therefore, that passage suggests that something of this *Whore* will be left burning until the final ages of the world, even into the era of the last trumpet. Therefore, let every part take its right place: let the seven Vials either run parallel to the seven Thunders (which were likely suppressed only because they were to be replaced by these Vials), or let them run within the seventh Trumpet, just as the seven Trumpets run within the seventh Seal. This appears to be the most easy, natural, and balanced way of arranging them. They seem to claim the right to this position because they are called the *seven last plagues in which the wrath of God is finished or ended*; this would not be the case if they were not the plagues of the last Trumpet. Or else, at the very least, let them synchronize with the first Thunder, just as the seven Thunders do with the last Trumpet. I shall discuss this more specifically in its proper place.

# Chap. VII. Within the Seventh Trumpet.

10. But after this comes the pouring out of the seven *Vials*, as is clear from the order of things in the text. This is true whether you look at those "Middle Synchronals" <note>Events occurring at the same time in the prophetic timeline.</note> which are defined by the length of their duration—such as the restored *Beast*, which is immediately followed by the *Virgin-Company* as a parallel opposition to it—after which the *Song of Moses* follows as a thanksgiving for those first victories over the *Beast*; or whether you consider the *Temple opened in Heaven*, which follows after this song and from which the Angels come who hold the *seven Vials*. From both perspectives, it is suggested that the *Vials* all occur within the timeline of the seventh Trumpet. This is further confirmed by *Chapter 11*, where the *Temple of God is also opened in Heaven* and the *Ark of the Covenant* is mentioned, just as it is here, along with a brief symbolic description <note>original: "compendious Symbolical Periphrasis"</note> of wrath and vengeance. Therefore, it is highly reasonable to believe they refer to the same event. But that appearance of the *Temple* and *Ark* in Chapter 11 occurs after the seventh Trumpet has begun to sound. Therefore, the *seven Vials* are contained within the sounding of the seventh Trumpet.

11. In short (to get to the bottom of this current matter), it is of extremely great importance to notice that the seven "Middle Synchronals" of the prophecies of the *opened Book* are fulfilled either in their kind <note>original: *quoad speciem*</note> or in their degrees <note>original: *quoad gradus*</note>—that is, as to the type of event or as to the various stages within that type. Achieving one stage is sufficient to fulfill the prophecy in its kind <note>original: *quoad speciem*</note>. Furthermore, one of these Synchronals cannot be fulfilled in its kind or its degrees without all of them being fulfilled by that very fact <note>original: *ipso facto*</note>, as they are so intimately united with one another. For example, suppose that in just one State or Kingdom in Christendom, the Church has become purely Apostolic in its Doctrine, Discipline, Life, and Conversation. It follows from this that, in its kind <note>original: *quoad speciem*</note>, the Reign of the Beast has ended. That is, there is one specimen or instance of this specific event: namely, such an ending of the Beast's rule that it brings with it the Resurrection of the Witnesses and the succession of the Kingdom of Christ in its place. If this happens at or toward the end of the 42 months from a suitable starting point <note>original: *Epocha*</note>, the prophecy is truly fulfilled in all its circumstances in its kind <note>original: *quoad speciem*</note> in this first example, though it may proceed further and further afterward in degrees or extent.

The point I am arguing for is this: that this first method of fulfillment—in its kind—is the only thing aimed at in these "Middle Synchronals" of the prophecies of the *opened Book*, and that the further degrees of fulfillment are reserved for the *Vials* in the last Trumpet.

12. And what I used as an example regarding the Reign of the Beast must be true of all the rest: that their fulfillment, which happens alongside the first six Trumpets and ends at the first blast of the seventh, is a fulfillment only in its kind <note>original: *quoad speciem*</note> or in its basic existence <note>original: *quoad esse*</note>, not in its full degrees <note>original: *quoad gradus*</note>, which are reserved for the seventh Trumpet. My reason is that all seven of these Synchronals are so closely united or signify so much of the same thing that they must necessarily advance or be delayed together. For example, we cannot imagine the Whore of *Babylon* being burned in any one Kingdom—that is, the...

14. I believe this is the truest and safest understanding we can have of the sequence of things in the *Apocalyptic Visions* <note>The visions in the Book of Revelation.</note>. Having adequately cleared this up, I shall—with greater satisfaction to myself and, I hope, to others—proceed to produce those passages from this prophetic volume that predict the various ways the *Church fell into Antichristianism*. We now know where to look for them: namely, among the "Middle Synchronals" of either prophecy, which span from about the year 400 AD to these current ages.

1. Besides those notable and leading prophecies regarding the idolatry of the Church in the thirteenth and seventeenth chapters of the *Book of Revelation*, there are further intimations of the same fall in other places. Indeed, no fewer than six of the seven "Middle Synchronals" of the prophecies of the *Opened Book* are predictions of this idolatrous state of the Church. Three of these we have already addressed: namely, the *Whore of Babylon*, the *Two-horned Beast*, and the *Beast with seven heads and ten horns*.

<margin>Revelation 11</margin>
The first of the three remaining prophecies is the *Outward Court* or *Holy City trampled underfoot by the Gentiles for the space of forty-two months.* That this *Outward Court* or *Holy City* is to be understood as those who make a visible profession of Christianity in the world is evident from the timing of these events. The *Temple* or *Inward Court* represents the Church from its beginning until it fell into a condition that could not be measured by the *Angel’s measuring rod* <note>In Revelation 11:1, the inner temple is measured to show God's approval, while the outer court is rejected.</note>, and was therefore rejected. The text says of the court that is outside the temple, "cast it out" <note>original: "ἔκβαλε ἔξω" (ekbale exo)</note>. However, since the *Outward Court* belongs to the *Inward*, and the Jewish people had been cast off long before this vision, it is plain that all of this refers to *Christendom*. It is no more surprising that the Jewish *Temple* or its *Courts* should represent the Christian Church than it was for the twelve *Tribes* to do so in Chapter 7. This is simply a common *Israelism* <note>The author's term for using Old Testament Jewish imagery to describe New Testament Christian realities.</note>.

Therefore, since Christendom is the scene of these transactions, and it is immediately added concerning this *Outward Court* that it is *given to the Gentiles, and that they shall trample the Holy City underfoot for forty-two months*—this *Holy City* and *Outward Court* are essentially the same thing. As Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential biblical scholar whose work on synchronizing the prophecies of Revelation was foundational for the author.</note> has well observed, the Camp of Israel was the "Outward Court" in the wilderness, and this Outward Court was the place where the people of Israel gathered during their solemn times of worship once the Temple was built. It is evident, then, that Christendom was to be overrun with *Gentilism*—that is, with *Paganism*, the life and soul of which is *idolatry*—for that specific length of time. This is because the *Holy City* or *Outward Court* is assumed to exist here; that is to say, there is a people who profess Christianity and are externally dedicated to God, but in the meantime, they have become overgrown with a heathen kind of superstition and idolatry.

<margin>Verse 17</margin>
The fact that this *Outward Court* is said *to be given to the Gentiles* corresponds to what is written in Chapter 17: *For God has put it into their hearts to fulfill His will, and to agree and give their kingdom unto the Beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled.* This apostasy <note>A total desertion or departure from one's religion or principles.</note> of the Church seems to be fated, and those great politicians of Italy have little reason to "sacrifice to their own nets" <note>original: "sacrifice to their own Nets," a biblical metaphor from Habakkuk 1:16 meaning to take credit for success through one's own cleverness or tools rather than recognizing God's hand in history.</note> and attribute everything to their own intelligence, when they have apparently hitherto...
