2. The next of those later synchronal events <note>original: "Synchronalls". These are different prophecies in the Book of Revelation that are believed to occur during the same historical period.</note> is *the Woman in the Wilderness*. Specifically, that woman who *wears on her head a crown of twelve stars*. Her glory is to be that pure and apostolic Church, untainted by later superstitions and idolatries. She is the woman said *to labor in birth and was pained to be delivered*, and after long labor and pangs—that is to say, sharp persecutions—finally *brought forth a male child who should rule the nations*. This *Woman*, though she did not change locations herself, is nonetheless said *to have the wings of an eagle given to her*, by which she fled into the wilderness. This was to keep her safe from the persecution of the old red dragon, which represents the bloody pagan powers of the Roman Empire before they converted to Christianity. Indeed, by escaping in this way, even if only into a *wilderness*, she was sheltered from them. However, the fact that she is said to be *in a wilderness* suggests she is hidden and mixed among those who, while outwardly professing Christianity, became *paganized* again in their superstitious and idolatrous worship. This can be understood from the accepted meaning of "wilderness" in the prophetic alphabet <term>The "prophetic alphabet" refers to a system of symbolic interpretation where natural elements like "wilderness" or "stars" represent political or spiritual realities.</term>. It is clear that *men*, not just a lonely place of trees and beasts, are meant by "wilderness" from the Gospel of Matthew: 
<margin>Matthew 3:3</margin>
*The voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.* John the Baptist did not speak to beasts and trees, but to *men*. These men resemble beasts when they are entirely consumed by the functions and pleasures of their basic physical and animal nature—one part of which is superstition and idolatry, as I suggested above.

3. Therefore, the meaning of this prophecy is that the pure and apostolic Church—though sheltered for a time from the red dragon—was overrun with a kind of *Christiano-Paganism* from one side to the other. This spread from the east wing to the west wing of the eagle, or Roman Empire. Because the Empire had its *Eastern* and *Western* Caesars, it is depicted 
<margin>* Chapter 7:6</margin>
with *two wings*. This is more easily understood than the *leopard* in the Book of *Daniel* having *four wings*, which represented the division of the Greek Empire into four parts. This imagery suggests that the *Greek* Church as well as the *Latin* Church is guilty of this idolatrous worship. This corresponds to what I said about the *two horns of the Beast*: they represent the two imperial patriarchates <term>A patriarchate is the office or jurisdiction of a high-ranking bishop, or "patriarch," in the early Church.</term>—one in Rome and the other in Constantinople. These were the two highest summits of the idolatrous clergy. I have no doubt that this is the meaning of the *Woman in the Wilderness*, even though it seems somewhat difficult that she is said *to fly into this desert*, when in reality this *desert* of corruption rather came upon or overran her.

4. But this is a *hypallage* <note>original: "Hypallage". A literary device where the natural relationship between two words is reversed for emphasis or poetic effect.</note>, of which this is not the only example. It is similar to the description of casting *Hades* into the lake of fire and sulfur, whereas that fire is actually cast into *Hades* during the destruction of the world by thunder and lightning. This is a literary figure that poets often use, sometimes even unnecessarily, for the sake of elegance.

### Chapter 8. The Vision of the Woman in the Wilderness.

->*The northwest wind striking the Bruttian sea.*<-
<note>original: "Brutium ponto feriente Corum." This line from the Roman poet Horace evokes a stormy, desolate setting, fitting the theme of the wilderness.</note>

I suspect a similar *hypallage* <term>original: "Hypallage." A rhetorical device where the natural relationship between words is reversed or swapped.</term> exists in *Daniel* chapter 7, where he speaks of the *Kingdoms under the whole Heaven being given to the Saints of the most High*. The meaning of this may simply be that those who possess these Kingdoms may turn into Saints—that is, people who become professors and supporters of the pure and apostolic religion, untainted by the idolatrous inventions and commands of *Antichrist*. However, it is desirable that those who are all too ready to imagine themselves as "Saints" (if this interpretation of the *hypallage* does not please them) would at least imitate the modesty of the text's expression and not try to take over kingdoms before they are actually given to them.

5. Mr. *Mede* <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638) was an influential English scholar known for his systematic study of biblical prophecy.</note> interprets this *Vision of the Woman in the Wilderness* in a sense somewhat different from ours. He parallels the *Israelites'* flight from *Pharaoh* into the wilderness with the Woman's flight from the red *Dragon*. He also compares their liberty in serving *Jehovah* there (according to the rites appointed by *Moses*) to the liberty that *Christians* had to practice their religion. He further links their lapses into idolatry to the idolatrous apostasy of the Church of Christ in this same condition. Finally, he compares their 42 journeys in the wilderness mentioned in *Numbers* 33 to the 42 months the Woman is said to stay in the desert. If these 42 months had been expressly written in those terms, and not only in the equivalent "1260 days" or "*a time and times and half a time*," his point would be more fitting and convincing. Nevertheless, his interpretation is very plausible and elegant, and it may be one valid sense of the *prophetic type* <term>original: "Type." A person, event, or object in the Old Testament or history believed to foreshadow something in the New Testament or the future.</term>, though not the only sense. It is the nature of these prophetic types to abound with allusions.

<margin>Verse 8.</margin>
But since the state of the Church in the wilderness is the same as her period of bondage in *Egypt* (as appears from *Revelation* 11), I consider the interpretation I have given more acceptable, or rather, more authentic. Yet, I see no reason why one should exclude the other. The reign of the Dragon was truly the reign of *Pharaoh* over these new *Israelites* (except that the Dragon's reign was bloodier). The state of the wilderness in which the Woman is hidden is not only a revival of that Egyptian bondage, but also a restoration of the Dragon's idolatry; this is done by creating such a vivid image of him in this new "Pagano-Christianity" <note>The author's term for a form of Christianity that he believes has adopted pagan-style idolatry.</note> which the apocalyptic visions so frequently predict.

6. The third and last of these later synchronal events in the *Book Prophecy* is
<margin>* Revelation 14:1.</margin>
the *Virgin Company*: the sealed soldiers of the Lamb upon *Mount Sion*, whose description is both admirable and mysterious. Because they are said to be 144 *chiliads* <term>original: "Chiliads." Groups of one thousand; 144,000 in total.</term> or regiments, this is not a literal definition of their number, but rather of their nature or quality. This follows the use of the ancient *Kabbalah* <note>original: "Cabbala." Here referring to a tradition of interpreting the mystical or symbolic meaning of numbers.</note>, which describes the properties of things through numbers. The square root of 144 is *twelve*, which plainly reveals them to be the true disciples and successors of the Church that Christ founded upon his twelve Apostles. It shows they had not corrupted the Christian religion with any idolatrous worship or unjustifiable human institutions. Instead, they were faithful to him whose name they bore on their foreheads as the marked servants of God and of the Lamb. Having been bought with the price of his most precious blood, they would not become the servants of men in anything that worked against the honor or interests of him who bought them.

I would have those who think it a matter of indifference whether one is *Papist* or *Protestant* to seriously consider this warning, as if such *tragic threats* as these were mere scarecrows and idle mockeries.

1. To these middle synchronisms <note>original: "Synchronalls"; events occurring at the same time in prophecy</note> of the *Book-Prophecy*, we will only add the vision of the *Sixth Trumpet*, St. *Paul's* prediction concerning the *apostasy of the later times*, and that prophecy in *Daniel* from which he seems to have drawn that prediction; and then we shall be finished.

And truly the vision of the Sixth Trumpet is very significant and well-known. That it refers to the *Turks* invading Christendom—as Mr. *Mede* <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), a famous scholar of biblical prophecy.</note> has interpreted—I have abundantly proved against *Grotius* <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch legal scholar and theologian who often disagreed with Mede’s historicist views.</note> in my book *The Mystery of Godliness*. <margin>* Book 5. Ch. 16. Sect. 5.</margin> To this we briefly add that it is plain the invasion of these *Euphratean horsemen* occurs long after the Empire became Christian—indeed, even *Pagano-Christian* <note>The author's term for a church that has adopted pagan-style idolatry while claiming to be Christian.</note>. This is because it is the *Sixth Trumpet*, the last of those that, taken together in order, synchronize with the reign of the Pagano-Christian power: *The Beast that was, and is not, and yet is.* And as for the place as well as the *time*, it appears that this vision belongs to the Empire from that often-repeated characteristic used to denote it: the proportion of a "third part." <margin>* Revelation 9:15.</margin> For the *third part of men* are said here to be killed. This prophecy is fulfilled in the *Collyridians* <note>A 4th-century sect that was criticized for offering small cakes (collyria) in worship to the Virgin Mary.</note>. It is plain that *Epiphanius* understands it in the former sense (as doctrines *about* demons), both because he places the word "myths" before "doctrines"—since fabulous stories are not thought to be told *by* demons, but *about* them—and also from what follows immediately: *For, he says, there will be those who will worship the dead, etc.* <note>original: "Ἔσονται γὰρ, φησὶ, νεκροῖς λατρεύοντες, &c."</note> Yet the Apostle Paul does not say this explicitly, unless the phrase "doctrines of demons" signifies doctrines concerning the souls of deceased men, as I have sufficiently explained elsewhere. The Angel tells Daniel, *The words shall be sealed until the time of the end*; and Mr. Mede shows plainly how the matter is revealed during this "time of the end," and even at those very points in time that these numbers point to, which is worthy of our consideration and admiration.

Therefore, Calvin <note>John Calvin (1509–1564), the influential Protestant Reformer.</note> has wisely ventured to interpret these verses as referring to the *Roman Empire*, which immediately followed the *Greek Empire* (in the last times of which Antiochus is said to have reigned, according to the prophecy of Daniel). Modin is a city in *Judea* carved out of a rock; in all likelihood, it was a stronghold, and was therefore called *Modin* <note>The author suggests the name refers to its nature as a fortress rather than a deity.</note>, but without any reference to this imaginary god of *Grotius*, the "strange god" of whom *Antiochus* was supposedly so zealous a worshipper. 4. Mr. *Mede*, therefore, following *Calvin* before him, supposes that at the thirty-sixth verse of this eleventh chapter, the prophecy of *Antiochus* breaks off and the *Roman Kingdom* comes into consideration. This is not doubtful or conjectural, but necessary for the reasons already mentioned. Therefore, the Hebrew phrase "And the king shall do according to his will" <note>original: ועשה כרצונו המלך (*ve-asah khirtsono hammelekh*)</note> is rightly rendered: *Then shall a King do according to his will*. The particle "and" (ו) has such a broad sense that there is no harm in giving it this specific meaning of "then." Similarly, *Pareus* renders the Greek phrase *kai klausontai* as "*Then they shall weep*" <note>original: *Tum flebunt*</note> in *Revelation* 18:9. By *King* here is meant—as elsewhere in the Book of *Daniel*—a *state or kingdom*. That the *Roman* state is meant here is implied by the order of succession: it follows the *Greek* empire according to all chronology. According to the consensus of historians, it is understood to have succeeded the *Greeks* upon the *Roman* conquest of *Macedonia*, which occurred in the later years of *Antiochus's* reign. Thus, things align perfectly regarding time in our hypothesis, which promises a smooth flow of meaning throughout, as follows:

5. In the first of these verses, it is predicted that the *Roman state* or *kingdom*, toward the end of *Antiochus’s* reign, shall sweep everything before them and dominate as they please. For to conquer a nation is to conquer their *gods*, whom the *Romans* vocally summoned out of those cities they captured by a certain ritual charm I mentioned earlier; thus, they led away the *gods* of the nations as captives just as they did the people.

# Daniel’s Prediction of Demon-worship. Book II

In this period, the *Roman Empire* would despise, neglect, and cast off the *gods* of their *ancestors*—that is, the *Pagan gods*—and turn into *Christians*. However, at the same time, *marriage* (which was held in such high regard by the *Romans* previously, as seen in the laws called *Julia* and *Papia* <note>The *Lex Julia* and *Lex Papia Poppaea* were Roman laws introduced under Augustus to encourage marriage and childbearing; Constantine later repealed their penalties against the unmarried.</note>, which *Constantine* repealed) would be greatly slighted at first. In the course of time, it would be superstitiously forbidden for both priests and monks. This occurred as that "Man of Sin" <note>A biblical term from 2 Thessalonians 2:3, used here by the author to refer to the Papacy.</note> gained control of the Empire. This figure respected no god, but because he nullified the laws of Christ and trampled on the authority of princes, he is justly said to *magnify himself above all*, exactly as it is written about him in the Epistle to the *Thessalonians*.

6. Suitably to this lawlessness and contempt for God, the next verse follows: "And for the god of fortresses [Mauzzim], on his pedestal, he shall honor..." <note>original Hebrew: וְלֶאֱלֹהּ מָעֻזִּים עַל כַּנּוֹ יְכַבֵּד (*ve-le-eloah ma’uzzim al kanno yekhabed*)</note>. That is to say, "for together with," or "besides" (as the Hebrew prepositions can signify), he will honor *Mauzzim* "in his own jurisdiction" <note>original Latin: *in sua ditione*</note>, as Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a Dutch scholar whose interpretation the author is challenging.</note> renders it, referring it to *Antiochus*. The Latin Vulgate reads "in his place" <note>original Latin: *in loco suo*</note>, referring it to the idol; Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1639), an influential English scholar of prophecy.</note> translates it as "in his seat," referring it to Christ, the true God. There may also be another sense for "on his pedestal" <note>original Hebrew: עַל כַּנּוֹ (*al kanno*)</note>, namely, "upon his base," as if the honor given to the *Mauzzim* was grounded in the honor intended for Christ. This is the argument of the <term>Pontificians</term> <note>A term for Roman Catholics, referring to their allegiance to the Pope (the Pontiff).</note>. 

The brief meaning is this: it is plain that this *Roman Power*, as mentioned in the previous verse, has cast away the true fear of God and exalts itself above everything called God, even Christ himself. This is because, contrary to the express law of God, they give divine honor to the *Mauzzim*—though under the pretense of worshipping the true God—with gold, silver, and wooden statues, and with everything costly and precious. As the text immediately follows: "Even together with a god whom their fathers did not know" <note>original Hebrew: וְלֶאֱלֹהַּ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדָעוּהוּ אֲבֹתָיו יְכַבֵּד בְּזָהָב וגו' (*ve-le-eloah asher lo yedauhu avotav yekhabed be-zahav...*)</note>. This "god" is *Christ*, who was truly "an unknown god" <note>original Greek: Θεὸς ἄγνωστος (*Theos agnostos*)</note>, a complete stranger among the *Roman* deities and one to whom the ancient *Romans* never sacrificed. "He will worship them," namely the *Mauzzim*, "with gold, etc."

From this, it is plain that the "demons" spoken of by St. Paul <note>A reference to 1 Timothy 4:1, which warns of "doctrines of devils" (demons) and forbidding to marry.</note> are prophesied here. These *Mauzzim* are the saints who were turned into *demons* by this idolatrous Empire. They are called *Mauzzim* here through a wonderful and strange foresight of God. In its meaning, this Hebrew word reflects the very language of those who, through superstitious zeal for the saints, introduced this *demon-worship*. They placed a more tangible trust and rest in the saints' relics and protection than in the omnipresent God himself. Therefore, they called the saints "towers, enclosures, walls, strongholds, guards, protectors" <note>original Greek: πύργους, περιβόλους, τείχη, ὀχυρώματα, δορυφόρους, ὑπερασπιστάς (*purgous, peribolous, teiche, ochuromata, doruphorous, huperaspistas*)</note>, and every other similar name. *Mauzzim* naturally and properly signifies all of these things, as you can see explained more fully in Mr. Mede’s work. The meaning flows easily regarding the abuse of *saint-worship*: though they claim Christ is the focus of all divine honor, it is plain the saints become partners with him in the dedication of temples and other religious worship.

### Chapter X. Daniel's Prediction of Demon-worship.

<margin>Book 1, Chapter 17, Section 4</margin>
The holy houses—churches, chapels, and monasteries—are dedicated to the honor of Christ and the saints. These holy places are called "strongholds" <note>original Hebrew: מִבְצָרִים (*mibzarim*)</note> in allusion to *Mauzzim*. The word *Mauzzim* carries a warlike meaning and signifies "military protectors and champions"; therefore, the buildings dedicated to them may appropriately be called "strongholds." The meaning of the entire verse is this: this Roman Power shall build temples and other religious houses for Christ and the saints. In this passage, Christ is indicated by the phrase "a foreign god" <note>original Hebrew: אֱלֹהַּ נֵכָר (*eloah nekhar*)</note>. He is described this way because, in his humanity, he was born from a lineage distinct from all pagan nations, making him more "foreign" than any other in that regard. Furthermore, as both perfect God and perfect man, he is a deity the nations had never imagined before. Therefore, the description of Christ in this prophecy as a "foreign god" is uniquely significant.

However, once Christ was known to them, they were supposed to give him fitting <note>original: "condign"</note> honor—except that they would share some of that honor with the *Mauzzim* (the saints). They would make these saints rulers over the Empire, dividing the world among them as a supposed reward for their sufferings. Thus, one saint is appointed as the patron or protector of one city or country, and another saint over another, as I have fully explained earlier.

8. This interpretation is so clear and straightforward that it is no wonder Saint Paul says the Spirit speaks *expressly* <note>original Greek: ῥητῶς (*rhetōs*)</note> that "in the latter times"—meaning during Daniel’s "time, times, and half a time," which is the final period of the Roman Empire—people would abandon the faith and embrace "the doctrine of demon-worship," or the worship of the *Mauzzim*. History matches this prophecy so exactly that a person must be remarkably blinded by prejudice not to see it. One would also have to be a strange critic of harmony and proportion not to appreciate how naturally this fills the terrible and awkward gap <note>original: *chasma*</note> between the predictions in the eleventh and twelfth chapters of *Daniel*. In this way, the chapters are filled with matters of great importance, and the sequence of time is carried forward continuously to the Day of Judgment.

9. Joseph Mede's <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638) was an influential English scholar known for his studies on biblical prophecy.</note> interpretation of these four verses in *Daniel* is itself beyond reproach, and for all I know, it may be the single consistent meaning intended throughout. However, when I look at the words of the Apostle in 2 Thessalonians 2—referring to the one "who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or that is worshipped"—it seems a clear allusion to Daniel’s words: "He shall exalt himself and magnify himself above every god." Therefore, I suspect that in a later fulfillment of the prophecy, the Roman Catholic power <note>original: "Pontifician Power," referring to the Papacy</note> is also criticized <note>original: *perstringed*</note> here. This power is a kind of revived image of the pagan imperial power of Rome, emerging as soon as the Pope surpassed the Emperor. Consequently, the first two of these four verses may also be interpreted as referring to the Pope and his devilish <note>original: *Luciferian*</note> pride, as I will show more clearly in the appropriate section.

<margin>Book 1, Chapter 4, Section 5.</margin>
For the *Two Witnesses* being contemporary <note>original: "Synchronal"</note> to the restored *Beast*, it is in vain to dream of anything at *Jerusalem* that should be the fulfillment of this prophecy. It is therefore, I say, the Church of *Rome* that is this Mystical *Egypt*, and the Pope the Pharaoh of this *Egypt*, with his hard taskmasters, who make the deluded people drudge and toil under the burdens of their superstition. And the overthrow of this Spiritual Pharaoh and his ecclesiastical host is manifestly foreshadowed <note>original: "typified"</note> by that of the *Egyptians* in the *Red Sea*, which corresponds to the blood of *Christ*. This blood is a wall on the left hand and on the right to the simple-hearted *Israelites* in their flight from these tyrants of *Egypt*, but it overwhelms Pharaoh and his host. This puts a Song of Thanksgiving into the mouths of those who, through serious meditation upon the proper virtue and intent of the bloody Passion of *Christ*, have escaped this *Egyptian servitude* <note>original: "Vassalage"</note>: *I will sing unto the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider has he thrown into the Sea:* Or, which is the same, that *Song of Moses and of the Lamb, Revelation 15:3: Great and marvelous are your works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are your ways, O King of Saints, etc.* But of these things I have spoken already, and therefore this brief mention shall suffice.

<margin>Revelation 15:2.</margin>
Only as a support <note>original: "corroboration"</note> for this symbolic <note>original: "Typical"</note> sense of *Egypt*, I cannot omit to take notice how this Song of *Moses* and of the *Lamb* is said to be sung *upon the sea of glass mingled with fire* <note>original: "ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί"</note>. This is a clear indication that the escape of the *Israelites* from Pharaoh through the *Red Sea* is alluded to in this Song. This is because the Sea upon whose shore it is sung is called a *Sea of Glass*, which represents the hard consistency which the sea then seemed to have, being like a thick glassy wall on this side and that side of the *Israelites*. (Indeed, it is said in the Song of *Moses* (Exodus 15:8): *The floods stood upright as a heap, and the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.*) It is also said to be *mixed with fire*, which suggests how these two massive walls of glass were penetrated by the sight of the Angel who went along with the *Israelites* through the *Red Sea* by night. The name or color of the sea may also likely be alluded to in this description, since *Red* is not an improper descriptor <note>original: "Epithet"</note> for *fire*.

There may also be an even more Mystical meaning of this *Sea mingled with fire* (the Spirit with the blood of *Christ*), which for brevity's sake I pass over, and will only add a short paraphrase upon the verse I first cited:

3. *In the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified* <note>original: "ὅπου καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν ἐσταυρώθη"</note>. This is usually rendered as *where also our Lord was crucified*, which is a very good and easy sense if we refer the word *where* <note>original: "ὅπου"</note> to the *Great City* and read [which is spiritually called *Sodom* and *Egypt*] as a parenthetical statement. But if we refer it to, or rather join it with, *Sodom* and *Egypt*, the sense seems more harsh, unless we understand...

1. *The reasons for his wordiness so far in discussing the prophecies of the Church's idolatry, and his future brevity regarding the other parts of the Antichristian system.*

1. In the meantime, I hope we have sufficiently cleared Divine Providence from any suspicion of neglect or defect, showing that it predicted as well as foresaw this general fall of the Church into this first and primary point of "Antichristianism" <note>Antichristianism: The system of beliefs and practices that the author believes opposes the true spirit of Christianity, often identified by Protestant writers of this era with the Roman Catholic Church.</note>: *Demon-worship* <note>original: "Dæmon-worship"; here referring to the veneration of saints and angels, which the author considers a form of idolatry similar to pagan worship of lesser spirits.</note> or *Idolatry*. I have been more thorough on this point because it is the chief characteristic of the Church's apostate state. Indeed, it is the root of most other Antichristian outrages that have crept into Christendom—certainly of the next most heinous one: the bloody persecution of God's beloved children and the faithful members of Jesus Christ who cannot submit to such idolatrous practices.

However, I shall now return to my original method and search out the prophecies for each part of *Antichristianism* in the order I previously mentioned. I will be able to do this much more briefly, having already established my main argument and needing only to refer to many of the prophecies I have already explained. Furthermore, most of the remaining parts of this Antichristian system are not as fully or frequently predicted as this matter of Idolatry.

Such fictions are invented for no other purpose than to uphold tyrannical power or to increase the unfair profits of the priesthood.

I do not doubt that the Spirit of God points to this condition of the Church in *Revelation 11*, where the dead bodies of the *Two Witnesses* are said to lie in the *streets of the Great City, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.* "Which is called spiritually" <note>original: "Ἥτις καλεῖται πνευματικῶς"</note>, that is, in "the mystery" <note>original: "τὸ μυστήριον"</note>, or *Typically* <note>Typically: Referring to a "type," a person or event in the Old Testament that foreshadows something in the New Testament.</note>, as Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645): A famous Dutch jurist and theologian.</note> him-

<header>Chap. XI. Egypt a Type of the Roman Bondage.</header>

[The author] himself acknowledges. I say, therefore, that this *Great City*, which is this *mystical Egypt*—that "House of Bondage" to the ancient Church of God in the type <note>type: a biblical event or person that foreshadows a future reality (the "antitype")</note> and to the modern Church in the antitype—is the so-called Catholic Church of *Rome*. This spiritual slavery under the superstitious impositions of the Pope, and any other clergy of that same character, is hinted at in this passage of the vision.

Because the *Two Witnesses* are synchronal <note>synchronal: occurring at the same time</note> to the restored *Beast*, it is useless to imagine that anything in *Jerusalem* could be the fulfillment of this prophecy. Therefore, I say, it is the Church of *Rome* that is this mystical *Egypt*, and the Pope is the *Pharaoh* of this *Egypt*. He and his harsh taskmasters force the deluded people to drudge and toil under the burdens of their superstition. 

The overthrow of this spiritual *Pharaoh* and his ecclesiastical army is clearly prefigured by the destruction of the *Egyptians* in the *Red Sea*. This corresponds to the *Blood of Christ*, which acts as a wall on the left hand and on the right for the simple-hearted *Israelites* fleeing from these tyrants of *Egypt*. However, it overwhelms *Pharaoh* and his army and puts a song of thanksgiving into the mouths of those who have escaped this *Egyptian servitude* through serious meditation on the true power and purpose of the bloody passion of Christ. They sing: "*I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea*" (Exodus 15:1). This is the same as the "Song of Moses and of the Lamb" in *Revelation 15*: <margin>Book 1, Chapter 4, Section 5.</margin> "*Great and marvelous are your works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are your ways, O King of Saints, etc.*" I have already spoken about these things, so this brief mention will suffice.

<margin>Revelation 15:2.</margin>
Merely to support this symbolic <note>original: "Typical"</note> sense of *Egypt*, I must note how the Song of *Moses* and of the *Lamb* is said to be sung "beside the sea of glass mingled with fire" <note>original Greek: "ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί"</note>. This is a clear indication that the *Israelites'* escape from *Pharaoh* through the *Red Sea* is alluded to in this song. First, the sea shore where it is sung is called a *Sea of Glass*, representing the firm consistency the sea seemed to have then, acting as a thick glassy wall on either side of the *Israelites*. Indeed, the Song of *Moses* (*Exodus* 15:8) says: "*The floods stood upright like a heap, and the depths were frozen <note>original: "congealed"</note> in the heart of the sea.*" Second, it is said to be *mixed with fire*, which suggests how those two massive walls of glass were pierced by the light <note>original: "sight"</note> of the Angel who accompanied the *Israelites* through the *Red Sea* by night. The name or color of the sea might also be alluded to in this description, as *Red* is a fitting adjective for *fire*.

There may even be a more mystical meaning to this *sea mingled with fire* (representing the Spirit with the Blood of Christ), which I will skip for the sake of brevity. I will only add a short paraphrase of the verse I first cited.

3. "In the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, *where also our Lord was crucified*" <note>original Greek: "ὅπου καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν ἐσταυρώθη"</note>. This is usually translated as "where also our Lord was crucified." This makes very good and easy sense if we apply "where" <note>original: "ὅπου"</note> to the "great city" and read "which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt" as a parenthesis. However, if we apply it to—or rather join it with—*Sodom and Egypt*, the meaning seems harsher, unless we understand...

<header>Egypt as a Symbol of Roman Bondage. Book II.</header>

...an *ellipsis* <note>ellipsis: a literary device where words are omitted but understood in context</note>, the missing portion of which would be: *and the city where our Lord was crucified* <note>original Greek: κ᾿ ἡ πόλις ὅπε ὁ Κύρι᾽ ἡμῶν ἐσταυρώθη</note>. This refers to the street of the great city, which is spiritually called *Sodom* and *Egypt*, and the city where our Lord was crucified—that is, the prophet-murdering *Jerusalem*. This is certainly what is alluded to, regardless of how this *ellipsis* is structured. The meaning of the text, I believe, is this:

That great body politic which pretends to be the Catholic Church—though it has so grossly apostatized <note>apostatized: abandoned its religious vows or principles</note> from apostolic doctrine and practice—is "the mystery" <note>original Greek: τὸ μυστήριον</note>, as Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645): a famous Dutch legal scholar and theologian</note> says. It is spiritually or mystically called *Sodom*, *Egypt*, and *the city where Christ was crucified*, as a just reproach to its false claims. 

It is as if the Spirit of God were speaking like this: 

"This degenerate Church of *Rome* boasts of its profession of vowed celibacy and perpetual virginity to appear as that true 'Virgin Company' and the holy, chaste spouse of Christ and the Lamb. However, I pronounce them a nest of unclean birds, as foul as *Sodom* and as polluted as *Gomorrah*. 

Furthermore, they pretend to be the only Church of my Son Christ (who declared that *if the Son makes you free, then you are free indeed*) and claim to be that *Jerusalem* which is free and is the *mother of all true believers*. Yet, I proclaim to all the world that they are, spiritually or mystically, that very land of *Egypt* and 'House of Bondage.' In it, my people are oppressed and exhausted by tedious, superstitious, and burdensome rituals <note>original: "observances"</note> that serve no purpose but to uphold the pomp and pride of that spiritual *Pharaoh* <note>meaning the Pope</note> and his unmerciful taskmasters—a tyrannical and idolatrous clergy. 

Lastly, they would have men believe they are that Holy City, a refuge and protection for the saints of God and a shelter from persecution, where all tears shall be wiped from their eyes—that *New Jerusalem* that descended from heaven. They would be this if they were what they boasted to be: the true visible Church of Christ. Instead, they are actually a continuation of that old *Jerusalem*—the superstitious and burdensome Scribes and Pharisees who were the crucifiers of my Son Jesus. They remain so to this very day toward his true members, for as Christ told them, he himself is persecuted as often as his members are persecuted."

Therefore, the phrase "where also our Lord was crucified" <note>original Greek: ὅπε καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν ἐσταυρώθη</note> may refer to the members of Christ as much as to Christ himself, even though the verb is in the first aorist tense <note>aorist: a Greek past tense</note>. For Grotius makes a good and true observation: "Aorists without a specific designation of time indicate what usually happens" <note>original Latin: Aoriſti ſine deſignatione temporis deſignant quod fieri ſolet</note>. Therefore, the word "crucified" <note>original Greek: ἐσταυρώθη</note> suggests the frequent persecution of Christ in his true members under the power of the Antichrist. For crucifixion, by definition <note>original: "diorism"</note>, signifies any kind of persecution.

Thus, *Jerusalem* is not understood here literally under the disguise of *Sodom* and *Egypt*. That would not be a mystical or spiritual meaning, but a mere synecdoche <note>synecdoche: a figure of speech where a part represents the whole, or vice versa</note> such as any schoolboy understands. Rather, the "Great City" is a political body of men who pretend to be the only true Catholic Church, despite having miserably fallen away from the faith. This city, in the mystical sense I have explained, is called *Sodom*, *Egypt*, and that *Jerusalem* which kills the prophets and crucifies our Lord by persecuting his members.

# Chapter 11. *Roman Catholic <note>original: "Popish"</note> Infallibility Foretold in the Figure of the False Prophet.*

But the thing that we note now especially is their being called *Egypt* for keeping the People of God in such Spiritual Slavery and Bondage.

4. Which Slavery and Vassalage <term>vassalage: a state of being a subordinate or servant</term> we may conceive also to be hinted at in the figure of the *Whore of Babylon* that *rides upon the Beast*. For the reason this dominating Clergy of *Rome* is so called seems not only to be because *Babylon* looks like the first precedent of idolatry in worshipping *Belus* <note>Belus: a Greek form of the Babylonian god Bel or Baal</note>, but for their tyrannical pride and for holding the people in such a forced captivity. From under this captivity no man might withdraw himself and return toward *Jerusalem* and the true Temple of God without exposing himself to the cruelty of this bloody *Whore*, who sits as a *Queen* and says *she shall never see sorrow*.

The Beast also being described as being ridden by the *Whore* suggests a kind of beastly drudgery and slavery the Christian Empire has groaned under for so many ages. To make the Empire more like a Beast (like a horse or mule that has no understanding), they endeavored to keep the people as ignorant as they could, so that the People might be the more patiently *priest-ridden* <term>priest-ridden: controlled or dominated by the clergy</term>, as the phrase goes, and carry their riders with more ease and safety.

5. These are the chief insights that occur to my mind in the Prophetic Visions that are applicable to this second member of "Antichristianism," and that only in this general way. That of *Saint Paul* is more particular—*forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats*—but it is so easy to be understood that the naming of it is sufficient. And therefore I shall pass to the next branches of Antichristianism: those oppositions that would undermine the *sacred offices of Christ* as he is *King, Prophet, and Priest*. 

The grand injury against the last of these (the Priestly office) is this: the making of other mediators besides *Christ* and giving them religious worship (which is predicted in *Saint Paul* and *Daniel* in those places we have already produced and explained, touching the *Demons or Mauzzim* <note>Mauzzim: a Hebrew word for "fortresses" or "protectors," interpreted by some reformers as the saints or relics worshipped in the Roman Church</note>). Otherwise, the injury is the suppressing or slighting the chief use of the death of Christ, which is a comfortable relief of conscience from all suspicion of God's displeasure or fear of punishment in the next world for want of "satisfaction" for our misdeeds here, so long as we have repented of them sincerely and have amended our lives according to the word of Christ. This abuse is one grand piece of that slavery and bondage that the People of God are held under in this spiritual *Egypt*; and therefore it is generally prefigured in that type we have already explained, and also in the *Whore of Babylon*, according to what we have hinted above. So we may pass over this office of Christ and proceed to his *Kingly and Prophetic office*.

6. The opposition to the latter (the Prophetic office) is plainly predicted in the mention of the *False Prophet* in the *Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note>. This is the same as the *Two-horned Beast*, who is the restorer of the *wounded Beast* (that is, of the *Pagan Empire* having become Christian) into a new kind of paganism. He is said *to work miracles in the sight of the Beast, with which he deceived those who dwell on the Earth, and made them worship the Image of the Beast and receive the Mark of the Beast, etc.* (*Chapter 13*). These things are so plainly said of the *False Prophet* in *Chapter 19:20* that there can be no doubt that the *Two-horned Beast* and the *False Prophet* are the same. *And the Beast was taken, and with him the False Prophet...*

Therefore, it is plain that the *False Prophet* and the *Two-horned Beast*, and consequently the *Whore of Babylon*, are all one and the same, as I have noted above. Therefore the *Roman* idolatrous clergy—who claim to be such an infallible Church, as if God did unfailingly inspire them in whatever is decided upon by their Pope, or at least by him together with what they choose to call a *General Council*—are represented here by this title or style of *Prophet* as a reproach to their boast of infallible *inspiration*. But because they delude the world with false doctrines, and either diabolical miracles or cunning cheats and forgeries of miraculous effects, the same company of men is more shamefully and openly branded for this impiety by the prefixing of that well-deserved epithet of *False*, <term>ho pseudoprophētēs</term> <note>original: ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης</note>, *The False Prophet*. What can be clearer than this? Or what could be a more wicked opposition to the *Prophetic Office* of Christ than for someone to take it upon himself to be his infallible Vicar-General of Christendom, and yet to fill the world with idolatry and lies? This body of pseudo-prophets has done this to some degree for about 1,200 years, as is manifest from the last corollary <note>original: "Consectary"</note> of our *Joint-Exposition*.

7. From this, we may be sure that the true prophets, who speak according to the tenour of Apostolic doctrine, would have a very difficult time. The *Prophetic Office* of Christ, as he enlightens these people by his Word and Spirit, would be opposed and resisted; indeed, these instruments of his would be contradicted and oppressed with every imaginable injury and violence as this *Mystery of Iniquity* grew up in the Church. This process seems to have begun about 400 years after Christ.

I believe this condition of the Church is prefigured in the vision of the *Two Witnesses*, whose mournful prophecy in sackcloth is synchronized <note>original: "Synchronal"</note> with the reign of the False Prophet, as has been demonstrated above. But the description of things is such that it includes the opposition to the *Kingly Office* of Christ as well as his *Prophetic Office*, as shall appear in our explanation of the vision. For if anyone takes it upon himself to be the infallible interpreter of the law of a King, he is effectively making laws for him and stripping him of his throne and scepter. By whatever other device his laws may be suppressed and kept from the people, and other laws put in their place, this *Kingly Office* is clearly rendered meaningless. I have sufficiently declared in my *Idea of Antichristianism* that the Word of God contained in the Old and New Testament is dealt with in this very way by this *False Prophet*.

# Chap. XII. The Vision of the Two Witnesses.

...mouths, Verse VI. That their power of shutting up Heaven from raining may be attributed to them only by a *metalepsis* <note>original: "Metalepsis" — a figure of speech where a word is used in a double sense or replaces a cause with an effect</note>. 2. 1. Let us now investigate what evidence there is of these injuries in this Vision of the *Two mournful Witnesses*; who do not complain without cause, as both the *Regal* and *Prophetic Office* of *Christ* are so clearly opposed by that *Man of Sin* <note>A biblical title often used by writers of this era to refer to the Antichrist or the corrupt papacy</note>. We shall give a brief explanation of the vision, proceeding in order from verse to verse, beginning at the third and continuing until the fourteenth, where the story of the *Witnesses* ends.

*Verse III. And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and sixty days in sackcloth.*

That these *days* are actually so many *years* is clear from the last corollary <note>original: "Consectary"</note> of my Joint-Exposition. That these *witnesses* are *two* is partly due to the symbolic figures <note>original: "Types"</note> they allude to in the Old *Testament*, and partly from the nature of the things they represent. The figures they refer to are *Moses* and *Aaron*, *Elijah* <note>original: "Elias"</note> and *Elisha*, and *Zerubbabel* <note>original: "Zerobabel"</note> and *Joshua* <note>original: "Jesua"</note>—three distinct pairs of holy men famous for their leadership of the People in times that are also analogous to these of the *Two Witnesses*. Their prophecy occurs during the trampling <note>original: "Conculcation"</note> of the *Outer Court* of the Temple by the *Gentiles*—that is, while it is polluted with idolatry. This is similar to how *Moses* and *Aaron* were over the *Israelites* in the wilderness, where they often fell into *idolatry* (which the *Woman in the Wilderness* may perhaps refer to); or *Elijah* and *Elisha* during the *idolatrous apostasy of Baal* <note>original: "Baalitical Apostasy"</note>; and *Zerubbabel* and *Joshua* when they were still in the *Captivity of Babylon*.

There are also three pairs of things that may be fitly represented by these *Two Witnesses*. Either the suppressed *civil government* <note>original: "Magistracy"</note> and *clergy* <note>original: "Ministry"</note> (by which I mean those who stand in opposition to the *Ten-horned Beast* and *False Prophet*, and bear a resemblance to *Moses* and *Aaron* or *Zerubbabel* and *Joshua*); or else the *Jewish people* (I mean those among them who are so sincere that, were it not for the dominance of *Antichristianity* in the world, would be converted to *Christ*), together with the *pure company of Christians* <note>original: "Virgin-company"</note>; or lastly (which corresponds to these last two *Witnesses*), the *Old Testament* and the *New*, which may be added to the others through a figure of speech that treats two things as one <note>original: "Henopœia"</note>.

*Verse IV. These are the two olive trees, and the two lampstands standing before the God of the earth.*

It is a plain *Israelism* <note>original: "Israelism" — a reference to the use of Jewish symbols or history to describe Christian spiritual realities</note>, alluding to that in *Zechariah, Chapter 4:11: What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the lampstand and upon the left side of it?* And then *verse 14: These are the two anointed ones, who stand by the Lord of the whole earth.* Interpreters universally understand these to be *Zerubbabel* and *Joshua* <note>original: "Zerobabel and Jesua" — the political and religious leaders who led the return from the Babylonian exile</note>.

*Verse V. And if anyone wants to hurt them, fire proceeds out of their mouth and devours their enemies; and if any man wants to hurt them, he must be killed in this manner.*

It is an allusion to the story of *Moses* and *Elijah* <note>original: "Elias"</note> bringing down fire upon their opponents. But here it is to be understood more mystically as the fire of the Spirit, or of the Law of God proceeding out of their <margin>Jeremiah 23:29.</margin> mouths, by which they convict the world. *Jeremiah 23: Is not my word like fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that breaks a rock in pieces?* <margin>Verse 4.</margin> Like that of the man out of the sea in *2 Esdras 13*, whose voice, whenever it went out of his mouth, burned all who heard it. And again in <margin>Verse 9, etc.</margin> the same chapter: *And lo, as he saw the violence of the multitude that came, he neither lifted up his hand, nor held a sword nor any instrument of war. But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth what seemed to be a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparks and tempests. And they were all mixed together—the blast of fire, the flaming breath, and the great tempest—and fell with violence on the great multitude which was prepared to fight, and burned them up every one; so that suddenly, out of an innumerable multitude, nothing was to be perceived but only dust and the smell of smoke.* This is afterwards interpreted in verse 38: *And he shall destroy them without labor by the Law, which is like fire.*

By this we may know what is meant by ["*If any man wants to hurt them, he must be killed in this manner.*"] And it was the word of the Lord to *Zerubbabel* <margin>Zechariah 4:6.</margin>, who is alluded to in these Witnesses: *Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of Hosts.* It is so plain that the weapons of the *Two Witnesses* during the time of their mournful prophecy are only spiritual. This is a thing worthy of noting and seriously considering.

*Verse VI. These have power to shut Heaven, so that it does not rain in the days of their prophecy; and they have power over waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with all plagues, as often as they please.*

In the days of their *prophecy*—that is to say, of their mournful prophecy, or in the days of their prophesying in sackcloth—as is plainly understood from the third verse. It is a manifest allusion to *Elijah* preventing rain in *Ahab's* time for three years and six months, which is exactly the time of the prophecy of these Witnesses: namely, 1260 days <note>In prophetic interpretation, 1260 days often represent 1260 years, and three and a half years also equal 1260 days</note>. But the meaning must be more mystical, as these days signify years. Therefore, by *rain* is meant the distilling of that pure, refreshing doctrine of the Gospel, unadulterated by the false interpretations <note>original: "Glosses"</note> of men; these heavenly drops do not descend during the mournful prophecy of the Witnesses. But this *shutting up of Heaven* is attributed to them, not because they positively hinder the descent of this celestial dew, but by a <margin>Revelation 6:4.</margin> *metalepsis* <note>original: "Metalepsis" — a figure of speech where a cause is substituted for an effect, or an indirect reference is made</note>, such as I have already observed regarding the *Rider of the Red Horse*, to whom power is said to be given to *take peace from the earth*, and to whom a great sword was given, even though there is no more un-

2. This is one justifiable interpretation, and yet there is an even better one. This is if the *shutting up of Heaven* is attributed to these two mournful Witnesses not just by a simple *metalepsis* <note>original: "Metalepsis" — a rhetorical figure where an effect is substituted for a cause</note>, but by a *zoopoeia* <note>original: "Zoopœia" — a figure of speech where life or action is attributed to something that does not act directly</note> of the second kind, such as I described above. In this case, although the party to whom the effects are attributed does not actively produce them, they still have a causal influence in some sense. For example, the absent Sun may be said to be the cause of Night and of all the crimes committed under its cover. In the same way, the suppression and removal of these Witnesses is the cause of the *shutting up of Heaven* and the scarcity of the pure Word of God among the people. This cannot be attributed to the *Witnesses* themselves except through a *metalepsis* or, rather, a *zoopoeia*.

3. Following this logic, the *turning of water into blood* and the *striking of the Earth with all plagues as often as they please* is attributed to them through *zoopoeia*. They have no active part in it, any more than the Sun has in all the murders and adulteries committed in its absence during the concealment of the dark night. Therefore, when it adds, *as often as they will*, it is simply the height and grandeur of this rhetorical style. It means no more than *as often as opportunities arise for such effects*, over which the mournful condition of these *Witnesses* has a resulting influence, though not an active one. And *Will* is attributed to them with as much reason and elegance as the *Activity* itself. Indeed, according to a necessary analogy, those occasional consequences correspond exactly to the occasional exercise of the acts of the will in a person who is said to act directly, rather than through *zoopoeia*. This is an allusion to *Moses* striking the land of *Egypt* <note>original: "Ægypt"</note> with those ten plagues. The infliction of these plagues, in a mystical sense, is ascribed to these two *Witnesses* while they are in this debased and dejected state.

The meaning, in brief, is this: the *Roman Empire* contains this spiritual *Egypt* that holds the people of God in bondage. Whether its waters are turned into blood by internal wars and civil strife; or whether it offensively abounds with frogs—meaning slimy, deceptive, and lustful <note>original: "venereous"</note> people; or if it is full of lazy and lice-ridden <note>original: "Lousy"</note> beggars, where a filthy and wretched poverty overwhelms most people because of either the oppression or poor discipline of those in power; or if men are infested and troubled by the persistent attacks of swarms of gnats and flies—that is to say, by a huge number of superstitious anxieties <note>original: "Scrupulosities"</note> and troublesome controversies in academic theology <note>original: "Polemical Theology"</note> that sting, bite, and disturb men's minds and consciences for no purpose other than affliction and unrest; or if the "Beasts" (which the *Platonists* call our bodies) are plagued with murrain <note>original: "Murrain" — a plague or infectious disease affecting domestic animals</note>, meaning they are weighed down with filth, corruption, and the disgusting poison of deadly sins; or if the common people are restless, as if enraged by angry boils and ulcers; or if the barbarian nations from the North invade the Empire like a violent hailstorm; or if the *Turk* and *Saracen* from the South, like a vast army of...

# The Vision of the Two Witnesses. Book II.

Locusts, or that tangible darkness in divine matters that seizes the minds of men, or that the first-born in every family be found dead—that is, says *Alcazar* <note>Luis de Alcazar (1554–1613), a Spanish Jesuit theologian</note>, the soul of every man liable to eternal death. It is as if he would not have the soul be **a body and born later** <note>original: "σῶμα & ὑστερογενῆ" (sōma & hysterogenē)</note> than the body, but rather the first-born in man, because she has the right of primogeniture <note>The right of the first-born to inherit the estate or leadership</note>, the right of ruling over the body. All these plagues of the mystical *Egypt*, whatever they may be (as they certainly cannot signify anything good), are attributed to the two mournful Witnesses by a *zoopoeia* <note>original: "Zoopœia" — a rhetorical figure where an effect is personified or life is attributed to a cause</note>. They are the necessary consequence of the *Witnesses’* disgrace, affliction, and deprivation of power and office, just as darkness, theft, murders, and adulteries are consequences of the absence of the sun.

**Verse VII.** *And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them and kill them.*

The Greek text says, **when they shall perform** <note>original: "ὅταν τελέσωσι" (hotan telesōsi)</note>, which signifies nothing more than "when they shall perform their act of witnessing." And "out of the bottomless pit" is **from the abyss** <note>original: "Ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου" (Ek tēs abyssou)</note>, which is either a deep pit in the earth or out of the sea; thus, it may suggest either the *Two-horned Beast* or the *Ten-horned Beast*. The "making war against them," by a *diorismus* <note>A rhetorical term for a clear distinction or definition</note>, signifies any manner of opposing them and any endeavor to suppress them, not excluding actual war and bloodshed. This happened to them toward the end of their prophecy among the *Waldenses* and *Albigenses* <note>Medieval Christian sects persecuted as heretics by the Catholic Church</note> and others. And just as *war* signifies any opposition, so *death* or *killing* signifies any change of their condition for the worse, so that they cease to be what they were before. It is plain that this is a *political death*, or a removal from power, because their *resurrection* is of the same nature. See "Death and Resurrection" in my *Prophetic Alphabet*. So the sense is this: no sooner shall they begin to perform their office of witnessing to the truth, but they shall be assaulted, suppressed, and politically killed—that is, kept out of power.

**Verse VIII.** *And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city that spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.*

I have explained this verse already. However, you may take notice here of how well this name "Egypt" agrees with the mention of the *Egyptian* plagues alluded to before; those plagues remained upon the land because the Egyptians still kept the people of God in bondage and would not allow them to serve God according to His own will and command.

**Verse IX.** *And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and a half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves.*

<margin>Book 5. Chapter 15. Section 4.</margin> This "not being buried" has a double meaning, as you may see in the *Prophetic Alphabet*. But I must confess I take the more favorable interpretation to be the truer one: that their *not being buried* is a pledge of their eventual *resurrection*—that is, *after three days and a half*. In my *Mystery of Godliness*, I have shown this to be *three times and a half*, or 1260 years, the very same length of time as their mournful prophecy. For since they are only "politically dead," it is not at all inconsistent with the truth of the symbolism that they should prophesy in a mournful condition; indeed, it is

# Chapter XII. The Vision of the Two Witnesses. 407

<margin><unclear>Revelation 11:7.</unclear></margin> It is necessary to be so. The Spirit of God, intending to present these two aspects of their condition—namely, their prophetic testimony and their loss of all political power (which Scripture calls the *death of a people*, just as it calls their restoration to a state of government their *resurrection*)—has designed the outer layer <note>original: "Cortex"</note> of this vision with such incredible skill. He did this partly because it would be very inconsistent to have them prophesy while they were dead, and partly because a duration of 1260 years—the length of their prophecy—is not a suitable amount of time for a dead body to lie unburied in the street before reviving. In this way, these logical difficulties are avoided through the double meaning <note>original: "Homonymia" — the use of a term that can have multiple meanings; here, the "days" of the vision representing "years" in prophecy</note> of the "three and a half days." All parts of the prophetic imagery are made to maintain proper proportion and balance, as well as the internal meaning of what they represent. Yet, this does not prevent a wise <note>original: "sagacious"</note> reader from finding the true meaning, as "three and a half days" easily suggests "three and a half times," which is the exact same duration as 1260 days. Whether there is a secondary meaning to these "three and a half days," such as the one Joseph Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), a famous English biblical scholar and expert on the Book of Revelation</note> suggested, only future events will tell. Personally, I see little or no evidence in the text for such an interpretation. See my *Mystery of Godliness* and what I have previously mentioned in this book.

They naturally rejoice when the *Two Witnesses* are killed, because the Witnesses' bold rebukes based on the word of God were very unsettling and tormenting to these worldly and carnally minded people. See my *Mystery of Godliness*.

**Verse XI.** *And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them; and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them that saw them.*

The fact that the *Spirit of life from God entered into them* corresponds to what we previously cited from Zechariah: *“Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,” says the Lord of Hosts.* You can find more evidence that this "resurrection" has a political meaning in my *Prophetic Alphabet*, specifically in my discussion of that term.

**Verse 12.** *And they heard a voice from Heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to Heaven in a cloud, and their enemies beheld them.*

I would prefer to translate the Greek phrase **and they heard** <note>original: "καὶ ἤκουσαν" (kai ēkousan)</note> as "For they heard," etc. This voice from Heaven raises them from the dead, just as the voice of Christ raised Lazarus. In this context, *Heaven* represents the high-ranking positions in the political universe. The slain Witnesses are called to these positions by a voice from above saying, *“Come up here.”* From this, we might observe that true witnesses will not seek power before they are called. # The Vision of the Two Witnesses. Book II. 408

...positions of honor <note>original: "Dignities"</note>. For it is not true of this Political Heaven, but of the Spiritual, that *the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.*
<margin>Matthew 11:12</margin>

The fact that these Witnesses are said to *ascend up to Heaven in a cloud* appears to be an allusion to Christ's own Ascension after his Crucifixion, which is also referenced here in the eighth verse. Furthermore, the duration of Christ's mournful prophecy before his Resurrection was about *three years and a half* (if we may trust the historians of time <note>original: "Chronologers"</note>), which makes the comparison even more perfect.

**Verse 13.** *And at the same time there was a great earthquake, and a tenth part of the city fell; and in the earthquake seven thousand names of men were slain: and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.*

It is obvious to any observer that an "earthquake" signifies political commotions and a change in public affairs. However, it has not been so easy for everyone to realize that the "city" mentioned here should be understood not as a city of brick or stone, but as a *Polity* <note>a system of government or an organized society</note>. But I believe it is plain enough that this city is the very same "great city" mentioned in the eighth verse. This *great city* is the *Whore of Babylon* <note>a symbolic figure in Revelation often associated by Protestant reformers with the corrupt Roman Church</note>, and the *Whore of Babylon* is nothing other than the body of the idolatrous clergy in the Empire. These belong to the *seventh* or last *Head of the Beast*, which is a "Head of Blasphemy" just like the first six—which is to say, it is an idolatrous leadership.

From this, we can understand what is meant by these *Seven thousand names of men*. Neither "seven" nor "thousand" signifies a specific, literal number (though by a clever <term>Diorismus</term> they appear to do so). Instead, they signify only the nature or property of those "names of men" said to be slain—namely, that they are the titles, honors, offices, or religious orders of men belonging to the state of Christendom while it is under that Seventh Head, which has become idolatrous and anti-Christian. 

Because this number "seven" is multiplied into a "thousand," it signifies a complete and permanent abolishing of all such corrupt offices and orders of men. If Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential English scholar of prophecy</note> had noticed this, it would have saved him the labor of trying to explain the exact meaning of "Names of men" <note>original Greek: Ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων / Onomata anthropōn</note>, as well as his anxiety regarding whether the number of people killed was proportional to the event. For no actual men are necessarily implied to be killed here; rather, all anti-Christian offices and brotherhoods are to be dissolved and abolished, and affairs are to be restored to the purity of the first four hundred years of the Church. To "slay," in this symbolic sense <note>original: "by a Diorismus"</note>, signifies nothing more than causing a thing to cease to exist. I have little doubt that this is the true meaning of this passage. Furthermore, the phrase "the tenth part of the city" <note>original Greek: τὸ δέκατον τῆς πόλεως / to dekaton tēs poleōs</note> has a meaning that coincides marvelously with this interpretation.

However, as for any intended destruction of the actual brick and stone, walls, and buildings of *Rome*—either in this present vision or any other in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note>—I must admit that I am currently too dim-sighted to see it. According to my view, the "Papal Polity" (the system of government), represented through <term>Hylasmus</term>, is what is intended in all the warnings against her, not the physical city itself. Therefore, if the physical city were to be burned, sacked, or sunk by literal earthquakes, it might only be a side-effect <note>original: "By-Accident"</note>, and not the thing directly pointed at or symbolized in the apocalyptic visions. But if such a thing should happen in circumstances that...

# That the Fourth Kingdom in Daniel Book II.

5. *Grotius's foolish <note>original: "fond"</note> and profane interpretation of the Son of Man, as if it meant the people of Rome.* 6. *A similar extravagance in his interpretation of the "stone cut out without hands" as referring to the same people.* 7. *The flaws of that idea more specifically revealed.* 8. *Further proof that the kingdoms of the Lagids and Seleucids <note>the dynasties of Alexander the Great's successors in Egypt and Syria</note> are not the Fourth Kingdom, based on the simultaneous existence of the Ten Kings according to the prophecy.* 9. *Proof from their vastly different time periods: one ending, according to Daniel, shortly after Antiochus, while the other does not end before the Day of Judgment.* 10. *From Daniel’s identification of the "great horn" as the first king in the Third Kingdom, with four lesser horns growing up after him on the same goat's head.* 11. *From the four heads of the Leopard, which are the four successors of Alexander in this Third Beast or Kingdom, and from Daniel’s placement of Antiochus at the end of this succession.* 12. *That the "little horn" necessarily belongs to the Roman Kingdom, which becomes ten-horned and both pagan and Christian at once.* 13. *That it lasts for the same duration as the Whore and the Two-horned Beast, and at least coincides in time with them and the restored Beast.* 14. *From this equality and coincidence, he is discovered to be the Whore or the Two-horned Beast.* 15. *That the Patriarch of Rome is specifically concerned in this symbolic type.* 16. *The perfect applicability of the characteristics of this "horn" to the said Patriarch.* 17. *The application of those characteristics that specifically concern his opposition to the kingly <note>original: "Regal"</note> office of Christ.*

1. That prophecy also in *Daniel* of the *little horn* that is said to *change times and laws* is an explicit prediction of that Antichristian opposition which is against the kingly office of Christ. For I think no one will hesitate <note>original: "scruple"</note> to believe that this *little horn* is the same as the *Two-horned Beast* or the *Whore* in the *Apocalypse* <note>the Book of Revelation</note>, if they consider that this horn is part of the *Roman* Kingdom which is described by *ten horns*. Furthermore, it belongs to that time when the kingdom is actually *ten-horned*. These ten horns exist at the same time, not in succession; just as the *ten toes* of the statue, which correspond to these *ten horns*, do not signify a succession of ten kings, but ten kings ruling at the same time. Like the toes of the feet of an image, they do not have a sequence of rank, but rather a coordinated position.

<margin>Daniel 2.</margin>
2. Now, there are these weighty reasons to convince us that the *Fourth Kingdom*—which is prefigured by the *iron legs, feet, and ten toes* of the *image*, and by the *Beast* with *iron teeth* and *ten horns*—is not that of the *Lagids* and *Seleucids*, as Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius, a Dutch scholar who argued for a more historical, less apocalyptic interpretation of Daniel</note> would have it, but rather the Kingdom of the *Romans*.

First, it is the universal opinion of all ecclesiastical writers *that the Fourth Beast is the Roman Empire*; as both Cornelius à Lapide and Gaspar Sanctius—both of whom were Jesuits—roundly assert. The words of the latter are these: *“Therefore, by the opinion of everyone, this unnamed and horrible beast is the Roman Empire; nor is it necessary to name anyone specifically, since everyone says so.”* <note>original Latin: "Est ergo omnium sententiâ innominata hæc atque horribilis bellua Romanum Imperium ; neque necesse est quenquam nominare, cùm nemo non dicat."</note>

Chapter XIII. The Fourth Kingdom is not that of the Lagids and Seleucids. 411

3. Secondly, it cannot be the Kingdom of the **Lagids** <note>original: "Lagidæ"; the Greek dynasty of the Ptolemies in Egypt</note> and **Seleucids** <note>the Greek dynasty in Syria and Mesopotamia</note>, as **Grotius** <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch jurist and theologian</note> would lead us to believe. In this odd whim of his, he abandons the judgment of the entire Church of Christ to follow the opinion of **Porphyry** <note>a 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher and critic of Christianity</note>, who was a sworn enemy to the Christian religion. This is clear from what is said in Daniel 7:23: *The Fourth Beast shall be the Fourth Kingdom upon Earth*, which shall be different from all kingdoms <note>original Hebrew: די תשנא מן-כל-מלכותא</note>, *which shall be greater than all kingdoms* <note>original Latin: "Quod majus erit omnibus regnis"</note>; so says the Vulgate Latin and **Vatablus** <note>François Vatable, a 16th-century French humanist and scholar</note>. The **Septuagint** <note>The "Seventy," the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> also translates it as "which shall surpass all kingdoms" <note>original Greek: ήτις υπερέξει πασας τας βασιλείας</note>. 

This agrees best with what follows: *and shall devour the whole Earth (which must be understood in the same sense as "Earth" was used before) and shall tread it down and break it in pieces.* It could not be said to do this unless it were as great a kingdom as is suggested here. Now it is obvious that the kingdom of the Seleucids and Lagids was neither greater, more excellent, nor a more victorious kingdom than any of the three preceding ones—namely, the **Babylonian**, the **Persian**, and that of **Alexander the Great**. Grotius's theory would make the Seleucid and Lagid kingdoms distinct from Alexander's kingdom. Therefore, their kingdom cannot be this Fourth Kingdom.

This logical conclusion is so plain to **Gaspar Sanctius** <note>a Jesuit biblical commentator</note> that he—quite justly, yet very severely—scolds Porphyry for this error which Grotius has so unluckily adopted. For he breaks out into these words regarding this text: "See the stupidity and laziness of Porphyry, that it could even enter his mind to think that the kingdom of those who succeeded Alexander was the greatest of all, and that it subjected and trampled the whole earth, when it was far weaker than the other kingdoms and was either cut to pieces or badly harassed by everyone" <note>original Latin: "Vide Porphyrii stuporem & oscitantiam, in cujus mentem venire potuit ut existimaverit regnum eorum qui Alexandro successere omnium esse maximum, quodque omnem terram sibi subjecerit conculcaveritque, cum reliquis regnis longè fuerit infirmius, & ab omnibus concisum aut malè vexatum."</note>. Indeed, the prophecy itself makes the kingdom of Alexander’s successors smaller than his in power and greatness; Daniel 8:22 says that four kingdoms shall stand up, but not with the power of Alexander—meaning they shall be inferior to him. This undoubtedly refers to them collectively, as it would be unnecessary to mention their weakness individually.

4. Thirdly, the Kingdom of the **Iron legs** and toes and the Ten-horned Beast with iron teeth are one and the same kingdom, according to Grotius's own acknowledgment; he identifies it as that of the Seleucids and Lagids.

Of this horn it is said in verse 21: *I beheld, and the same horn made war with the Saints, and prevailed against them, until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the Saints of the most High.* This is the same as the Son of Man's coming in the clouds of Heaven to receive the King-

# That the Fourth Kingdom in Daniel Book II.

[The king]dom of the ***Ancient of Days*** <note>original: "Ancient of days"; a title for God from Daniel 7:9</note>, verse 13. And both [the Son of Man and the Stone] agree with the ***Stone cut out without hands***, to show it is not the work of man, but of the ***Ancient of Days***—God himself. This is indeed the very Kingdom of ***Christ***, as interpreters have always explained it. This perfectly contradicts ***Grotius’s*** dream that the Fourth Beast with iron teeth and the iron legs of the statue denote the Kingdom of the ***Lagids*** <note>original: "Lagidæ"; the Greek dynasty of the Ptolemies in Egypt</note> and ***Seleucids*** <note>the Greek dynasty in Syria and Mesopotamia</note>, and that ***Antiochus*** is this "little ***Horn***."

For ***Antiochus Epiphanes*** was dead almost two hundred years before Christ even preached the ***Doctrine of the Kingdom*** or had any disciples to follow him. Yet it is said in ***Daniel*** 2:44, *And in the days of these kingdoms shall the God of Heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed*. (From this passage, I have no doubt that the phrase [***The Kingdom of God***], as well as the phrase [***The Kingdom of Heaven***], occurs so often in the Gospel. It is also the source of the title which Christ so often gives himself: the ***Son of Man***. And ***Grotius*** himself, in his commentary on ***Matthew*** Chapter 8:20, acknowledges that the "Son of Man" <note>original Aramaic: בר אנש (Bar Enash)</note> mentioned in ***Daniel*** 7:13 is to be understood as the ***Messiah***.) Therefore, it is impossible for the Kingdom of the ***Lagids*** and ***Seleucids*** to be the Fourth Kingdom.

5. But here ***Grotius***, contrary to the judgment he held when he wrote on ***Matthew***, has devised a strategy that can scarcely be spoken of without horror and astonishment. I am infinitely amazed that a man otherwise so learned and praiseworthy (as he himself says of ***Porphyry*** <note>a 3rd-century critic of Christianity</note>) should be misled into such a bad venture. ***The Son of Man coming in the clouds of Heaven*** is, according to him, ***the Roman people having no king among themselves*** <note>original Latin: "Populus Romanus nullum intra se habens regem"</note>. When our Savior Christ suggested to the High Priest that he was that ***Son of Man who should come in the clouds of Heaven***, it seemed like such a high presumption <note>original: "Arrogation"</note> that the priest tore his clothes and said ***he had spoken blasphemy***. And truly, I think that neither Jew nor Christian can easily acquit ***Grotius*** of that crime, as he attributes the unique character of the ***Messiah*** to a profane and pagan people—and does so simply because they had no king, as if they were somehow better for that. But they had kings at first; and both in the infancy of their Empire and afterward, they possessed a supreme power so great and imperial that it excuses them from the slightest appearance of being "lowly." They always had a sovereignty over them, so they could not be considered the ***Son of Man*** based on any supposed "private" or "obscure" condition. For ***Supreme Power*** <note>original Latin: "Summa Potestas"</note> is ***Supreme Power*** under whatever name or form it takes, and it possesses the same real grandeur. Besides, they were a most glorious and victorious people before ***Antiochus’s*** time. Thus, it is a very weak and lifeless <note>original: "dilute and sapless"</note> idea of ***Grotius*** to apply the phrase "Son of Man" to them due to any supposed insignificance or obscurity, for they were not obscure in the times of ***Antiochus***.

6. Again, the Kingdom of the ***Son of Man*** and the ***Stone cut out without hands*** are one and the same, both in truth and according to ***Grotius’s*** own admission. But this ***Stone*** is ***Christ*** and his Kingdom, being heavenly and ***not made with hands*** <note>original Greek: ἀχειροποίητον (acheiropoieton)</note>—a thing established not by human power, but by...
