by the power and Spirit of God. That this is the meaning of [*without hands*] is the general consensus <note>original: "vote"</note> of interpreters: St. Jerome, Irenaeus, Justin, Epiphanius, St. Augustine, Theodoret, and several others.

Where do you think Grotius seeks refuge <note>original: "take shelter"</note> now? Why, this figure which is so appropriate to Christ, and mentioned of him so often in the New Testament—*this Stone*—must be cast away, as if it were neither precious nor a cornerstone, and be bestowed instead upon a pagan people, the *Romans*. For Grotius does not hesitate <note>original: "stick"</note> to profess: *The Stone and the Son of Man are the same* <note>original Latin: "Idem Lapis & Filius hominis"</note>; and he previously argued that the *Son of Man* represented the people of *Rome*. But can a man believe that the origin or success of that people was *not made by human hands* <note>original Greek: ἀχειροποίητον (acheiropoieton); a term used in the New Testament to describe things of divine rather than human origin</note>—a thing brought to pass by the special power and Spirit of God—and not *after the manner of men* <note>original Latin: "more humano"</note>, according to the usual course of the world? And even that was not of the best kind, as their beginnings were aided by a rabble of ruffians and robbers.

7. No, but you will say that is not Grotius’s interpretation <note>original: "gloss"</note>. Let us therefore hear what it is: the *Stone cut from the mountain without hands* <note>original Latin: "Lapis abscissus de monte sine manibus"</note> is, according to him, *An army of a people who were of their own will and subject to no king; the origin of which people was from a mountain, namely the Palatine* <note>original Latin: "Exercitus populi qui suæ esset spontis nullique regi pareret; cujus populi origo à monte, nempe Palatino"</note>. In this, there is nothing sound nor solid. For was this *Roman Army* anything more *of its own will* <note>original Latin: "suæ spontis"</note> simply because they did not have a kingly government in Rome? The supreme power of the *consuls* and *senators* was as directive and coercive <note>original: "coactive"</note> as if it had been *regal*. So the movement of this army was not any more spontaneous because of this. Again, the *Stone cut from the mountain without hands* implies that it was spontaneously divided from the mountain at the moment it is said to be *cut* from it. But when the *Romans* first emerged from Mount *Palatine*—indeed, as soon as they became the *Roman people* <note>original Latin: "populus Romanus"</note>—*regal government* existed among them, it being the first government of this people. Therefore, they were not then *a people of their own will* <note>original Latin: "Populus suæ spontis"</note>, according to Grotius’s whim <note>original: "conceit"</note>; thus, he cannot make his argument consistent <note>original: "bring both ends together"</note>. And, lastly, to interpret *mountain* here in a literal sense is unskillfully done; it fits neither the analogy of the prophetic style nor the very suggestion <note>original: "intimation"</note> of the text itself, which says the *little stone* became a *great mountain* itself and filled the whole earth. Therefore, since this *mountain* signifies something political rather than literal, there is no question that the other mountain does so too, and that the stone is in some sense of the same nature <note>original: "homogeneall"</note> as this rocky mountain.

From this, the meaning is plainly this: that out of the great mountain—that is, the *Roman Empire*—there should be a people raised, not by human power or policy, but by the Spirit of God and the preaching of the Gospel by *Jesus Christ* and his Apostles. These people would be a "peculiar people" <note>A biblical term (Titus 2:14) meaning a people belonging exclusively to God</note> to him and become the subjects of his Kingdom. That is to say, the Church of *Christ* should be cut out of the *Roman Empire* without human help. This is a most simple and undistorted interpretation, against which no objection can be raised.

# That the Fourth Kingdom in Daniel Book II is not that of the Ptolemies and Seleucids.

8. Eighth <note>The original text numbers these points sequentially but restarts the internal count at "fifth".</note>, the *Ten toes* imply that the *Ten Horns* exist at the same time, because of how they are positioned together. This means there must be ten kings reigning simultaneously in the Fourth Kingdom. But in the Kingdom of the *Seleucids* and *Ptolemies* <note>original: "Seleucidæ and Lagidæ"; the latter refers to the dynasty of Ptolemy I, son of Lagos</note>, there were never ten kings reigning all at once. Therefore, that kingdom is not the Fourth.

9. Ninthly (or fifthly), *Antiochus Epiphanes*, who was part of this kingdom of the *Ptolemies* and *Seleucids*, is said to *rise up in the latter time of the kingdom of the successors of Alexander* (Daniel 8:22–23). Therefore, this kingdom of the *Ptolemies* and *Seleucids* expired nearly two thousand years ago. But the Kingdom of the Fourth Beast reaches even to the Day of Judgment, as seen in Daniel 7:9–10: *I watched until the thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His throne was like a fiery flame, and its wheels were like burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him; thousand thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; the judgment was set, and the books were opened, etc.* That this is a description of the Day of Judgment is the general opinion of both Christians and Jews. It corresponds exactly to the *lake of fire* and the opening of the books in Revelation <note>original: "Apocal." (Apocalypse)</note> 20, which Grotius himself interprets as the Last Day. From this, we may safely conclude that the kingdom of the *Ptolemies* and *Seleucids* is not the Fourth Kingdom, since it ceased so long before that time. This holds true even if we understood the *Day of Judgment* in the sense used by the Rabbis <note>original Hebrew: יום דינא רבא (Yom Dina Rabba), meaning "the Great Day of Judgment"</note>. According to that view, the meaning of [*I watched until the thrones were set—and the books were opened*] is that the prophet Daniel had a vision reaching to the very end of that Great Day. However, he begins more specifically with the start of that Day in the eleventh verse. But I have only noted this in passing.

10. Tenthly (or sixthly) and lastly, Alexander's kingdom and that of his successors are all one and the same kingdom. Yet Alexander’s is the Third Kingdom, according to Grotius's own admission. Now, it is evident from Daniel 8:21 that the kingdom of his successors (which includes the *Ptolemies* and *Seleucids*) is one kingdom with Alexander’s: *The rough goat is the king of Greece <note>original: "Græcia"</note>, and the great horn between his eyes is the first king. Now, since that was broken and four stood up in its place, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not with his power.* This is clear proof that the kingdom of Alexander and his successors is all one kingdom. By calling Alexander the *first king*, it necessarily implies that his successors are the second, third, and so on, and that they all belong to one and the same kingdom. Indeed, he says plainly that *these four horns stand up in place of that great one*—that is, as his replacements. What is this but to succeed him as the heads of the very same empire? No new "beast" is said to succeed this beast; rather, new horns succeed the original horn. Furthermore, the comparison saying *but not in his power* further suggests a kinship <note>original: "cognation"</note> and succession within one line, showing he is not speaking of the heads of two different kingdoms.

This appears further from verse 8: *Therefore the goat grew very great; and when he was strong, the great horn was broken, and in its place came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven.* But where should these

<meta>This page continues the author's critique of Hugo Grotius's interpretation of Daniel's prophecies. ### Chapter XIII. The Fourth Kingdom is not that of the Ptolemies and Seleucids.

These [horns] come up, but they appear on that same head that had lost its great horn, which is replaced with four smaller ones, though they are significant in their own way. For it is very inconsistent and far-fetched to imagine them appearing on any other head. And surely, if they had belonged to any other beast, that beast would not have failed to be named. Therefore, they must either grow out of this goat's head or nowhere at all—unless they grow out of the ground, which is ridiculous. And therefore it is plain that *Alexander's* kingdom and that of his successors is but one single kingdom. For that goat is one and the same goat throughout the succession of this variety of horns.

11. And yet there is still greater evidence of this truth from Daniel 7:6: *After this I looked, and behold, another beast like a leopard, which had on its back four wings of a bird; the beast also had four heads, and dominion was given to it.* That the four heads of this beast are the four successors of *Alexander*—namely, *Perdiccas*, *Seleucus*, *Ptolemy*, and *Meleager*—*Grotius* himself frankly admits. The *wings*, therefore, represent the four kingdoms *Alexander's* Empire was divided into after his death; yet it is still looked upon as one beast regardless, just as the *Roman* Empire is seen as one despite its division into ten kingdoms (marked by ten horns) or into the Eastern and Western Empires (represented by the two wings of an eagle).

Here *Grotius*, if he would speak plainly, would make *Alexander* the beast itself, just as he has done with *Domitian* and others in the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note> against all the laws of prophetic interpretation—indeed, against all rhyme and reason. For he explains it this way: *The leopard is a diverse animal; so Alexander was a man of diverse character* <note>original: "Pardus varium Animal, sic Alexander moribus variis"</note>. But consider how grossly inconsistent this is. If that were the case, then *Alexander* would be inferior to his four chief officers, and they would be his "heads," which is a political absurdity. Even worse, they would be his "heads" after he had ceased to exist, which is a metaphysical absurdity. Therefore, *Alexander* is the first "head" or "great horn" of this beast, not the body of the beast itself. This allows him to be superior to his four grand officers, and ensures he is not the beast itself, which must bear these four horns or heads long after he has left the stage of history. For these were not *heads* nor *horns* before he was dead. *Alexander*, therefore, is the first in the succession of the heads or horns of this beast, not the beast itself.

But to get closer to our point: I say it is very manifest from these four heads and four wings that this *leopard* is said to have, that the *Third Kingdom* includes the four first successors of *Alexander*. Nothing can be clearer than this from the text itself. For the *leopard* is described in the *third place*, and immediately after him the Fourth Beast is mentioned and called the *fourth* (v. 7). Therefore, this four-headed *leopard* is plainly the Third Beast. Furthermore, the fact that the succession of these four heads, continuing down to *Antiochus Epiphanes*, constitutes one and the same kingdom is plain from Daniel 8:22: *As for the horn that was broken, in place of which four others rose up, four kingdoms shall rise up out of that nation, but not with its power.* And *in the latter time of their kingdom* (the original Hebrew has it <term>ובאחרית מלכותם</term> <note>transliteration: "u-be-acharit malkutam"</note>, which the seventy translators of the Septuagint render <term>ἐν ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάτων τῆς βασιλείας αὐτῶν</term> <note>transliteration: "en ep’ eschaton tes basileias auton"</note>, which is the very same as our *English*, and there is no doubt of the translation) *a king of fierce countenance... shall stand up.* This king is someone whom *Grotius* and everyone else admits is *Antiochus Epiphanes*.

# The Vision of the little Horn with Eyes. Book II.

From this it is evident that the entire succession of *Alexander’s* captains, from the first four inclusive even to the time of *Antiochus*, is one succession and one kingdom. For the scripture calls the times of *Antiochus* the *last times of their kingdom*.

Therefore it is plain, seeing that the kingdom of *Alexander* is one and the same as the kingdom of the four captains (for that is the *Third Kingdom*), and the kingdom of the four captains is the same as their successors even to the time of *Antiochus*; the entire succession from *Alexander* to *Antiochus* is one succession and one kingdom. If this is not demonstrably true, then there is no such thing as a mathematical demonstration. But if this is true, the kingdoms of the *Ptolemies* <note>original: "Lagidæ"; the dynasty of Egypt founded by Ptolemy I Soter</note> and the *Seleucids* <note>original: "Seleucidæ"; the dynasty of Syria and Persia founded by Seleucus I Nicator</note> are not the *Fourth Kingdom*. Instead, the Fourth Kingdom is that of the *Romans*, as all level-headed men have traditionally held.

12. Since we are so firmly assured of this, we shall easily know where to seek for this *little horn* that is said to *change times and laws*. For where can we find it but among those many horns in the *Roman* kingdom or empire? We cannot find it in the *Greek* kingdom, to which *Antiochus Epiphanes* belongs. And we have already plainly shown that the Beast in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Apocalyptick Beast"</note> with seven heads and ten horns *is this Roman kingdom*. We have also shown that this Beast, once *healed*—or in such a condition that it may be said of him that he is the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is* (which happens when he has become *Pagano-Christian*)—is this Empire actually divided into ten kingdoms. Together with this division, the Empire began to slide back gradually into idolatry under the agency and guidance of the "Two-horned Beast" or the *Whore*, whom I have also shown to exist at the same time <note>original: "Synchronal"</note> as the healed Beast, or the *Beast that was, and is not, and yet is*.

13. The duration of the Beast restored or healed is 42 *months*, which is 1,260 *days*, or a *time and times and half a time* <note>A "time" signifies a year, "times" two years, and "half a time" six months, totaling three and a half years in prophetic calculations</note>. For the stay of the *Woman in the Wilderness* is expressed interchangeably by either of these latter terms; and the first and the second are joined together in the vision of the *outer court* and the *Two Witnesses*. Therefore, since 42 *months* and a *time and times and half a time* are the same as 1,260 *days*, they are all the same as one another. But the reign of this *little horn* in *Daniel* that we are speaking of is also described as lasting a *time and times and half a time*. Therefore, it is of the same duration as the *Whore* or the Two-horned Beast, which exists at the same time as the *restored Beast*, whose duration is 42 *months*.

Therefore, there is a strong suspicion that there is at least a coincidence of time, if not of affairs, or a mixing of natures (if not an actual identity) between this *little horn* in *Daniel* and those three contemporary entities: the *restored Beast*, the *Whore*, and the *Two-horned Beast*. For that expression in *Daniel 7:24*, *And another shall rise after them*, does not hinder this interpretation at all, since the Greek translators <note>original: "Seventy"; referring to the Septuagint</note> translate the Hebrew word <term>behind them</term> <note>original: "אחריהון"</note> as <term>behind them</term> <note>original: "ὀπίσω αὐτῶν"</note>. This signifies the order of their physical position as well as their order in time. And being placed *behind* is the most convenient position for such a feat as is attributed to this *horn*, which is said to *throw down or humble three kings*—something achieved more by treachery and craft than by open force.

### Chapter XIII. The Vision of the Little Horn with Eyes.

14. Now, from this equality of duration, it also follows that the lifespan of this *little horn* is 1,260 years, according to the final logical consequence <note>original: "Consectary"</note> of our joint interpretation. This again shows how impossible it is for this horn to be *Antiochus Epiphanes*. To this, you may add that it is said to be different from the rest of the horns in their explanation. <margin>* Daniel 7:24.</margin> *And the ten horns out of this kingdom* (that is, the *Roman kingdom*, as has been demonstrated) *are ten kings that shall arise; and another shall rise* after them <note>original: "ὀπίσω αὐτῶν"; behind or following them</note>, *and he shall be distinct from the rest, and he shall conquer three kings.* Now I ask: which one of the ten kings or kingdoms is so different from all the rest, unless it is a *religious kingdom* <note>original: "Ecclesiastical Kingdome"</note>?

Therefore, the fact that its timeline coincides with the *Pagano-Christian* Empire <note>The period when the Roman Empire transitioned to Christianity while retaining pagan-like structures or ceremonies</note>, its long duration, and the difference of this kingdom from the other ten, creates more than a strong suspicion. It suggests that this is part of the succession of a religious kingdom which must necessarily run alongside the Empire while it professes Christianity. But if the question is whether this part of the religious kingdom is the uncorrupted Kingdom of Christ or the reign of Antichrist, the solution is not difficult. It is plain that it is not the Kingdom of Christ, because Christ is said to come *to burn and consume it*. From this, it is manifest that the Church has not been wrong in its opinion <note>original: "Conjecture"</note> in considering this *little horn* to be *Antichrist*. Therefore, I say, it is the same as the *Two-horned Beast* and the *Whore of Babylon*, who clearly exists for the same duration <note>original: "Isochronal"</note> and, I do not doubt, starts and ends at the same time <note>original: "Synchronal"</note> as this *little horn*. Furthermore, she is judged to be burned in the *Book of Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note>, just as this *little horn* is here in *Daniel*.

15. To speak briefly, therefore: this *little horn* represents the clergy of the Empire who encourage idolatry <note>original: "Idolatrizing Clergy"</note>, but more chiefly and particularly that great and notorious part under the *Pope* <note>original: "Bishop of Rome"</note>. He has been an exceptionally persistent advocate <note>original: "stickler"</note> for both establishing this corrupt religious empire within the *Roman Empire* and for allowing the Empire to fall back into and remain suppressed by superstition and idolatry. Therefore, he is rightly said to be a *horn growing out of this Beast*, as the symbol of the *Beast* itself—according to the scholar *Grotius’s* own confession—suggests *Idolatry*.

16. If an exceptionally perfect fit of application can assure us of the right sense of a prophecy, we cannot fail in this one when examining every characteristic of this *little horn*. For just as it is described as *little*, so were the origins of the Popes humble and unknown <note>original: "mean and obscure"</note>, and their worldly territory <note>original: "Secular Principality"</note> remains small in comparison to those princes they have competed with. Again, as this *horn had the eyes of a man*, it is well known that for political shrewdness <note>original: "politick quick-sightedness"</note> there has been no body of men comparable to the *Roman Hierarchy*. Indeed, it has become a proverb to say, *“That the Roman religion is nothing else but a mere political trick to increase and keep up the honor, power, and wealth of the Pope and his clergy.”* See Sir *Edwin Sandys’* book *Speculum Europae* (A View of Europe), and you shall find this part of the prophecy fulfilled to an admirable degree. It is not for nothing that this *little horn* is said to have the *eyes of a man* in it, a detail mentioned for no other *horn* in all the prophecies. Thirdly, as this *horn* is said to have a *mouth speaking great things*, whether you mean by that its boasting of its own sovereignty or its *blaspheming*...

# The Vision of the Rider of the white Horse. Book II.

And cruel force did what it could to smother, stifle, and extinguish them. But here the scene of things has changed, and the pure Word of God has gained the victory over the corrupt, *superstitious*, *idolatrous*, and contradictory opinions and foolish <note>original: "fond"</note> institutions of that *Antichristian* body of men over whom the *Pope* has a special headship and sovereignty.

3. There is no great difficulty in understanding this prophecy if we refer to my *Prophetic Alphabet* <note>The author’s specialized system for decoding symbolic language in the Bible</note>, where I have set down what a *Horse* and the color *White* signify. That the *eyes* of this *hero* <note>original: "Heros"</note> are said to be like a *flaming fire* suggests his sharp-sightedness, as it is said in the book of *Hebrews*:
<margin>Hebrews 4:12.</margin>
> *That the Word of God is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart, and that there is no creature that is not manifest in his sight, but that all things lie naked and open unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do:*
Where the *Written Word* (Scripture) and the *Eternal Word* (Christ) are jointly spoken of, as they seem to be here in this vision, by a "union of meanings" <term>original: "Henopœia"; a rhetorical figure where two distinct things are treated as one</term>.

Again, in that his eyes are said to be a *flaming fire*, we may also note how *fire* is a symbol of *intelligence* <note>original: "Intellectuality"</note>, especially a *flaming fire*, which implies light, as is easily understood from the philosophical *Cabbala* <term>A tradition of mystical or spiritual interpretation</term> of the first day’s creation.

-> These seeds have a fiery vigor and a heavenly origin. <-
<note>original: "Igneus est illis vigor & cælestis origo Seminibus." — Virgil, Aeneid VI. 730</note>

And we read of a "fiery mind" <note>original: "πυριὸς νοῦς"</note> in the *Magic Oracles*, and of "shining fire" <note>original: "πῦρ φαεινὸν"</note> attributed to the soul as being "a certain divine and intellectual essence" <note>original: "θεία τις οὐσία καὶ νοερά"</note>, as *Plethon* <note>Gemistus Plethon, a Neoplatonist philosopher</note> speaks. Therefore the *Logos* <note>The Word</note> here is rightly said to have *eyes like a flaming fire*, because he is not only *intellectual*, but that *Great and Eternal Intellect* from which all *intellectual beings* come; as also all their *operations* are exercised by virtue of the more pure, ethereal, and fiery <note>original: "igneous"</note> *spirits*.

4. Also, the detail of *having a name written that no man knew but himself* seems to agree with the *Cabbalistic doctrine*, which makes *Aaron* <note>The first High Priest of Israel</note> a symbol of the *Eternal Word* that fills the universe, as also of *Christ* who is this *Word Incarnate*. The allusion, therefore, may be to *Aaron* having the *Tetragrammaton* <term>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</term> written upon his mitre—that name which is said to be "unutterable" <note>original: "ἄρρητον"</note> and "unpronounceable" <note>original: "ἀνεκφώνητον"</note>, and could be read only by the High Priest who had it written upon the golden plate on his mitre, as *Alcazar* <note>Luis de Alcázar, a Jesuit theologian</note> has observed. But in brief, it signifies the incomprehensibility and the impossibility of searching out the divinity of our Savior; only he who is that divinity is able to fully understand it.

5. And in that *his garment is said to be dipped in blood*, it is a symbol of his Passion <note>The suffering and death of Jesus</note>. So we may know that it is the *Messiah* <note>original: "Messias"</note> who is meant here, of whom *St. John* in his Gospel said, "The Word was made flesh" <note>original: "ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο"</note>. And here he is called "The Word of God" <note>original: "ὁ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ"</note>, and yet appears in a *bloody garment*, which indicates his humanity or *terrestrial* body (for this body is but a garment of the soul, not part of the man himself, according to the *Platonists* <note>Followers of Plato who viewed the soul as distinct from the physical body</note>), which made him capable of suffering death.

# Chapter 14: With a sharp sword going out of his mouth.

Upon white *horses* belongs, as appears in the fourteenth verse. They also have *flaming and fiery eyes* because of their intellectual graces <note>original: "Intellectual Graces"; refers to spiritual or mental gifts and enlightenment</note>, and it is said that *the spiritual man discerns all things* (1 Corinthians 2). They also have *a name that no man knows besides themselves*, which represents their *new birth*, or their participation in the *Divine Nature*. Their garments are also *dyed in blood*, signifying that so many have suffered *martyrdom* for the testimony of the Gospel against the idolatry and tyranny of *Antichrist*. Furthermore, all have been "martyred"—that is, slain and mortified <note>original: "mortifi'd"; the spiritual practice of "putting to death" sinful desires</note> as to the life of sin—and also besprinkled with the blood of the Lamb through the pardon of whatever transgressions are past. And, lastly, they are to be crowned and reign as kings upon earth, for *the Kingdom is given to the Saints of the most High* (Daniel 7).

<margin>Hebrews 4</margin>
6. But to return to the description of this heavenly *hero*: *a sharp-edged sword is said to go out of his mouth*. This is analogous to the passage in *Hebrews*: *The word of God is living and powerful, sharper than any two-edged sword*. And where he is said to *rule the nations with a rod of iron*, it is an allusion to the second Psalm, which is a *prophecy of the Messiah*: *You shall rule them with a rod of iron, and break them in pieces like a potter's vessel*. This is a prophetic symbol of that wonderful contrition of heart which the powerful Word of God creates when it is sincerely and opportunely brandished <term>original: "evibrated"; to brandish, vibrate, or thrust a weapon</term> against the enemies of his Kingdom. As it says in the Epistle to the *Hebrews*, it *divides asunder and cuts between soul and spirit, and hews down into the very joints and marrow*. Such is the *warfare* <note>original: "Militia"</note> of this *heavenly host*. *He shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips will he slay the wicked* (Isaiah 11:4).

7. And where he is said to *tread the wine-press of the fierceness of the wrath of Almighty God*, it appears to refer to *Isaiah* 63: *Who is this that comes from Edom, with his dyed garments from Bozrah, this who is glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength? I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save*. This matches the current vision: *Whose name is Faithful and True, and in righteousness does he judge and make war*. But *Isaiah* continues: *Why are you red in your apparel, and your garments like him who treads in the wine vat? I have trodden the wine-press alone, and of the people there was none with me. For I will tread them in my anger, and trample them in my fury, and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment. For the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the day of my redeemed is come*. This corresponds to what is said of the *Rider of the white horse* in this vision—that he was *clothed in a vesture dipped in blood*. In both of these prophecies, this refers both to the Passion of Christ and his spiritual victories over his enemies. The *wine-presses* also correspond to one another in each vision.

Since the *harvest* is, as our Savior says, *the end of the world*, the *vintage* (which occurs somewhat later than the harvest) must be a later part of the end of the world. So this vision of *Edom* and *Bozrah* fits very well in that respect with this part of the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. It is further significant that *Bozrah* signifies "vintage" <note>original: "Bozrah signifies Vintage"; a translation from Hebrew</note> and *Edom* signifies the carnal, persecuting church—the real enemies of the true *Jerusalem*, just as the *Edomites* were to *Israel*. And I need not add that *Edom* and *Ishmael* are types of one and the...

8. Lastly, because it is *written upon his thigh*, KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS, it shows the royal descent of Christ even according to the flesh. It is as if he had laid claim to this sovereignty by descent from King *David*, just as it is said in *Chapter 22: I am the root and offspring of David, and the bright morning star.* He is the *root of David* regarding his divinity, and the *offspring of David* regarding his humanity. But the meaning of this part of the vision is that the Word of God—that is to say, the Law of Christ, both inward and outward—is at last in a visible triumph, though it had been kept down and plainly trodden into the dirt for so long during the reign of the *Two-horned Beast* or the *Whore* <note>The "Two-horned Beast" and the "Whore" are symbols from Revelation often interpreted by Protestant writers of this era as the Papacy or corrupt church structures</note>.

9. It is also easy to see that the Church of Christ, which is his body, shares in this part of the vision. Because this title of *King of Kings and Lord of Lords* is written upon his thigh, it also signifies the dominion of his posterity, the Church, as *Ribera* and *Alcazar* <note>Francisco Ribera and Luis de Alcázar were famous Jesuit commentators on the Apocalypse</note> have rightly noted, and as it is said elsewhere in the *Apocalypse*: *He has made us Kings and Priests, etc.* And as for the treading of the *wine-press of the wrath of God*, or the subduing of *Edom* <note>original: "Edom"; a traditional biblical enemy of Israel, used here to symbolize the worldly or ungodly</note>, does Christ not do it by the powerful and convicting zeal of his saints and the faithful ministers of his Word? By seriously and weightily applying the Law and the heavy wrath of God against sinners to the hearts and consciences of these worldly-natured *Edomites*, they squeeze out, if I may so speak, their corrupt blood—that is, the principle of that ungodly life in them (for "the life is in the blood"). Thus, by making them dead to sin, they later revive them into righteousness for everlasting salvation.

And so it is for that *sharp-edged sword* which is said here to *come out of the mouth of Christ*; it is in effect the very same sword that comes out of the mouths of his saints, who rule the world by convincing people of their wickedness and causing them to return to God. He inspires them by his Spirit, and they are only his <term>ministers</term> <note>original: ὑπηρέται (hyperetai); meaning assistants, servants, or subordinates</note> who transmit *this fiery Law, this blast of fire and flaming breath*, as it is called in the book of *Esdras* <note>2 Esdras 13:10-11 describes a figure destroying his enemies with a "blast of fire" from his mouth</note>, by which the wicked are consumed. They are, I say, but as a captured gate or passage through which this sharp-edged sword, with which the nations are struck, is so powerfully brandished by our victorious Savior. For this *flame* and this *sword* I take to be clear truth and sound, searching reason inspired by the *Eternal Word*. When sharpened with a holy, sincere, and natural kind of enthusiastic zeal, and backed by an irreproachable life and behavior <note>original: "conversation"; in this period, it referred to one's entire conduct or way of living</note>, it will be like a sharp-edged sword with the weight of running mercury <note>original: "Quick-silver"; mercury was sometimes added to the spine of a sword to increase the momentum and force of a strike</note> in the back of it. Its stroke will fall with such force that it will even split the enemy through the backbone at one blow; it will *divide soul and spirit, and pierce through the joints and marrow*, as the Apostle speaks.

<margin>2.</margin> 2. And the first were those that opposed the *Divine Life* in general. This is known to be a gross corruption in the Church of *Rome*, and is in my mind most vividly and graphically prefigured and depicted in that *Lamentation upon the Ruin of Babylon*, Revelation 18, beginning at the ninth verse.

I will briefly try to explain this further as I recount the prophecy.

9. *And the kings of the earth, who have committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her, shall bewail her and lament for her when they see the smoke of her burning,*

10. *Standing far off for fear of her torment, saying, "Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! For in one hour your judgment has come."*

I have clearly proved in my *Joint-Exposition* that this city *Babylon* is not a *city* of brick and stone, but a *form of government* <note>original: "Polity"</note>, and specifically the *Roman Hierarchy*. Truly, it seems improbable to me that the Spirit of God would lead the Apostle to compose such a long and detailed *lamentation* <note>original: "Threnodia"</note> upon her ruin and desolation if it meant nothing more than the literal burning of the *city of Rome*—especially if it were done as insignificantly and with as little purpose or effect as when *Totilas* attacked it. <note>Totilas was a King of the Ostrogoths who sacked Rome in 546 AD but did not permanently destroy the city's power.</note> Therefore, let us continue to briefly explain the text according to the meaning we have already established, which we do not doubt is the true one.

In these first two verses, we see the *lamentation of the kings of the earth*. These are the ones who "committed sexual immorality" with her—meaning they shared in her *idolatrous* religious profession. However, seeing how events unfolded, they did not dare to help her out of fear, but instead let her burn to the end. This again shows that the fall of *Babylon* does not happen all at once, but by degrees, as I have already noted. For though her judgment arrives in *one hour*, the actual execution of that judgment may take a considerable amount of time.

Verse 11. *And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her, for no man buys her merchandise anymore:*

12. *The merchandise of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, scarlet, all citron wood* <note>original: "Thyine wood"; a fragrant, costly wood used in ancient luxury furniture</note>, *all kinds of ivory vessels, all kinds of vessels made of most precious wood, brass, iron, and marble,*

13. *And cinnamon, perfumes, ointments, frankincense, wine, oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and the souls of men.*

The first group of mourners seems to be those of the *secular power*. But by these *merchants of the earth* <note>original Greek: "ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς" (emporoi tēs gēs)</note>, we should understand *church officials* <note>original: "Ecclesiastick persons"</note> who trade within the Church, where everything is expected to be exchanged or settled for money or earthly gain. Therefore, they are reproachfully called the *merchants of the earth*, even though their titles and professions supposedly point only to Christ, God, and Heaven—with "Divine," "Holy," "Sacred," or "Religious" serving as the external labels for them all.

The variety of commodities they deal in is so numerous that it would be too much *needless effort* <note>original Greek: "περιεργία" (periergia)</note> to look for a hidden mystery in every single one. It is likely nothing more than a *focus on material things* <note>original: "Hylasmus"</note>, dwelling on physical objects in a repetitive way to decorate the outward *shell* <note>original: "Cortex"</note> of the prophecy. But the general reason for the *lamentation of these merchants* is *that no one buys their cargo anymore* <note>original Greek: "ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι" (hoti ton gomon autōn oudeis agorazei ouketi)</note>. The *marketplace* <note>original: "Fair"</note> has been violently shut down or is entirely deserted, so that there is no more buying and selling of such goods in *Babylon* as there used to be, since *Babylon* herself

There is no more *citrus wood* <note>original: "Thyine wood," a fragrant, costly wood used in antiquity</note> for the roofs of their temples or for carved idols to whom sacrifice is offered; (for I suspect some such allusion in the Greek phrase *all citrus wood* <note>original: πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον</note>). And *Achmetes* says in Chapter 12: *If the idol is made of gold, iron, or lead, he who sees it shall be falsely rich; for all these are the vessels of the world.* <note>original Greek: Ἐὰν δὲ ὃ εἴδωλον χρυσοῦν ἢ σιδηροῦν ἢ μολιβδοῦν ᾖ, ὁ τοῦτο ἰδὼν ψευδόπλουτος ἔσται· ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα σκεύη τοῦ κόσμου εἰσίν.</note>

But to proceed: there will be no more trafficking in *aromatic odors, oils, or ointments* for sacred anointings. No man will participate any longer in her *blessed bread* <note>original: Panis benedictus</note>, nor taste her idolized wafer made of the *finest flour*, nor sip the *wine* of her chalice, even if they were to offer it to the common people <note>original: "Laiety"</note>. The tithe calf and lamb, along with its consecrated wool, shall fail; nor shall there be any more redemption of souls out of Purgatory by masses hired for money. The trade in *horses, chariots, and slaves* shall also cease on that day.

The Greek text says, *of horses and of chariots and of bodies* <note>original: ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων</note>. These three words are in the genitive case alone among all the rest, and are not grammatically linked to other words <note>original: <term>in regimine</term></note>. This suggests they must go together to make up one thing. I believe this refers to the *equipage* <note>the formal arrangement of a carriage, horses, and attendants</note> of the high-ranking officials in this mystical *Babylon*. This provides a key to understanding the rest of these commodities—that they should be interpreted in the same way I have explained them. I would interpret these not literally as *horses, chariots, and slaves*, but as *horses, coaches, and lackeys* running beside them in livery <note>original: <term>in querpo</term>, meaning dressed in a tight-fitting vest or uniform without a cloak</note>. It would be strange for these to be put up for sale jointly if it were meant literally. Therefore, the meaning is that the trade in such high church offices—where the status includes a coach, horses, and lackeys—will also fail along with the rest during the ruin and desolation of *Babylon*.

> Ver. 14. *And the fruits that your soul lusted after have departed from you, and all things that were dainty and goodly have departed from you, and you shall find them no more at all.*

That is to say: those great and rich <note>original: "opime"</note> promotions and positions which your ambitious and worldly mind so longingly craves. For these are the *fruit of desire* <note>original: ὀπώρα τῆς ἐπιθυμίας; the Latin Vulgate calls them *Poma desiderii*</note>, the *bright and the fat things* <note>original: τὰ λαμπρὰ καὶ τὰ λιπαρὰ</note>—those rich and attractive objects that make their mouths water in this crowded *Babylonish* market, where everything can be bought for money, and nothing can be had without it.

> 15. *The merchants of these things, who were made rich by her, shall stand far off for fear of her torment, weeping and wailing,*

> 16. *And saying, "Alas, alas, that great city that was clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls!"*

The meaning is this: both the buyers and sellers of high religious offices <note>original: "Spiritual Preferments"</note>, who had prospered from this trade, will be very sorry to see the ruin of the political system that supported them. They will be unable to help it and will praise the great pomp and splendor of the "Prostitute" <note>A common Reformation-era term for the Roman Catholic Church</note> while they lament their own personal losses. It is notable that this sixteenth verse is essentially the same as the fourth verse of the previous chapter, where the clothing of the **Prostitute** is described. This is understood to refer to the **Pope**, the **Cardinals**, and other high-ranking officials of that idolatrous Church.

> *Verse 17. And every shipmaster, and all the passengers in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood at a distance,*

If we consider what "sea" signifies in the prophetic style <note>original Latin: "stylo prophetico"</note>—the multitudes of people on Earth—then analogy will easily lead us to understand what may be hinted at by "ships." These would be consecrated houses separated from the rest, just as ships are usually separate in the sea. It seems, therefore, to provide a glimpse into the "Babylonian" churches that were misused for profitable idolatry and superstition. In these places, they sell the use, the sight, or the possession of various sacred objects, exchange the release of souls from Purgatory for money, and "peddle the word of God" <note>original Greek: <term>καπηλεύειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ</term></note>, turning the very Word of God into a corrupted piece of merchandise.

It might perhaps seem a bit too imaginative to suggest that these "merchant ships" <note>original Greek: <term>πλοῖα ἐμπορικὰ</term>; original Latin: *Naves Mercatoriæ*</note> have any connection to the well-known architectural term for the central part of a church, the **Nave** <note>The "nave" of a church comes from the Latin word *navis*, meaning ship</note>. Nor is it improbable (to anticipate the objections of those who rightly have a great respect and reverence for places consecrated to Divine worship) that **Christ**, who complained that the **Jews** had made the **Temple** in **Jerusalem** a "den of thieves," should in this vision—being equally provoked—rebuke them just as severely. He suggests these men of **Babylon** have turned his **churches**, which exist for better purposes, into so many **ships of deceitful and cunning merchants**. See the *Prophetic Alphabet*.

# Chapter XV. The Lamentation over Babylon.

...lamentation for you, and lament over you, saying, *“What city is like Tyre, like the one destroyed in the midst of the sea?”* This is very similar to the passage concerning *Babylon*: *“Alas, alas, that great city,”* etc. *“What city is like this great city?”* There are so many similar passages in both this vision of *Ezekiel* and in *Isaiah* chapter 23 that I must confess I suspect these are also prophecies of the same event. This is especially likely considering that the spiritual prostitution <note>original: "Whoredome"</note> of *Tyre* is so heavily criticized in those prophecies, just as it is here to *Babylon*.

*“For in one hour she is made desolate”*; that is to say, she is being made desolate suddenly and unexpectedly. She may be burning for a long time and not be set on fire in all places at once, as I have mentioned above. But the reason these *seamen* should raise such a pitiful cry and lamentation is plain: their trade and livelihood are gone. *“For they were made rich by reason of her costliness”*; so the English translation says, and appropriately enough in the literal sense. But the phrase "from her wealth" <note>original Greek: ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος</note> could just as well signify that treasure of honors, dignities, promotions, and offices with which she was able to enrich these *merchants*.

> 20. *Rejoice over her, you heaven, and you holy apostles and prophets, for God has avenged you on her.*

That is to say: Rejoice, you heavenly-minded people, over these *merchants of the earth*. And you who are teachers of pure and apostolic doctrine, who declare the plain truth of things to the world, be glad that the Lord has avenged the blood of your predecessors upon her—the blood of the *Waldenses* and *Albigenses* <note>Medieval groups persecuted by the Church for their dissenting religious views</note>, and those who suffered during *Queen Mary’s* reign <note>Mary I of England, who famously executed many Protestants</note>, along with the rest of the holy martyrs of *Jesus*.

> *Verse* 21. *And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying, "Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all."*

The meaning is that eventually there will be an utter ruin and scattering of this idolatrous city or political system, specifically at the pouring out of the seventh vial <note>A reference to the final judgments in the Book of Revelation</note>. In the meantime, I cannot fail to note how unlikely it is that this great triumph and rejoicing—and that final, perfect destruction symbolized by a *mighty angel* plunging a *millstone* to the *bottom of the sea*—should signify nothing more than the sacking of *Rome* by *Totilas* <note>A king of the Ostrogoths who captured Rome in 546 AD but did not destroy it permanently</note>. Rome recovered shortly after that event. The idea of the spirits of the *apostles* and *prophets* looking down through the windows of *heaven* and celebrating that spectacle—which would have been very sad and tragic for many good *Christians*—is improbable.

> 22. *And the voice of harpers and musicians, and of pipers and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in you; and no craftsman, of whatever craft he be, shall be found any more in you; and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in you.*
> 23. *And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in you, and the voice of the bridegroom and the bride shall be heard no more at all in you. For your merchants were the great men of the earth; for by your sorceries were all nations deceived.*
> 24. *And in her was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.*

The twenty-second verse and part of the twenty-third describe the grim silence and desolation of this city; the remainder explains the reason for her destruction.

# The Lamentation over Babylon. Book II.

And the *voice of Harpers and Musicians, etc.* All this first part may be nothing more than a prophetic **Hylasmus** <term>original: "Hylasmus"; a rhetorical device where a single concept is described by listing many specific, vivid details</term>, illustrating one single thing: the destruction, silence, and vast solitude of this idolatrous hierarchy. This is shown by the removal or absence of such obvious and tangible things that occur in an inhabited city, such as the noise of musicians, the hammering and knocking of craftsmen, the grinding of mills, the light of candles in the night, and the singing and dancing at weddings, and the like. 

Or else, there may be a more specifically designed allegory regarding this mystical city meant here. For instance, we might understand the "music" to refer to the music used in their idolatrous worship; these specific mentions would then be a **Diorismus** <term>original: "Diorismus"; a rhetorical term for a vivid or distinct definition</term>. By these **craftsmen** <note>original Greek: τεχνίται (technitai)</note>, we might understand those who "weave sophisticated and political schemes" <note>original Latin: "technas confuere sophisticas & politicas"</note> in theology and church administration for the interest of their hierarchy. These are the "architects of a kingdom within a kingdom" <note>original Latin: "Artifices Imperii in Imperio"</note>, and also those who produce intricate work in **Scholastic Divinity** <note>A formal system of theology taught in medieval European universities</note>. By the *sound of the millstones*, we can understand their fraudulent profit, for "the mill is interpreted to mean life and wealth" <note>original Greek: ὁ μύλος εἰς ζωὴν καὶ πλοῦτον κρίνεται</note>, as you may see in the writings of **Achmetes** <note>Achmet son of Seirim, a 9th-century author whose work on dream interpretation was well-known in the early modern period</note>. By the *light of a candle*, we understand honor and prosperity, as you may read in the same author. And, lastly, by the *Bridegroom* and the *Bride*, we should understand not the spiritual marriages between Christ and a nun, or the Virgin Mary and a monk in the monasteries, but the propagation of this false Catholic religion—meaning it shall no longer spread, for the purpose of marriage is propagation.

*For your merchants were the great men, etc.* Now follows the reason for this great desolation, which is threefold. 

The first reason is the extravagance and lordly behavior of these "mystical merchants." They were "the great men of the earth" <note>original Greek: μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς (megistanes tēs gēs)</note>; that is to say, men of the world who were highly worldly, ambitious, greedy, and sensual—which is the very essence of an earthly mind. History and the talk of all men are full of examples of how much this has been found among the Popes, Cardinals, Abbots, and other **leaders** <note>original: "μεγιστᾶνες, Primates or Maximates"; terms for high-ranking officials</note> of the Roman Church.

The second reason is the corruption of the world with idolatry. This was accompanied and supported by the claim of a plainly magical power to change the elements in a way that all the magicians of Pharaoh could never do, nor even dared to attempt, it being so far beyond all belief <note>This is a critique of the doctrine of Transubstantiation, where bread and wine are believed to become the body and blood of Christ</note>. Besides this, there are other magical feats of a lower rank, and **necromantic** <note>Communicating with the dead</note> stories of the apparitions of dead saints. This is why idolatry is indicated here by the word **sorcery** <note>original Greek: φαρμακεία (pharmakeia)</note>. Likewise, that *cup in the hand of the Whore* is looked upon as a **love potion** <note>original: "Philtrum"</note>. Their being said to be "deceived" by these sorceries implies that they were seduced into idolatry, as appears plainly from what is written about the miracles of the *Two-horned Beast* in Revelation chapter 13, verses 13 and 14.

The third and last reason is the bloody cruelty of this *Roman Hierarchy*. *In her was found the blood of Prophets and of Saints, etc.*—namely, the blood of those who, out of conscience toward the law of God and Christ, could not submit to their idolatrous profession and practice, but instead bore witness against them. And not only is their blood laid to her charge, but also the general bloodshed throughout Christendom caused by wars and riots. To better establish themselves in various countries and kingdoms, the hierarchy drags the world into these conflicts, supporting and encouraging them once they have been started by secular powers. If they were the true successors of the Apostles, as they boast, they would make it their business to ensure that Christians did not spill one another's blood, and that conscientious men did not lose their liberties or lives for being faithful professors of...

# The Visions of the King of Tyre. Book II.

God says, *“Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, ‘I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas’; yet you are a man, and not God, though you set your heart as the heart of God.”*

Is this not clearly he who sits between the seas in Italy and exalts himself above everything that is called God? But this belongs more properly to that aspect of *Antichristianism* that is the opposite of the divine grace of *humility*.

3. *Behold, you are wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from you.*

This is only a <term>diorismus</term> <note>original: "Diorismus"; a rhetorical term for a definition or distinction, here used to mock the Pope's claim to unique insight</note>, but it describes the pretended *infallibility* and unerring inspiration of that great false prophet in *Rome*. It may also hint at their exquisite cunning, sagacity, and general intelligence used for the management of their affairs. Some interpret the text as referring to *political wisdom*, in which *Daniel* was also exceptional <note>original: "eximious"</note>. Indeed, the very pretense of infallibility in divine matters is, for this false prophet, only a *political trick*. Their entire political framework is directed toward gaining power and riches. 

In pursuit of this, they do not hesitate to alter, nullify, or abolish the laws, institutions, and decrees of God himself. Some would imagine this is alluded to in the name *Daniel*, which means *the judgment of God*, as if they could create laws and decrees more wisely than He can. In reality, these are nothing but political schemes for obtaining wealth, as I mentioned, and as is clearly suggested in the following verse:

4. *With your wisdom and with your understanding you have gained riches, and have gathered gold and silver into your treasures.*

This is a further hint at the mystical meaning of this prophecy.

This vision applies so naturally to the same entity represented by the *Whore of Babylon*—and fits the historical *King of Tyre* so poorly in some passages—that we can be quite certain the prophecy's main purpose is to target the *Bishop of Rome* rather than the ancient *Tyrian Prince*. We can be further assured of this by another similar prophecy in *Isaiah*. There, the scholar *Forerius* <note>original: "Forerius"—Francisco Forerio (1523–1581), a Portuguese Dominican theologian</note> believes that not only is Pagan Rome being discussed (as *Alcazar* <note>original: "Alcazar"—Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Jesuit theologian known for interpreting Revelation as past history</note> argues), but he says explicitly that the Apostle *John* seems to mean "the City of the Antichristians" <note>original: "Civitatem Antichristianorum"</note> by this *City* of *Tyre* in *Revelation* 18, though he does not name the city directly in verse 19: *Alas, alas, that great city, where all who had ships at sea were made rich!* Combining the views of *Forerius* and *Alcazar*, I believe that by *Tyre* we should understand *Rome* after it became Antichristian; its religious hierarchy is being pointed out here just as it is in the vision of *Babylon*. For St. *John*, as I have suggested before, has clearly directed us toward this meaning by transplanting the exact same phrases into his vision of *Babylon*. This is clear from the eighth verse of this chapter, in addition to what we have already noted: *Who has planned this against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the honored of the earth?* (Isaiah 23:8). I will not dwell on how perfectly the phrase *Crowning City* fits that government which, "in relation to spiritual matters" <note>original: "in ordine ad spiritualia"—a legal phrase used by the Papacy to justify its authority over secular rulers</note>, claims the right to take off and put on the crowns of kings and emperors, which they have done with the greatest possible arrogance. I only note that the rest of the verse exactly matches *Revelation* 18:23: *Your merchants were the great men of the earth*; just as here it says, *Princes and the honored of the earth*. It is easy for anyone to see how well these terms describe the grandeur of the Pope, the Cardinals, and other high-ranking figures of that Church. But there is something more encouraging that follows, which is a good omen. Verse

15. 
> *In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, according to the span of one king's life; after the end of seventy years, Tyre will sing like a prostitute.*

There is both good news and bad news in this verse. By *Tyre*, as already suggested, is meant *Idolatrous Rome*, which must be "forgotten" for seventy years according to the "days of One King." I argue that this refers to one of the eight kings in the *Revelation*, Chapter 17. Through the mystical <note>original: "Cabbalistical"</note> meaning of the number 70, it is easily discovered who this "king" is: specifically, the *Seventh King*, which is the succession of the Christian Emperors (the Caesars), as I have noted elsewhere. The length of their reign is not meant literally here; rather, the number describes their character by multiplying 10 by 7. The mystical meaning is that during the entire reign of those *Caesars* (since *Ten* is a symbol of completeness), *Tyre* should be forgotten. This means the Roman government would not be openly *Idolatrous*. But after this period ends, then *Tyre* shall again "sing as a prostitute," as follows in Verse

16. 
> *Take a harp, walk through the city, you forgotten prostitute; play the strings well, sing many songs, so that you may be remembered.*

# Chapter 16: The Vision of the City of Tyre

That is to say, that the **Roman** hierarchy—after the era when pagan idolatry was abolished—shall, through deceptive pretenses and captivating speeches, adapt their messages and exhortations to harmonize with the corrupt inclinations of the people. Through these persuasive arguments and other superficial <note>original: "meretricious"—alluring but false or flashy</note> ceremonies and invitations that strike the senses, they shall bring idolatrous worship back into the Empire. As far as I can see, it is the will of God that this should be so, as it follows in verse 17:

<margin>Isaiah 23:17</margin> 17. *And it shall come to pass after the end of seventy years, that the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall turn to her hire, and shall commit fornication with all the kings of the earth.*

*And it shall come to pass:* The more specific sense is, *For it shall come to pass*, otherwise it looks like a redundancy <note>original: "Tautologie"</note>. Her fall into idolatry is described here much like that of the **Whore** of **Babylon**, with whom the kings of the earth are said to commit fornication. And where it is said, *For the Lord will visit Tyre*, that corresponds to Revelation 17:17: *For God has put it in their hearts to fulfill his will*. This apostasy <note>term: "apostasy"—the abandonment of one's religious faith or principles</note> also begins here after **seventy years**, just as it does in the **Apocalypse** <note>original: "Apocalyps"—the Book of Revelation</note> after the **Seventh King**. But what follows next is most welcome:

Verse 18. *And her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Lord: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise shall be for those who dwell before the Lord, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.*

Here the scene changes again, and for the better. Interpreters generally agree that this refers to a conversion to **Christ**. However, **St. Jerome** and some Hebrew writers understand it as the conversion of the city of **Tyre** itself; the scholar **Alcazar** <note>original: "Alcazar"—Luis del Alcázar (1554–1613), a Jesuit theologian</note> believes it refers to **Pagan Rome**. But I conceive this conversion to be that of **Pagano-Christian Rome** to ancient, pure, and apostolic Christianity; the logic of the situation in both this vision of **Isaiah** <note>original: "Esay"</note> and those of **Ezekiel** seems to sufficiently confirm this for us.

<margin>Book 7. Chapter 7. Sections 2, 3, 4.</margin> It should be expected—since it is so clear that the **Jewish** people were a great "type" <note>term: "type"—a person, event, or institution in the Old Testament believed to foreshadow something in the New Testament</note> of the future Church of Christ—that the nations who were enemies of the Jews would also represent the enemies of the true Church. This concept is repeated over and over again in the Book of Revelation, which is full of the figure I have ventured to call *Israelismus* <note>term: "Israelismus"—a term coined by the author to describe the use of Jewish history, names, and geography as a symbolic language for Christian prophecy</note>. I say, it cannot but be expected that the prophets, when predicting things about these nations in a literal sense, would—through their inspired spirit—use expressions more suitable for the future entities they symbolize than for the ancient nations themselves. This is how several prophecies concerning Christ are framed and noted accordingly by scholars; they are either purely allegorical or a mix of literal and symbolic, as I have discussed in my work, *The Mystery of Godliness* <note>original: "Mystery of Godliness"—a major work by the author, Henry More, published in 1660</note>.

6. And truly, I think these two visions of **Tyre** are such perfect predictions of the Antichrist and his fall that they deserve to be categorized as this second kind of prophecy, because they contain details that do not fit their original literal fulfillment. Among these is **Tyre** being called a **Whore**, and her being said to commit fornication with all the kings of the earth. This makes no sense when understood literally regarding the city of **Tyre**, but it is easily and naturally understood regarding **Antichristian Rome**. Regarding what the scholar **a Lapide** <note>original: "a Lapide"—Cornelius a Lapide (1567–1637), a Flemish Jesuit and influential biblical commentator</note> says about the word *harlot* <note>original: "זונה" (Hebrew: zonah)—a harlot or prostitute</note> that...

<margin>Isaiah 23:17</margin>
The argument that the word signifies *Innkeeper* <note>original: "Caupona"</note> as well as *Harlot* <note>original: "Meretrix"</note> is but a poor excuse. It is as if the Prophet, for the sake of a verbal joke, would so severely reproach a city for its useful trades and business negotiations. Besides, though the Hebrew word *Zanah* <note>original: זנה</note> can signify an *Innkeeper* as well as a *Harlot*, the specific form *Vezantah* <note>original: וזנתה</note> only signifies *to commit harlotry* <note>original: "scortari"</note>. Therefore, the phrase *with all the kingdoms of the earth* <note>original: את-כל-ממלכות הארץ</note> must determine the meaning of the rest.

Also, the seventy years of silence and being forgotten is so inapplicable to the literal city of **Tyre** that **Grotius** <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645), a famous Dutch jurist and theologian known for literal interpretations of prophecy</note> (though I cannot approve of his boldness) is forced to change the seventy years into *seven*, as if the Text were corrupt. This is an odd way of interpreting Scripture—somewhat like curing a headache by decapitation <note>original: "decollation"—beheading</note>. And even when he has reduced these years to seven, neither the life nor the reign of **Shalmaneser** <note>original: "Salmanassar"—a King of Assyria</note> was seven years, nor was he King of that city; yet, according to common sense, that seems necessary to be understood.

Again, the fact that the *Prince of Tyre* is threatened with the "death of the uncircumcised" implies that he is a pretended member of the Church of God. This is especially true given that he is called the *anointed Cherub*, is described with the ornaments of the **High Priest**, is threatened with being cast out of the Mountain of God as profane, and is finally reproved for defiling the Sanctuaries. All these are more than mere hints that the *King of Tyre* is a "type" <note>term: "type"—a person or thing in the Old Testament believed to foreshadow something in the New Testament or the future church</note> of some great person who is a **Priest** in the Church of God. This vision chiefly belongs to him and will hardly make sense in several parts if it is not understood as referring to him.

7. But I will not dwell any longer on this subject. Let me only give a brief account of the meaning of this last verse: *And her merchandise*, that is to say, *Then*, or *After this, her merchandise* (for the Hebrew prefix "and" has such a broad meaning, as we noted regarding **Daniel 11:36**), *her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Lord*. The meaning is this: those revenues and honors which **simony** <note>term: "simony"—the buying or selling of ecclesiastical privileges, such as pardons or benefices</note> and other dishonest and unjust administrations of Church affairs had made into mere merchandise—as well as that wealth which had been the *hire of a harlot* (meaning what had come to the **Church of Rome** through her idolatrous and seductive deceits)—shall be taken and put to good use. It shall be laid out in the true and substantial service of God and be dedicated to Him; that is, it will be appropriated for His real service. 

*It shall not be treasured nor laid up*; that is, it shall not be scraped together into the hands of a few men to build a fortune for them and their families. They shall not seize it and possess it as their own (for the Hebrew word *Chasan* <note>original: חסן</note> seems to suggest this) to satisfy their own luxury or greed. *For her merchandise shall be for those who dwell before the Lord*; that is, it shall be for the "Household of Faith"—those who live as if always in the sight and eye of God and have a reverent sense of His presence in all their conduct. It is for those who hold the Christian faith, not the Antichristian faction, whether they are laity or clergy. *To eat sufficiently*: this means that men may have enough food, that good hospitality may be maintained, and that the poor and hungry may be satisfied.

8. *And for durable clothing* <note>original: למכסה עתיק; "limkhasseh atiq"</note>. This may signify either *durable clothing* or *comely, grave clothing*, such as is suitable for elderly men. *So that they may be clothed in honorable and decent garments, such as become old men and Priests*; this is **Cornelius a Lapide's** <note>A 17th-century Jesuit Bible commentator</note> own explanation of **Vatablus's** <note>François Vatable, a 16th-century French humanist and scholar</note> interpretation: *For a covering*—

### CHAPTER XVII.

1. Their "lying legends" rebuked <note>original: "perfringed"</note> in Saint Paul’s prophecy of the later times. 2. A more complete foreshadowing of that anti-Christian opposition against faith, found in part of his prophecy regarding the "Man of Sin." 3. A clear explanation of that part of the prophecy. 4. Brief observations in the visions of Revelation <note>original: "Apocalyptick Vifions"</note> for the same purpose. 5. The pride of the Bishop of Rome foreshadowed in the King of Tyre, as well as his downfall and how it happens. 6. His magnificent splendor described both in the King of Tyre and in the Whore of Babylon. 7. The pride and downfall of this Patriarch symbolized by the King of Babylon. 8. The meaning of the twelfth and thirteenth verses. 9. Verse 14: The meaning of the prophecy from the fourteenth to the nineteenth verse. 10. Verse 20: An explanation of the twentieth verse. 11. Further foreshadowing of Papal pride in the "Whore" and the "Little Horn." 12. A straightforward and natural explanation or paraphrase of the thirty-sixth and thirty-seventh verses of the eleventh chapter of Daniel, where the impious self-exaltation of the Bishop of Rome is clearly foretold. 13. That the meaning of the two following verses of this prediction may still be the same as that proposed by Mr. Mede <note>Joseph Mede (1586–1638), an influential scholar of biblical prophecy</note>.

1. We come now to the parts of the *spiritual life* <note>original: "Divine life"</note>: the *Root* and the *Branches*. We will not dwell long on the former, as the prophecies concerning it are not as extensive or frequent. However, prophecy is not entirely silent about those things that so grossly oppose or undermine our belief in the Christian religion. For example, regarding those "legendary stories" we have taken notice of: are they not plainly foretold in that prophecy concerning the abandonment of faith <note>original: "Apostasy"</note> in the latter times? It states that *doctrines of demons* <note>original: "Doctrines of Damons"</note> would be introduced "through the hypocrisy of liars" <note>original: "ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων"</note>. These people, through a hypocritical display of their professed abstinence from certain foods and marriage—as if they were saintly and angelic men themselves—use this disguise to gain a reputation for holiness with the people. Therefore, they more easily convince them to worship saints by inventing *lying legends* that contain their supposed miracles. People are very ready to believe these because of the reverence they hold for these masks <note>original: "vizards"</note> of holiness. What can be more plain than this?

<header>An Explanation of the latter part of Book II.</header>

2. Again, in 2 Thessalonians 2, there is a more complete foreshadowing <note>original: "Prefiguration"</note> of the state of the fallen <note>original: "lapsed"</note> Church on this point. Verses:

> 8. *And then shall that wicked one be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the glory of his coming;*
> 9. *Even him whose coming is according to the activity of Satan, with all power and signs and lying wonders,*
> 10. *And with all the deception of unrighteousness in those who perish; because they did not receive the love of the Truth, that they might be saved.*
> 11. *And for this cause God shall send them a strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:*
> 12. *That they all might be condemned who did not believe the Truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

3. The description seems to consist of those two parts that are briefly expressed in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note> as "he who makes" <note>original: "ὁ ποιῶν"</note> and "he who loves a lie" <note>original: "ὁ φιλῶν ψεῦδος"</note>. This wicked one—that is, the Pope with his Clergy—is the "lie-maker" <note>original: <term>ὁ ποιῶν ψεῦδος</term></note>, whose coming is according to the working of Satan, the Father of Lies; "with all power, signs, and lying wonders" <note>original: <term>ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους</term></note>. In this phrase, "lying" <note>original: <term>ψεύδους</term></note> applies to all of them together <note>original: <term>ἀπὸ κοινοῦ</term></note>, as if he were saying: *In all manner of false and counterfeit displays of power, signs, and miracles*. For he seems to add by way of further explanation, "in all unjust or harmful deception" <note>original: <term>ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἀδικίας</term></note>. This is the same accusation that seems to be made against <margin>Chapter 9:21.</margin> them in Revelation, "that they did not repent of their thefts" <note>original: <term>ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν</term></note>.

But now the "lover of lies" <note>original: <term>ὁ φιλῶν ψεῦδος</term></note> follows: namely, the description of those who *love* these *lies*. They are the ones who perish because they lack a sincere love of the Truth that would save them. For **hypocrisy** is usually at the bottom of those who can be tricked <note>original: "gulled"</note> by these imposters. Because they do not sincerely seek the Kingdom of God and his righteousness, they become prey for these deceitful men. As is further hinted in verse 12, where they are said *to take pleasure in unrighteousness*. For this reason, God sends them *strong delusion, so that they may believe lies*; that is, all the legendary impossibilities of <term>Transubstantiation</term> <note>the Catholic doctrine that the bread and wine of the Eucharist become the actual body and blood of Christ</note>, mythical miracles from legends, and frightening stories of <term>Purgatory</term>. Thus, one part of their Church becomes fools <note>original: "Sotts"</note> and fanatics <note>original: "Bigots"</note>; and the other part who witness this scene—though they claim to be members of that Church—become a company of profane **atheists** and secret <note>original: "clancular"</note> mockers of all religion. In this way, the Christian faith is miserably ruined <note>original: "goes to rack"</note> by these deceptions <note>original: "Impostures"</note>. Indeed, it is a question whether those who cling most superstitiously to them do so out of any firm belief, or rather out of a kind of confusion and numbing <note>original: "obstupefaction"</note> of the mind driven by fear and suspicion, rather than any real certainty in the things they outwardly profess.

This interpretation does not conflict at all with the claims of those who believe that extraordinary things do sometimes happen in that Church. For it is enough that they so heavily rely on and boast of their miracles, while so very few of those countless stories are true at all. Furthermore, none of them are genuine miracles, but are instead deceptive tricks of the Devil—that notorious "maker of lies" <note>original: <term>ψευδοποιός</term></note>, as **Theodoret** <note>a 5th-century Christian theologian and bishop</note> calls him.

# Chapter XVII: Of the Prophecy of the Man of Sin

4. To these you may add *Revelation* 13 <note>original: "Apocal. 13"</note>, where the **Two-horned Beast** (who is the same as the **False Prophet** and this **Man of Sin**) is said to perform great miracles *before the eyes of men* <note>original: "ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων"</note> and *in the sight of the beast* <note>original: "ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου"</note>. That is, as Aretas <note>A 10th-century commentator on Revelation</note> says, *stealing the eyes of the onlookers* <note>original: "κλέπτων τὰς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῶν ὁρώντων"</note> or *dazzling the eyes of men* <note>original: "Oculos hominum præstringens"</note>; and accordingly Bellarmine <note>Robert Bellarmine (1542–1621), a prominent Jesuit Cardinal</note> also interprets those words. This trickery <note>original: "juggle"</note>, however, concerns the eyes of the Mind as well as those of the Body. For **Transubstantiation** does not make the **Bread** look different to the outward eyes than usual, but it does to the eyes of Faith and Reason. Their claim to be able to make a consecrated wafer appear to be the very Body and Person of Christ is such a piece of deception <note>original: <term>prestigiousness</term>; in the 17th century, this meant sleight-of-hand or sorcery</note> that it has no parallel.

The obvious appearance of calculated human political strategy <note>original: "accurate humane Policy"</note>, if not worse, in the framework of their religion, is rebuked <note>original: "perstringed"</note> in the Vision of the **little Horn with eyes** <note>A reference to Daniel 7:8, symbolizing a power that is both small and shrewdly observant</note>. Their Atheism and Infidelity in general are addressed in those passages of the **Revelation**, Chapter 21:8: *But the fearful and unbelieving*, etc., and Chapter 22:15: *For outside are dogs*. In what sense these places apply to the present theme, I have already declared in my *Idea of Antichristianism*, and therefore I consider it unnecessary to repeat it here.

5. We come now to the oppositions to the **branches of the Divine life: Humility, Purity, and Charity**. The opposition against the first of these is clearly that unmatched loftiness and haughtiness which we have described in the previously mentioned *Idea*, and which history everywhere complains of in the **Bishop of Rome**. I believe this is very vividly portrayed in that vision of *Ezekiel* concerning the **King of Tyre**. For I think I have previously shown it to be very rational that **Tyre** is a symbolic type of **Antichristian Rome**.

<margin>Ezekiel Chapter 28:2.</margin>
The words which I had occasion to recite before were these: *Son of man, say unto the Prince of Tyre, Thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, "I am a God, I sit in the seat of God in the midst of the seas."* Is this not the very language that the Pope accepts, such as "**Our Lord God the Pope**" <note>original: "Dominus Deus noster Papa"</note>? And the claim that the Seat and Tribunal of the Pope is the very Seat and Tribunal of God? Again, verse 6: *Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you have set your heart as the heart of God, behold, I will bring strangers upon you, the most terrible of the nations, etc.* To **set his heart as the heart of God** is to have his will in all things. *Who has resisted his Will?* And do they not make the Will of the Pope a Law? He is treated as the **Supreme Deity on earth** <note>original: "Supremum Numen in terris"</note>, at whose command and nod all things are to be done, right or wrong; indeed, they cannot be wrong if he wills them. This is to make him have a heart like God indeed—not only an irresistible heart, but an infallible one. He has climbed this high in the confidence of his own subtlety and political skill.

*But the terrible of the nations shall draw their swords against the beauty of his wisdom, and they shall defile his brightness*, says the Prophet. What this means in the literal sense is easy to understand, and accordingly it applies to the **King of Tyre**; it may also, by extension <note>original: "ex accidenti"</note>, be applicable to the destruction of **Rome**. But it may also have a more mystical sense. In that case, the "terrible of the nations" <note>original: "עריצי גוים" (areetsay goyim), which the Latin renders as "robustos gentium"</note> may signify nothing other than the zealous and resolute defenders of the Truth, for nothing is more powerful and strong than Truth.
