# Chapter X. A Summary of All His Answers.

[Di]vine Nature, that *passive and contemptible Divinity* <note>original: "contemptible Divinity"; the author uses "contemptible" here in its older sense of "worthy of being despised by the world," rather than literally lacking value.</note> that lived within him. According to the sense the objection seems to imply, this would be nothing less than a charge of blasphemy. However, I have plainly demonstrated that in those passages where the objection is raised, I do the exact opposite. For since I was not speaking at all of the Divine Nature in the Scholastic sense <note>original: "Scholastick sense"; refers to the formal, technical definitions used by medieval academic theologians.</note>—which I therefore could not have termed *Passive*—I instead highly praise that *Divine Temper of Mind* that was in the Holy *Jesus*. I show that although it was *contemptible before men*, yet God, that righteous Judge, esteems it above all things.

And regarding the fourth objection, which would claim that I take away all authority in <term>things indifferent</term> <note>original: "things indifferent"; also known as *adiaphora*, these are church practices or rituals neither specifically commanded nor forbidden by Scripture.</note>, I show in great detail that I am an outspoken supporter of authority in such matters, even in that very Preface from which the objection is raised.

Furthermore, whereas in the third objection they would make me claim that Episcopacy <note>Church government led by bishops.</note> is a faction and against God’s word, I not only prove that I do not call it a "faction" in that cited passage of my Preface, but I also provide several passages in the same Preface that demonstrate the great esteem I have for Episcopacy.

In the second objection, it is hinted that I denied the Resurrection by denying that the same body shall rise again. I have made it exceedingly plain that I do not deny the "sameness" of the body—not even in the technical sense used by the Schools—but in the meantime, I positively state that our bodies at the Resurrection shall be as truly and really the same as the bodies we have here, just as this current body is the same as itself. The only difference is that they shall be *Celestial, Spiritual, and Glorious Bodies*. We shall feel ourselves to be just as much the same person, and we will seem just as much the same to others who look upon us. Indeed, unless I wanted to lose the clarity of my meaning regarding the truth of this identity of the body when speaking to any ordinary person, I could not express my view better than in those very words of *Job* which the Church uses in her Order for the Burial of the Dead:

> *I know that my Redeemer lives, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin, worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God, whom I shall see for myself, and my eyes shall behold, and not another.*

So far am I from introducing anything new or revolutionary into the Article of the Resurrection.

And as for the charge in the first objection—as if I made the Body of Christ after his Ascension merely "organized light" rather than flesh and bones, contrary to the Fourth Article of the Church—I show plainly that my meaning is not that Christ’s body is a thin light such as they might imagine, as if it were *organized sunshine*. Rather, it is a palpable body, radiant and clear, shining like the sun in its strength—nay, more bright than the sun, as the Scripture testifies. Therefore, I do not err in saying it is a *Lucid Body*. I add further that if the meaning of that Article is that this glorious, lucid body consists of flesh and bones (though I have shown reason to doubt that specific interpretation), I have no objection to it, provided that, according to the plain testimony of Scripture, we remember they are *Celestial and Spiritual Flesh and Bones*. For a *Spiritual Body* must consist of such things.

# The Duty of Church and People Concerning Opinions. Chapter X.

And now for 그 accusation of **Anthropomorphism** <note>original: "Anthropomorphitism"; the belief that God has a human form or body.</note>, which is the latter of the two objections reaching me through rumor and conversation: I have shown, regarding the very passage from which they would raise this accusation, that I have expressly asserted that **it is impossible that the Divine Nature should have any shape at all, as it is absolutely infinite.**

2. And lastly, regarding **Preexistence** <note>The doctrine that the human soul existed before the body was conceived.</note>, which some denounce me for as if I were dogmatically teaching it: I have plainly declared, and do declare again, that although I look upon the opinion as very rational, I give no assent to it any further than what is consistent with the truly Catholic and Apostolic Faith, and the doctrine of the **Church of England**. (Which I would have understood also regarding whatever other theories occur in any of my writings.) I do this all the more willingly because I think it is the duty of all men to do so who live in a Church so judiciously and faithfully purified <note>original: "repurgated"</note> and freed from all the frauds and **worthless deceptions** <note>original: "Trumperies"</note>, and from all the superstitions, idolatries, and tyrannies of **Antichristianism** <note>A term often used by Reformers to describe the perceived corruptions of the Roman Catholic Church.</note>.

Regarding other matters, I think everyone ought—out of a noble gratitude to the illustrious memory of the **First Reformers**, and out of a sense of that great happiness and comfortable protection we enjoy under those who succeed them (both in the profession of the same religion and in the right of power and jurisdiction)—not to thwart, contradict, or openly oppose what they declare true or fitting. This holds even if we might incline in our own judgments toward another persuasion. In this, we should follow that sober advice of one of the **Wise Men of Greece**, that **"we should not argue with our parents, even if we are speaking the truth."** How much less, then, will it become us to do so in things where we cannot even be certain whether we are in the right or not—unless we wish to be so insufferably puffed up in our own conceits as to believe ourselves infallible?

Therefore, is it not better for everyone to abandon any such false boasting <note>original: "gloriation"</note> rather than in the slightest manner disturb the peace of the Church, or break any order, just to please oneself with such a vain, needless, unjustifiable, and ill-timed satisfaction? Instead, we should make use of those clear and indisputable truths of Christianity which the Church preserves entirely for us, and spend our zeal in a sincere endeavor to conform our inner self and all our outward actions to such a holy and blameless rule.

3. Certainly, on the other hand, it would be the glory and interest of all the **Reformed Churches** to exercise their power and jurisdiction, and afford their primary support toward furthering the conformity of men's lives to those indisputable rules of righteousness. We are all agreed that these are the indispensable commands of God and of the Lord **Jesus**. As for such opinions as neither help nor hinder the known and acknowledged goals of the Gospel of Christ, the Church should set no value upon them one way or the other. They should not needlessly ensnare <note>original: "illaqueate"</note> any man’s mind by any definitions or decrees of their own, nor by adhering to the decisions of others in points that contribute nothing to the aforementioned goals. Instead, in these cases, they should act according to those measures I have ventured to suggest in my ***Mystery of Godliness***, Book 10, Chapter 3. Doing so would prevent the sowing of the seeds of endless squabbles in the Church,

...and disable malicious men from doing unearned harm to free and honest people by representing them as *heterodox* <note>original: "Heterodox"; holding opinions at odds with established religious dogma.</note>, even if it is only in such matters as the interests of the Church of *Christ* are not at all concerned with, whether those points are true or false.

Therefore, the duty of conforming with one's Church regarding doubtful and debatable opinions does not mean there is no duty on the Church's side not to multiply decisions that needlessly restrict people's liberties and create conflict. This is similar to the philosopher *Epictetus* <note>A Stoic philosopher (c. 50–135 AD) who taught that we should focus on what is within our control.</note> arguing that a son must do his duty to his father because he is his father (and he will not allow the excuse, "But he is a bad father" <note>original Greek: "Ἀλλὰ πατὴρ κακὸς"</note>). <header>His Expostulation with the Sectaries. Chap. 2.</header>

If they had half the true zeal and purity they boast of, their presence in the Church would so warm, strengthen, and support her that she would easily purge <note>original: "sweat out"; the author uses a medical metaphor of a body sweating out an infection.</note> all that corruption thought to have grown within her, and recover to perfect strength and health.

You who claim to be inspired in such a special way—as if your hearts were the only Temples of the Holy Spirit—is not the fruit of the *Spirit Love*, both according to your own boastful confessions and the actual truth? And is not *Love* the Mother of Peace and Union, the very bond of Perfection? Are not the works of the Flesh instead Wrath, Strife, Sedition, and Division? How carnal and cursed a thing, then, must *schism* <term>original: "schism"; a formal split or division within a religious body.</term> be? It is the worst of divisions and entirely contrary to the Spirit of God.

You who are so focused on prophecy and the end times, and who delight in the hope and expectation of a *Fifth Monarchy* <term>A 17th-century radical belief that the four worldly empires of Daniel's prophecy had passed and the fifth—the reign of Christ and his saints—was about to begin.</term> to come (which you imagine is clearly prefigured in the books of *Daniel* and the *Revelation* <note>original: "Apocalyps"</note>): what blurred vision <note>original: "πρεσβυτερία" (presbyteria); literally meaning "eldership" or "old age," used here as a pun on "presbyopia" to suggest the dim-sightedness of the elderly.</note> has ruined your eyesight? Why do you see more clearly far away than up close? You can discern a *Fifth Monarchy* coming in the Book of Revelation, and yet you cannot recognize it when it has already arrived. For the *Fifth Monarchy* surely began with the *Reformation*, in which neither the *Pope* nor anyone else is acknowledged as the *Universal Head* or *Monarch*, but the Lord *Jesus* alone. Why then are you so profoundly ignorant and barbarously rude as to refuse to show civil respect to all the rulers and magistrates who serve under him? You act as if the honor due to his deputies were the "worship of the Beast" <note>A reference to the idolatry described in the Book of Revelation; the author argues that respecting government is not the same as religious worship.</note>—or as if it were not lawful to pay civil respect and duty even to pagan magistrates, if it happened to be our lot to live under them.

And lastly, you who speak so constantly of *Antichrist* and *Antichristianism*—staining your vision and imagination so much that even things which are truly Apostolic and Christian seem *Antichristian* to you if they go against your own mood—why do you not consider this? Your excessive opposition to all good order and decent traditions in a Church that is not at all *Antichristian*, and your choice to separate yourselves from it based on these imaginary grounds, is actually siding with *Antichrist* and doing his work for him. This work is the weakening of Christ’s Kingdom by breaking it into sects and factions. As these factions grind against one another, they wear away the strength of the *Reformation* and turn the orderly state of the Church into a ruinous heap of rubbish and confusion. This is something not only wished for, but actively and vigilantly pursued by the dangerous agitators <note>original: "Incendiaries"</note> and agents of the Church of *Rome*. They are your partners in this, as you can see, working to fulfill the designs of that very *Antichrist* you so foolishly and clumsily claim to oppose. Through your wild tendency toward schism within the Church of *England*, you join forces with the *Man of Sin* <note>A biblical title for the Antichrist, frequently used by Protestants to refer to the Pope.</note>. You help his workers <note>original: "Pioneers"; historically, laborers who dig trenches or undermine walls during a siege.</note> to undermine and dig down the most significant shelter and the most unbreakable fortress in the entire Reformation against the flood of Roman idolatry and tyranny.

Therefore, in the fear of God and with a proper regard for your own safety and interests, wake up from this frantic dream! See the danger you are in—and the danger you naturally bring upon others—through these unnecessary, lawless, and un-Christian divisions. Consider that, as much as it lies within your power, you are laying the

### Chapter X. The Multifarious Sinfulness of Schism.

...groundwork and pathways for a victory for him whom you sincerely oppose—unless you are merely hypocrites. If he ever triumphs, he will build his monuments upon your ruin. If you are not hypocrites but his real opponents, he will celebrate his victory with bonfires <note>original: "Bone-fires"; the author uses the older sense of the word, implying a fire for burning bones.</note> that shall burn your bones and flesh to ashes. That is, he will burn you at the stake <note>original: "fire and faggot"; the traditional method of executing heretics using bundles of wood.</note> as heretics because you will not become idolaters and worship the golden image that this "King of Babylon" <note>A common Protestant rhetorical strategy identifying the Pope with the biblical King Nebuchadnezzar.</note> has set up. By this, I mean submitting to that elaborate idolatry which the Pope of Rome has appointed instead of the pure and rightful worship of the living God.

7. Therefore, wake yourselves up, rub your eyes, and look around you, all you members of various sects <term>original: "Sectaries"; people who belong to a sect or group that has separated from an established church.</term> within the Reformed world. Consider the danger into which you bring yourselves and the entire Reformation by splitting it into such small fragments and factions. But if you are so foolhardy that the peril of your bodies does not move you, consider further that betraying the Church to ruin and persecution is a sin of the deepest stain against your own souls. You are choosing to follow your own whims rather than the peace and security of the whole Reformation.

<margin>*Isaiah* 65:5</margin>
Furthermore, your persistence in these divisions <term>original: "Schisms"; formal splits or separations within a religious body.</term> is a constant practice of sin—and not just one type of sin. For besides the fact that schism itself is a sin, and one of the most hateful and horrid "works of the flesh," it is also accompanied by several most shameful and grievous sins. It brings with it pride and a wicked arrogance of spirit, like those people God complains about in the book of *Isaiah*. They say to the Prophets who have the authority to rebuke them: "Keep away! Stay where you are; don't come near me, for I am holier than you are!" But God declares of them: "These are like smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns all day long." Despite how highly they thought of themselves, they were as unpleasant to Him as smoke in a man’s eyes or nose. These are the people who, though they claim to be God’s people, take the liberty to break His laws. They sacrifice in *private gardens* instead of the public Temple; they seek inspirations and revelations in dark corners among the filthy *tombs* of the dead; and they think nothing of trampling on the respectable traditions of God’s Church if those traditions go against the force of their own moods or desires. Meanwhile, what a wonderful stupidity exists in these men, that they should imagine themselves holier than others while (as I said above) their consciences are so hardened and unfeeling that they have no sense of the guilt of one of the most dangerous and harmful sins: the sin of stirring up division and separating from the Church, thus needlessly crumbling it into dust and fragments.

Therefore, in the second place, this sin of schism has hypocrisy as its inseparable companion. While they pretend to be gathering together a "purer Church," what is more likely to be at the heart of it than a desire to show off their own holiness? They wish to display their own personal "gifts" separately, even though they are not authorized to use them in such a way. In reality, they are strictly required to practice the Christian virtues of humility, wisdom, and obedience to their superiors and to the command of Christ, who tells us to perform our devotions in secret, so that *He who sees in secret may reward us openly*. And I know of no place more...

# The Multifarious Sinfulness of Schism. Chap. X.

There is no place more secret than a private closet or a public church, where even the most remarkably devout and pious people appear no different from the rest; the unique perfection of their holy performances lies hidden and concealed within the mixed multitude. However, to separate into <term>conventicles</term> <note>original: "Conventicles"; secret or illegal religious meetings held by dissenters outside the established Church of England.</note> clearly looks like an attempt to show off one's own special sanctity. And it would be well if it were only that, but it is all too evident, thirdly, that many separations are made for a false liberty—to be fed with the "sweet sugar-sops" <note>original: "Sugar-sops"; bread soaked in sweetened liquid, used here metaphorically to describe pleasing but spiritually hollow or indulgent doctrines.</note> of <term>Libertinism and Antinomianism</term> <note>The belief that because of God's grace, Christians are not bound by moral or religious laws.</note>. I also suspect that greed is a fourth factor among most of their leaders. Furthermore, I fear that the hideous monster of total apostasy <note>Renouncing one's faith.</note> from the Christian faith follows some of these schisms—specifically those who turn the history of Christ into a "heartless mythology" <note>Treating the life of Jesus as a symbolic fable rather than historical fact.</note> and cancel all the roles of our ever-blessed Savior. Such schisms as these certainly serve the goals of *Antichrist* <note>In this context, a common Protestant term for the Pope or the Roman Catholic system.</note> and harden his followers against any suggestion of reform. Therefore, you can be sure that his cunning and wicked agents will unfailingly assist, spark, and manage this schism above all others. It makes the Reformation look so hateful, ridiculous, and dangerous—as if leaving the Church of Rome must eventually unravel into nothing but hypocritical paganism.

Lastly, these schisms must necessarily be accompanied by superstition, even in the best-case scenario—namely, that the separation is made out of a sincere conscience. For how ignorant and superstitious is that conscience which is so fearful of offending God, or so confident of gaining His favor, by rejecting or practicing things that the Divine Majesty is neither provoked nor appeased by? This, assuredly, is the very inner nature and essence of superstition. Thus, by pretending to separate themselves from superstition, they clearly become truly superstitious in their schism and separation from our Church, since it contains nothing that is either against Christ or against the teachings of the Apostles. 

But while they boast so much of "the Spirit," they actually do the "works of the flesh" <note>A reference to Galatians 5:19-21, where Paul contrasts the Fruit of the Spirit with the sinful works of the flesh, which include "dissensions and factions."</note>. Most certainly, all schism and separation from such a blameless church as the Church of *England* must be the result of a carnal <note>Worldly or fleshly, as opposed to spiritual.</note> mind, not a fruit of the Spirit of God. Such disorderly breaches greatly ruin the beauty of the Protestant Reformation (which I have no doubt was the special work of God, carried out by the power of His Spirit). They cause an unspeakable weakening of its interests, betray it to the insults and shame of the *Roman* party, and act as an invitation to the hidden agents of the *Pope*—who can talk as religiously as the best of you and disguise themselves in any form—to mingle with you, inflame you, and <term>dementate</term> <note>original: "dementate"; to drive someone mad or deprive them of their reason.</note> you to your own ruin.

8. Therefore, in the fear of God, as I said before, and with a timely concern for your own safety, the safety of your King and Nation, and for the Protestant Reformation and the spreading of the Gospel (which you claim to be so zealous for), stop this obvious folly. Return to a sober mind. Submit to your superiors in things that are <term>indifferent</term> <note>original: "indifferent"; things considered "adiaphora," or matters of religious practice not specifically commanded or forbidden by the Bible, which the Church has the authority to regulate for order.</note>, and reach a compromise with them in matters that are truly debatable. Do this so that even those outside our faith, seeing the proper liberty, decent order, and peacefulness of Reformed Christendom, may be more easily persuaded to shake off the *Roman* yoke,
